articles.title: Old woman with left lower extremity pain.
Successful systemic fibrinolysis in pulmonary embolism with a thrombus-in-transit.
articles.journal_full: Blood coagulation & fibrinolysis : an international journal in haemostasis and thrombosis

abstract.text: Right heart thrombus-in-transit with acute pulmonary embolism (PE) is a rare but potentially lethal clinical finding. Optimal management remains controversial, particularly when major contraindications or risk factors coexist. We present a 72-year-old male admitted to the emergency room with leading diagnosis acute coronary syndrome who was later diagnosed with acute PE and a massive, mobile right heart thrombus along with a concomitant ascending aortic aneurysm. Due to high surgical risk, systemic fibrinolysis was performed under close monitoring. Follow-up echocardiography demonstrated complete resolution of the intracardiac thrombus, rapid right ventricular recovery, and an intact thoracic aorta. This case highlights the importance of echocardiography in initial evaluation of patients with acute cardiovascular symptoms and also systemic thrombolysis as a viable, life-saving strategy for right heart thrombosis even in complex clinical scenarios.

articles.title: Hyperbaric oxygen therapy ameliorates cyclophosphamide-induced spermatogenic impairment by suppressing the RhoA/ROCK signaling pathway in mice.

abstract.text: Hyperbaric oxygen (HBO) therapy has shown potential to improve sperm quality and reproductive outcomes, but the mechanisms underlying its protective effects remain unclear. This study investigated whether HBO ameliorates cyclophosphamide (CYP)-induced spermatogenic impairment and whether Rhoa/Rock signaling is involved. Male BALB/c mice were assigned to control, CYP, and CYP + HBO groups. CYP was administered intraperitoneally for 5 consecutive days, followed by HBO treatment at 2.5 ATA for 60 min/day, 5 days/week for 2 weeks. Sperm parameters, serum sex hormones, testicular histopathology, oxidative stress indices, and Rhoa/Rock-related proteins were assessed. Rhoa knockout (KO) mice were additionally used for mechanistic evaluation. Compared with CYP treatment alone, HBO treatment increased sperm count by 80.95% (p < 0.0001) and progressive motility by 160.96% (p < 0.0001), while decreasing the sperm abnormality rate by 38.88% (p < 0.0001). HBO also reduced testicular MDA levels by 40.90% (p < 0.0001) and increased SOD activity by 69.53% (p = 0.0005). These changes were accompanied by reduced Rhoa and Rock1 protein expression and increased Nrf2 and Ho-1 expression. In Rhoa KO mice, the beneficial effects of HBO on serum hormone levels, sperm parameters, testicular indices, oxidative stress markers, and Nrf2/Ho-1 expression were largely abolished. These findings indicate that HBO therapy alleviates CYP-induced testicular oxidative stress injury and spermatogenic impairment, with Rhoa/Rock signaling contributing to the protective response.

articles.title: Demographic and clinical factors associated with Syphilis treatment initiation in a tribal health system: a retrospective cohort study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: American Indian/Alaska Native (AI/AN) individuals are disproportionately burdened by syphilis compared with other racial and ethnic groups. Early syphilis treatment is important to reduce transmission and prevent negative health outcomes. Understanding the characteristics of individuals who test positive and the factors associated with initiating treatment will support syphilis prevention and treatment efforts.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Cherokee Nation conducted a retrospective cohort study of individuals who tested positive for syphilis between 2016 and 2023. Data were collected from electronic health records and analyzed descriptively using counts and percentages and inferentially using Chi-square tests and multivariable logistic regression.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Overall, 356 individuals tested positive for syphilis and 314 (88.2%) initiated treatment. Most individuals who tested positive were ≤ 34 years (60.7%), single (83.4%), diagnosed during the COVID-19 pandemic (75.8%), residing in a county with a Cherokee Nation clinic (84.3%), and had a non-emergency healthcare visit within one year (70.5%). Approximately half (52.0%) had documented substance use and 31.2% had an STI co-infection within one year. Individuals diagnosed outside of an emergency department or urgent care setting had higher odds of initiating treatment compared with those diagnosed in an emergency department or urgent care setting (aOR=2.01, 95% CI: 1.02-3.97). Individuals with an STI co-infection had higher odds of initiating treatment compared with those without an STI co-infection (aOR=2.96, 95% CI: 1.19-7.33).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: This study suggests that focusing public health and clinical syphilis treatment efforts on emergency department and urgent care providers and patients may increase syphilis treatment initiation.

articles.title: Evidence-based management of kawasaki disease in the emergency department.

abstract.text: Kawasaki disease is currently the leading cause of acquired heart disease in children in developed countries. Signs and symptoms of Kawasaki disease may mimic other childhood illnesses, making it difficult to diagnose, especially in children who present with an incomplete form of the disease. Untreated Kawasaki disease may lead to the formation of coronary artery aneurysms and sudden cardiac death. Emergency clinicians should consider Kawasaki disease in pediatric patients presenting with prolonged fever, as prompt evaluation and management can significantly decrease the risk for serious cardiac sequelae. This review discusses the presentation, diagnostic criteria, and management of Kawasaki disease in the emergency department.

articles.title: Diagnosing and treating influenza in the emergency department: an evidence-based update.

abstract.text: Influenza is a common emergency department presentation that can cause serious complications, particularly in young children, older adults, pregnant and postpartum patients, and patients with underlying conditions. Because its clinical features overlap with those of other respiratory illnesses, emergency clinicians must determine when testing will inform care, which patients need prompt antiviral treatment, and who can be safely discharged. This review presents evidence-based recommendations for the evaluation and management of influenza in the emergency department, with attention to diagnostic testing, antiviral selection, complications, disposition, and common risk management pitfalls.

articles.title: Prehospital Pediatric Ventilation Quality Following Use of a Feedback Device: A Randomized Study.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Manual ventilation is a lifesaving intervention for children in respiratory arrest, yet the quality of pediatric ventilation delivered by emergency medical services (EMS) clinicians across geographically distinct sites is poorly characterized. We evaluated baseline EMS ventilation performance and whether a ventilation feedback device (VFD) improves adherence to national and international ventilation guidelines for ventilation rate, tidal volume, and mask seal.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a single-anonymized, randomized, crossover study of EMS clinicians from 5 EMS agencies across 3 metropolitan sites in the United States. Using a simulated 3-year-old toddler manikin, participants completed 2 sequential 2-minute respiratory arrest scenarios separated by a 10-minute washout period. Participants performed ventilation with and without real-time VFD feedback in randomized order. The EOLifeX VFD recorded ventilation rate, tidal volume, and mask leak with each breath. Adherence to age-based guidelines was analyzed using generalized linear mixed-effects models with participants nested within sites.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: We enrolled 123 participants across 5 agencies. With VFD feedback, guideline-recommended tidal volumes were achieved in 87% of breaths compared with 16.2% without feedback. Ventilation rate adherence improved from 65% to 88.6%. Mask leak of less than 30% occurred in 88.4% of ventilations with feedback vs 80% without feedback.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: In our simulation study, EMS clinicians rarely met manual ventilation guidelines for pediatric patients in respiratory arrest. The use of a VFD substantially improved guideline adherence, suggesting broad potential to improve ventilation performance.

A multifaceted intervention to increase bystander CPR rates after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest in France: a stepped-wedge, cluster-randomised, controlled trial.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Bystander cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) is a key determinant of survival after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA), but rates remain suboptimal worldwide. We evaluated whether a multifaceted intervention targeting emergency dispatch systems and community response could increase bystander-initiated CPR before emergency medical service (EMS) arrival.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a stepped-wedge, cluster-randomised trial in 15 French EMS agencies. The intervention combined dispatcher training for early recognition of cardiac arrest and telephone-assisted CPR, activation of trained volunteers through a geolocation smartphone application, and structured audit and feedback provided to EMS agencies. Consecutive adults (≥18 years) with non-traumatic OHCA were included. Randomisation was stratified by tercile of OHCA volume managed by each EMS in 2015. The intervention was implemented during a 1-month transition period before the intervention period at each EMS centre. A dedicated protocol guided dispatchers to identify cardiac arrest from unresponsiveness and abnormal breathing, then gave scripted compression-only instructions and activated volunteers, targeting recognition within 60 s of call pick-up and first compression within a further 60 s. The primary outcome was bystander-initiated CPR before EMS arrival. The trial was prospectively registered on ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT03633370) and is completed.

abstract.label: FINDINGS
abstract.text: Of the 15 EMS agencies initially randomised, two withdrew before recruitment began and were replaced, and one enrolled no patients. Therefore, between Aug 27, 2018, and Feb 20, 2022, 14 EMS agencies recruited a total of 2160 patients. The intention-to-treat analysis included 1684 patients (686 control, 998 intervention) enrolled across the 12 originally randomised EMS agencies. The mean age for all patients included in the intention-to-treat analysis was 67 years (SD 15), and 1205 (71·6%) were male. Bystander-initiated CPR before EMS arrival occurred in 421 (61·4%) patients in the control group and 708 (70·9%) patients in the intervention group (adjusted odds ratio [OR] 1·54 [95% CI 1·09-2·19]; p=0·017). Estimates were consistent across six prespecified sensitivity analyses (OR range, 1·38-1·55), remaining significant in four, but not after adjustment for cluster-specific secular trends (1·38 [0·98-1·94]) or baseline characteristics (1·39 [0·97-1·98]). No intervention-related adverse events were reported.

abstract.label: INTERPRETATION
abstract.text: A multifaceted intervention was associated with increased bystander-initiated CPR after OHCA, although the estimate was sensitive to the modelling of secular trends, and it did not translate into improved clinical outcomes. These findings support further investigation of coordinated community-based strategies to strengthen the early links in the chain of survival at a population level.

articles.title: To increase bystander CPR rates after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest, bystanders alone are not sufficient.
Trends in Australian Alcohol Consumption and Related Harms, 2010-2023.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Alcohol consumption is a substantial contributor to Australia's total disease burden. Various studies have examined trends in specific measures of consumption or harm, but a comprehensive analysis of trends is needed to understand the changing impact of alcohol in Australia. The current study synthesised data across multiple national indicators to assess long-term trends in alcohol consumption and related harms.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Publicly accessible data were compiled from 2010 to 2023 (or until the most recent year available) and categorised into the following: non-survey consumption measures (i.e., alcohol available for consumption and wastewater estimates); survey consumption measures (i.e., three nationally representative surveys); and alcohol-related harm measures (i.e., deaths, hospitalisations, ambulance attendances, injuries, random breath tests and alcohol treatment episodes). Data were analysed using joinpoint regression analysis to assess trends and quantify annual percentage change.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Survey and wastewater measures of alcohol consumption generally declined from 2010 onwards, while per-capita consumption as measured via tax and import data slightly increased. Rates of most alcohol-related harms increased substantially over the same period.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION AND CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Alcohol-related harms in Australia have generally increased over the past 15 years. This trend, alongside declines in survey-measures of consumption and relative stability in tax-based estimates of per-capita consumption raises potential concerns about the ongoing validity of population surveys as tools to measure consumption trends. Increasing harms also point to the urgent need for evidence-based interventions in Australian alcohol policy.

articles.title: Challenges that define approaches for rectovaginal fistula repair.

abstract.label: PURPOSE OF REVIEW
abstract.text: This article reviews recent literature to assess the challenges that define approaches in rectovaginal fistula (RVF) repair. RVFs remain a significant clinical challenge because of their profound impact on patient quality of life and the absence of standardized management strategies. The predominance of small studies and case series limits the ability to determine the most effective repair techniques. Consequently, a synthesis of contemporary evidence is needed to better inform decisions regarding surgical timing, technique selection, and optimization of patient comorbidities.

abstract.label: RECENT FINDINGS
abstract.text: Sphincter-preserving techniques continue to show promise for low- and mid-level fistulas. Fecal diversion may benefit patients with recurrent RVF or prior failed repairs, and the Martius flap remains a mainstay for complex cases, with the Musset technique emerging as a potential alternative. Multidisciplinary teams remain essential for repair success. Postoperative strategies, including negative pressure dressings and hyperbaric oxygen therapy, show potential for improving healing and reducing RVF recurrence.

abstract.label: SUMMARY
abstract.text: RVF remains a debilitating condition. Optimizing surgical timing, managing comorbid conditions, and tailoring operative and postoperative care through multidisciplinary collaboration are essential to achieving optimal patient outcomes. Further research is needed to clarify long-term functional results and refine emerging repair techniques, especially in those with recurrent RVFs.

articles.title: Diagnostic accuracy of high-sensitivity point-of-care troponin assays in emergency department for patients presenting with chest pain: a systematic review.
articles.journal_full: European journal of emergency medicine : official journal of the European Society for Emergency Medicine

abstract.text: Background High-sensitivity cardiac troponin (hs-cTn) assays have significantly enhanced the diagnosis in patients suspected of acute coronary syndrome (ACS). New hs-cTn point-of-care (POC) devices (turnaround time <20 min) may significantly reduce time to diagnosis. Purpose We evaluated the diagnostic accuracy of four currently commercially available hs-cTn POC devices to assess their potential for clinical implementation at the emergency department (ED). Methods We conducted a search in PubMed Central on 20 November, 2025. Studies were included if they investigated patients greater than or equal to 18 years presenting with chest pain suggestive of ACS and evaluated commercially available hs-cTn POC devices. Studies had to report diagnostic accuracy [sensitivity, specificity, negative predictive value (NPV), positive predictive value] for the diagnosis of acute myocardial infarction (AMI). Studies were assessed for risk of bias and applicability using the QUADAS-3 tool. Results We identified 436 articles. The 11 included studies consisted of both derivation and validation studies, including a total of 10 115 patients. The hs-cTn POC assays demonstrated the best diagnostic accuracy when applied as a single-test rule-out upon arrival at the ED, showing the following sensitivity and NPV: Atellica VTLi sensitivity 98.8-100% for troponin less than 4 ng/L (NPV: 99.8-100%) and 100% for troponin less than 7 ng/L (NPV 100%). Pathfast sensitivity 96.3-100% for troponin less than 3 ng/L (NPV: 98.1-100%). i-STAT sensitivity of 99.8% for troponin less than 5 ng/L (NPV: 100%). TriageTrue sensitivity of 100% for troponin less than 3 ng/L (NPV 100%). VTLi, Pathfast, and TriageTrue were also tested using the 99 th percentile with a 0 + 1/2/3 h troponin protocol. Reported sensitivities: VTLi 64.8-100%, Pathfast 87% for plasma and 83% for whole blood, and TriageTrue 79.8%. Conclusion Hs-cTn POC assays are reliable for integration into the diagnostic pathways for patients presenting with chest pain at the ED, mainly when used for rapid rule-out of AMI in patients with very low troponin values upon arrival.

articles.title: Adherence to Preoperative Ceftriaxone and Metronidazole Improves Outcomes in Acute Appendicitis.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Acute appendicitis is the most common pediatric surgical emergency, with approximately 70 000 cases annually in the United States. Preoperative antibiotic regimens vary widely. Prior to 2024, our institution used cefoxitin or meropenem based on perceived perforation status. To align with evidence supporting narrow-spectrum regimens, we implemented a standardized antibiotic protocol, aiming to increase use of recommended first-line preoperative antibiotics-intravenous ceftriaxone and metronidazole (CRO-MTZ)-for pediatric emergency department (PED) patients undergoing appendectomy for acute appendicitis from 0% to 75% within 8 months.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Our "Appendicitis Antibiotic Bundle" interventions included targeted education, pathway revision, and electronic health record updates. The primary measure was administration of CRO-MTZ. Secondary measures included preoperative antipseudomonal antibiotic use and antibiotic cost. Balancing measures were PED and hospital length of stay (LOS) and surgical site infections (SSIs). Statistical process control methods were used for analysis. We evaluated measures for both PED and all appendicitis patients, including those transferred from other facilities.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Administration of CRO-MTZ increased from 0% to 86% for PED and to 77% for all appendicitis patients. Preoperative antipseudomonal antibiotic use decreased from 19.1% to 5.5% in PED patients. The hospital-wide appendicitis SSI rate declined from 4.0% to 1.4%. There was a 21% decrease in preoperative antibiotic costs, a 25-minute reduction in PED LOS, and a 9.9-hour reduction in hospital LOS. All measures achieved special cause variation.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Associated with standardizing preoperative antibiotics for acute appendicitis, we noted reduced broad-spectrum antibiotic use and cost without increasing SSIs or LOS.

articles.title: The Bag Is Not Always Bad: Intrahospital Spread of 2-Step Urinary Tract Infection Screening.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: Urine cultures are frequently collected in hospitalized children for urinary tract infection (UTI) screening, despite often being unnecessary, invasive, and resource intensive. We aimed to decrease the proportion of unnecessary urine cultures in admitted children aged 90 days to 24 months from 65% to 45% over 1 year.

abstract.label: METHODOLOGY
abstract.text: The Model for Improvement guided problem understanding and change ideas. The main intervention included a 2-step UTI screening pathway previously implemented at our institution's emergency department with emphasis on completing point-of-care urinalysis (UA) on noninvasive urine bag sample. If positive for pyuria, bladder catheterization was performed for urine culture. Additional interventions included electronic medical record order set, education, interdisciplinary collaboration, and alignment with the institution's Choosing Wisely program. The primary outcome was the proportion of urine cultures completed without preceding positive UA screen. The balancing measure was the number of missed UTIs. Analysis used Statistical Process Control charts.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Baseline data (April 2020-March 2021) demonstrated that 65% of urine cultures were collected without a preceding positive UA. Postintervention data (April 2021-January 2025) demonstrated a decreased proportion of urine cultures collected without preceding positive UA screen from 65% to 22%. Special cause variation was detected 1 year following implementation of the pathway with sustained change during the study period. There was no increase in missed UTIs.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Process standardization using 2-step UTI screening pathway reduced unnecessary invasive urine culture collection in hospitalized children. The novel spread of this initiative to inpatient pediatric units aligns with best practices promoting high-value care.
