articles.title: Point-of-care ultrasound for assessing fetal head descent during labor.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: Ultrasound assessment of fetal head station is more accurate than digital examination, but its use is limited by the lack of equipment dedicated to the labor ward. Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) may overcome this barrier. We assessed the agreement between a handheld POCUS device and a conventional high-end system in measuring fetal head descent.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Seventy singleton pregnancies were examined in the second stage of labor. Two experienced operators, blinded to each other's results, performed translabial scans in randomized sequence, one with a handheld wireless device and one with a conventional system. Angle of progression (AoP) and head-perineum distance (HPD) were compared by intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC) and Bland-Altman analysis. Intraobserver repeatability was assessed in a subgroup by repeating both measurements de novo with each device. A blinded observer scored image quality (IQS) and measurement quality (MQS) from 0 to 3.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Mean AoP was 121.8 (12.0)° with the conventional system and 121.9 (12.3)° with POCUS (p=0.71); mean HPD was 31.5 (7.8) and 31.4 (8.1) mm (p=0.69). The ICC was 0.96 (95 % CI 0.94-0.98) for AoP and 0.97 (0.95-0.98) for HPD, with a bias of 0.16° (limits of agreement -6.6 to 6.9) and -0.10 mm (-4.2 to 4.0). IQS and MQS did not differ between devices. Intraobserver ICC ranged from 0.93 to 0.98, with a within-subject coefficient of variation of 2.4-4.2 %.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Handheld POCUS measurements of fetal head descent agree closely with those obtained with conventional equipment, with comparable repeatability and image quality, and may facilitate wider use of intrapartum ultrasound.

articles.title: Can Emergency Physicians Identify Frozen Tissue on Ultrasound? Implications for Frostbite Management.

abstract.text: IntroductionFrostbite injuries cause disfigurement and loss of functionality. The role of early imaging in management remains unclear because most modalities require infrastructure that prevents field application. Providers use point-of-care ultrasound to assess a range of soft tissue and musculoskeletal pathologies. The primary objective of this study is to determine the accuracy with which emergency physicians can identify frozen tissue on ultrasound.MethodsThree emergency medicine physicians evaluated whether porcine tissue was frozen or unfrozen by viewing standardized ultrasound clips. The team recorded clips of tissue thawing in a water bath from -10 to +10°C using a handheld ultrasound device. Each physician independently reviewed randomized clips and recorded their assessments. A 2 × 2 table was used to calculate the pooled sensitivity and specificity.ResultsEmergency medicine physicians reviewed 75 clips. They achieved a pooled sensitivity of 76% (95% CI 0.60-0.87) and a specificity of 87% (95% CI 0.68-0.96) for detecting frozen tissue compared with the tissue thermometer as the standard. Their results showed an overall accuracy of 80% (95% CI 0.69-0.88).ConclusionsIn this pilot study, emergency medicine physicians with advanced point-of-care ultrasound training identified frozen tissue on ultrasound 80% of the time. Future research should explore the sonographic features of frozen tissue in cases of frostbite and the test characteristics for sonographers with varying skill levels.

articles.title: Six-degree-of-freedom manikin neck for immobilisation training, incorporating linear potentiometers for real-time motion feedback.
articles.journal_full: Proceedings of the Institution of Mechanical Engineers. Part H, Journal of engineering in medicine

abstract.text: Neck immobilisation manoeuvres are performed by clinicians when moving patients with suspected cervical spine injuries and may mitigate further harm to the spinal column and spinal cord. Existing patient simulator manikins (PSM) do not have realistic neck articulations and are not instrumented to provide the user with feedback regarding manikin neck motion. The aim of this study was to design, manufacture, and test a proof-of-concept instrumented and articulated neck for an existing PSM. The neck comprised 3D-printed ball-and-socket articulations with 'intervertebral' motion limiting stoppers and extension springs to provide passive neck stiffness. Aluminium adaptor plates and locking mechanisms were designed to interface the neck with existing attachment points without modification of the existing manikin. A passive Stewart-Gough platform arrangement of linear slide potentiometers and a forward kinematics algorithm were used to measure the pose of the head with respect to the torso. Head angle accuracy, range of motion (ROM) and stiffness were assessed. Optoelectronic motion capture in 3D was used for verification measurements. ROM of the neck for flexion (25.0°), extension (29.3°), left (24.7°) and right (21.0°) lateral bending were limited by the potentiometer assembly, while ROM for left (52.5°) and right (48.4°) axial rotation was limited by the stoppers. Neck stiffness remained low until close to the end of ROM (range 5.8-28.3 Nmm/° across all axes) at which point stiffness increased by up to an order of magnitude (43.4-404.5 Nmm/°). Measured head-to-torso angle had root-mean-squared error less than 0.89° compared to motion capture measurements. The PSM neck prototype demonstrates design elements that enable six-DOF motion, low stiffness and real-time head-neck motion feedback. Adjustments to improve ROM, stiffness variation throughout ROM, anatomical realism and evaluation in paramedic training settings, would be required to implement the prototype in immobilisation training.

articles.title: Trends in Opioid Prescribing for Nonspecific Low Back Pain After CDC Guidelines and California Prescription Drug Monitoring Programs, 2012-2024.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Nonspecific low back pain (ns-LBP) is a widespread health challenge, and opioids were frequently prescribed upon first LBP presentation in the United States during the opioid epidemic. We assessed temporal changes in quarterly (Q) opioid prescriptions for new-onset ns-LBP from 2012 through 2024 at a California medical center amid evolving voluntary federal recommendations and mandatory state regulations.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We analyzed opioid prescription rates (prescription within 6 months of diagnosis) for ns-LBP patients diagnosed in all departments and stratified by emergency department (ED), and we compared high- versus low-dose prescription (≥50 morphine mg equivalents/day). Change point detection identified transitions without policy priors, and interrupted time series regression quantified level changes and trend modifications.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 31 940 ns-LBP patients, 2077 (6.5%) received opioids (mean [SD] age, 51.0 [17.6] y; 45.3% male; 53.7% White). Change points occurred at 2015 Q2 and 2018 Q4. Prescribing odds declined 2.7% per quarter from 2012 Q1 through 2024 Q4 (95% CI, 0.4%-5.0%; P = .02). ED patients (16.5% prescribed opioids vs 5.8% non-ED) showed a 54.2% immediate reduction at 2015 Q2 (95% CI, 18.8%-74.2%; P = .008), declining from 27.4% to 12.2% before plateauing; non-ED patients showed a 42.8% reduction at 2018 Q4 (95% CI, 27.5%-54.9%; P < .001). High-dose prescribing remained unchanged among opioid recipients.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Change points coincided with anticipatory adoption of the 2016 Centers for Disease Control and Prevention recommendations and 2018 California mandatory drug monitoring implementation. ED settings showed disproportionate reductions at 2015 Q2, consistent with knowledge diffusion of voluntary guidelines in settings with frequent opioid prescribing, while non-ED reductions coincided with immediate regulatory compliance at 2018 Q4. This distinction can guide future policy selection to address environment-specific adoption barriers.

articles.title: National memory path study: Formation of register-based cohorts of persons diagnosed with dementia in Finland in 2019 and 2021.

abstract.label: AIMS
abstract.text: This study describes the study design and methodology for the formation of novel National Memory Path cohorts, outlined to investigate dementia incidence and health and social service use preceding dementia diagnosis in Finland before and after the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic, and to enable further national-level analyses.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A register-based study was conducted, consisting of all Finnish home-dwelling adults who received a dementia diagnosis in 2019 or 2021. Dementia was defined based on the diagnosis in the Finnish Health Care Registers, or on the prescription of an anti-dementia drug in the Finnish Prescription Centre. Health and social service use within 12 months before the diagnosis included visits to outpatient and inpatient care in primary and secondary healthcare, emergency departments and home care recorded in the Finnish Health Care Registers.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Altogether, 23,121 and 22,419 persons were diagnosed with dementia in 2019 and 2021, respectively, corresponding to an incidence of 520 and 501 per 100,000 in mean population. The highest number of diagnoses occurred in the 75-84 age group. Within 12 months before the diagnosis, 98% had used health and social services. Outpatient care in primary healthcare was the most often used service, followed by outpatient care in secondary healthcare and emergency department use.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: National health registers enable comprehensive analysis of dementia incidence and service use. Frequent service use prior to the dementia diagnosis creates opportunities for dementia symptom detection across various parts of the health and social care system.

articles.title: Earlier Versus Later Extracorporeal Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation in Refractory Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest: A Nationwide Sequential Landmark Target Trial Emulation.
articles.journal: Eur Heart J Acute Cardiovasc Care
articles.journal_full: European heart journal. Acute cardiovascular care

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) may improve outcomes in refractory out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA), but the optimal timing of initiation remains uncertain, partly because prior comparisons did not restrict controls to patients still in refractory arrest at the same decision point.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We employed target trial emulation with a sequential landmark design in the Korean nationwide OHCA registry (2016-2023). Among patients with presumed cardiac aetiology who were still receiving emergency department (ED) CPR 15 minutes after ED arrival, landmarks were set at 15, 30, and 60 minutes, each comparing ECPR initiation within the subsequent window with no ECPR during that window among patients still in refractory arrest. Treatment effects were adjusted risk differences estimated by propensity score overlap weighting with 22 covariates.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 58,668 patients with refractory OHCA, 909 received ECPR. Weighted 30-day survival (ECPR vs. control) was 31.0% vs. 16.0%, 21.6% vs. 7.2%, and 10.9% vs. 3.2% at the 15-, 30-, and 60-minute landmarks; adjusted risk differences were +15.0 percentage points (95% CI 8.0 to 22.0), +14.4 (10.4 to 18.4), and +7.7 (3.7 to 11.7) (all P<.001). Favourable neurological outcomes showed a similar pattern, and in the exploratory timing-gradient analysis, the adjusted risk difference decreased with longer door-to-ECMO times but remained statistically significant through 120 minutes.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: ECPR was associated with improved survival and neurological outcomes at every landmark, including initiation beyond 60 minutes, where weighted 30-day survival with continued conventional CPR was 3.2%. Benefit was largest with early initiation but did not disappear at the commonly applied 60-minute benchmark, which may be overly restrictive for selected patients in capable systems.

articles.title: Can Planned Renewable Development Mitigate Near-Term Dry-Year Electricity Risk in Aotearoa New Zealand?
articles.journal_full: Journal of the Royal Society of New Zealand

abstract.text: Dry-year electricity shortfalls are a defining energy security challenge in Aotearoa New Zealand. Low hydro inflows and ongoing hydro releases deplete seasonal energy storage, increasing reliance on thermal generation, particularly during winter. Amid declining domestic gas reserves and tightening climate commitments, debate persists over how best to maintain system reliability. Our viewpoint provides quantitative modelling evidence, using the open-source PyPSA-NZ framework, on whether renewable energy projects in late stages of development can provide reliable electricity during a dry year within the next 5 years. These projects would add 3200 MW of solar photovoltaics, 500 MW of wind power, 130 MW of firm geothermal and 1050 MW of battery storage providing short-duration flexibility. Because solar and wind are dispatched ahead of hydro, this capacity would displace hydro generation year-round and raise reservoir storage entering winter. Reliability is secured primarily by this additional stored energy. Using the 2012 hydrological dry year as a stress test, we show that, if these projects are delivered, the modelled system maintains reliable supply without further investment in firm capacity or fuel supply. This suggests the main near-term risk to electricity reliability is not a shortfall of generation, but constraints on integrating new renewables, including transmission capacity and financing. We propose that near-term energy security policy prioritises the timely delivery of planned renewable energy projects.

articles.title: Accuracy of deep learning in quantifying epicardial adipose tissue: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

abstract.text: Epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) is significantly associated with cardiovascular disease and poor prognosis. Deep learning (DL) models have been explored for automatic EAT segmentation, but systematic evidence verifying their effectiveness is currently lacking. We conducted this meta-analysis to evaluate the accuracy of DL models for EAT segmentation and quantification, aiming to support the development of automated tools. We searched the Cochrane Library, Embase, Web of Science, PubMed, and IEEE Xplore through February 20, 2026. Studies reporting DL-based quantitative EAT segmentation were included. Quality was assessed with QUADAS-2. The Dice similarity coefficient (Dice), correlation coefficient (R), and Bland-Altman bias were used to evaluate segmentation efficacy, the correlation between automated segmentation and reference standards, and consistency, respectively. A random-effects model with the Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman method pooled these measures. Thirty eligible studies were included, covering five image types. For non-contrast computed tomography (NCCT), the pooled Dice was 0.888 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.853-0.924), and the pooled R reached 0.973 (95%CI: 0.958-0.982). The contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CECT) subgroup performed best, yielding a Dice of 0.910 (95% CI: 0.881-0.939) and an R of 0.989 (95% CI: 0.976-0.995). This meta-analysis quantifies the accuracy of DL models for EAT segmentation and volume quantification. The findings indicate that DL achieves robust accuracy on both NCCT and CECT images. However, given that most current studies rely on internal validation, future work should prioritize large-scale, multicenter external validation to support the translation of these promising DL tools into robust clinical diagnostic systems.

articles.title: Clinical significance of "complex" multimorbidity in hospitalised adult patients.

abstract.text: The term "complex multimorbidity" lacks universal consensus and its relevance remains unclear. We aimed to assess the prevalence of complex multimorbidity and its association with major healthcare outcomes. This was a prospective, single-centre study (internal medicine ward). We collected sociodemographic and clinical data and we categorised patients into non-overlapping categories, namely no multimorbidity, basic multimorbidity (two or more chronic conditions, with no qualifiers of complex multimorbidity), or complex multimorbidity ([a], ≥ 3 chronic conditions from ≥ 3 different body systems; [b], at least one physical and one mental condition; and [c], being ≥ 65 years old with ≥ 4 chronic conditions, including vision/hearing problems). The prevalence of multimorbidity sub-definitions and their association with major outcomes were assessed. Among 1415 patients (median age 80 years, IQR 69-86, F:M 1.15:1), multimorbidity (96.2%) and complex multimorbidity (93.8%) were highly prevalent. Complex multimorbidity was associated with older age, female sex (b 62.3% and c 62.4%), low income (b, 55.3%), and frailty (c, 94.1%), and significantly correlated with 12-month readmission to ward/emergency department, 12-month outpatient visits, and prescription changes. At multivariable analysis, complex multimorbidity a (OR 2.97; 95% CI 1.46-6.06; p = 0.003) and b (OR 2.98; 95% CI 1.37-6.47; p = 0.006) were associated with polypharmacy at discharge. Five-year mortality increased from no multimorbidity (0.076 per 100 person-months) to complex multimorbidity, being higher in complex a (1.947 per 100 person-months), b (2.428 per 100 person-months), and c (2.284 per 100 person-months). Complex multimorbidity provides meaningful clinical information in internal medicine. Further studies are needed to validate these observations.

articles.title: Mimics and Chameleons: A Patient with Accidental Hypothermia and Myocardial Infarction.

abstract.text: BackgroundAccidental hypothermia is an unintentional drop in core temperature below 35 °C, typically resulting from exposure to cold environmental conditions. Clinical presentations may vary widely depending on the severity of hypothermia and the presence of coexisting conditions complicating diagnosis and treatment. We report a case of accidental hypothermia caused by environmental exposure and associated with cardiogenic shock from a myocardial infarction with complete heart block.Case PresentationA group of ski tourers found a 62-y-old male skier at 3000 m in severe distress with abdominal pain, shivering, and profound exhaustion. On arrival at a mountain hut, he was agitated, then became unconscious and bradycardic with a weak femoral pulse. Once advanced medical equipment reached the hut, a 12-lead electrocardiogram showed an inferior ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) with complete third-degree atrioventricular block and a ventricular escape rhythm. The first measurable axillary temperature was 32.2 °C. Consciousness progressively improved, but bradycardia persisted during rewarming. The patient was evacuated 6 h after the diagnosis of acute STEMI. He underwent percutaneous coronary intervention and was successfully treated with a stent.ConclusionsThis case illustrates that hypothermia and environmental factors can complicate the diagnosis of atypical presentations of life-threatening conditions, such as STEMI, and how unexpected clinical findings not fully explained by hypothermia may indicate the presence of an underlying condition. In such situations, hypothermia staging systems should be used with caution. Early electrocardiography, awareness of cognitive biases, and the use of safe rewarming practices are essential to ensure timely diagnosis and prevent complications.

articles.title: Peripheral Nerve Blocks for Headaches.
articles.journal_full: Journal of primary care & community health

abstract.text: Patients have numerous options for headache management at home, yet when those fail, use of peripheral nerve blocks (PNBs) in the outpatient clinical or emergency department setting can be useful. Peripheral nerve blocks (PNBs) targeting the occipital and trigeminal scalp nerves are increasingly used by primary care and emergency medicine providers for acute headache relief and prophylaxis. The purpose of this article is to provide context, with an overview of epidemiology, diagnostic considerations, and trial evidence, along with procedural guidance for use of PNBs to treat headache disorders in the primary care setting. Despite methodological and outcome heterogeneities amongst randomized controlled trials (RCTs), evidence supports the use of PNBs, particularly greater occipital nerve block (GONB), for both acute headache relief and prophylaxis. It is within the scope of the primary care clinician to provide the option of PNB for appropriate patients. Further RCTs are warranted to define optimal nerve block combinations and procedural standards.

articles.title: Chemically Informed Artificial Intelligence Decoding of Full-Spectrum SERS Fingerprints for pH-Guided Intraoperative Assessment of Freshly Excised Melanoma Specimens.

abstract.text: Precise intraoperative delineation of melanoma margins remains a clinical challenge; incomplete resection causes recurrence, whereas over-excision compromises aesthetic and functional outcomes. While surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) provides chemically rich vibrational fingerprints, accurate intraoperative quantification is hindered by complex, coupled full-spectrum responses. Herein, we report a chemistry-informed artificial intelligence (AI)-SERS platform designed to support melanoma margin assessment via the detection of tumor-associated metabolic acidification. A pH-responsive HemS-SERS microarray was developed to translate the phenolic protonation/deprotonation of a hemicyanine-xanthene reporter into coordinated intensity redistributions across multiple Raman bands. Guided by this acid-base chemistry, our AI model (CIMPA-pH) encodes these pH-responsive vibrational anchors as learnable directional chemical priors, integrating full-spectrum attention with Henderson-Hasselbalch-guided prediction. This global decoding strategy accurately captures coupled pH responses, reducing prediction errors by approximately 85% and 54-78% compared to manual peak-ratio features and conventional deep-learning baselines, respectively, while a quality-control risk metric further reduces high-error readouts by 29.1%. Providing rapid (10 s) pointwise pH measurements, the platform distinguishes melanomas from normal skin with distinct pigmentation phenotypes in animal models and shows preliminary applicability for assessing melanoma-associated regions, including grossly atypical areas, in human resection specimens. Ultimately, this chemical-prior-guided SERS decoding strategy provides an interpretable framework with potential for metabolism-guided intraoperative margin assessment.

articles.title: Investigation and Management of Neonates Presenting to Hospital With Fever: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.journal_full: Journal of paediatrics and child health

abstract.label: AIM
abstract.text: Guidelines for neonates presenting to the emergency department (ED) with fever, including fever at home, recommend a full septic work-up and prompt administration of parenteral antibiotics. However, compliance is unknown. We sought to determine rates of guideline compliance in this population, reasons for non-compliance and rates and outcomes of serious bacterial infection (SBI).

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a single-centre retrospective cohort study of all neonates aged ≤ 28 days presenting to the ED with documented fever ≥ 38°C. We extracted and analysed hospital data from an electronic medical record for guideline compliance, reasons for non-compliance, rates of SBI, and clinical outcomes. Our primary outcome was the rate of guideline compliance.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: We included 475 patients, less than half (46.5%) of whom received guideline-compliant care. The primary contributor to guideline non-compliance was fever at home but no fever in the ED. Overall, 65/475 (15%) of patients had SBI, the majority of which were urinary tract infections (UTIs). 42/65 (64.6%) of patients with SBI had a confirmed concurrent viral infection. 107/475 (22.5%) were discharged home from ED, only one (0.9%) of whom was readmitted within 72 h.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Fewer than half of febrile neonates presenting to the ED receive guideline-compliant care, with the lowest compliance in infants who are febrile at home but not in the ED. Rates of SBI are high, and viral-bacterial co-infection is common. In some low-risk infants, a tailored approach to investigation and management may be suitable, though risk mitigation strategies and potential future guideline adaptation warrant further exploration.

articles.title: Self-Reported Completeness of Neurological Documentation in Prehospital Emergency Care: Associations With Neurological Training and Professional Experience.
articles.journal_full: Medical science monitor : international medical journal of experimental and clinical research

abstract.text: BACKGROUND Neurological assessment is a critical component of prehospital emergency care, particularly in time-sensitive conditions including stroke and traumatic brain injury. Neurological documentation practices in this setting remain insufficiently characterized. This study aimed to evaluate self-reported completeness of neurological documentation among paramedics, then examine its associations with neurological training and professional experience. MATERIAL AND METHODS A cross-sectional study was conducted between June 2025 and March 2026 among 348 paramedics working in emergency medical services in southeastern Poland. Data were collected using a structured electronic questionnaire. Self-reported documentation completeness was assessed using a composite score based on the reported frequency of documenting 7 neurological examination elements rated on a 5-point Likert scale (range: 7-35). RESULTS Overall self-reported documentation completeness was moderate (mean score: 24.57). Respondents frequently reported documenting basic neurological parameters (eg, level of consciousness: 81.0%); more detailed components were reported less consistently. Only 9.2% of respondents reported consistently documenting temporal neurological changes. The greatest self-reported deficiencies involved documentation of temporal neurological changes and detailed focal neurological findings. Participation in neurological training was associated with higher completeness scores (26.20 vs 23.24; P<0.001). Self-reported documentation completeness was positively correlated with professional experience (ρ=0.359; P<0.001). CONCLUSIONS Self-reported neurological documentation completeness among paramedics was moderate and selective; self-reported rates were lowest for dynamic and detailed focal neurological components. Participation in neurological training and greater professional experience were associated with higher self-reported documentation completeness scores. These findings suggest that standardized documentation protocols and targeted educational interventions contribute to more consistent neurological documentation practices in prehospital settings.

articles.title: The effect of using a dragon-themed nebulizer mask on treatment application duration, adherence, and fear in children presenting to the emergency department: A randomized controlled trial.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Nebulizer therapy can be distressing for young children, increasing fear, reducing cooperation, and prolonging treatment. This study examined the effects of a dragon-themed nebulizer mask on treatment duration, adherence, and fear in children receiving inhalation therapy in the pediatric emergency department.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This parallel-group randomized controlled trial was conducted between January and March 2026 in the pediatric emergency department of a tertiary hospital in Istanbul. A total of 140 children aged 3-6 years requiring nebulizer therapy were randomized to either the intervention group (dragon-themed nebulizer mask, n = 70) or the control group (standard care, n = 70). Data were collected using the Demographic Information Form, Fear Scale, and Treatment Duration and Adherence Assessment Form. The researcher-nurse recorded outcomes. The study followed CONSORT guidelines and was registered as a clinical trial (Clinical Trial ID: NCT06568120).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Baseline demographic characteristics were comparable between the groups (p > 0.05). The intervention group had significantly lower fear scores (p < 0.001, d = 3.05; 95% CI: 2.56-3.54) and shorter treatment duration (p = 0.012, d = 0.47; 95% CI: 0.14-0.81) than the control group. No significant between-group differences were observed in behavioral responses, including crying, treatment refusal, anger, or mask removal (all p > 0.05).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The dragon-themed nebulizer mask reduced fear and shortened treatment duration in preschool children receiving inhalation therapy in the pediatric emergency department. Child-friendly medical equipment may therefore represent a simple, low-cost strategy to improve treatment adherence and the overall treatment experience.

articles.title: The clinical efficacy of acupuncture therapy in patients with sudden sensorineural hearing loss: A systematic review, meta-analysis and network meta-analysis.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Acupuncture has gained increasing attention for the treatment of sudden sensorineural hearing loss (SSNHL). Hence, it is necessary to systematically evaluate and rank the effectiveness of acupuncture therapies for SSNHL.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A systematic search was conducted across PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, Web of Science, SinoMed, CNKI, VIP, and Wanfang databases from inception to January 1, 2026. Risk ratios (RR), mean differences (MD), and 95% conﬁdence intervals (CI) were used to estimate the eﬀect using R 4.4.1.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 36 studies involving 3360 patients diagnosed with SSNHL were included. Acupuncture combined with guideline treatment, especially glucocorticoids, could improve the overall effective rate (RR = 1.19, 95% CI 1.15-1.23, I2 = 11.1%, 95% CI: 0.0-42.8%, p < 0.0001, k = 36), with most trials reporting consistent enhancements in pure-tone audiometry. Among them, extra acupuncture emerged as the preferred adjunct, with routine acupuncture next, while moxibustion may serve as an alternative to either. A three-week course is currently recommended, and extending beyond that is unlikely to yield further meaningful efficacy. However, based on current findings, point injection may not be recommend for SSNHL. Hyperbaric oxygen therapy, currently used as a salvage therapy, may overlap with the complementary effects of acupuncture, and evidence to distinguish their efficacy remains limited.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Certain acupuncture therapies may be a complementary or alternative treatment for SSNHL, though the certainty of evidence rating by the CINeMA is too low to permit more than a tentative interpretation.

articles.title: Perioperative Management of Decompensated Peripartum Cardiomyopathy With Severe Left Ventricular Dysfunction: A Case Report.

abstract.text: Peripartum cardiomyopathy (PPCM) is a potentially life-threatening cause of heart failure that may be difficult to distinguish from the physiological symptoms of pregnancy. We report the case of a 42-year-old woman at 34 weeks of gestation who presented with progressive dyspnea and was found to have severe global left ventricular systolic dysfunction with an ejection fraction of approximately 20%. Despite initial improvement with diuresis, she developed recurrent acute decompensated heart failure requiring intensive care unit readmission. Point-of-care ultrasonography (POCUS) demonstrated pulmonary congestion and reduced forward flow, with a left ventricular outflow tract velocity-time integral (LVOT VTI) of 10 cm. Following hemodynamic optimization with diuresis and inotropic support, cesarean delivery was performed under general anesthesia with invasive monitoring and titrated vasoactive support. Postoperatively, LVOT VTI increased to 15 cm with corresponding clinical improvement. This case highlights the value of serial hemodynamic assessment, including POCUS, and multidisciplinary perioperative management in severe PPCM with recurrent decompensation.

articles.title: Feasibility of an Early Care Intervention for Acute Knee Injuries: A Mixed-Methods Study.

abstract.text: OBJECTIVE: We developed and evaluated the feasibility of a physiotherapist-led blended subacute-phase intervention. METHODS: In this mixed-methods feasibility study, participants were recruited from two emergency departments in Region Zealand, Denmark, within one week of acute knee trauma. They attended a weekly goal-oriented subacute-phase intervention combining progressive exercise, education, self-directed Acceptance and Commitment Therapy-based psychological support, and peer narratives delivered through a digital platform. Primary feasibility targets at 6 weeks were acceptability ≥75%, recruitment ≥5/month, retention ≥75%, and outcome completion ≥80%. Post-intervention interviews explored participant experiences and perceived value, expanding on the acceptability domain in an explanatory sequential mixed-methods approach. RESULTS: Twenty participants were enrolled (11 women, 9 men; median age 20 years), yielding recruitment of 2 participants/month. Sixty-seven per cent of participants attributed important improvement due to study participation. Fourteen participants (70%) completed the subacute-phase intervention, and 60% completed 6-week outcomes. Eight interviews revealed high perceived value through early support, meaningful rehabilitation, and promotion of future knee health. CONCLUSION: Although predefined quantitative feasibility criteria were not met, the intervention showed clinical promise and high participant value. Recruitment and retention barriers highlight the need for alternative early-care delivery pathways.

articles.title: Conservative Management of a Displaced Iliopsoas Avulsion in an Adolescent: A Case Report and Systematic Review.
articles.journal_full: Clinical journal of sport medicine : official journal of the Canadian Academy of Sport Medicine

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To report a case of traumatic iliopsoas tendon avulsion with displacement exceeding the commonly cited 2-cm surgical threshold, managed successfully without surgery, and to systematically review the literature on optimal treatment and return-to-sport outcomes.

abstract.label: DESIGN
abstract.text: Case report combined with a PRISMA-compliant systematic review of PubMed, Cochrane Library, and Embase.

abstract.label: SETTING
abstract.text: Level I university trauma center; systematic review of published case reports and series.

abstract.label: PARTICIPANTS
abstract.text: A 16-year-old male competitive soccer player (index case) and 58 additional patients from the literature, predominantly adolescent males with sports-related iliopsoas avulsion.

abstract.label: INTERVENTIONS
abstract.text: The index patient received conservative treatment with staged weight bearing and structured physiotherapy. Across the literature, 90% (52/58) were treated conservatively and 10% operatively.

abstract.label: MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES
abstract.text: Clinical recovery, strength restoration, radiographic union on MRI, and return to sport.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Eighteen studies (58 patients; 59 including this case) were analyzed. A bony lesser-trochanter avulsion was present in 98% (57/58). Of at least 9 patients with displacement >2 cm, 5 recovered fully nonoperatively. The index patient was pain-free with full strength and unrestricted soccer return at 3 months; 6-month MRI showed radiographic nonunion despite complete functional recovery. Return to sport approached 100%, typically within 10 to 12 weeks.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Available very low-certainty evidence suggests that nonoperative management can achieve favorable clinical recovery and return to sport after traumatic iliopsoas avulsion, including in some cases with displacement greater than 2 cm. Return-to-sport decisions may reasonably prioritize restored, pain-free function over radiographic union, but larger prospective studies are needed.

articles.title: Knowledge, attitudes, and practices on paediatric tuberculosis in rural Tanzania: insights for enhanced detection and care.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Paediatric tuberculosis (TB) remains underdiagnosed worldwide, with nearly 50% of cases missed. This issue is especially prominent in high-burden settings, where data on healthcare capacity for paediatric TB detection are limited. We assessed the knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) regarding paediatric TB among healthcare workers (HCWs), community health workers (CHWs), and families in rural Tanzania.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a cross-sectional KAP survey in Kondoa District (Dodoma Region) from November 2023 to October 2024. We measured knowledge and attitudes using validated questionnaires and assessed practices through reported TB-related activities.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Our sample included 87 HCWs, 86 CHWs, and 78 caregivers. Median knowledge scores (maximum = 18) were 11.2 (interquartile range (IQR) = 9.2-12.9) for HCWs and 8.9 (IQR = 7.9-9.8) for CHWs. Clinicians outperformed paramedical staff (P < 0.01), with those who had <5 years' experience scoring better. Attitude scores were high at 3.25/4 for HCWs and 3.1/4 for CHWs, with a moderate knowledge-attitude correlation among HCWs (ρ = 0.344, P = 0.001). Practice gaps were substantial: 17.2% of HCWs never diagnosed paediatric TB, only 24% referred for advanced diagnostics, and 38% of CHWs reported no cases. Although 92% of caregivers were aware of TB, only 1.8% of children had documented diagnoses.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Despite adequate knowledge, implementation gaps persist, suggesting systemic barriers. Strengthening diagnostics, referrals, training and stronger integration of CHWs into paediatric TB care pathways is essential.

articles.title: GDF-15 as an early marker for prognosis in patients with out-of-hospital cardiac arrest - Experience from the HAnnover COoling REgistry.
articles.journal: Am J Respir Crit Care Med
articles.journal_full: American journal of respiratory and critical care medicine

articles.title: Pediatric Ocular Trauma Associated with Sports and Recreational Activities: An 11-Year Retrospective Cohort Study.

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: To characterize the features of pediatric ocular trauma associated with sports and recreational activities presenting to a Level 1 pediatric trauma center.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A retrospective study was conducted using an ocular trauma registry of patients ≤ 18 years presenting to the emergency department between January 1, 2010, and March 10, 2021. Cases were categorized as activity-related or non-activity-related. Activity-related injuries were further grouped into contact sports, non-contact sports, and recreational activities. Demographic, clinical, and treatment variables were analyzed. Continuous variables were compared using t-tests or analysis of variance (ANOVA), and categorical variables using chi-square or exact tests.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 3,965 ocular trauma cases, 278 were activity-related. Patients with activity-related injuries were significantly older (p < 0.0001) and more frequently male (p < 0.0001) than those with non-activity-related injuries, while race distribution was similar (p = 0.155). Basketball (21.6%), biking (12.2%), baseball (11.9%), and football (11.5%) were the most common activities. Recreational activities predominated among children aged 0-6 years, whereas contact sports increased with age (p < 0.0001). Primary diagnoses varied by age (p = 0.006), with adnexal lacerations occurring more frequently in younger children (p = 0.008). Orbital fractures differed by activity type (p < 0.001), occurring predominantly in non-contact, projectile-related activities, and were more common among White than Black children (p = 0.047).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Activity-related pediatric ocular trauma disproportionately affects older children and males. Injury patterns vary by age and activity type, with high-velocity projectile sports causing a disproportionate number of orbital fractures. These findings support targeted prevention strategies, including age-appropriate education and increased use of protective eyewear.

articles.title: Reflections on Hurricane Katrina Two Decades Later: Findings From a Retrospective Population-Based Sample of Survivors.
articles.journal_full: Disaster medicine and public health preparedness

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To characterize morbidity, health care-seeking, and medication-related needs among survivors of Hurricane Katrina.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We used a two-stage sampling method to survey and interview 210 Hurricane Katrina survivors in Louisiana from 2006 to 2007. Interviews assessed injury, illness, environmental exposures, disaster-related damage, medication use, and health care-seeking behavior. Descriptive statistics were calculated.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Nearly 25% of respondents reported direct contact with hurricane-related floodwater. Nearly all experienced substantial property damage; wind (75.6%) and floodwater (67.5%) were the most common causes of damage. Before Hurricane Katrina, 70% of respondents reported good/excellent health; afterward, 35% reported worse health. Physical injury was reported by 17% of participants, emotional injury by 85%, and illness by 32%. Among those reporting injury/illness, 64% sought care for physical injuries, 21% for emotional injuries, and 63% for illnesses. Medication provision was common among those receiving care (70%-88%). Notably, 47% of respondents reported using at least one medication before the disaster, and 42% were unable to identify the specific medication they were taking.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Hurricane-related morbidity extends beyond health care system encounters and is likely underestimated by facility-based surveillance alone. Medication continuity and health care access represent important but understudied dimensions of disaster-related morbidity that remain relevant in contemporary disaster preparedness and response efforts.

articles.title: Assessment of the Health Research Response and Investments in Relation to Large-Scale Disasters in the United States.
articles.journal_full: Disaster medicine and public health preparedness

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: To describe health research following high-impact disasters (costs exceeding $1 billion) from 2010 to 2020 in the United States (U.S.) and to identify gaps and opportunities for improving post-disaster research to reduce adverse health impacts across communities.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Nine high-impact disasters were selected, and associated health research (N = 129 articles) was evaluated to characterize the health research response.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Sixteen different health outcomes were studied, with most data collection occurring more than a year after the disaster. Most studies used a surrogate of exposure (n = 92, 71%). No studies evaluated interventions, and few informed public health policies (n = 20, 16%) or resources (n = 7, 5%).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Even among the most high-impact U.S. disasters, this study identified a fragmented health research response that is largely descriptive. Improvements in post-disaster data collection and generalizable research studies are needed to better characterize health impacts, evaluate interventions, and foster evidence-based strategies to reduce morbidity and mortality of those impacted. Enhanced efforts to improve investments in, and processes to support the conduct of, health research are critical to improve disaster preparedness, response, and recovery efforts.

articles.title: While You Were Sleeping: Public Confidence in Rapid-Onset Hazard Warning Reception During Overnight Hours.
articles.journal_full: Disaster medicine and public health preparedness

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Rapid-onset hazards such as flash floods and tornadoes often provide limited warning lead time. When these events occur overnight, residents may be asleep and less likely to receive warnings, increasing injury and mortality risk. This study examined confidence in receiving overnight flash flood and tornado warnings and factors associated with warning reception confidence.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A cross-sectional survey of 1,008 adults across 12 southeastern U.S. states assessed confidence in receiving overnight flash flood and tornado warnings (12:00-6:00 AM) and factors associated with warning reception confidence.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Approximately half of respondents reported confidence in their ability to receive overnight flash flood (47.8%) and tornado (51.5%) warnings. Greater confidence was associated with greater warning source reliance, having a nighttime household emergency plan, higher nocturnal hazard risk perception, and greater trust in weather information. Mobile home residents reported lower confidence in receiving overnight tornado warnings than respondents residing in other housing types.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Many respondents remained uncertain about their ability to receive overnight warnings. Efforts to increase access to multiple warning sources capable of awakening residents, strengthen nighttime household preparedness planning, and improve awareness of nocturnal hazard risks may help improve overnight warning reception and support protective action.

articles.title: Compassion Fatigue in Emergency Department Nurses: A Cross-Sectional Evaluation of Predictive Models.

abstract.text: Compassion fatigue (CF) is a potential risk for Emergency Department (ED) nurses when workload increases, they experience repeated exposure to trauma or have a long-term emotional burden. A cross-sectional study was conducted to explore the connection between workload, trauma exposure, coping, and compassion satisfaction, and to assess the performance of logistic regression, Random Forest, and Support Vector Machine for internal binary classification. The sample included 150 full-time registered ED nurses from three tertiary hospitals, who completed a structured self-administered questionnaire. The analyses encompassed descriptive statistics, group comparisons, multiple linear regression, train-test split (80:20), and stratified five-fold cross-validation. The relationships between workload and trauma exposure were positive (r = 0.75 and r = 0.62, respectively), while the relationships between coping mechanisms and compassion satisfaction were negative (r = -0.52 and r = -0.60, respectively) with CF. The four-predictor regression model explained most of the variance in CF (adjusted R2 = 0.852), with coping and compassion satisfaction being the strongest negative predictors (β = -0.25; β = -0.35), and trauma exposure and workload being the strongest positive predictors (β = 0.32; β = 0.42). Random Forest outperformed Support Vector Machine (accuracy 83%, ROC-AUC 0.83) and logistic regression (accuracy 80%, ROC-AUC 0.80) in terms of internal classification (accuracy 85%, precision 82%, recall 80%, F1-score 81%, ROC-AUC 0.84). These findings suggest that the following interventions can be used to reduce compassion fatigue among ED nurses: workload management, trauma-informed support, coping, and compassion satisfaction.

articles.title: A Case Report of Lyme Carditis Presenting as New-Onset Atrial Flutter in the Emergency Department.

abstract.text: Lyme disease (LD) is the most common vector-borne disease in the United States and has several well-known pathologic sequelae if not treated, including third-degree atrioventricular block. However, an association between Lyme carditis and atrial arrhythmias has been described in some cardiology literature but has not been reported in emergency medicine or wilderness medicine literature. This case report describes an older adult with new-onset atrial flutter with rapid ventricular rate in the setting of early disseminated LD, who ultimately was treated with antibiotics, had resolution of atrial flutter, and has had no recurrence. As cardiac inflammation secondary to organ infection may manifest as multiple forms of arrhythmia, this case report highlights the importance of considering LD as a differential diagnosis when treating tick-exposed patients with new cardiac arrhythmias, including atrial flutter.

articles.title: Emerging Antiplatelet Agents: Revised Applications, Novel Targets, and Future Directions.

abstract.text: Current antiplatelet therapies reduce thrombotic, particularly atherothrombotic events but remain constrained by bleeding risk, residual ischemic events, and pharmacokinetic or pharmacogenomic limitations. This review first evaluates the evolving strategies to optimize established agents, including P2Y12 monotherapy, genotype-guided de-escalation, aspirin formulation research, and aspirin in cancer chemoprevention. Second, it examines emerging agents designed for prehospital use in acute myocardial infarction and CYP2C19-independent clopidogrel alternatives aimed at improving global access. Finally, novel molecular targets including glycoprotein VI, protease-activated receptor 4, 12-lipoxygenase, and glycoprotein Ibα that aim to decouple thrombosis from hemostasis are discussed.

articles.title: Direct Visualization of Congenital Pulmonary Airway Malformation by Neonatal Point-Of-Care Lung Ultrasound.

abstract.text: Congenital pulmonary airway malformation (CPAM) is usually assessed prenatally and further characterized postnatally with cross-sectional imaging. Direct visualization by lung ultrasound may be limited when normally aerated lung overlies the lesion. We report a term (39 weeks' gestation) neonate with a prenatally suspected CPAM in whom bedside point-of-care ultrasound directly demonstrated a peripheral heterogeneous multicystic lesion in the left lung. This case illustrates the characteristic sonographic appearance of a pleural-accessible CPAM and highlights lung ultrasound as a rapid, radiation-free adjunct for bedside assessment while emphasizing that a normal ultrasound examination cannot exclude a deeper congenital lung malformation.

articles.title: Fever, seizures and mydriasis in an 18-month-old girl.
articles.journal: Arch Dis Child Educ Pract Ed
articles.journal_full: Archives of disease in childhood. Education and practice edition

articles.title: Escape, Relearn and Retain: using escape rooms as a simulation based quality improvement project to reinforce Pediatric Advanced Life Support retention at a teaching hospital.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Reliable delivery of paediatric resuscitation care depends on effective teamwork, leadership and timely application of Pediatric Advanced Life Support (PALS) principles. In teaching hospitals, infrequent exposure to real-life paediatric emergencies can lead to variability in team performance and decline in confidence and variability in application of resuscitation principles between certification cycles. Innovative, low-cost strategies are needed to support ongoing team readiness and reliability of emergency care.

abstract.label: PROBLEM
abstract.text: At a tertiary teaching hospital, paediatric resident doctors and nurses receive formal PALS certification early in training with limited opportunities for structured reinforcement thereafter. This created a local quality gap in maintaining consistent team performance and confidence during paediatric emergencies.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: To assess the feasibility and preliminary impact of an escape room–based simulation intervention as a quality improvement strategy to reinforce PALS knowledge, team readiness, confidence and application of PALS principles among paediatric resident doctors and nurses.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A single-centre, mixed-methods quality improvement feasibility initiative with educational outcome measures using a pre–post design was conducted over 6 months. An interprofessional escape room–based simulation comprising three paediatric emergency scenarios (cardiopulmonary arrest, respiratory emergencies and shock) was implemented. Outcome measures included changes in knowledge scores, self-efficacy ratings and team performance assessed using the validated Team Emergency Assessment Measure (TEAM). Qualitative feedback from structured debriefings informed process evaluation and iterative refinement.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The self-efficacy questionnaire significantly improved confidence across the cognitive, affective and psychomotor domains, with median scores increasing from 3.5 (IQR 2.6–4.0) to 4.8 (IQR 4.6–5.0), p=0.005. Immediate post-intervention knowledge scores increased from 66% to 70% (p=0.004). The TEAM scores indicated excellent teamwork, particularly in the cardiopulmonary scenario. The participants described the escape room as engaging, novel and helpful in enhancing clinical reasoning and collaboration.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Escape room–based simulation is a feasible and acceptable quality improvement intervention to reinforce paediatric resuscitation knowledge and support team readiness in paediatric emergency training. While not a replacement for formal PALS certification, it may serve as a sustainable adjunct to reduce variability in team performance between certification cycles. Further work is needed to evaluate longitudinal impact and scalability.

articles.title: Does a nurse-led intervention improve medication adherence among older adults with hypertension in Spanish primary care? Protocol for a pragmatic cluster randomised controlled trial (NURSE-ADHERE-HTN).

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Poor long-term adherence to antihypertensive medication remains a major challenge in hypertension management, particularly among older adults, contributing to suboptimal blood pressure control, cardiovascular morbidity and reduced quality of life. Nurse-led educational and behavioural interventions delivered in primary care may improve medication adherence; however, evidence from pragmatic cluster randomised trials integrated into routine clinical practice remains limited. This study aims to evaluate whether a nurse-led multidimensional educational and behavioural intervention improves adherence to antihypertensive treatment among older adults with hypertension in primary care.

abstract.label: METHODS AND ANALYSIS
abstract.text: NURSE-ADHERE-HTN is an ongoing pragmatic, open-label, cluster randomised controlled trial being conducted in 14 primary care centres of the Navarra Health Service–Osasunbidea, Spain. The trial was prospectively registered in the ISRCTN registry (ISRCTN35559821). Primary care centres were centrally allocated in a 1:1 ratio to the intervention or usual-care group, with seven centres per group and two participating nurses per centre. The target sample size is 280 participants aged 60 years or older with hypertension, prescribed at least one antihypertensive medication and identified as non-adherent using the 4-item Morisky Medication Adherence Scale (MMAS-4). The intervention consists of a nurse-led multidimensional educational and behavioural programme integrated into routine primary care, comprising individualised education, motivational interviewing, review of antihypertensive treatment and medication-taking routines, Mediterranean diet counselling, physical activity support and telephone reinforcement. The primary outcome will be adherence to antihypertensive treatment at 6 months, assessed using the MMAS-4 in accordance with the licensed wording, structure and standardised scoring method. Adherence will also be assessed at baseline and 12 months, with the 12-month assessment used to evaluate whether any intervention effect observed at 6 months is maintained over time. Electronic prescription dispensing records will provide a complementary measure of adherence. Secondary outcomes will include blood pressure assessed using 24-hour ambulatory monitoring, health-related quality of life, cardiovascular-related emergency department visits and hospital admissions, symptoms of anxiety and depression, Mediterranean diet adherence, physical activity, reasons for non-adherence, anthropometric and selected laboratory variables, medication burden and concordance between adherence measures. Outcomes will be assessed at baseline, 6 months and 12 months. Prespecified exploratory analyses will assess effect modification by sex. Statistical analyses will account for clustering at the primary care centre level.

abstract.label: ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION
abstract.text: The study was approved by the Navarra Clinical Research Ethics Committee (reference PI_2023/92). Written informed consent is obtained from all participants before enrolment. Findings will be disseminated through peer-reviewed publications, conference presentations and reports to healthcare stakeholders.

abstract.label: TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER
abstract.text: ISRCTN35559821.

articles.title: FRAILTY AND POSTOPERATIVE OUTCOMES IN PATIENTS AGED ≥80 YEARS UNDERGOING EMERGENCY ABDOMINAL SURGERY.
articles.journal_full: Journal of gastrointestinal surgery : official journal of the Society for Surgery of the Alimentary Tract

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: The number of patients aged ≥80 years undergoing emergency abdominal surgery is increasing. Although frailty has been associated with adverse surgical outcomes, its impact in this population remains insufficiently characterized. We aimed to describe the clinical and frailty characteristics of this population and identify factors associated with postoperative complications and mortality.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a prospective single-center cohort study including consecutive patients aged ≥80 years undergoing emergency abdominal surgery between September 2018 and March 2023. Frailty was assessed using the Clinical Frailty Scale (CFS). Functional status (Barthel Index), cognitive impairment (GDS-R), nutritional status (MNA-SF), comorbidity burden (CIRS-G), serum albumin, and postoperative outcomes were assessed. Surgical complications were graded according to the Clavien-Dindo classification.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 178 patients were included (mean age, 86.1 years; 24.7% nonagenarians). Surgical complications occurred in 38.4%, medical complications in 76.1%, and major complications (Clavien-Dindo ≥III) in 107 (71.3%). In-hospital mortality was 6.2%. Hypoalbuminemia was associated with surgical complications. Medical complications were associated with functional dependence, cognitive impairment, malnutrition risk, hypoalbuminemia, and frailty. Major complications were associated with functional dependence, cognitive impairment, hypoalbuminemia, and frailty. Frailty was not associated with 12-month mortality or 30-day Emergency Department visits.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Frailty is associated with postoperative medical complications and their severity in patients aged ≥80 years undergoing emergency abdominal surgery. Functional dependence and hypoalbuminemia identify high-risk patients who may benefit from multidisciplinary geriatric co-management.

articles.title: Comparison of delivery room wrist versus earlobe pulse oximetry in newborns: A randomized controlled trial.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Rapid acquisition of reliable pulse oximetry signals in delivery room is challenging due to transitional circulation, low peripheral perfusion, motion artifact, vernix, and skin edema. This randomized controlled trial compared right earlobe and right wrist pulse oximetry to determine differences in time to reliable signal acquisition.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Pregnant women at ≥34 weeks gestation were randomized before delivery. Pulse oximetry probe was applied to either the right earlobe or right wrist immediately after birth using sensor-to-oximeter-first technique with Masimo® SET® rainbow® Radical-7® CO-Oximeter®. The primary outcome was time from completion of sensor application to reliable display of oxygen saturation and heart rate. Secondary outcomes included time from birth to start of sensor application, sensor application time, time from birth to reliable signal, perfusion index, and number of probe reapplications.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Ninety-six neonates were randomized, with 48 in each group. Time from completion of sensor application to reliable signal was similar between ear and wrist groups (67.1 ± 41.4 vs 74.5 ± 48.2 s; mean difference -7.4 s; 95% CI -25.6 to 10.8; P = 0.42). Sensor application time was shorter in ear group (mean difference -16.3 s; 95% CI -17.7 to -14.9; P < 0.001), resulting in shorter time from birth to reliable signal (mean difference -28.8 s; 95% CI -53.9 to -3.7; P = 0.02). Perfusion index was lower, and reapplication rates were higher in ear group.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Time to reliable signal acquisition after probe placement did not differ between the earlobe and wrist. Further studies using neonatal-specific ear probes are warranted.

articles.title: Unexpected coagulopathy in thrombolyzed stroke: experience from a single center in Chile.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: The effectiveness of intravenous thrombolysis (IVT) for acute ischemic stroke (AIS) is time-dependent, and waiting for coagulation tests (COT) may delay treatment initiation. In several countries, IVT is initiated without waiting COT results; this approach has not been evaluated in South America. In this region, excessive alcohol consumption may increase the prevalence of unrecognized chronic liver disease.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To determine the frequency of unsuspected coagulation abnormalities among patients with AIS treated with IVT at a single tertiary care center in Chile.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A prospective analysis of all patients treated with IVT at Clínica Alemana between June 2016 and July 2025, assessing the proportion of individuals with unexpected coagulation abnormalities.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 480 patients with AIS received IVT. The COTs were normal in 445 patients (92.7%), abnormal in 9 (1.88%), and incomplete or not performed in 26 (5.42%). No clinical differences were observed among the three groups. Patients with coagulation abnormalities or incomplete/not performed COT were significantly less frequent in the Emergency Room (ER) during the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic (p = 0.001). Among those with abnormal COT results, significant differences were found in international normalized ratio (INR) values (p < 0.000) and platelet count (p = 0.001). The functional outcomes at 3 months, as well as mortality and rate of symptomatic intracerebral hemorrhage, did not differ across groups.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Unexpected coagulation disorders are an infrequent finding in patients with AIS treated with IVT at our center in Santiago, Chile. Therefore, blood test results should not be awaited before initiating IVT.

articles.title: Educational Interventions to Improve Preparedness for Mass Casualty Incidents and Armed Conflict: A Systematic Review.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Mass casualty incidents (MCIs), terrorist attacks, and armed conflicts place significant demands on healthcare systems and require rapid triage, effective teamwork, and life-saving interventions under resource-limited conditions. Training and educational programs are widely implemented to improve disaster preparedness among healthcare providers, but the measurable effectiveness of these interventions remains unclear. This systematic review aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of educational interventions on measurable preparedness outcomes among healthcare professionals.

abstract.label: MATERIALS AND METHODS
abstract.text: A systematic review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA guidelines. Medline (Ovid), Embase, Web of Science Core Collection, Cochrane CENTRAL, and Google Scholar were used. Studies evaluating pre- and post-intervention outcomes following educational or training interventions for MCIs or war-related scenarios were included. Outcomes of interest included knowledge, clinical skills performance, and triage accuracy.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 1,836 records were identified, of which 42 studies met the inclusion criteria. Most studies used single-group pre-post designs (n = 32, 76%), while 6 were randomized controlled trials (14%) and 4 were controlled non-randomized studies (10%). Educational interventions included course-based training, simulation-based training, e-learning, and blended learning approaches. The majority of studies reported significant improvements in knowledge (14/15 studies), hands-on clinical skills (13/14 studies), and triage performance (6/7 studies) following training. Only 4 studies assessed long-term retention.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Educational interventions improve preparedness for mass casualty incidents and war-related scenarios. Simulation-based and multidisciplinary training appear most effective. However, the certainty of evidence quality remains limited. Preparedness should therefore be viewed as a continuous process requiring repeated training, objective evaluation, and stronger civil-military collaboration.

articles.title: Ischemic stroke after bivalent mRNA COVID-19 vaccination and influenza vaccination during the 2022-2023 season: a multi-site self-controlled case series study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: The Vaccine Safety Datalink (VSD) detected a statistical signal for ischemic events (ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack) following bivalent mRNA COVID-19 vaccination through prospective surveillance during 2022-2023. Although multiple studies from other surveillance systems and countries reported no increased risk, important methodological limitations remained. This U.S. study addressed those limitations by evaluating the ischemic stroke risk following bivalent mRNA COVID-19 vaccination, influenza vaccination, and their same-day coadministration using an event-dependent self-controlled case series (SCCS) design.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Study outcomes included first-ever ischemic stroke (primary outcome), first-in-1-year ischemic stroke (secondary outcome), and ischemic events (exploratory outcomes), identified using ICD-10-CM codes in inpatient and emergency department settings during September 1, 2022-March 31, 2023, among individuals aged ≥12 years across eight VSD sites. Analyses were conducted separately for Pfizer-BioNTech and Moderna bivalent vaccines, with relative incidences (RI) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) estimated for 1-21-day and 1-42-day risk intervals, using person-time outside these intervals as the control period. Subgroup analyses were performed by age group (12-64, ≥65 years) and history of documented SARS-CoV-2 infection.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 6510 first-ever ischemic strokes were identified among more than 6.8 million participants. Among recipients of Pfizer-BioNTech bivalent COVID-19 and influenza vaccines, no statistically significant increased risk of first-ever ischemic stroke was observed following bivalent COVID-19 vaccination (RI = 0.94; 95% CI: 0.63-1.41), influenza vaccination (RI = 0.95; 95% CI: 0.82-1.10), or same-day coadministration (RI = 1.15; 95% CI: 0.88-1.49) within 1-21-day risk intervals; findings were similar for 1-42-day intervals. Comparable null results were observed for Moderna vaccine and across all subgroups, secondary, and exploratory outcomes.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: No increased risk of ischemic stroke was found following bivalent mRNA COVID-19 vaccination, influenza vaccination, or their coadministration in this multi-site SCCS study. These findings are consistent with previous studies and underscore the importance of continued vaccine safety monitoring.

articles.title: β-Blockade reprograms trauma-induced changes in bone marrow exosomal microRNAs.
articles.journal_full: The journal of trauma and acute care surgery

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Severe trauma produces sustained sympathetic activation that contributes to bone marrow dysfunction, impaired hematopoiesis, and persistent injury-associated anemia. Although β-adrenergic blockade improves bone marrow recovery after injury, the downstream mechanisms remain incompletely defined. We hypothesized that propranolol reprograms trauma-induced bone marrow extracellular vesicle (EV) microRNA (miRNA) expression toward restoration of hematopoietic homeostasis.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Sprague-Dawley rats were randomized to naïve, polytrauma (PT), PT plus propranolol (PT+BB), PT with chronic restraint stress (PTRS), or PTRS plus propranolol (PTRS+BB) groups (n=6-8 per group). Propranolol (10 mg/kg intraperitoneally) was administered daily. On day 7, complete blood counts were obtained, and bone marrow-derived EV miRNAs were profiled using the NanoString nCounter platform. Differentially expressed miRNAs were identified using an absolute log2 fold change ≥1.5 and p<0.05. Predicted pathways were assessed using Ingenuity Pathway Analysis, and miR-125b-5p was validated by quantitative PCR.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: PT altered 45 EV miRNAs compared with naïve animals, including suppression of miRNAs involved in hematopoietic stem cell maintenance and erythropoiesis. Chronic restraint stress amplified this response, with 93 differentially expressed miRNAs following PTRS. Propranolol altered 12 miRNAs after PT and 43 after PTRS, increasing hematopoietic regulatory miRNAs, including miR-125b-5p, while suppressing several stress- and inflammation-associated miRNAs. Pathway analysis identified alterations in NOTCH, RUNX1, PTEN, thyroid receptor/retinoid X receptor, and histone modification signaling. Quantitative PCR confirmed a 2.4-fold increase in EV miR-125b-5p following propranolol in PTRS animals (p=0.018).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Trauma and persistent adrenergic stress broadly remodel bone marrow EV miRNA signaling. β-Adrenergic blockade selectively reprograms these networks toward pathways associated with hematopoietic recovery, identifying EV miRNAs as potential mediators of posttraumatic bone marrow dysfunction.

abstract.label: LEVEL OF EVIDENCE
abstract.text: Not applicable-Animal research.

articles.title: Massive envenomations by bees in French Guiana: A ten-year retrospective study (2014-2023).

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Massive bee stings can cause systemic manifestations and life-threatening complications. In French Guiana, data on such envenomations are scarce. This study aimed to describe the epidemiology, clinical characteristics, and management of patients presenting to the emergency department.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We retrospectively reviewed medical records of all patients admitted for bee stings over the period 2014-2023 at Cayenne Hospital. A composite variable of systemic involvement was created (neurological, respiratory, hemodynamic and digestive). All analyses were descriptive. An exploratory two-graph receiver operating characteristic (TG-ROC) analysis was used to describe the sensitivity and specificity of sting-count cut-offs for four binary indicators of systemic involvement.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 143 patients included, 40% (n = 57) presented at least one systemic manifestation. The median number of stings was 50 [20-150]. In the exploratory TG-ROC analysis, the cut-offs maximizing the Youden index were approximately 72 stings for digestive and hemodynamic manifestations and 99 stings for neurological and respiratory manifestations, with modest sensitivity (0.50-0.76) and specificity (0.68-0.76). Overall mortality was low (0.7%, n = 1/143).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: This study provides the first detailed epidemiological and clinical description of massive bee envenomations in French Guiana. Exploratory analyses suggested that systemic manifestations may occur at sting counts below the conventional 200-sting threshold. These findings should not be interpreted as a validated clinical cutoff and require confirmation in prospective multicenter studies.

articles.title: The impact of presentations in scientific conferences: Publication and citation rates in trauma surgery.
articles.journal_full: The journal of trauma and acute care surgery

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Understanding the publication rates and citation patterns of conference abstracts is critical for program committees and investigators alike. However, the downstream scholarly outcome of conference abstracts remains poorly characterized. We hypothesized that across contemporary US trauma-related scientific meetings, a substantial proportion of conference abstracts would not progress to peer-reviewed publications, and that publication rates and citation patterns would vary by presentation format and conference.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a cross-sectional study of abstracts presented at four major US trauma surgery conferences from 2017 to 2019. We identified peer-reviewed manuscripts associated with conference abstracts via Google Scholar and PubMed. We collected presentation format, publishing journal, 2024 journal impact factor, and citation count. A cohort of directly submitted peer-reviewed manuscripts was also analyzed. Mixed-effects Poisson regression models assessed the association between presentation and citation counts, adjusting for publication timing.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 1,157 abstracts, 762 (66%) were published as peer-reviewed manuscripts. Most manuscripts were published in the Journal of Trauma and Acute Care Surgery (JTACS) (55%), with 5 in journals with a higher-impact factor than JTACS. On regression analysis, abstracts presented as oral presentations, and published in journals with an impact factor higher than JTACS, were associated with a greater number of citations. When comparing manuscripts presented as abstracts to directly submitted peer-reviewed manuscripts, abstract presentation was associated with 22% more citations (incidence rate ratio: 1.22; 95% CI [1.16-1.29]; p<0.001).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: This cross-sectional study of four trauma societies found that approximately a third of presented abstracts did not progress to peer-reviewed publication, with publication rates varying by conference and presentation format. Exploratory analyses found that among those published in JTACS, published manuscripts originating from presented abstracts demonstrated a modestly higher citation count compared with directly submitted manuscripts. Our findings highlight an opportunity to better understand how conference time and investigator effort translate into downstream scholarly output.

abstract.label: LEVEL OF EVIDENCE
abstract.text: Prognostic/Epidemiological; Level IV.

articles.title: Association between nighttime heat exposure and emergency hospitalization for out-of-hospital cardiac arrest: A time-stratified case-crossover study in Japan.

abstract.text: Few studies have explored the adverse health effects of nighttime heat exposure. This study examined the association between nighttime heat exposure and emergency hospitalization for out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) in Japan. Hospitalizations were identified from a nationwide administrative database covering the period from May to September between 2011 and 2021. Days with minimum temperatures higher than region-specific 92.5th percentile temperatures were considered as exposed to nighttime heat. Daily maximum temperature was adjusted for as a proxy for daytime heat exposure. First, a time-stratified case-crossover study using conditional quasi-Poisson regression analysis was conducted to estimate location-specific heat-related relative risks (RRs) of emergency hospitalization for OHCA over lag 0-6 days. Second, a random-effects meta-analysis was conducted to estimate pooled RRs. The analysis was further stratified by age, sex, and region. Third, in an attempt to account for the geographical heterogeneity in RRs, the location-specific penetration rate of air conditioners (ACs) was included as a meta-regressor. A total of 135,898 hospitalizations for OHCA were identified. Nighttime heat exposure was associated with increased emergency hospitalizations for OHCA (RR: 1.090 (95% confidence interval (CI): 1.047-1.135). Higher RRs were observed among people aged ≥ 75 years and females living in northern areas (1.295 (95%CI: 1.117-1.500) and 1.352 (95%CI: 1.145-1.596), respectively). In locations with a lower penetration rate of ACs, females and those aged ≥ 75 years were at higher RRs.

articles.title: Rise of Lower Respiratory Tract Infections Other than Respiratory Syncytial Virus in the Emergency Room: Results from the Season (2024/25) of the RISE Study.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Acute respiratory infections (ARI) are a major cause of pediatric emergency department (ED) visits and hospitalizations. Although respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), influenza, and rhinovirus (RV) are common etiological agents, pathogen-specific data from pediatric emergency settings remain limited.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This prospective surveillance study quantified ARI-related ED visits, described pathogen-specific epidemiology, and assessed attendance and hospitalization rates as well as the distribution of lower versus upper respiratory tract infections (LRTI/URTI) in children younger than 60 months in two pediatric EDs in Berlin between November 1, 2024 and May 31, 2025. Respiratory pathogens were identified using nasopharyngeal swab samples tested by multiplex real-time RT-PCR (QIAstat-Dx® Respiratory Panel Plus).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Within the study period 4042 ARI-related ED visits occurred. A total of 310 children were enrolled in our study (median age 18 months); 115 (37.1%) had LRTI and 195 (62.9%) URTI. At least one respiratory pathogen was detected in 271 children (87.4%). The attendance rate for RSV was 24.4% (66 cases), for FLU 25.8% (70 cases), and for RV 29.5% (80 cases). Overall, 93 children (30.0%) were hospitalized, including 65 with LRTI and 28 with URTI.
