Hospitalization rates were highest for RSV infections (26/65, 40.0%) and RV infections (28/65, 43.1%), and lower for FLU infections (13/69, 18.8%). Hospitalization due to LRTI predominated among children with RSV (24/26, 92.3%) and RV infections (20/28, 71.4%), whereas FLU infections were less frequently observed (7/13, 53.9%). Furthermore, younger age, a history of pneumonia, a history of bronchiolitis, and the absence of breastfeeding were associated with hospitalization.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In contrast to the previous season, in which RSV was associated with the highest attendance and hospitalization rate, we observed a high burden of RV infections in the 2024/2025 season. These findings may impact surveillance strategies, clinical management, and future public health strategies.

articles.title: Clinical outcomes of combined MPFL-reconstruction with MPTL-augmenting patellar distalization using hamstring autograft versus isolated MPFL in adolescents with patella alta: a retrospective comparative study.
articles.journal_full: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Patella alta is a major risk factor for recurrent patellar dislocation in adolescents. This study aimed to compare the clinical outcomes of isolated medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) reconstruction with those of MPFL reconstruction augmented by medial patellotibial ligament (MPTL)-distalization, both using a semitendinosus hamstring autograft, in adolescent patients with patella alta.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A retrospective cohort study was conducted on 28 adolescent patients (mean age 11.2 ± 1.6 years; 9 males, 19 females) treated for recurrent patellar dislocation between May 2020 and July 2025. All patients had patella alta (Caton-Deschamps index > 1.2) and a history of at least one dislocation, with varying degrees of trochlear dysplasia (Dejour types A-B). All patients underwent MPFL reconstruction using a semitendinosus hamstring autograft harvested with preservation of its native distal tibial insertion, fixed via a single oblique transpatellar tunnel and femoral interference-screw fixation proximal to the distal femoral physis. Group A (n=14) underwent isolated MPFL reconstruction. Group B (n=14) underwent the same MPFL reconstruction with an additional MPTL-augmenting patellar distalization step using the same graft, secured by trans-osseous periosteal suture at the lateral patella. Surgical techniques emphasized physeal spare during reconstruction. Preoperative and postoperative assessments included the Kujala score, Lysholm score, Caton-Deschamps index, and sulcus angle. Follow-up averaged 12- 24 months. CT was performed using a low-dose pediatric protocol specifically for TT-TG measurement and trochlear bony morphology; MRI was used for soft-tissue and cartilage assessment. Group assignment was not randomized; patients with more pronounced patella alta and higher-grade clinical instability were preferentially treated with the combined procedure.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Both groups showed significant improvements in functional scores. In Group (A), Kujala scores improved from 59.3 ± 8.3 to 84.3 ± 5.1, and Lysholm scores from 50.3 ± 7.5 to 74.7 ± 9.3. Caton-Deschamps index decreased from 1.27 to 1.20. In Group (B), Kujala scores improved from 56.2 ± 7.4 to 88.9 ± 4.5, and Lysholm scores from 51.4 ± 7.6 to 87.4 ± 6.2. Caton-Deschamps index decreased from 1.28 to 1.11, indicating better patellar height correction. Complications occurred in 36% of Group A and 21% of Group B. Recurrent instability occurred in 2 patients (14%) in Group A and 1 patient (7%) in Group B; all were subluxation episodes managed non-operatively, and no revision surgery was required.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: This study demonstrated that MPFL reconstruction with MPTL-augmenting patellar distalization using a hamstring autograft yields greater functional improvements, superior patella alta correction, and fewer complications compared to isolated MPFL reconstruction in adolescents with recurrent patellar instability.

abstract.label: LEVEL OF EVIDENCE
abstract.text: Retrospective comparative study; level IV.

abstract.label: CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION
abstract.text: Clinical trial number: not applicable. This study is a retrospective comparative cohort study and does not meet the definition of a clinical trial as per the International Committee of Medical Journal Editors (ICMJE) guidelines, as it involves retrospective analysis of routinely collected clinical data without prospective intervention or randomization.

articles.title: Health economic evaluation of polytrauma treatment in the current aG-DRG system - Results of a Level I Trauma Center.
articles.journal_full: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: Resource-intensive polytrauma care is associated with high treatment and readiness costs and poses a financial challenge for hospitals. The aim of this retrospective single-center study of the years 2020 to 2022 was to analyze polytrauma reimbursements and costs.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Based on billing and clinical data of 201 polytrauma cases from a German University Hospital and Level I Trauma Center, revenues and costs of the eleven MDC 21 A polytrauma DRGs were analyzed. Ratios of the revenue in relation to LOS, ventilation hours, OR time and implant costs as well as personnel costs were calculated. Contribution margins were determined as an upper-bound estimate.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: DRG reimbursement was highest for the most severely injured patients (50,852 €, DRG W36Z). It was lowest for patients who died within five days (2,214 €, DRG W60Z) or without surgeries (4,056 €, DRG W61B). The contribution margin was also highest for the most severely injured patients (52,775 €, DRG W36Z). Revenues in relation to ICU LOS (3,455 €/day, DRG W36Z) and ventilation time (238 €/hour, DRG W01B) were lowest for the most severe polytraumas. Regarding OR time and implant costs, reimbursement was lowest for injuries of the spine, pelvis and extremities with 62 €/min (DRG W02B) and 5 €/€ (DRG W02A).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Treatment of polytrauma patients with long ICU stay, extended mechanical ventilation and multiple injuries of the extremities, pelvis and spine is not adequately reflected by the current per-case reimbursement in relation to the resources used (ICU days, ventilation hours, OR time and implant costs).

articles.title: External Validation of Risk Scores for Pediatric Pneumonia.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Neither the Pneumonia Risk Score (PRS) nor the VALS-DANCE diagnostic tool has been externally validated using a reference standard specific for bacterial pneumonia. We used a previously published cohort of children with suspected bacterial pneumonia to externally validate these scores.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Children attending Canadian pediatric emergency departments with suspected pneumonia had extensive standardized data collected that were provided to an expert panel to reach a consensus diagnosis. This diagnosis was used to externally validate both clinical scores. Proportions, point estimates and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated, as appropriate, for the classifications and cutoffs recommended for PRS and VALS-Dance.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: In a cohort of 236 children, the PRS classified 69 as low risk, 155 as moderate risk and 12 as high risk for "radiographic" pneumonia. Of these, 11/69 (15.9%), 44/155 (28.4%) and 5/12 (41.7%), respectively, had bacterial pneumonia, yielding a receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.64 (95% CI 0.56-0.71). The PRS low-risk grouping yielded negative likelihood ratio (-LR) 0.56 (95% CI 0.24-0.88) and the high-risk grouping a positive LR (+LR) 2.10 (95% CI -0.23 to 4.42) for bacterial pneumonia. In a cohort of 94 children, the VALS-DANCE Step1 cutoff yielded +LR 2.97 (95% CI 1.52-4.08) and -LR 0.19 (95% CI 0.05-0.33) for distinguishing bacterial from viral pneumonia. In a cohort of 53 children, the VALS-DANCE Step2 cutoff yielded +LR 13.1 (95% CI 0.83-208.8) and -LR 0.65 (95% CI 0.51-0.84) for distinguishing typical from atypical bacterial pneumonia.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: The PRS may have limited utility in the emergency department in guiding clinicians as to whether children with suspected pneumonia need antibiotics. For children hospitalized with community-acquired pneumonia, the VALS-DANCE Step1 diagnostic tool may have some utility for ruling out, but little for confirming bacterial pneumonia. For those with bacterial pneumonia, VALS-DANCE Step2 has uncertain utility for confirming typical and little utility for diagnosing atypical pneumonia.

articles.title: Delayed Presentation of a Traumatic Retroperitoneal Hematoma With Low-Grade Renal Injury After a Low-Speed Electric Scooter Handlebar Impact in a Child: A Case Report.

abstract.text: Electric scooters (e-scooters) are an increasingly common cause of injury in children, but their capacity to cause occult intra-abdominal injury is under-recognized. We report a seven-year-old boy with type 1 diabetes mellitus who presented to the pediatric emergency department seven days after a witnessed low-speed fall from an electric scooter with a direct handlebar impact to the right abdomen. He was initially asymptomatic, developed right-sided abdominal pain on the second day after injury, and became progressively pale. On arrival, he was hemodynamically stable, with right upper quadrant tenderness and fullness, no peritonism, and no external signs of injury. Bedside sonography showed no free intraperitoneal fluid, but marked anemia prompted contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT), which demonstrated a large right retroperitoneal hematoma extending from the subhepatic region into the right hemipelvis, a right perinephric hematoma, and no active contrast extravasation. Targeted renal Doppler ultrasonography identified a small inferior-pole cortical laceration that was not discernible on computed tomography, and the renal injury was classified as low grade. He received a single red blood cell transfusion, was managed nonoperatively in a pediatric high-dependency unit, and was discharged in stable condition on day 5. This case shows that a low-speed handlebar impact without external signs can cause major retroperitoneal bleeding with a delayed presentation, that unexplained anemia after blunt abdominal trauma warrants cross-sectional imaging despite normal vital signs and negative bedside sonography, and that large retroperitoneal hematomas can be managed nonoperatively in stable children without active extravasation.

articles.title: Utility of POCUS to avert surgery and reduce operative time: Experience in seven cases.

abstract.text: The depth of an obstructed collection, the location of pus and the cause of peritonitis are often only approximately determined clinically. Formal imaging is frequently slow, unavailable after hours or inaccessible in resource-limited settings and is usually interpreted by clinicians who have not examined the patient. Point-of-care ultrasound performed by the treating gynaecologist addresses these limitations.

articles.title: Development and Application of an Infectious Disease Risk Assessment Framework for Mass Gatherings in the Republic of Korea.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: This study outlines the development of the Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency (KDCA) infectious disease risk assessment framework for mass gatherings, highlights its key components, and examines its application to domestic mass gathering events.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Government-funded policy research reports, the risk assessment manual, and documentation from exemplary mass gathering risk assessments were reviewed to analyze the framework's development, key components, and application outcomes.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The KDCA developed an infectious disease risk assessment tool for mass gatherings through a government-funded research project in 2024. This tool was subsequently integrated into standard operating procedures for preparedness and response to establish a national infectious disease risk assessment framework. Beginning in 2025, the framework has been applied to domestic mass gathering events. An analysis of two events involving iterative risk assessments demonstrated that deficiencies identified during the initial assessment were successfully addressed by strengthening education, hygiene and ventilation management, medical and response systems, and risk communication. These targeted interventions reduced the overall risk level to low or very low in the final assessment.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: The Korean infectious disease risk assessment framework for mass gatherings provides a standardized approach for systematically assessing infectious disease risks and preparedness, identifying areas for improvement during event planning, and informing preparedness and response measures. Further application across diverse types of mass gatherings and evaluation of the association between assessment results and actual infectious disease events or response outcomes are warranted.

articles.title: Predictive and operational artificial intelligence in emergency radiology for early risk stratification in acute care settings: a scoping review.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Emergency departments face increasing overcrowding, resulting in diagnostic delays, higher mortality, and rising healthcare costs. Early risk stratification is essential to optimise clinical decision-making. Although medical imaging plays a central role in initial assessment, workload pressures and operational constraints have driven the development of artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support triage and prioritisation in emergency radiology.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To map and synthesise evidence on the applications, performance, and limitations of AI in emergency radiology for early risk stratification in acute care.

abstract.label: MATERIALS AND METHODS
abstract.text: A scoping review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA-ScR guidelines and Joanna Briggs Institute recommendations. The protocol was developed a priori and registered in the Open Science Framework. A systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science identified studies published between 2015 and 2025 that evaluated AI applications in medical imaging in acute care settings. Evidence was synthesised using conceptual mapping and thematic analysis.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Seventy-one studies were included. Computed tomography was the most frequently evaluated modality, followed by radiography and ultrasound. Major domains included neurovascular disease, acute cardiopulmonary conditions, trauma, COVID-19, and acute aortic syndromes. Studies reported high diagnostic performance and potential workflow benefits; however, evidence was predominantly retrospective and internally validated, with limited prospective evaluation, external validation, or evidence of improved patient-level outcomes.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: AI applications in emergency radiology show promising diagnostic and workflow-support capabilities. However, current evidence largely reflects early-stage development, with limited prospective validation, scarce real-world impact assessment, and insufficient evaluation of clinically meaningful outcomes.

abstract.label: KEY POINTS
abstract.text: Question How clinically mature are AI applications designed to support early risk stratification and prioritisation in time-sensitive emergency radiology workflows? Findings Most studies report high diagnostic performance in time-sensitive conditions, yet evidence remains predominantly retrospective with limited external validation or prospective real-world implementation. Clinical relevance AI may support earlier identification and prioritisation of critical imaging findings, but routine adoption requires prospective external validation and evidence of meaningful effects on clinical decisions and patient outcomes.

articles.title: Clinical applications of remote patient monitoring.
articles.journal: Curr Probl Pediatr Adolesc Health Care
articles.journal_full: Current problems in pediatric and adolescent health care

abstract.text: Remote patient monitoring (RPM) utilizes a variety of technologies that enable rapid transmission of health data, allowing healthcare providers to manage medical conditions outside the hospital setting. As an increasingly important component of pediatric telehealth and healthcare delivery, RPM has been successfully implemented across multiple specialties. This review highlights RPM programs at the Children's Hospital of Philadelphia (CHOP), including initiatives in cardiology, neonatology, primary care, gastrostomy tube care, and neurology. These programs have demonstrated success in reducing unnecessary hospitalizations and emergency department visits, increasing access to care and subspecialty follow-up, and lowering mortality among children with chronic diseases. The review also examines the digital health technologies that support these programs. In addition, artificial intelligence is playing an expanding role in RPM through predictive alerts, risk stratification, and agentic monitoring tools that enable more personalized and proactive care. Despite these benefits, important challenges remain, including disparities in digital literacy, language barriers, and licensing restrictions. We propose that a hybrid care model integrating RPM, digital health technologies, and in-person visits provides a comprehensive framework for pediatric healthcare delivery. As RPM continues to expand across pediatric subspecialties, the development of telehealth "neighborhoods" may help strengthen medical homes for children with complex chronic conditions. Such models have the potential to improve clinical outcomes, enhance care coordination, and reduce healthcare disparities among vulnerable pediatric populations.

articles.title: Cost-effectiveness of adjunctive hyperbaric oxygen therapy for fibromyalgia: an economic evaluation alongside a single-centre randomised controlled trial in Brazil.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Fibromyalgia is a chronic, polysymptomatic syndrome associated with widespread pain, fatigue, functional impairment and a substantial economic burden. Hyperbaric oxygen therapy has demonstrated neuromodulatory, anti-inflammatory and neuroplastic effects in clinical and preclinical studies; however, no prior evaluation has examined its cost-effectiveness in the treatment of fibromyalgia.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To assess the cost-effectiveness of hyperbaric oxygen therapy as an adjunct to standardised clinical care for fibromyalgia in Brazil, using data from a randomised clinical trial and deterministic economic model.

abstract.label: DESIGN, SETTING AND PARTICIPANTS
abstract.text: A cost-effectiveness evaluation was conducted alongside a single-centre, assessor-blinded, sequential-group, randomised clinical trial at the Department of Rheumatology at Juiz de Fora Federal University in Brazil, applying a 4-month decision-tree model and deterministic sensitivity analyses. The subjects were 56 women aged 18 to 70 years with a diagnosis of fibromyalgia according to the 2016 revisions of the American College of Rheumatology criteria. The intention-to-treat analysis included all participants.

abstract.label: INTERVENTIONS
abstract.text: Standardised clinical management combined with hyperbaric oxygen therapy at 2.3 atmospheres absolute for 90 min, 5 sessions per week for 32 to 40 sessions. The early start group received the intervention during weeks 0–8, and the delayed start group during weeks 8–16.

abstract.label: OUTCOMES
abstract.text: Direct medical and non-medical costs: quality-adjusted life-years derived from utilities obtained through deterministic mapping of the 12-Item Short-Form Health Survey to the European Quality of Life 5 Dimensions instrument using Brazilian valuation weights.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: At 8 weeks, the mean total costs were US$1068.46 for standardised care and US$2477.59 for hyperbaric oxygen therapy, with utilities of 0.477 and 0.630, respectively. The incremental cost was US$1409.13 for a gain of 0.153 quality-adjusted life-years, yielding an incremental cost-effectiveness ratio of US$9210 per quality-adjusted life-year. At 16 weeks, the costs increased to US$2136.93 for standardised care and US$3546.06 for hyperbaric oxygen therapy, with utilities of 0.477 and 0.642, respectively. The incremental cost-effectiveness ratio improved to US$8540 per quality-adjusted life-year, reflecting an incremental gain of 0.165 quality-adjusted life-years. Both incremental cost-effectiveness ratios were below the Brazilian willingness-to-pay threshold of US$9315 per quality-adjusted life-year, although the 8-week estimate was only marginally below this threshold. Deterministic sensitivity analyses confirmed robustness, with treatment costs and utility gains exerting the most significant influence on model outcomes.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Within the assumptions of this deterministic analysis, hyperbaric oxygen therapy added to standardised clinical management met the Brazilian cost-effectiveness criterion for fibromyalgia from the healthcare provider perspective, although it was not a dominant strategy and the 8-week estimate was close to the applied threshold. Multicentre evaluations incorporating directly measured utilities, probabilistic modelling and longer time horizons are warranted.

abstract.label: ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION
abstract.text: The study was approved by the institutional ethics committee and assigned the number 53058421.9.0000.5133 (Version 4).

abstract.label: TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER
abstract.text: This study was registered in the Brazilian Registry of Clinical Trials under RBR-6prps8g, with a Universal Trial Number of U1111-1278-3224.

articles.title: Clinical yield and operational cost-threshold analysis of HPV self-sampling send-outs for long-term non-attenders in cervical cancer screening: a population-based, real-world, registry study in Sweden.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: To evaluate the clinical yield and operational costs of a targeted ‘send-to-all’ human papillomavirus (HPV) self-sampling strategy for long-term non-attenders in cervical cancer screening.

abstract.label: DESIGN
abstract.text: Population-based, real-world observational registry study.

abstract.label: SETTING
abstract.text: The regional organised cervical cancer screening programme in Region Örebro County, Sweden.

abstract.label: PARTICIPANTS
abstract.text: A total of 9123 women identified as long-term non-attenders. Long-term non-attendance was defined as having no recorded cervical screening test for at least one routine screening interval plus an additional 4 years.

abstract.label: INTERVENTIONS
abstract.text: A total of 11 283 vaginal HPV self-sampling kits were dispatched via direct mail to the registered home addresses of all 9123 eligible women between 2022 and 2024.

abstract.label: PRIMARY AND SECONDARY OUTCOME MEASURES
abstract.text: Clinical yield was evaluated using the number of tests analysed (NTA) and number of kits dispatched (NKD) to detect one case of high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion or worse (HSIL+). Resource utilisation was measured as the average cost per screened woman/detected HSIL+, and the economic break-even point against standard letter invitations was established using a deterministic threshold analysis.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of the 11 283 self-sampling kits dispatched, 1826 kits were returned and analysed. This direct response yielded 27 HSIL+ cases (NTA: 68; NKD: 418), at an average cost of 2031 SEK (€183) per screened woman and 134 103 SEK (€12,114) per histologically confirmed HSIL+ case. Incorporating an additional 190 long-term non-attenders who underwent clinical screening within 1 year of dispatch yielded a total of 32 HSIL+ cases. This cumulative response decreased the NTA to 63 and the NKD to 353, with an average cost of 2045 SEK (€185) per screened woman and 126 068 SEK (€11 388) per HSIL+ case. To match the cost per screened woman of the self-sampling strategy, standard letter invitations must achieve a participation rate of 9.5% (based on kit returns alone) or 6.4% (based on cumulative participation).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Direct mailing of HPV self-sampling kits effectively identifies high-grade lesions in a hard-to-reach population. From an operational perspective, previous research indicates that participation from standard letters rarely reaches the calculated 6.4%–9.5% break-even points, suggesting self-sampling is a resource-efficient initial outreach strategy for long-term non-attenders. However, full economic evaluations incorporating long-term health outcomes are required to establish comprehensive cost-effectiveness.

articles.title: Pott's puffy tumour in a healthy adolescent following sinus barotrauma from underwater training.

abstract.text: Pott’s puffy tumour (PPT) formation is a rare but serious complication of frontal sinusitis characterised by subperiosteal abscess and frontal bone osteomyelitis. While typically associated with untreated infection or direct head trauma, barosinusitis from high pressure underwater environments is a less recognised risk factor. In this case, a teenage boy with a history of intensive underwater training developed acute frontal headache and forehead swelling following upper respiratory illness. Imaging demonstrated frontal and ethmoid sinus opacification with subperiosteal abscess consistent with PPT. He underwent functional endoscopic sinus surgery with drainage and received targeted intravenous then oral antibiotics for methicillin-sensitive Staphylococcus aureus. His clinical course improved rapidly with no complications. This case highlights repetitive underwater training at high pressures as a precipitating factor for PPT in otherwise healthy adolescents. Clinicians should inquire about diving and other causes of sinus barotrauma when evaluating patients with refractory sinusitis and forehead swelling.

articles.title: Compromised nasal skin in functional rhinoplasty: a literature review and proposal of a clinical management protocol.

abstract.text: Rhinoplasty is one of the most complex procedures in facial surgery, particularly in the context of revision surgery. The integrity of the nasal skin-soft tissue envelope (SSTE) is a critical factor for both aesthetic and functional outcomes, and vascular compromise of this structure may lead to one of the most feared complications: cutaneous necrosis. The aim of this review is to synthesize the available evidence regarding risk factors and therapeutic strategies in the management of compromised nasal skin following rhinoplasty. A literature review was conducted in PubMed and Embase to identify studies describing cutaneous necrosis following rhinoplasty surgery. The main risk factors identified were revision surgery, smoking, and aggressive thinning of the cutaneous flap. The available literature suggests that early initiation of therapies such as topical nitroglycerin, hyperbaric oxygen therapy, and pentoxifylline may improve tissue salvage in selected cases. A clinical protocol integrating preoperative assessment and an early intraoperative and postoperative management algorithm is proposed. Early identification of high-risk patients and the implementation of a standardized multimodal approach may help optimize skin viability in complex rhinoplasty procedures.

articles.title: Emergency Department Diagnosis of Concussion in Very Young Children with Head Injury.

abstract.text: Although very young children aged 1-4 years accounted for the largest proportion of head injury encounters across a pediatric emergency department network, they had the lowest proportion of concussion diagnoses compared with older groups. These findings highlight the need for age-appropriate concussion assessment and may suggest under-recognition in young patients.

articles.title: MDeID: A dataset for multilingual medical de-identification.

abstract.text: Medical Text De-identification (DeID) is a critical process in securing Protected Health Information (PHI) in compliance with regulations such as the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA). Multiple benchmark datasets exist for English, but there is a paucity of multilingual datasets. We introduce MDeID, a multilingual dataset formedical text de-identification. It comprises 6034 syntheticclinical notes. MDeID covers 28 PHI categories in seven languages: English, Spanish, Portuguese, French, Italian, Dutch, and German. MDeID encompasses seven clinical note types for each language: discharge summaries, provider notes, diagnosis and health plans, nursing notes, emergency medical services notes, scratch notes, and Subjective, Objective, Assessment and Plan (SOAP) notes. MDeID is synthetically generated, seeded with real-world data, and constructed by enriching rare-category coverage and PHI density. We analyze the behavior of models both trained and evaluated on MDeID and contrast it with experiments using real-world and translated datasets. Our work demonstrates MDeID is an effective benchmark for evaluating multilingual DeID difficulty and dataset-specific transfer patterns across the reported models. MDeID is planned for public release at https://github.com/microsoft/MDeID, with the applicable license and use terms provided in the repository.

articles.title: TQP mortality reporting system case reports: Palliative care-transfers in with anticipated death.
articles.journal_full: The journal of trauma and acute care surgery
authors: American College of Surgeons Trauma Quality Programs Mortality Reporting System Work Group

articles.title: Otolin-1 for differentiating central and peripheral causes of acute continuous dizziness.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Patients with isolated acute-onset continuous dizziness (iAOCD) are commonly seen at the emergency department (ED). Distinguishing peripheral vestibular disorders from central causes remains challenging. Existing diagnostic tools, including bedside examination and neuroimaging, have important limitations. Otolin-1, an inner ear-specific glycoprotein, has been proposed as a biomarker of peripheral vestibular pathology. This study evaluated whether otolin-1 could serve as a diagnostic biomarker for this differentiation.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This study analyzed samples from a prospective multicenter cohort of adult patients who were seen at the ED with acute onset, continuous dizziness without focal neurological deficits. Patients were included within 24 hours of symptom onset. Otolin-1 plasma concentrations were measured using an enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. Final diagnoses (central versus peripheral) were determined by an expert panel based on clinical assessment, diffusion-weighted magnetic resonance imaging and 3-month follow-up.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: We analyzed 245 patients (179 peripheral, 66 central). Median otolin-1 concentrations did not differ significantly between peripheral and central causes (517.6 [IQR 443.7-592.8] pg/mL vs 487.9 [424.9-644.4] pg/mL; p = 0.349). No significant differences were observed in hyperacute (<4.5 hours after symptom onset) or acute (4.5-24 hours after symptom onset) subgroups. Similarly, otolin-1 concentrations did not differ between central iAOCD and specific peripheral diagnoses. Substantial overlap in concentration ranges was observed across all comparisons. Receiver operating characteristic analysis similarly showed no useful discrimination (AUC 0.539, 95% CI 0.455-0.623).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Otolin-1 does not differentiate between central and peripheral causes of iAOCD in the ED setting. Although biologically linked to inner ear pathology, otolin-1 lacks sufficient discriminatory value as a stand-alone diagnostic biomarker.

articles.title: Community Paramedics Addressing the Evolving Opioid Crisis: A Case Series Addressing the Kratom Derivatives 7-Hydroxymitragynine and MGM-15.

abstract.text: Concentrated 7-hydroxymitragynine (7-OH) and dihydro-7-hydroxymitragynine (MGM-15) are derived from the primary psychoactive alkaloid in kratom, and until recently were sold over the counter with kratom products. These highly potent kratom derivatives can produce opioid-like dependence, but evidence around prehospital treatment of 7-OH and MGM-15 withdrawal symptoms remains limited. This case series assesses two cases of community paramedics (CPs) providing treatment and linkage to care for individuals in acute opioid withdrawal from 7-OH and MGM-15. In our first case a 74-year-old individual called 9-1-1 experiencing acute opioid-like withdrawal symptoms after abruptly discontinuing over the counter 7-OH following six months of progressively escalating use. Connection was made with a prehospital buprenorphine program (PBAP) and the CP administered 24mg of buprenorphine and expedited connection to outpatient treatment with medication for opioid use disorder (MOUD). Our second case involved a 38-year-old individual who called a CP requesting expedited linkage to MOUD following a period of escalating use of 7-OH and MGM-15. This patient was linked to MOUD treatment within 48 hours of contacting the CP and required 32mg/8mg of buprenorphine/naloxone to treat severe opioid withdrawal symptoms after discontinued use of MGM-15 tablets. Both patients were retained in MOUD treatment at 30 days. These cases describe use of CP-based PBAPs addressing severe 7-OH withdrawal and expediting treatment to outpatient MOUD, highlighting that concentrated over the counter 7-OH products can produce physical opioid dependence leading to opioid use disorder, and requiring full-dose buprenorphine induction which may be considered within existing prehospital opioid withdrawal treatment protocols. Additional research is necessary to characterize withdrawal from concentrated 7-OH products and to determine implications for PBAP protocols and 7-OH dosing in the United States.

articles.title: Economic evaluations in emergency medicine: a 25-year systematic review of patient-level cost-effectiveness analyses (2000-2025).
articles.journal_full: European journal of emergency medicine : official journal of the European Society for Emergency Medicine

abstract.text: Emergency departments (EDs) face rising demand and resource constraints. Cost-effectiveness analyses (CEAs) can inform resource allocation, but patient-level CEAs in emergency care remain methodologically heterogeneous. This review aimed to identify and describe patient-level CEAs in emergency care between 2000 and 2025, appraise their methodological quality, and explore temporal trends and evidence gaps. This systematic review was reported according to Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020. PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, CENTRAL, and gray literature were searched for patient-level CEAs of clinical or organizational interventions across prehospital, ED, and postemergency settings. Data were synthesized narratively across key methodological domains. Methodological quality of the economic evaluations was assessed using the quality of health economic studies (QHES) instrument. Descriptive and exploratory analyses were performed. Forty-seven studies were identified, of which 96% were conducted in EDs. Infectious diseases and ED crowding were the most addressed topics, followed by cardiovascular conditions and trauma, although a broad range of issues was covered. Studies were mainly conducted in high-income countries and evaluated organizational or diagnostic interventions. Healthcare system or hospital perspectives and short time horizons predominated. QHES scores were moderate-to-high (mean: 80.0, SD: 9.2, range: 56-96), with substantial variability and only a weak exploratory temporal trend toward higher scores. Prehospital and postemergency settings were underrepresented. Patient-level CEAs in emergency medicine are increasing, with many studies achieving high QHES scores, but remain heterogeneous in scope and methods. This review highlights the range of interventions evaluated and the methodological features relevant to interpreting economic evidence in emergency care.

articles.title: Rapid Transport to Extracorporeal CPR: Urging Caution Prior to Implementation.

abstract.text: Out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) has survival that remains near 10% despite years of research and advancements in care. Extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) has been explored as an option for patients who suffer OHCA and are refractory to traditional therapies. In nearly every system that implements ECPR for OHCA, there is a requirement to incorporate intra-arrest transport (IAT). There are three major randomized controlled trials which have evaluated the role of ECPR in OHCA. These include ARREST, INCEPTION, and Prague OHCA. While ARREST has the strongest data to support ECPR, it includes only 30 patients. The larger trials such as INCEPTION and Prague OHCA did not show statistically significant results in favor of ECPR. Each trial has a unique study design and statistical analysis.The current evidence is not strong enough to support widespread adoption of ECPR into the prehospital systems of care. Examining the statistical pitfalls, potential biases, and methodological confounders of the existing ECPR literature against the background of previously reported data surrounding IAT─the full impact of effect of ECPR cannot exclude consideration of the impact of the effect of IAT. As more data is needed to better understand the full impact of implementing ECPR into a system of care, we encourage caution and thoughtful analysis to leaders who may be considering the addition of ECPR into an existing system of care. ECPR shows early promise for select patients. The development of an ECPR system is complex and has numerous facets, typically including the incorporation of early IAT for OHCA. At this time, more studies are needed on the full impacts of implementing ECPR into a system of care for OHCA.

articles.title: Patterns, and outcomes of airbag -related penetrating injuries: a retrospective analysis from a level 1 trauma center.
articles.journal_full: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: The deployment of defective airbag inflators can generate high-velocity metallic fragments that cause face, neck or chest penetrating injuries with potentially lethal consequences. This study aimed to describe the injury patterns, management, and outcomes of suspected airbag-related penetrating injuries (ARPI) among patients in a Middle Eastern country.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A retrospective observational study of patients presenting with penetrating injuries suspected of being related to defective airbag deployment. Data were obtained from the Qatar National Trauma Registry (QNTR), electronic medical records, emergency medical services (EMS), emergency department (ED), and Mortuary. Data were collected and analyzed descriptively.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 16 patients had suspected ARPIs between April 2019 and February 2026. The mean age was 33.1 ± 8.3 years, and 93.8% were male. Metallic foreign bodies (FBs) from airbag inflator fragmentation were documented in 11/16 (68.8%) patients by imaging, and surgical removal while in 4/16 patients there were only entry-exit wounds after deployment of airbags following car crash. In one case, airbag deployed while mechanic was repairing a car steering wheel. Penetrating neck (43.8%), thoracic (31.3%), and maxillofacial injuries (31.3%), predominantly mandibular fractures, were most common. Surgical intervention was required in 11 (68.8%) patients and 7/16 required intensive care unit admissions. Five patients died (31.3%), including one at the scene (transported directly by the EMS, no CPR, and moved to the hospital mortuary), two died at the ED after unsuccessful CPR and two died during the hospital course (one presented with cardiac arrest and died on the sixth day and the other one required prolonged ECMO for acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) and died after 4 months).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Airbag inflator rupture can produce serious injury patterns resembling patterns of ballistic trauma, characterized by penetrating neck wounds, maxillofacial fractures and thoracic injuries. These injuries are potentially associated with high mortality, surgical intervention, and critical care utilization. The full extent of these injuries is undetermined as some victims may have simply died at the scene without the benefit of trauma center evaluation or post-mortem examination.

articles.title: Familiar name, unfamiliar reality: a case study of heat illness knowledge gaps among Japanese junior high and high school students.

abstract.text: Early recognition of exertional heat illness (EHI) is critical for preventing severe outcomes. However, the relationship between perceived knowledge and actual understanding remains unclear. This study investigated the recognition and correct matching of EHI and its symptoms among Japanese junior high and high school students. A paper-based, self-administered questionnaire was distributed under conditions of anonymity and voluntary participation. The questionnaire included recognition of the term "EHI" and its condition types and severity classifications (mild, moderate, and severe). EHI knowledge was evaluated by asking students to select all symptoms corresponding to each EHI condition and severity classification from a predefined list, based on previous guidelines. Valid responses were obtained from 533 junior high and 646 high school students. Almost all students recognised the term "EHI," with most reporting school health education as the primary source of learning. However, correct matching of EHI types with their associated symptoms was low (junior high school/high school): 1.9/3.1% for heat syncope, 22.1/26.9% for exercise-associated muscle cramps, 4.1/7.9% for exertional heat exhaustion, and 0.4/0.5% for exertional heat stroke. These results indicate that, although recognition of EHI terminology was nearly universal, correct matching of symptoms was extremely low. These findings reveal a substantial gap between perceived knowledge and actual understanding of EHI. This discrepancy may lead to delayed recognition and inappropriate responses in real-world situations, potentially increasing the risk of adverse outcomes during heat exposure. Addressing this gap may be important for improving safety and public health preparedness in school-based settings.

articles.title: Clinical Nursing in Times of War and a Pandemic.

abstract.text: Nurses who served in the Vietnam War and those who cared for patients during the 2020 COVID-19 pandemic surge may be separated by decades, but they share the experience of caring for large numbers of critically injured, ill, or dying patients while risking their own lives. This article reviews the findings of two studies, one conducted in 1986 based on interviews with Vietnam War nurses, and one conducted in 2020 based on interviews with nurses during COVID-19, and explores the idea that professional nurses from different generations have similar thoughts when their lives are in danger and patient mortality is high. After removing political, geographic, and generational contexts from the analysis, the authors found that these nurses shared similar experiences, including working despite the risk of death, witnessing mass casualties or a deluge of patient admissions, communicating with patients and families as a priority, and the sustaining power of camaraderie. These wartime and pandemic nurses understood that while their clinical skills were essential, their presence was equally important to people cut off from home, friends, and family. The authors explore the similar experiences of both groups of nurses, using photos and excerpts from their interviews to illustrate how nurses can maintain compassionate care no matter the era or how extreme the circumstances.

articles.title: Psychosocial interventions for adult survivors and responders exposed to mass casualty events: A systematic review and network meta-analysis.

abstract.text: This systematic review and network meta-analysis evaluated and ranked psychosocial interventions for reducing posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD), depression, and anxiety among adults exposed to mass casualty events (MCEs). English- and Spanish-language databases were searched for randomized and nonrandomized trials comparing interventions with inactive (e.g., waitlist) or active (e.g., treatment-as-usual) controls. Primary outcomes were posttreatment symptoms of PTSD, depression, and anxiety. Risk of bias was assessed (Cochrane Risk of Bias 2, ROBINS-I), and random-effects network meta-analyses were conducted using standardized mean differences (SMDs), with ranking based on P-scores. Primary analyses excluded studies with a high or serious risk of bias. Fifty-four studies (N = 10,721) across 25 countries met the inclusion criteria. Compared with inactive controls, large effects for PTSD were observed for early eye movement desensitization and reprocessing (E-EMDR), SMD = 2.48; exposure therapy, SMD = 1.60; and cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT), SMD = 1.40, with E-EMDR and CBT remaining significant versus active controls, SMDs = 2.36 and 1.28, respectively. For depression, exposure therapy, SMD = 1.36; interpersonal psychotherapy, SMD = 1.15; mind-body practices, SMD = 1.01; CBT, SMD = 0.85; and integrative therapies, SMD = 0.67, outperformed inactive controls, with exposure therapy, mind-body practices, and CBT remaining significant versus active controls. For anxiety, exposure therapy, CBT, and integrative therapies outperformed both control types, with less precise estimates. Exposure and CBT ranked highly across outcomes; E-EMDR ranked highest for PTSD. The findings support prioritizing trauma-focused interventions following MCEs while highlighting the need for additional comparative and long-term research.

articles.title: A Community Partnership Initiative in Utah to Enhance Prehospital Perinatal Care in the Prevention of Postpartum Hemorrhage.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: In Utah, a confluence of factors over the last 10 years has led to an increase in prehospital births attended by emergency medical system (EMS) providers. Utah is a rural and frontier state where a large segment of the population lives far from obstetric care and where transport times to a facility for birth can be long or hazardous because of seasonal weather. Before March 2024, Utah EMS protocol guidelines only allowed paramedics to administer oxytocin and then only for the treatment of postpartum hemorrhage (PPH). In many cases, a paramedic is not available (because rural fire agencies are often staffed by volunteers, tight budgets do not support full paramedic coverage, or paramedics are not required), and thus, advanced emergency medical technicians (AEMTs) are first on the scene. A community-based interprofessional quality improvement initiative was designed and implemented to expand state EMS protocol guidelines to address the timing, route and administrator of oxytocin.

abstract.label: PROCESS
abstract.text: Using stepwise processes from Powell's Expert Recommendations for Implementing Change implementation science taxonomy, we combined bottom-up and top-down strategies, including stakeholder and decision-maker interviews, community-level focus groups, partner surveys, and coalition building to foster change.

abstract.label: OUTCOMES
abstract.text: In April 2024, the Utah EMS protocol guidelines were successfully changed to include the administration of oxytocin by paramedics for the prevention of PPH and to AEMTs for intramuscular prevention and treatment of PPH.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: This expansion of medication administration provides an additional tool to prevent PPH while increasing safety and equity of prehospital birth services. This may be particularly crucial in a rural and frontier state where maternity deserts, desire for community-based birth, and obstetric-care hurdles are increasing. It is hoped this quality improvement initiative can serve as a guide to others wanting to implement similar practice changes in their state.

articles.title: Hospital Specialization and Geographic Access as Determinants of Pediatric Emergency Mortality: A Nationwide Multilevel Study in South Korea.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: To examine individual, hospital, and community-level determinants of in-hospital mortality-defined as death during the emergency department visit or after hospitalization at the same hospital-among critically ill pediatric emergency patients in South Korea.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We analyzed data from the National Emergency Department Information System, comprising 26,206 pediatric patients (aged ≤18 y, triage levels 1 to 2) at emergency medical centers in 2021, using multilevel logistic regression. The null model confirmed substantial between-hospital [intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC)=0.17] and between-community (ICC=0.01) variation, justifying the multilevel approach.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Overall, in-hospital mortality was 2.3%. At the individual level, compared with self-transport, patients arriving by 119 ambulance (OR=2.73, 95% CI: 1.85-4.05) and private ambulance patients (OR=3.14, 95% CI: 1.72-5.73) had higher odds. Intentional and unintentional injuries showed 2.06-fold and 2.97-fold higher odds versus noninjury, respectively. Consciousness level showed a dose-response association (coma: OR=228.64). Severe illness was associated with a 4.94-fold higher odds ratio. At the hospital level, higher critically ill proportions were associated with lower mortality (≥10%: OR=0.43), while hospitals with ≥45 combined pediatric and neonatal intensive care beds had higher odds (OR=2.43), likely reflecting case-mix concentration. At the community level, metropolitan cities showed higher odds (OR=1.64), while a higher Timely Relevance Index (TRI; percentage of residents accessing care within 60 min) was associated with lower mortality (≥95%: OR=0.55).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Pediatric emergency mortality was associated with factors across all 3 levels. Risk-adjusted performance metrics are needed for tiered systems, and timely geographic access supports distributed initial stabilization capacity.

articles.title: Acute heart failure in emergency settings.

abstract.text: Acute heart failure (AHF) represents a major cause of emergency medical care worldwide and continues to carry a substantial burden of morbidity and mortality despite advances in chronic heart failure management. Most patients with AHF present to emergency departments (EDs), where the first hours of care are critical to determine prognosis. Of these, some have been previously evaluated and treated by prehospital emergency medical services before ED arrival. This consensus document summarizes the current evidence and provides practical advice to emergency physicians for the diagnosis, treatment, and disposition of patients with AHF in these emergency settings (emergency medical services and ED). It emphasizes the importance of a rapid phenotypic classification into acute decompensated heart failure, acute pulmonary oedema, isolated right ventricular failure, or cardiogenic shock, as a key tool to guide early management and triage decisions. It reviews evidence on prehospital and ED management, including the use of biomarkers, imaging, ventilatory support, diuretic and vasodilator strategies, and early initiation or continuation of guideline-directed medical therapy. It also discusses risk stratification and disposition decisions supported by validated tools. Finally, it identifies major knowledge gaps and future research priorities, including pragmatic trials to assess prehospital interventions, biomarker-guided therapy, and early initiation of disease-modifying treatments. Ultimately, this consensus document is aimed to contribute to the improvement of outcomes in AHF.

articles.title: Low-Titer O+ Whole Blood Implementation in the EMS System for Metropolitan Oklahoma City and Tulsa: Significance, Success, & Sharing Lessons Learned.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: Over 300 emergency medical services (EMS) organizations across the United States have implemented transfusion programs for traumatic injuries using packed red blood cells, platelets, plasma, or whole blood before hospital arrival. Beginning in December of 2022, the EMS System for Metropolitan Oklahoma City (OKC) and Tulsa began carrying low-titer O-positive whole blood (LTOWB) for adult patients in traumatic hemorrhagic shock, specifically those exhibiting elevated shock indexes. We aim to describe establishing our prehospital LTOWB program and its first two years of operations across OKC and Tulsa.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We used an observational study design and retrospective descriptive analysis of patients receiving LTOWB by paramedic transfusion from the Emergency Medical Services Authority Ambulance Service, Oklahoma City Fire Department, or Tulsa Fire Department between December 1, 2022, and February 1, 2025. Descriptive analysis and univariate logistic regression quantify the relationship of patient characteristics against survival to hospital arrival and survival to hospital discharge outcomes.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Penetrating trauma was the most common mechanism of injury recorded for patients receiving EMS LTOWB (71.6%). Following LTOWB transfusion, prehospital vital signs (systolic blood pressure, heart rate, and shock index) significantly improved (p < 0.05). Systolic blood pressure improvement conferred 9.7 times greater odds of survival to hospital arrival (95% CL 1.6-58.6). Occurrence of prehospital traumatic arrest was significantly related to lower odds of survival to hospital arrival and survival to hospital discharge (OR 0.01 and OR 0.03, respectively).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Transfusion of LTOWB in a large, urban EMS system in the Southwestern United States confers a positive benefit to patients with measurable improvement in median systolic blood pressure, heart rate, and shock index. Continuous review of cases and misses empowered our system in dynamic protocol adjustments to best meet our population's needs. Patients often had secondary deterioration during transit, illustrating that blood transfusion "bought" temporary time during transport of critically injured patients to definitive care.

articles.title: Clinical and radiographic features of fractures raising suspicion of non-accidental trauma in young children: A retrospective emergency department study.

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: To explore clinical and radiographic patterns that may generate hypotheses regarding early indicators of non-accidental trauma (NAT).

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective observational study included 649 children aged 0-6 years who presented to a tertiary pediatric emergency department between January 2023 and December 2024. Fractures were classified as moderate- or high-specificity injuries according to established NAT criteria. For children classified as having possible abuse, records were reviewed for abuse notification and protective-care placement.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The median age was 40 months, and 54.4% of participants were male. Fractures occurred in 277 children (42.7%), while 38 (5.9%) were classified as having possible abuse. These children were significantly younger than those without possible abuse (18.5 vs. 42 months; p<0.001). Among them, 34 (89.5%) had high-specificity fracture patterns, including metaphyseal corner and transphyseal lesions, whereas 4 (10.5%) had moderate-specificity patterns. No significant differences were observed according to sex or study year. Twenty-five children in the overall cohort were hospitalized. Despite fracture patterns concerning for abuse, no abuse notifications were made by pediatric emergency physicians or social services, and no child was placed under protective care.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Younger age and high-specificity skeletal injuries may increase suspicion of NAT. Interpretation should consider the injury mechanism, developmental stage, physical examination, and multidisciplinary assessment. Standardized fracture classification and coordinated child-protection pathways may facilitate earlier recognition and referral.

articles.title: Applicant Rank List Preference for Emergency Medicine From 2020 to 2026.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Emergency medicine (EM) training programs have experienced disruptive challenges in recent years. However, enthusiasm for EM, as measured by National Resident Matching Program (NRMP) rank order list preference data, remains high among senior United States (US) allopathic (MD) applicants who apply to the specialty. Although osteopathic (DO) and international medical graduate (IMG) applicants comprise a growing share of the EM resident workforce, there is little data evaluating their preference for EM.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective analysis of NRMP rank order list preference data includes four types of applicants: US MD seniors, US DO seniors, IMGs with US citizenship, and IMGs without US citizenship. For each applicant category, we recorded the number (and calculated the percentage) of EM applicants who ranked EM as their only choice, first choice, and not first choice during the 2020-2026 NRMP. The number and percentage of applicants ranking EM as their preferred choice were determined by combining the first choice and only choice categories.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: During the study period, the percentage of EM applicants ranking EM as their preferred choice ranged from 91.8% to 95.8% among US MD seniors, from 86.9% to 93.6% among US DO seniors, from 76.5% to 88.8% among US IMGs, and from 57.3% to 83.3% among non-US IMGs. The percentage of EM applicants ranking EM as their "not first" choice peaked in 2024 and then declined for each applicant category in 2025 and 2026.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Despite recent challenges, our findings demonstrate that EM remains the preferred specialty choice for the majority of US MD senior, US DO senior, US IMG, and non-US IMG applicants who ranked EM residency programs.

articles.title: [Telemedicine in prehospital emergency care : light and shadow of an emerging practice].

abstract.text: Swiss hospital and prehospital emergency services are under increasing pressure. In this context, community emergency response systems aim to optimize the deployment of human and material resources in a way proportionate to prehospital settings in which emergencies are predominantly classed as non-urgent. Nevertheless, professionals occasionally encounter more complex situations whose resolution could be supported through. This article explores the potential of telemedicine in prehospital emergency care. Specifically, the pressures on emergency services are presented, and community emergency models are described as a possible solution. Finally, we discuss the benefits and challenges of prehospital telemedicine and suggest avenues for adaptation to the needs of community paramedics.

articles.title: Near Real-Time Quantitative Ultrasound Imaging Using an Ultra-Portable Handheld Ultrasound System.

abstract.text: Clinical ultrasound is widely used because of its low cost, portability, safety, and real-time imaging capability, making it well suited for point-of-care applications. However, conventional B-mode imaging is inherently qualitative and primarily sensitive to tissue morphology. Quantitative ultrasound (QUS) methods exploit information contained in backscattered radiofrequency (RF) signals to extract fundamental acoustic tissue properties, such as the backscatter coefficient (BSC) and attenuation, which more directly quantify tissue microstructure and provide complementary information to B-mode imaging. Although QUS methods have been implemented on conventional cart-based ultrasound scanners, their integration into portable handheld systems remains limited. Motivated by the growing availability and clinical potential of ultra-portable ultrasound devices, this protocol presents a QUS imaging pipeline implemented on the DKPOC probe (portable linear ultrasound probe; Vermon SA, Tours, France), which interfaces directly with a laptop through a USB-C connection. The protocol integrates multiple QUS processing methods based on spectral analysis and envelope statistics of RF data acquired using focused-wave or plane-wave transmit modes. QUS processing begins with a user-defined region of interest (ROI). The reference phantom method is used to estimate the BSC and attenuation within sliding sub-ROIs. Model-based fitting of the estimated BSC is then performed to extract tissue microstructure-related parameters, including effective scatterer diameter and effective acoustic concentration. In addition, envelope statistics parameters are estimated using three probability density functions. Computed QUS parameter maps are displayed as translucent color overlays on corresponding B-mode images. The workflow is implemented in a numerical computing software-based graphical user interface, enabling near real-time QUS processing, parameter map visualization, interactive parameter adjustment, and rapid evaluation of different processing configurations. The pipeline is adaptable to different imaging sequences and ultrasound probes, providing a practical framework for quantitative point-of-care ultrasound imaging and clinician-led QUS studies in human subjects.

articles.title: Nursing Quality Management in Trauma Centers: A Descriptive Cross-Sectional Study.

abstract.text: This descriptive study examined the current status of nursing quality management in trauma centers across 30 provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities in China, identified existing challenges, and offered evidence-based recommendations for improvement. A self-designed questionnaire was used to collect basic information about the hospitals' trauma centers and their nursing quality management practices. A total of 98.9% of respondents indicated that there was no nursing quality management program specifically for trauma centers; 72.2% reported the absence of a trauma quality control specialist; and 67.2% noted a lack of specialty-specific nursing quality indicators for trauma care. The most widely used quality management tools were data analysis and reporting tools (60.4%) and electronic health record systems (59.7%). Additionally, 40.1% of centers did not have a designated person responsible for trauma patient data reporting, and most trauma centers did not systematically collect patient data. It is crucial to establish nursing quality management programs and standards for trauma centers at all levels, create relevant databases, and develop sensitive quality indicators.

articles.title: Spontaneous Renal Hemorrhage Secondary to MRSA Renal Abscess Requiring Nephrectomy After Failed Percutaneous Drainage: A Case Report.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Spontaneous renal hemorrhage (SRH) caused by renal infection is extremely rare. Furthermore, sepsis caused by methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) has a high mortality rate and requires prompt source control.

abstract.label: CASE PRESENTATION
abstract.text: A 63-year-old man with severe diabetes presented to the emergency department in shock. Computed tomography revealed a left renal subcapsular hematoma. Based on his clinical course and history, infection-induced SRH was suspected. Blood and urine cultures yielded MRSA. Although percutaneous drainage was performed after the initial bleeding stabilized, persistent infection was followed by rebleeding, necessitating left nephrectomy. The patient recovered postoperatively. Histopathology confirmed abscess formation and chronic inflammation without malignancy.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: For inadequately controlled infections following percutaneous drainage, particularly when recurrent hemorrhage is suspected, early nephrectomy may be considered for definitive source control.

articles.title: High-Entropy Materials as a Design Paradigm for Low-Temperature Sodium-Ion Batteries.

abstract.text: Low-temperature (LT) operation remains a major barrier to the practical deployment of sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) because reduced thermal activation magnifies coupled limitations in bulk Na+ transport, phase stability, and interfacial kinetics, resulting in strong polarization growth, rapid capacity loss, and poor rate capability. Conventional optimization approaches based on incremental compositional tuning target a single bottleneck at a time and therefore struggle under sub-zero conditions, where transport and interphase evolution become tightly intertwined. High-entropy materials (HEMs) offer a distinct design paradigm in which configurational disorder is used as a controllable variable to reshape thermodynamics and kinetics, stabilize vulnerable frameworks, and broaden the distribution of accessible Na+ migration pathways. In this review, we analyze how entropy engineering influences LT performance across cathodes, anodes, electrolytes, and interfaces, emphasizing mechanistic links between realized disorder, transport activation penalties, and the accumulation of interfacial resistance in the solid-electrolyte interphase and cathode-electrolyte interphase. We synthesize quantitative descriptors and minimum reporting metrics that enable meaningful comparison across studies, and we highlight a unifying entropy-percolation framework connecting bulk ionic conduction with solvation/desolvation and interphase transport in liquid systems. We conclude by outlining key trade-offs, manufacturability constraints, and research directions required to translate high-entropy strategies into robust LT-SIB operation.

articles.title: Prognostic value of early point-of-care blood gas analysis in critically ill non-trauma patients.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Critically ill non-trauma patients treated in the emergency department have a high risk of in-hospital mortality. While point-of-care diagnostics such as blood gas analysis are established tools for urgent management, data on their prognostic value in this specific patient cohort remain limited. This study aimed to evaluate whether initial blood gas parameters are independently associated with in-hospital mortality in critically ill non-trauma patients.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective cohort study included adult critically ill non-trauma patients treated in the emergency department of a German university hospital. Initial blood gas parameters and clinical data were analyzed using univariate and multivariable logistic regression to assess their association with in-hospital mortality.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 879 screened patients, 542 met the inclusion criteria. In-hospital mortality was 20% (n = 110). In addition to older age and out-of-hospital cardiac arrest, anemia (hemoglobin < 12 g/dL; OR of 2.07, 95% CI 1.20-3.58; p = 0.009), acidosis (pH < 7.35; OR 2.26, 95% CI 1.09-4.95; p = 0.033) and hypobicarbonatemia (< 22 mmol/L; OR 2.79, 95% CI 1.42-5.69; p = 0.004) were independently associated with in-hospital mortality. The association for hyperlactatemia was borderline (> 2.2 mmol/L; OR 1.85, 95% CI 0.93-3.77; p = 0.08). Multivariate analysis did not reveal significant associations between other electrolyte imbalances and in-hospital mortality in this cohort.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: In this retrospective cohort, the presence of anemia, acidosis or hypobicarbonatemia on admission to the resuscitation room were independently associated with an elevated risk of in-hospital mortality in critically ill non-trauma patients. These readily available point-of-care parameters may support early risk stratification. Prospective studies are needed to validate these findings.

articles.title: Association of Transabdominal Ultrasound Evaluation of Pelvic Free Fluid Presence, Depth, Morphology, and Location with Pathology in Reproductive-Aged Females Presenting to the Emergency Department.
articles.journal_full: Journal of ultrasound in medicine : official journal of the American Institute of Ultrasound in Medicine

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: To evaluate the association between nontraumatic pelvic free fluid (PFF) characteristics (presence, depth, morphology, and location) and pathology in reproductive-aged females presenting to the emergency department (ED).

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study of patients aged 18-40 years with a uterus who were non-pregnant or in their first trimester of pregnancy and underwent pelvic ultrasound from January 1, 2020 to December 31, 2024. Exclusion criteria were bilateral oophorectomy, known ascites, recent trauma or abdominal surgery, concurrent reproductive endocrinology treatment, or inadequate ultrasound images. The primary outcome was pathology based on a composite clinical reference standard. Two blinded, ultrasound-trained emergency physicians reviewed point-of-care ultrasound (PoCUS) images for PFF presence, morphology (stripe, small pocket, large pocket, sliver), location, and maximal depth. Multivariable regression analyses evaluated associations between PFF characteristics and pathology. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis determined optimal depth thresholds for predicting pathology.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 746 pelvic ultrasound examinations, 672 patients were included. Pathology was identified in 126 of 672 (18.8%) patients and PFF was present in 174/672 (25.9%). PFF was associated with pathology (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 3.0; 95% CI 2.0-4.6). A 6.9-mm threshold demonstrated modest discrimination for pathology (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve 0.69); mean PFF depth was 9.5 ± 7.8 mm. Stripe morphology, observed in 54 of 174 (31.0%) patients with PFF, was associated with increased odds of pathology compared with other morphologies (aOR 3.6; 95% CI 1.8-7.3; p < .001). Anteriorly located fluid relative to the uterus was associated with gynecologic pathology (aOR 3.4, 95% CI 1.2-9.4).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: PFF characteristics on PoCUS may help refine diagnostic prioritization for pathology in reproductive-aged females presenting to the ED.

articles.title: The impact of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists on post-anesthetic pulmonary and gastrointestinal adverse events: a target trial emulation using multinational database.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) delay gastric emptying, raising concerns about perioperative aspiration and postoperative complications. This target trial emulation aims to evaluate the association between the use of GLP-1 RAs and the risk of postoperative pulmonary and gastrointestinal adverse events in patients undergoing general anesthesia.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Data was utilized from the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network. The study analyzed data from January 1, 2023, to December 31, 2023. Patients aged 20 years or older who underwent general anesthesia were included. These patients were divided into two groups: those using GLP-1 RA and those who were not. Propensity score matching was used to balance baseline characteristics. The primary outcome measures were the incidence of pulmonary and gastrointestinal adverse events within one-month post-anesthesia. Hazard ratios were calculated using Cox proportional hazards regression models to estimate the risk of these adverse events associated with GLP-1 RA use.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 21,948 patients were included after matching. Patients who used GLP-1 RAs demonstrated a significantly lower risk of pulmonary adverse events (HR 0.682 [0.496-0.938]). Secondary outcomes further revealed a reduction in the risk of postoperative respiratory failure, as well as postoperative hospitalization and emergency department revisits. However, there was a marginally increased risk of gastrointestinal adverse events in the GLP-1 RA group (HR, 1.034 [1.003-1.067]).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: The use of GLP-1 RAs prior to general anesthesia was not associated with higher risk of pulmonary adverse events. A slight elevation in gastrointestinal risks was observed, although the signal remained modest.

articles.title: Impact of extreme rainstorm-induced flooding on emergency healthcare demands in a mountainous district: a multi-group interrupted time-series analysis.

abstract.text: Floods have severe impacts on human health and emergency healthcare systems; however, research on their short-term acute health effects remains insufficient, particularly in vulnerable mountainous regions. The severe floods that occurred in Beijing from July 29 to August 2, 2023, had a substantial significant impact on remote mountainous districts. Utilizing daily emergency department (ED) visit data from a hospital in these remote areas, this study employed a difference-in-differences interrupted time series design to compare the 2023 disaster period with the corresponding periods in 2024 and 2025. We assessed temporal trends in all-cause ED visits, as well as cause-specific visits for cardiovascular disease (CVD), respiratory diseases, and physical trauma, across the acute blockade, and short-term recovery phases. During the acute blockade phase, all-cause ED visits (relative risk [RR] = 0.74, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.58-0.96) and CVD visits (RR = 0.50, 95% CI: 0.28-0.91) exhibited significant immediate declines. This reduction may reflect decreased healthcare accessibility resulting from physical isolation caused by extreme rainfall and road disruptions. Moreover, the daily slope of CVD visits showed an increasing trend (RR = 1.26, 95% CI: 1.04-1.54). Upon entering the short-term recovery phase, there was an immediate compensatory surge in all-cause ED visits (RR = 1.28, 95% CI: 1.13-1.44), particularly in visits for physical trauma (RR = 2.23, 95% CI: 1.82-2.75). This rebound was primarily driven by males and adults aged 18-64 years. These findings suggest that acute physical blockades in mountainous regions may temporarily suppress healthcare utilization by limiting access to emergency services, followed by a substantial delayed compensatory surge in ED visits, predominantly for physical trauma. Accordingly, primary healthcare capacity for the management of physical trauma and CVD should be strengthened at the grassroots level to enhance the resilience of emergency medical systems.

articles.title: Right ventricular function across different non-invasive respiratory support strategies in severe community-acquired pneumonia.
articles.journal_full: Heart & lung : the journal of critical care

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Right ventricular (RV) systolic impairment is clinically relevant in acute respiratory failure, but its relationship with respiratory support modality in severe community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) outside the intensive care unit (ICU) is poorly defined.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: To compare RV longitudinal systolic performance and hospital length of stay (LOS) among patients receiving non-invasive ventilation (NIV), high-flow nasal cannula (HFNC), or Venturi-mask oxygen therapy.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In this single-centre prospective observational study, adults with severe CAP (Pneumonia Severity Index class IV-V) requiring high-concentration oxygen or non-invasive respiratory support were enrolled. The modality was selected in the emergency department according to the treating physician's clinical and gas-exchange assessment. Echocardiography was performed shortly after ward admission while patients remained on the initial support modality.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Seventy patients were included (NIV, n = 21; HFNC, n = 22; Venturi mask, n = 27). Baseline demographic and cardiometabolic characteristics were comparable across groups. TAPSE and lateral tricuspid annular systolic velocity (S') showed a graded pattern, with the lowest values during NIV, intermediate values during HFNC, and the highest values with the Venturi mask (p < 0.001 for both). Mean LOS was 27.8 ± 5.0, 27.4 ± 2.9, and 15.2 ± 4.0 days, respectively (p < 0.001). In multivariable analysis, age and respiratory support modality were associated with LOS.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: RV systolic performance and LOS differed across clinically selected respiratory support groups. These associations may reflect clinical severity rather than device-related effects. These findings reinforce the often-overlooked clinical importance of RV assessment in acute respiratory failure, extending observations from ARDS cohorts to severe CAP outside the ICU.

articles.title: Using Over-the-Counter Retail Medication Sales to Detect and Track Influenza-Like Illnesses Including Novel Diseases: Surveillance Modeling Study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Traditional disease surveillance systems often rely on clinical or laboratory-confirmed data, which may delay detection of emerging outbreaks. The National Retail Data Monitor (NRDM), established in 2002, collects anonymized over-the-counter (OTC) health product sales data from more than 28,000 retail outlets across the United States and provides a complementary data source for syndromic surveillance.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: This study evaluated the use of NRDM data for detecting and tracking influenza-like illness (ILI), including purchasing patterns suggestive of novel disease outbreaks.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: NRDM data from Allegheny County, Pennsylvania, collected between 2016 and 2021, were analyzed using a probabilistic modeling framework to estimate daily ILI activity from OTC purchasing patterns. An expectation-maximization algorithm was applied to data from the training period (June 2016-May 2019) to estimate conditional probabilities of OTC product purchases under ILI and non-ILI conditions. These estimates were then applied to daily sales data from the test period (June 2019-December 2021) to infer daily ILI counts.
