The framework was further extended into a monitoring system, termed NRDM Tracker, which uses daily log-likelihoods and false discovery rate-adjusted P values to detect statistically significant anomalies in purchasing behavior.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: NRDM-derived ILI estimates were moderately correlated with emergency department (ED)-based ILI counts (r=0.66). Compared with other OTC product categories (eg, thermometers and antifever medications), cough and cold medications showed the strongest association with ILI-related purchasing behavior and higher estimated purchase probability under ILI conditions (0.792) than under non-ILI conditions (0.695). During the early phase of the COVID-19 pandemic in March 2020 in Allegheny County, when COVID-19 testing capacity was limited and public awareness and health-seeking behaviors were rapidly evolving, NRDM-based ILI signals increased before corresponding rises in confirmed ED-based COVID-19 counts. Moreover, NRDM Tracker identified significant anomalies in OTC purchasing behavior during major outbreak periods, including a pronounced decline in log-likelihood in March 2020 corresponding to the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic. Multiple product categories exhibited statistically significant deviations in sales during these periods.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: OTC product sales data, analyzed using probabilistic modeling and anomaly detection methods, can provide timely insights into population-level health activity and may help identify anomalies associated with emerging disease outbreaks. NRDM-based surveillance systems may complement traditional clinical surveillance and strengthen local and national biosurveillance capabilities.

articles.title: Reducing energy and air consumption in scuba diving with underwater exoskeletons.

abstract.text: Assisting underwater locomotion with exoskeletons could reduce energy and air consumption during scuba diving.

articles.title: Nonfatal Drug Overdoses and Naloxone Use.
Workplace and age associated with severity of occupational injuries and cardiovascular emergencies: a nationwide study in Japan.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Among working-age populations globally, occupational injuries and workplace cardiovascular emergencies remain major contributors to morbidity and mortality. This study examined the associations between workplace settings, age groups, and the severity of occupational injuries and cardiovascular events.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a nationwide retrospective registry-based observational study using emergency medical services data from Japan, including 454 043 working-age individuals recorded in 2021-2023. Workplace settings (office, indoor worksite, factory, outdoor worksite, construction, agriculture, and others) and age groups were analysed in relation to event severity, categorized as non-life-threatening or life-threatening. Multivariable regression models estimated the associations, and workplace-age interactions were assessed.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Compared with office settings, all other workplaces were associated with higher odds of life-threatening injuries, particularly agriculture and construction. Increasing age groups were progressively associated with greater injury severity. The workplace setting was associated with the severity of stroke and ischaemic heart disease, particularly in uncontrolled outdoor environments. Stroke severity was elevated in those aged 45-59 and 60-69 years, while all older age groups were associated with severe ischaemic heart disease. Workplace-age interactions were significant only for occupational injuries.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Workplace and age were interactively and independently associated with the severity of occupational injuries and cardiovascular emergencies.

articles.title: Association between SGLT2 inhibitor use and functional outcomes in elderly patients receiving ferric carboxymaltose: a retrospective observational cohort study.

abstract.text: Anemia and iron deficiency (ID) are extremely common comorbidities in elderly patients with chronic heart failure (CHF), and are associated with reduced functional capacity and worse prognosis. The objective of this study was to evaluate the association of one-year therapy with SGLT2i as add-on to intravenous infusion of ferric carboxymaltose (FCM) with improvement in functional abilities, in a cohort of elderly patients with HFrEF/HFmrEF with ID anemia. This study enrolled outpatients with CHF with ID anemia receiving intravenous administration of FCM and stratified into two groups according to SGLT2i use. The study endpoint was an achievement of Short physical performance battery (SPPB)>8pt at one year of follow-up. 222 patients, with a mean age of 75.5±6.0 years were enrolled and 53 received SGLT2i while 169 not. After 1 year of follow-up, a significant improvement in the main clinical, laboratory, echocardiographic and CGA parameters were observed in both groups; however, these improvements were statistically greater in those patients receiving also SGLT2i. The mean dose of FCM administered to the entire population at baseline was 734.2 ± 331.7 mg, with no significant differences between the two groups (p=0.475). Add on therapy with SGLT2i was associated with a greater improvement in functional abilities (OR 7.66; CI 95% 3.70-15.9, p<0.0001), while the presence of obesity was associated with a reduced probability of functional abilities improvement of 68% (OR 0.32; CI 95% 0.14-0.71, p=0.005). In patients with CHF and ID anemia, improvements in clinical symptoms and physical function were observed at one-year follow-up, as reflected by changes in SPPB scores. These improvements were greater among patients receiving concomitant SGLT2i therapy.

articles.title: Initial empiric carbapenem versus non-carbapenem β-lactam/β-lactamase inhibitor therapy in sepsis across simplified SENECA phenotypes: a retrospective study of two independent cohorts.
articles.journal: Eur J Clin Microbiol Infect Dis
articles.journal_full: European journal of clinical microbiology & infectious diseases : official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: Whether initial empiric carbapenem therapy is associated with better outcomes than non-carbapenem β-lactam/β-lactamase inhibitor (BL/BLI) therapy in sepsis remains uncertain. We examined this association overall and across simplified Sepsis Endotyping in Emergency Care (SENECA) phenotypes.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective study included 4,091 patients from MIMIC-IV and 405 patients from a single-center hospital cohort. Initial therapy was defined by the first eligible carbapenem or BL/BLI regimen initiated within 24 h of admission. The primary outcome was 28-day mortality. Secondary outcomes included selected clinical and in-hospital microbiological detection outcomes. Each cohort was analyzed separately using inverse probability of treatment weighting and weighted logistic regression.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: After weighting, no overall association with lower 28-day mortality was observed in MIMIC-IV (OR 0.91, 95% CI 0.71-1.17) or the hospital cohort (OR 0.74, 95% CI 0.48-1.16). However, evidence of treatment-by-phenotype interaction was observed in both cohorts (P for interaction = 0.039 and 0.019, respectively), with lower odds of 28-day mortality among patients with the γ phenotype in MIMIC-IV and the hospital cohort (OR 0.66, 95% CI 0.44-0.97, and OR 0.13, 95% CI 0.04-0.46, respectively). A similar direction was observed among mechanically ventilated patients. In MIMIC-IV, carbapenem therapy was associated with longer hospitalization and more frequent detection of fungal organisms and Clostridioides difficile; these associations were not observed in the hospital cohort.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Initial empiric carbapenem therapy was not significantly associated with lower 28-day mortality overall. Consistent findings in the γ phenotype suggest possible treatment heterogeneity. These findings should be considered alongside patient characteristics and potential clinical and microbiological trade-offs.

articles.title: Beyond 30-day mortality: causes and risk factors of half-year postdischarge mortality after gastric cancer surgery.
articles.journal_full: Gastric cancer : official journal of the International Gastric Cancer Association and the Japanese Gastric Cancer Association

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Conventional 30-day or in-hospital mortality underestimates the true burden of postoperative death after gastrectomy. This study aimed to characterize post-discharge mortality and its evolving determinants following gastric cancer surgery.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We retrospectively analyzed patients who underwent gastrectomy for primary gastric cancer at Seoul National University Hospital between 2013 and 2019. Mortality data were updated through national death registry linkage with complete follow-up of at least 5 years. In-hospital deaths were reviewed using medical records, while out-of-hospital deaths were classified using death certificates and family interviews. Cox regression analyses were performed across sequential postoperative intervals up to 5 years.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 4802 patients included in the analysis, overall mortality within 6 months was 1.2% (n = 57), of which 89.5% occurred after discharge. Thirty-day and 90-day mortality were 0.1% and 0.5%, respectively, demonstrating substantial underestimation by conventional short-term endpoints. Early mortality was primarily associated with emergency surgery and postoperative complications. Mid-term mortality was strongly linked to psychiatric disorders and systemic comorbidities, while low body mass index emerged as a significant predictor from 6 months onward. With longer follow-up, older age, renal or hepatic disease, multiple comorbidities, and incomplete (non-R0) resection became dominant risk factors. Tumor stage showed a strong association with mortality at 3 years.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Postoperative mortality after gastrectomy is a dynamic process extending far beyond hospital discharge and shaped by distinct risk factors over time. Because most early deaths occur after discharge, improved survival requires surveillance strategies that target high-risk patients beyond the conventional 30-day window.

articles.title: Anesthetic technique is associated with complication risk and healthcare utilization following total shoulder arthroplasty.
articles.journal_full: European journal of orthopaedic surgery & traumatology : orthopedie traumatologie

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: Compare perioperative complications and healthcare utilization among total shoulder arthroplasty (TSA) patients receiving general (GA), regional (RA), or combined anesthesia (RA + GA).

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Using the TriNetX database, patients undergoing primary TSA were identified and stratified into three groups based on anesthetic technique: GA, RA, and combined RA + GA. 1:1 Propensity score matching was performed to using the GA cohort as reference to control for baseline demographic and clinical covariates. Outcomes of interest included 90-day complication rates including UTI, venous thromboembolism (VTE), acute kidney injury (AKI), prosthetic joint infection (PJI), pneumonia, constipation, and revision TSA, emergency department (ED) visits and hospital readmission, Foley catheter insertion, postoperative opioid prescriptions and mean opioid number of prescriptions. Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Comparing GA with RA, each cohort consisted of 28,564 patients. RA was associated with lower rates of UTI, AKI, constipation, pneumonia, fewer patients prescribed opioids and fewer opioid prescriptions per patient while being associated with increased healthcare utilization compared to GA alone. Comparing RA + GA with GA alone, 17,926 matched patients were included in each cohort. RA + GA was associated with lower rates of UTI and opioid prescriptions, and higher rates of healthcare utilization compared to GA alone.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: These findings suggest that while RA provides early analgesic and opioid-sparing benefits after TSA, it is associated with increased post-operative healthcare utilization. These findings help guide surgical decision making and highlight the need for standardized perioperative protocols to optimize postoperative pain control and manage rebound pain-related care utilization with RA techniques.

abstract.label: LEVEL OF EVIDENCE
abstract.text: III.

articles.title: Deep learning-based renal-trauma classification: comparison of two-dimensional convolutional neural network and vision-transformer models on arterial- and venous-phase computed-tomography images.

abstract.text: Rapid and accurate detection of renal trauma is essential in emergency medicine. This study aimed to automatically classify renal trauma using 2D convolutional neural network (CNN) and vision transformer (ViT) models on arterial- and venous-phase computed tomography (CT) images. We analyzed CT images from 94 patients, including 47 without renal trauma and 47 with renal trauma (30,951 and 15,086 images, respectively). Arterial- and venous-phase CT images were reconstructed into axial, coronal, and sagittal images, with the renal regions cropped to construct the image datasets. Five pretrained CNN-based and five pretrained ViT-based 2D models were fine-tuned to classify renal trauma, and their performance was evaluated at the slice and patient levels using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), sensitivity, and specificity. At the slice level, the sagittal Inception-V3 model achieved the highest AUC values of 0.986 for venous-phase and 0.975 for arterial-phase images. At the patient level, the coronal Inception-V3 model achieved the highest AUC values of 0.991 for venous-phase and 0.945 for arterial-phase images. CNN-based models outperformed ViT-based models at both levels, with slice-level mean AUC values of 0.971 and 0.940 for venous-phase and 0.942 and 0.914 for arterial-phase images and patient-level values of 0.947 and 0.928 for venous-phase and 0.914 and 0.886 for arterial-phase images, respectively. The 2D models demonstrated high diagnostic performance for renal trauma, even when using arterial-phase images alone, supporting their potential for rapid decision-making in emergency settings.

articles.title: Tenant Right-to-Counsel and Emergency Department Use in Low-Income and Uninsured Populations.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Evictions are associated with numerous health harms, contributing to increased emergency department (ED) use. In 2017, New York City introduced the nation's first tenant right-to-counsel program, which lowered eviction rates by providing free legal representation to low-income renters facing eviction. Health implications of this policy are uncertain.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To test whether right-to-counsel decreased all-cause and cause-specific ED visits by low-income and uninsured individuals.

abstract.label: DESIGN
abstract.text: Retrospective cohort study of all-payer ED utilization data (1/2016-2/2020) leveraging the staggered implementation of right-to-counsel by ZIP code as a natural experiment. Subgroup analyses assessed heterogeneity by right-to-counsel implementation phase and age group. Secondary analyses examined cause-specific ED visits.

abstract.label: PARTICIPANTS
abstract.text: Medicaid-insured and uninsured individuals in New York, NY.

abstract.label: INTERVENTION
abstract.text: Right-to-counsel implementation status by ZIP-month.

abstract.label: MAIN MEASURES
abstract.text: All-cause and cause-specific ED utilization rates per 10,000 Medicaid-insured or uninsured ZIP residents.

abstract.label: KEY RESULTS
abstract.text: In total, 8,206,986 ED visits (21% by residents of right-to-counsel ZIP codes) were aggregated to 8550 ZIP-months. While there was no overall association between right-to-counsel implementation and all-cause ED visits (difference-in-differences estimate -10.8 [95% CI -32.8, 11.2] visits per 10,000), we observed a significant reduction in ED visits in ZIP codes targeted for the earliest intervention phase due to their high eviction risk (-26.4 [95% CI -52.6, -0.2] visits per 10,000) and a marginally significant reduction among children (-32.4 [95% CI -67.2, 2.4] per 10,000). In cause-specific models, right to counsel was associated with increased mental-health- and substance-use-disorder-related ED visits (2.5 [0.2, 5.8] and 2.7 [0.4, 5.0] per 10,000, respectively), with no significant differences in visits for ambulatory-care-sensitive conditions.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Tenant right to counsel was associated with reduced all-cause ED visits among residents of neighborhoods included in the first of three intervention phases and possibly among children, suggesting health improvement in certain populations. Further research is needed to understand increased ED utilization for mental health and substance use following right-to-counsel. Policymakers considering similar eviction-prevention programs may want to consider potential health benefits.

articles.title: Guideline adherence in helicopter versus ground emergency medical services: an indication-based analysis of 129,783 patients from the TraumaRegister DGU®.
articles.journal_full: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Helicopter emergency medical services (HEMS) are associated with higher intervention rates and improved access to specialized trauma centers compared with ground emergency medical services (GEMS). However, it remains unclear whether these differences reflect increased intervention intensity alone or more consistent implementation of guideline-recommended care. This study aimed to compare rates of selected guideline-recommended prehospital trauma interventions between HEMS and GEMS using a nationwide trauma registry.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective multicenter cohort study was based on data from the TraumaRegister DGU® (TR-DGU) from 2016 to 2024. Adult patients (≥ 16 years) with severe trauma, defined as maximum Abbreviated Injury Scale (MAIS) ≥ 3, receiving physician-staffed prehospital care and primary admission to German trauma centers were included. After exclusion of secondary transfers, missing key data, and treatment in local trauma centers (level 3), 129,783 patients remained, of whom 25.0% were transported by HEMS. Rates of selected interventions recommended by the German S3 guideline on the treatment of polytrauma/severe injuries were assessed using predefined indication-based subgroups derived from available registry variables as surrogates for potential clinical indications to improve comparability between transport modalities. Analyses were performed descriptively.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Patients transported by HEMS were younger and more severely injured than those transported by GEMS (mean ISS 23.5 vs. 20.8; ISS ≥ 16: 72.9% vs. 65.4%) and more frequently presented with impaired consciousness and shock. Across all predefined indication-based subgroups, HEMS was associated with higher rates of the evaluated interventions, including advanced airway management in patients with impaired consciousness (96.5% vs. 82.9%), overall chest tube placement in patients with thoracic injuries consistent with pneumothorax (50.5% vs. 40.9%), with substantially higher rates of prehospital chest tube placement in HEMS (14.0% vs. 5.5%), pelvic stabilization in patients with pelvic injuries of AIS severity 3-5 (56.7% vs. 44.0%), cervical spine immobilization in cervical spine injuries (84.1% vs. 77.7%), and tranexamic acid administration in suspected major bleeding (48.7% vs. 22.8%).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: In this nationwide trauma registry analysis, HEMS was consistently associated with higher rates of selected guideline-related interventions across predefined indication-based subgroups. By focusing on patients with predefined guideline-related indications, the present study aimed to improve comparability between HEMS and GEMS beyond crude intervention frequencies. Nevertheless, the observed differences should be interpreted in the context of the observational study design and residual indication-related confounding. Higher intervention rates do not necessarily indicate superior guideline adherence or quality of care in individual patients.

abstract.label: LEVEL OF EVIDENCE
abstract.text: III, retrospective comparative cohort study.

articles.title: Preoperative prevalence and risk factors for thromboembolic events following tibial plateau fractures: a retrospective analysis of an underestimated risk.
articles.journal_full: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Tibial plateau fractures (TPF) are complex intra-articular injuries carrying a high risk of deep vein thrombosis (DVT), muscular vein thrombosis (MVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE). Preoperative thrombosis is frequently clinically silent yet may cause serious complications, whereas its detection delays definitive surgery. This study assessed the prevalence and risk factors of preoperative venous thromboembolic events (VTE) in surgically treated TPF before and after implementation of routine duplex ultrasound screening.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In this retrospective single-centre study at a level 1 trauma centre, all adult patients surgically treated for traumatic TPF (AO 41B/C) between January 2015 and August 2025 were reviewed (547 patients, 554 fractures). Until August 2020 duplex ultrasound (DUS) was performed only on clinical suspicion; from August 2020 onward routine preoperative DUS was progressively implemented. VTE were confirmed by DUS or CT angiography. Prevalences are reported per fracture and patient characteristics per patient; regression analyses were performed at fracture level, except for the patient-related model.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: With DUS restricted to clinical suspicion (cohort A; 246 fractures), the detected prevalence of preoperative VTE was 3.7% (95% CI 1.9-6.8) and that of DVT 2.4% (1.1-5.2). Under routine screening (cohort B; 205 screened fractures) it was 20.0% (15.1-26.0) and 17.1% (12.5-22.8), respectively, 82.9% of DVT being distal. Given the different diagnostic strategies, this reflects the higher diagnostic yield of screening rather than a true increase in VTE. In cohort B, 28 of 41 VTE (68.3%) and 24 of 35 DVT (68.6%) were clinically silent. Two patients had in-hospital cardiac arrest from PE: one died from a DVT undetected before screening was introduced, the other had an asymptomatic DVT identified by screening. VTE was independently associated with pre-existing therapeutic anticoagulation (adjusted OR 2.96, 95% CI 1.10-7.98) and with the duration of external fixation (adjusted OR 1.11 per day, 1.02-1.20). High-grade closed soft-tissue injury (adjusted OR 2.41, 1.07-5.45), polytrauma (adjusted OR 2.24, 1.07-4.68) and initial external fixation (univariable OR 3.60, 1.76-7.35) were also associated with VTE, but none remained significant after accounting for fixation duration (adjusted OR 1.42, 0.52-3.89; 1.96, 0.76-5.05; 0.62, 0.12-3.27), i.e. risk was driven by time in the fixator rather than by external fixation as such.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Surgically treated TPF carry a substantial burden of preoperative VTE, and routine DUS reveals a high proportion of clinically silent thrombosis that would otherwise remain undetected. Severe closed soft-tissue injury, pre-existing therapeutic anticoagulation and, above all, the duration of external fixation may help to identify patients at increased risk. As two diagnostic rather than two treatment strategies were compared, the study cannot determine whether screening improves outcomes or reduces PE; prospective evaluation of structured screening and risk-adapted thromboprophylaxis is warranted.

articles.title: Cluster Versus Individual Randomization in Prehospital, Emergency and Critical Care Trials: A Meta-Epidemiological Study.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: Cluster-randomized clinical trials (cRCTs) are pooled with individually randomized clinical trials (iRCTs) in meta-analyses. However, cRCTs are associated with methodological characteristics potentially inducing systematic differences compared with iRCTs. In acute settings, trial inclusion is time-sensitive, exacerbating inclusion-based biases. We conducted a meta-epidemiological study to assess deviations in effect estimates between cRCTs and iRCTs in these settings.

abstract.label: DATA SOURCES
abstract.text: A systematic literature search was conducted in PubMed and Embase.

abstract.label: DATA SELECTION
abstract.text: We screened and identified all meta-analyses in prehospital, emergency, or critical care within the last decade that included at least one cRCT and one iRCT.

abstract.label: DATA EXTRACTION
abstract.text: Data were extracted in duplicate from the meta-analyses. If overlapping trials were identified, results were pooled. The primary outcome was mortality; the secondary outcome comprised length-of-stay- or days-alive-type outcomes.

abstract.label: DATA SYNTHESIS
abstract.text: Using absolute ln(odds ratio [OR]) for mortality and absolute Hedges' g for the secondary outcome, mean differences (MDs) in effect estimates between cRCTs and iRCTs were analyzed using mixed regression models, presented with 95% CIs. We identified 94 eligible meta-analyses; 44.7% reported on randomization type (cRCT or iRCT). We included 65 meta-analyses in quantitative analyses, encompassing 212 randomized clinical trials (39 cRCTs and 173 iRCTs) and 315,276 patients. No statistically significant difference in absolute ln(OR) for mortality between cRCTs and iRCTs was found (MD, -0.110; 95% CI, -0.093 to 0.313). For length-of-stay- or days-alive-type outcomes, a significant difference in absolute Hedges' g was found (MD, -0.202; 95% CI, -0.392 to -0.012).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: A systematic difference between cRCTs and iRCTs in length-of-stay- or days-alive-type outcomes, but not mortality, was identified, with cRCTs reporting smaller effect size magnitudes than iRCTs. With under half of identified meta-analyses reporting on randomization modality, these results highlight the need for improved transparency and statistical consideration of randomization type in future meta-analyses in prehospital, emergency, and critical care.

articles.title: Pediatric Clinical Interventions and Adverse Safety Events Among Emergency Medical Services Encounters in Agencies With and Without a Pediatric Emergency Care Coordinator: An Observational Study.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: The purpose of this study was to compare the frequency and types of adverse safety events (ASEs) and potential harm in a diverse population of pediatric emergency medical services (EMS) encounters. As a secondary aim we evaluated the association between prehospital pediatric emergency care coordinators (PECCs) in EMS agencies on the frequency, type and harm severity of ASEs.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This was a cross-sectional study of EMS and hospital records for children <18 years who received care from 15 EMS agencies from 2019 to 2023, using a validated ASE chart review tool. Frequency and types of ASEs associated with three different categories of clinical interventions (procedures, medication, and fluid administration) were captured. ASEs were assigned to three severities of harm: Harm Unlikely, Mild Temporary Harm, or Permanent/Severe Harm. EMS Physicians verified ASEs and harm severity.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: There were 2219 records included in the analysis, 995 from PECC agencies (44.8%). Median patient age was 12.5 years (IQR 6-15). In total, 551 (55.4%; CI: 52.3, 58.5) PECC agency patients had a procedure compared to 328 patients of agencies without a PECC (26.8%; CI: 24.3, 29.3; p < 0.001). Compared to non-PECC agency patients, PECC agency patients were more likely to receive medications (23.4% vs 7.7%, p< 0.001) and receive intravenous fluids (12.9% vs 4.6%, p< 0.001). In total, 290 ASEs were identified, the most frequent of which was the failure to perform a procedure or administer a medication or fluids (43.1%, CI: 37.4, 48.8). There were differences between PECC and non-PECC agencies in the frequency of ASEs in procedures (13.7% vs, 20.0%, p = 0.003). The assigned severity of ASE Mild Temporary and Permanent/Severe Harm was lower for procedures in PECC versus non-PECC agencies, respectively (28.6%, CI: 29.5, 48.5 and 63.3%, 95% CI: 69.6, 88.4, p < 0.001).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Compared to non-PECC agency care, pediatric care by PECC agencies was associated with more procedures, medication and fluid administration, but fewer ASEs for procedures and lower severity of harm when an ASE occurred. These results indicate that the PECC role may be associated with increased interventions and a reduction in harm associated with procedural care.

articles.title: Evaluation of first aid guidance for dermal chemical exposure in Safety Data Sheets (SDSs) used in occupational settings.

abstract.text: BackgroundSafety Data Sheets (SDSs) are widely used to guide first aid following occupational chemical exposure. However, the clarity and adequacy of SDS recommendations for dermal exposure remain uncertain.ObjectivesThis study evaluated the adequacy and clarity of first aid instructions in sub-section 4.1 of SDSs used in a biotechnology research workplace.MethodsFirst aid instructions in 45 SDSs were assessed against World Health Organization guidelines and peer-reviewed burn management literature. Key criteria included instructions on removal of contaminated clothing and accessories, irrigation procedures (duration of irrigation and source of water), wound care guidance, and recommendations to seek medical attention.ResultsFor chemicals capable of causing dermal burns (Category 1 skin corrosives), only 22% of SDSs recommended immediate removal of contaminated clothing, and 44% advised seeking urgent medical attention after irrigation. Although irrigation was mentioned in all SDSs, essential details such as irrigation duration, use of running water, and the role of emergency showers were omitted. Similar deficiencies were observed for chemicals associated with less severe dermal injuries.ConclusionsMany SDSs provide limited and nonspecific first aid guidance for dermal chemical exposure. Insufficient instructions may compromise early response to workplace chemical accidents and increase reliance on emergency medical services. Strengthening SDS guidance, together with enhanced occupational health training and involvement of occupational health professionals in workplace safety programs, may improve preparedness for chemical exposure accidents.

articles.title: Prehospital point-of-care ultrasound as a decision-support tool: A structured narrative review.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) may support focused bedside decisions, but prehospital implementation remains limited by operational constraints, heterogeneous protocols, variable training, and limited outcome-focused evidence. This narrative review examines prehospital POCUS as a clinical decision-support tool across cardiac, thoracic, trauma, pediatric, and obstetric applications.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A structured narrative review was conducted in MEDLINE/PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Central from April 2017 to February 2026. Search terms combined the prehospital setting, ultrasound, and clinical applications. Of 464 records identified, 38 full-text articles were included, including nine systematic reviews on cardiac evaluation (n = 2), thoracic evaluation (n = 3), and trauma assessment (n = 4). Screening and full-text assessment were performed by a single reviewer. No formal risk-of-bias assessment, certainty grading, quantitative synthesis, or meta-analysis was performed.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: In cardiac arrest, prehospital POCUS may identify cardiac activity and selected reversible causes, guide interventions, confirm return of spontaneous circulation, and support prognostic assessment, provided that image acquisition does not interrupt resuscitation or delay defibrillation. In nontraumatic shock and cardiac dysfunction, focused cardiac, lung, and vascular ultrasound may help characterize shock mechanisms, guide fluid therapy, and identify actionable findings such as pulmonary congestion, pericardial effusion, right ventricular strain, or major aortic pathology. In acute dyspnea, lung ultrasound may improve diagnostic confidence, particularly for cardiogenic pulmonary edema. In trauma, E-FAST has high specificity and may support triage, destination choice, trauma pathway activation, and preparation for definitive care; however, limited sensitivity prevents its use as a rule-out test. Pediatric and obstetric applications are feasible but remain emerging.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Prehospital POCUS is an adjunctive decision-support tool rather than a standalone diagnostic test. Its value lies in answering actionable questions that may influence treatment, triage, transport destination, hospital prealert, or pathway activation. Implementation requires protocols, training, quality assurance, and governance, and must not delay time-critical care or transport.

articles.title: Geophysical and Hydrological Hazard-Related Disasters in Europe, 2000-2025: A Retrospective Analysis.
articles.journal_full: Disaster medicine and public health preparedness

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To examine the frequency, distribution, and human impact (specifically fatalities and injuries) of geophysical and hydrological hazard-related disasters in Europe from 2000 to 2025.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a retrospective analysis of Emergency Events Database (EM-DAT, CRED/UCLouvain, Brussels, Belgium) records. Included events were earthquakes, volcanic activity, dry mass movements, floods, wet mass movements, and wave action. Deaths and injuries were summarized descriptively and compared using appropriate statistical tests.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 566 events were identified, of which 510 (90.1%) were hydrological and 56 (9.9%) geophysical. Floods were the most frequent events (n = 492), while earthquakes ranked second overall (n = 52). Southern Europe recorded the highest number of deaths, whereas Eastern Europe had the highest number of injuries. Overall, the examined events caused 3,547 deaths and 14,470 injuries. Median deaths did not differ significantly between groups (P = 0.791), while median injuries were higher in geophysical events (P = 0.036).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In Europe, hydrological hazard-related emergency events were more common than geophysical hazard-related emergency events. However, most fatalities and injuries resulted from a few severe floods and earthquakes with distinct geographic patterns. Because event frequency does not directly reflect harm to humans, these findings further highlight the importance of an all-hazard approach to emergency planning; disaster preparedness should align resilience strategies with regional hazard profiles, population vulnerability, and health-system capacity.

articles.title: Hospital resuscitation in patients with primary hypothermic cardiac arrest.
articles.journal_full: Emergency nurse : the journal of the RCN Accident and Emergency Nursing Association

abstract.text: Hypothermia is recognised as a reversible cause of cardiac arrest along with hypoxia, hypovolaemia and hypo or hyperkalaemia. However, hypothermia is the rarer one of these 'four Hs'. Because cardiac arrest caused primarily by hypothermia is a rare occurrence, resuscitation teams may lack real-world experience of it. This article sets out essential information for emergency department staff to understand this presentation and its management. It provides background information on hypothermia, describes the usual pattern of deterioration leading to cardiac arrest, and explains the key interventions required to give patients the best chance of survival, whether or not extracorporeal life support is accessible. It details the guideline recommendations that differ from standard advanced life support procedures and are specific to the management of hypothermic patients in cardiac arrest.

articles.title: Chlorine Gas Exposure: Clinical Course, Outcomes, and Lessons Learned Following a Mass-Exposure Incident in Oman.
articles.journal_full: Disaster medicine and public health preparedness

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: To characterize the clinical manifestations of acute chlorine gas exposure and evaluate recovery outcomes at 48 hours and 14 days post-exposure.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Retrospective observational case series of 31 patients exposed to chlorine gas during a mass incident in Sohar, Oman. Information regarding clinical presentation, treatment outcomes, and post-treatment complications was collected using a structured data collection tool to ensure consistency and accuracy during data extraction. Data analysis was performed using IBM SPSS v31.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Thirty-one patients presented to the study site and were included in the analysis. All were male with a mean age of 32.3 ± 9.4 years. At presentation, 90.3% of patients were symptomatic, with respiratory manifestations being the most reported symptoms. Eight patients (25.8%) required admission, including 3 admitted to the intensive care unit. At 48-hour follow-up, 18 (58.1%) remained symptomatic. Nine of 29 patients who attended follow-up on day 14 reported persistent symptoms, most commonly cough. No fatalities occurred.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: This study reports on the clinical course of acute chlorine exposure, highlighting that recovery often exceeds 2 weeks. Findings underscore the need for standardized clinical management, public awareness, and more rigorous industrial safety oversight to mitigate future chemical surge impacts.

articles.title: From Single Impact Sites to Dispersed Corridors: A Disaster Report of Emergency Medical Services Command Adaptation to Cluster-Munition Pattern Missile Strikes in Israel.

abstract.text: This Disaster Report describes a series of missile impact events managed by Magen David Adom (MDA), Israel's national Emergency Medical Services (EMS) organization, during the March 2026 missile campaign. The report focuses on a recurring operational distinction between compact single-warhead impact events and dispersed cluster-munition pattern events. Unlike routine mass-casualty incident recognition, MDA dispatch did not need to infer the possibility of a dispersed event only from accumulating emergency calls. While missiles are in flight, the Home Front Command (HFC) broadcasts real-time threat alerts through multiple public channels: the official HFC app, direct cell broadcasts to all phones in the threatened area, and live overlays on all television channels. Command and dispatch personnel from MDA used this publicly available information as an early threat layer at or before the initial dispatch phase. Emergency calls, motorcycle first-responder reports, volunteer responder reports, and ambulance crew updates then refined the actual medical footprint. Across six events, cluster-munition pattern events involved four-to-six municipalities and maximum geographic spread of 6.9km to 11.5km, whereas single-warhead events remained within one municipality and had maximum geographic spread of less than 400 meters. The events suggest that dispersed missile attacks require EMS command to combine prehospital warning-system visibility with a distributed responder network that functions as a forward sensor layer for dispatch and command.

articles.title: Service availability and readiness of primary healthcare facilities in Cambodia (2020-2025): a systematic review.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: To synthesise evidence published between 2020 and 2025 on the availability and readiness of primary healthcare (PHC) services in Cambodia and identify key gaps for health system strengthening.

abstract.label: DESIGN
abstract.text: Systematic review conducted following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 guidelines.

abstract.label: DATA SOURCES
abstract.text: Seven electronic databases (Web of Science, PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Google Scholar, PubMed Central, CINAHL and Western Pacific Regional Health Indexes) were searched, supplemented by grey literature from the WHO, World Bank and Cambodia's Ministry of Health.

abstract.label: ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA
abstract.text: Studies published in English between January 2020 and December 2025 reporting quantitative measures of PHC service availability or readiness in Cambodia were included. Eligible facilities comprised health centres, health posts and community-based primary care facilities assessed using Service Availability and Readiness Assessment (SARA), WHO Package of Essential NCD Interventions (PEN) or comparable frameworks. Hospital-based studies, qualitative studies, editorials and conference abstracts were excluded.

abstract.label: DATA EXTRACTION AND SYNTHESIS
abstract.text: Two reviewers independently screened studies and extracted data using a standardised form. Risk of bias was assessed using the Risk Of Bias In Non-randomised Studies of Interventions (ROBINS-I) tool. Due to methodological heterogeneity, findings were synthesised narratively.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Eight studies met the inclusion criteria, with facility sample sizes ranging from 45 to 1288. Maternal and child health services had the highest availability, with approximately 62%-85% of facilities providing them. Overall readiness scores ranged from 42% to 74%, with an average of about 58%, below commonly reported low- and middle-income country benchmarks. The lowest readiness levels were observed for essential medicines (~49%), infection prevention and control (~37%), non-communicable disease (NCD) services (~32%) and emergency care (~24%). Significant rural-urban disparities were consistently reported. Risk of bias was low in one study, moderate in four and serious in three.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Cambodia's PHC system demonstrates moderate service availability but inadequate readiness, particularly for NCD and emergency care services. Strengthening rural workforce distribution, medicine supply chains, infrastructure, NCD capacity and national monitoring systems is essential to achieve universal health coverage.

articles.title: Assessment of Carotid Doppler Parameters to Evaluate Volume Status: A Prospective Observational Study.
articles.journal: J Am Coll Emerg Physicians Open
articles.journal_full: Journal of the American College of Emergency Physicians open

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: Accurate assessment of volume status and fluid responsiveness is essential to guide fluid therapy, as unnecessary fluid administration may lead to fluid overload and adverse outcomes. Carotid Doppler ultrasound has emerged as a rapid, noninvasive alternative to more technically demanding echocardiographic measures. This study evaluated the utility of carotid Doppler-derived corrected flow time (FTc) and velocity-time integral (VTI), and their changes after passive leg raise (PLR), in assessing volume status and preload responsiveness.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a prospective observational study during Ramadan at a tertiary academic medical center. A total of 202 participants were enrolled, including 103 fasting individuals assessed during presumed relative dehydration and after rehydration, and 99 nonfasting hydrated controls. Carotid Doppler measurements of FTc, VTI, and Vmax were obtained before and after PLR. Diagnostic performance of percent changes in FTc (ΔFTc) and VTI (ΔVTI) was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic analysis.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Participants in the fasting group underwent a mean fasting duration of 12.4 ± 1.1 hours and consumed a mean of 920 ± 352 mL of fluid after breaking the fast. PLR induced significantly greater increases in FTc and VTI during presumed relative dehydration. A ≥10% increase in VTI was observed in 57.2% of presumed relative dehydrated participants compared with 26.3% of hydrated controls and 20.4% of rehydrated participants. Similarly, a ≥5% increase in FTc was observed in 47.6%, 17.2%, and 22.3% of participants, respectively. Receiver operating characteristic analysis demonstrated moderate discriminatory performance for presumed relative dehydration, with areas under the curve of 0.708 for ΔVTI and 0.715 for ΔFTc. Optimal cutoff values were 5.92% for ΔVTI and 5.05% for ΔFTc.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Carotid Doppler-derived FTc and VTI are promising noninvasive markers of volume status and preload responsiveness. ΔVTI demonstrated greater sensitivity, whereas ΔFTc provided higher specificity, supporting the potential role of carotid Doppler ultrasound as a practical bedside tool for hemodynamic assessment.

articles.title: Data environment requirements for a clinical toxicology learning health system: A mixed-methods survey.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Clinical toxicology research depends on reusable observational data, but toxicology information is often fragmented across systems and difficult to extract reliably. Learning health systems (LHS) use routinely collected data to generate knowledge and improve care. This study examined the conditions needed to support an LHS for clinical toxicology through reliable, clinically meaningful and reusable data.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a cross-sectional mixed-methods survey of professionals with expertise in clinical toxicology, poisons information services, emergency care, digital health, informatics, data governance, data engineering or health service data use. Survey items assessed six areas: data quality and standardisation, data access and governance, technical infrastructure, clinical workflow fit, organisational readiness, and future use and scalability. Open-text responses were analysed using descriptive content analysis and integrated with quantitative findings using a joint display.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Thirty-four respondents initiated the survey, and 21 provided analysable Likert data. Section summaries showed strongest agreement for future use and scalability and technical infrastructure, and lowest agreement for data quality and standardisation. Strong support was observed for timely clinical access (19/19), co-designed governance, workflow and technical design (17/17), sustainability through standards and stewardship (16/16), automation with human validation (16/17), and a concise essential dataset (19/21). Agreement was lower for integrating clinical terminologies into extraction and reporting (5/21) and prioritising completeness and accuracy over real-time entry speed (10/21). Integrated findings identified clinically meaningful source data, automation with clinical validation, timely access, proportionate governance, reliable and adaptable infrastructure, workflow fit and sustained stewardship as conditions supporting reliable data extraction and use.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Establishing an LHS for clinical toxicology depends on source data quality, validation, governance, workflow fit and organisational capacity to sustain data use. These findings can guide data environment design for research, surveillance and quality improvement. Targeted, non-probability recruitment and the Australia-New Zealand sample may limit representation and transferability.

articles.title: Serial Serum Nicotine Concentration During VA-ECMO for Nicotine-Induced Cardiac Arrest: A Case Report.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Acute nicotine intoxication can cause cardiac arrest. We report a case of cardiac arrest managed with veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) alongside serial serum nicotine monitoring.

abstract.label: CASE PRESENTATION
abstract.text: A 36-year-old woman collapsed after ingesting an unknown amount of liquid nicotine, up to 20 g. Emergency medical services found her in cardiac arrest with pulseless electrical activity (PEA). On arrival, she remained in cardiac arrest with PEA/asystole and severe acidosis, and VA-ECMO was established 82 min after ingestion. Cardiac function gradually improved, and VA-ECMO was discontinued on Day 3. However, she died on Day 28 from post-cardiac arrest brain injury. Liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC/MS) revealed an admission serum nicotine concentration of 6.44 μg/mL, declining to 0.057 μg/mL within 18 h. This decline paralleled hemodynamic recovery.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Although neurological outcome was unfavorable, VA-ECMO may provide temporary circulatory support during the toxic phase of massive nicotine intoxication.

articles.title: Prehospital management and hospital outcomes of severely injured patients during routine civilian mass casualty incidents: a 1:4 matched cohort analysis of the TraumaRegister DGU®.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Mass casualty incidents (MCIs) pose substantial challenges to prehospital emergency medical systems due to limited resources and the need for rapid prioritization. Evidence regarding the impact of routine civilian MCIs on the management and outcomes of severely injured patients remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate the influence of MCIs on prehospital care, transport strategies, and clinical outcomes compared with routine individual care.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Data from the TraumaRegister DGU® were analysed for patients treated in Germany between mid-2020 and 2023. Patients with severe trauma (Maximum Abbreviated Injury Scale; MAIS ≥ 3) were included. Mass casualty incident cases were identified based on registry documentation. A 1:4 matched cohort was performed using age group, injury pattern and traffic involvement as matching criteria. The primary endpoint was in-hospital mortality; secondary endpoints included prehospital time intervals, performed interventions, and transport strategies. An additional multivariable logistic regression was performed as a sensitivity analysis of the primary endpoint.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 65,152 patients were included, of whom 430 were treated during mass casualty incidents (MCIs). After matching, 423 MCI patients were compared with 1,692 controls. Patients treated during MCIs had slightly higher injury severity (Injury Severity Score (ISS) 24.8 vs. 20.3). Median total prehospital time was significantly longer in the MCI group (85 [IQR 67-100] vs. 67 [IQR 53-83] minutes; p < 0.001). Invasive interventions, including prehospital intubation (33.6% vs. 20.9%) and administration of tranexamic acid (32.1% vs. 15.0%) were more frequently performed in the MCI group. Helicopter emergency medical services (HEMS) transport was used more frequently (34.5% vs. 20.7%). In the matched cohort, in-hospital mortality did not differ significantly between groups (13.5% vs. 11.7%; p = 0.317). In an additional multivariable sensitivity analysis, MCI status was not significantly associated with in-hospital mortality (adjusted OR 1.19, 95% CI 0.77-1.85).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Mass casualty incidents (MCIs) were associated with prolonged prehospital care and modified transport strategies. No statistically significant difference in in-hospital mortality was observed between MCI patients and matched controls. These findings describe outcomes among severely injured patients captured by the TraumaRegister DGU® but should be interpreted in light of residual confounding and the observational study design.

articles.title: Skull Base Osteomyelitis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Epidemiology, Microbiology, Diagnosis, and Treatment Outcomes.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Skull base osteomyelitis (SBO) is a life-threatening infection arising predominantly from necrotizing external otitis, producing progressive osteitis of the temporal and central skull base. Originally described in elderly diabetic patients, its demographic profile has broadened to encompass immunocompromised hosts of diverse etiologies. Although historical mortality exceeded 50%, advances in imaging, microbiology, and antimicrobial therapy have improved prognosis substantially.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: To systematically review the epidemiology, microbiology, clinical features, diagnostic modalities, therapeutic strategies, and outcomes of SBO and to identify evidence gaps requiring further investigation.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A comprehensive search of PubMed/MEDLINE, EMBASE, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library (inception to March 2025, updated to March 2026) was performed. Studies reporting primary data on SBO (n >=5 patients) with defined diagnostic criteria, microbiological findings, treatment protocols, and outcome measures were included. Two independent reviewers screened records, extracted data, and assessed quality using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Findings are presented as a narrative synthesis per PRISMA 2020 guidelines. For the outcomes most consistently reported in primary cohorts, a random-effects meta-analysis of pooled proportions (DerSimonian-Laird, logit scale) was additionally performed.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Forty-five studies encompassing 1,628 patients met inclusion criteria. The median patient age was 68 years (IQR 57-76); diabetes mellitus was present in 74.2%. Pseudomonas aeruginosa predominated (62.4%), with ciprofloxacin-resistant strains identified in 11.3% of post-2000 series. Fungal SBO, principally Aspergillus spp., accounted for 7.8% of cases and was consistently associated with higher mortality across reported series. Gallium-67 scintigraphy demonstrated the highest sensitivity (94%) for treatment monitoring; FDG-PET/CT sensitivity exceeded 96%. Combined fluoroquinolone-based therapy yielded a cure rate of 71.4%. Evidence for adjunctive hyperbaric oxygen therapy remains limited to uncontrolled series and a single small comparative study, with no randomized trials, so its efficacy is unproven. The overall mortality was 15.3%. In a proportion meta-analysis of primary cohorts, pooled estimates were: diabetes 82.4% (95% CI 68.2-91.1), Pseudomonas aeruginosa 55.6% (48.4-62.6), clinical cure 84.7% (74.6-91.2), cranial nerve involvement 28.0% (16.1-43.9), and mortality 8.4% (4.3-15.8).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: SBO remains a serious condition requiring multimodal diagnostic evaluation and prolonged antimicrobial therapy. Emerging fluoroquinolone resistance constitutes a pressing clinical challenge. Standardized diagnostic criteria, prospective multicenter trials, and consensus treatment protocols are urgently required.

articles.title: Occupational injury patterns in a hospital-based cross-sectional study in Türkiye: sectoral characteristics, injury profiles, and determinants of multiple injuries (2019-2023).
articles.journal_full: Archives of public health = Archives belges de sante publique

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Occupational accidents remain a major public health and economic burden, particularly in middle-income countries. While healthcare workers and high-energy industrial sectors are often examined separately, hospital-based injury data derived from forensic medical records provide a structured opportunity to compare sector-specific injury patterns within a unified analytical framework.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective hospital-based cross-sectional study included all occupational injury cases presenting to a tertiary emergency department and systematically documented through forensic medical records between 2019 and 2023 (n = 402). Sociodemographic characteristics, sector, accident mechanism, injury location, and injury count were analysed. Associations were assessed using chi square tests and Cramérs V. Independent predictors of multiple injuries were examined using binary logistic regression, and sector- and mechanism-specific within-sample relative risks were calculated.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The study population was predominantly male (66.9%) and young (45.5% aged 18-29 years). Construction, healthcare, and logistics were the most represented sectors. Physical trauma accounted for 95.3% of cases, while infectious exposure risk was identified in 21.4%, mainly from needlestick injuries and body-fluid splashes in healthcare. Multiple injuries occurred in 35.8% of cases and were disproportionately concentrated in high-energy sectors, including electrical-mechanical work (OR = 44.43; 95% CI = 3.72-531.12), manufacturing (OR = 12.82; 95% CI = 2.91-56.50), construction (OR = 4.64; 95% CI = 1.58-13.62), and logistics. Traffic incidents and falls were the strongest contributors to multi-region trauma. Upper-extremity injuries, particularly hand and finger trauma, predominated in healthcare workers, mainly nurses and healthcare technicians, and were more frequent among females.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Among workers presenting to a single tertiary hospital, injury patterns differed by sector, with infectious exposure predominating in healthcare and high-energy mechanisms in industrial sectors. These within-sample patterns identify potential targets for sector-specific prevention; however, without workforce denominators, they do not establish which sectors or age groups carry the highest injury risk, and broader prioritization requires population-level evidence.

articles.title: Ensuring equitable emergency, critical and operative care.
articles.journal_full: Journal of health, population, and nutrition

abstract.text: Conditions requiring emergency, critical and operative (ECO) care account for a substantial proportion of preventable mortality and disability worldwide, yet ECO systems remain fragmented and underdeveloped in many settings. Recent global policy advances, including the adoption of the World Health Organization (WHO) Global Strategy and Action Plan for Integrated ECO Care by the World Health Assembly, provide an important opportunity to strengthen these systems. However, implementation must prioritise equity. ECO care spans a wide spectrum of complexity and cost, from basic triage, oxygen therapy and essential operations to advanced intensive care and specialised surgery. Given finite resources, health systems should first ensure universal access to foundational ECO care: early recognition of illness, basic airway and oxygen support, essential medications, monitoring, infection prevention, and timely referral. Approaches such as Essential Emergency and Critical Care (EECC) offer a feasible, highly cost-effective minimum standard of care, and prioritising such foundational ECO care is both an ethical imperative and the most effective pathway to achieving equitable population-level health gains.

articles.title: Head, face, and neck injury patterns across the life course: a 20-year NEISS analysis of 2,345,287 emergency department visits in the U.S.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Head, face, and neck injuries impose a substantial burden for emergency departments (ED); the mechanisms driving them across the life course however remain poorly understood at the population level. Large-scale, integrated analysis spanning anatomical regions, injury mechanisms, age groups, settings, and associated products or environmental surfaces offers an opportunity to identify the patterns and vulnerable populations that smaller or shorter-term studies cannot resolve.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We queried National Electronic Injury Surveillance System (NEISS) records from 2006 to 2025 for injuries to the head, face, eyes, mouth, neck, or ears. Demographics, anatomical region, injury setting, associated products or environmental surfaces, and ED disposition were extracted, and a rule-based narrative classifier assigned 1 of 17 injury mechanisms from free-text descriptions. Non-routine ED disposition was defined as admission, transfer, observation, or fatality. Analyses were descriptive and based on unweighted NEISS case records.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 2,345,287 ED presentations, representing 31.8% of all NEISS-coded visits, the head was most often injured (51.2%), followed by the face (28.2%). Annual volume rose 35.2% (105,727 in 2006 to 142,918 in 2025), driven mainly by head injuries (+ 83.4%). Median age was 14 years and 56.4% of patients were male, but among older adults (≥ 65 years), females predominated (60.6%). Falls were the leading mechanism (53.0% across subcategories). Most patients were treated and discharged (89.4%) and admission rate rose roughly 18-fold from toddlers (1.3%) to older adults (23.3%). Non-routine ED disposition increased with age, and syncope- or medical-related falls had the highest non-routine ED disposition rate (33.9%). The home was the most common injury setting (63.1%). Injury exposures varied by age group, with beds most common in infants, tables in toddlers, sports equipment in children and adolescents, and floors in older adults.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Head, face, and neck injuries represent a large and growing share of NEISS-coded ED presentations, with distinct patterns by age, sex, injury mechanism, setting, and clinical outcome. These findings may assist in the planning of targeted prevention strategies and future research on risk stratification for vulnerable age groups and injury mechanisms.

articles.title: Alcohol-positive polytrauma patients: injury patterns, ICU resource use and mortality at a German Level I trauma center.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: In most countries, alcohol consumption is so culturally ingrained that even small amounts are permitted while driving. Even at a blood alcohol concentration of 0.5 g/L, ethanol impairs mental and cognitive performance. Studies from the US and Europe estimate that elevated blood alcohol levels may be detected in 10%-40% of all emergency department patients. Against this background, we investigated the impact of alcohol consumption on injury severity, injury patterns, as well as primary and secondary outcomes in polytrauma patients.

abstract.label: MATERIALS AND METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective, single-center cohort study included patients admitted to a Level I trauma center via the trauma room and documented in the TraumaRegister DGU® between 2015 and 2023. Serum ethanol was determined routinely in all adolescent and adult trauma room patients. Patients without serum ethanol measurement or younger than 13 years were excluded. Patients with detectable serum ethanol (> 1 mg/dL, detection limit of the laboratory; ALC) were compared with patients without (noALC) using the χ² and Mann-Whitney U tests. Multivariable logistic and linear regression analyses were adjusted for age, sex, Injury Severity Score (ISS), severe traumatic brain injury (TBI) and pre-injury ASA classification. A dose-response analysis was performed using serum ethanol categories.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 1,524 patients were analyzed: 431 (28.3%) were alcohol-positive (ALC) and 1,093 (71.7%) were not (noALC). ALC patients were younger, more often male and had a lower prehospital Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score (p < 0.001), whereas the ISS did not differ (p = 0.396). They were more frequently victims of violent crime and were overrepresented among pedestrians and falls from < 3 m, whereas motorcyclists were more often sober. Alcohol-positive patients were more often treated in the ICU (90.0% vs. 86.3%; p = 0.048), but this association was attenuated after multivariable adjustment (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 1.40; 95% CI 0.96-2.03). Length of ICU stay and duration of mechanical ventilation did not differ, and alcohol was not independently associated with mortality (aOR 0.91; 95% CI 0.56-1.47). Severe TBI was more frequent in alcohol-positive patients (38.5% vs. 29.5%), increased with serum ethanol concentration, and was the strongest predictor of ICU treatment and mortality.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Nearly one in three severely injured patients had detectable serum ethanol. After adjustment for confounders, alcohol was not independently associated with mortality or intensive care resource use, and no dose-response relationship was found for these outcomes. The more frequent ICU treatment of alcohol-positive patients appears to be explained by their distinct injury pattern, particularly the concentration-dependent increase in severe TBI.

articles.title: Contrast-Enhanced NeuroPOCUS in Neurocritical Care: Overcoming Technical Barriers to Bedside Transcranial Ultrasound.

abstract.text: Neuro-point-of-care ultrasound (NeuroPOCUS) is an emerging bedside modality that extends the neurological examination through real-time assessment of cerebral structure and hemodynamics in neurocritical care. Despite increasing integration into clinical pathways and endorsement of transcranial ultrasound-based neuromonitoring by international guidelines, implementation is often hampered by inadequate acoustic windows and poor image and Doppler signal quality, frequently leading to nondiagnostic examinations. Ultrasound contrast agents (UCAs), traditionally used in specialist neurosonology, may overcome these barriers and recover diagnostic information in patients with limited acoustic windows. This clinically oriented narrative review synthesizes the available evidence on contrast-enhanced transcranial ultrasound and examines its potential translation into NeuroPOCUS as a bedside tool for frontline clinicians across vasospasm monitoring, intracranial pressure assessment, evaluation of steno-occlusive cerebrovascular disease, assessment of cerebral circulatory arrest, and other neurocritical care applications. A literature search of PubMed/Medical Literature Analysis and Retrieval System Online (MEDLINE), Embase, and Scopus was conducted through June 2026, and relevant studies, reviews, and guideline documents were descriptively synthesized according to clinical application. Available evidence indicates that UCAs improve Doppler signal quality, enhance visualization of intracranial vessels, and increase the proportion of diagnostic examinations in patients with limited acoustic windows, thereby improving the interpretability of bedside hemodynamic assessments. However, implementation remains constrained by operator dependence, heterogeneous acquisition and interpretation protocols, limited standardization, and the need for structured training and validated, application-specific velocity cutoffs. Looking ahead, contrast enhancement may expand the scope of bedside neurovascular assessment, including in emergency and acute-care settings where dedicated probes and presets are not readily available. Its favorable safety profile and enhanced bedside feasibility may help bridge the gap between guideline recommendations and clinical practice, although further technical and clinical validation is needed to define its role in frontline NeuroPOCUS.

articles.title: Intravenous ibuprofen versus ketorolac for acute low back pain in the emergency department: a triple-blind randomized clinical trial.

abstract.text: Considering the frequency of recurrence in low back pain (LBP), there is no single medication group with promising efficacy in acute settings. Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) provide better pain relief with rather low complications. Since ketorolac has been relatively effective, we compared its safety and efficacy with ibuprofen as an alternative for pain relief in acute LBP. In this multi-centric triple-blind randomized clinical trial, we compared intravenous (IV) ibuprofen and ketorolac in patients with acute LBP presenting to the EDs of three university hospitals. Group 1 received IV ibuprofen (800 mg), and group 2 received IV ketorolac (30 mg), based on a computerized random sequence. Trained head nurses prepared analgesics in blocks of four. Neither patients nor the researcher or the statistician knew about the medication. We applied Visual Analog Scale (VAS) for patients to score their pain at baseline and 10 and 30 min after pain medications. Of 73 enrolled patients, 39 were in the ketorolac group and 34 participants in the ibuprofen group. Pain scores were significantly lower in the ibuprofen group at both 10 min (49.6 vs 57.4; p =0.013) and 30 min (32.2 vs 40.7; p =0.038). Based on the pain intensity after 30 min, the majority of patients in the ibuprofen group (70.6%) rated their pain as mild, while only 35.9% of the ketorolac group reported pain relief to a mild level (p <0.001). The mean ED length of stay was significantly lower in the ibuprofen group, whereas rescue analgesia and adverse events were comparable between the groups. Pain intensity was significantly lower in the ibuprofen group than in the ketorolac group after 10 and 30 min, without a significant difference in side effects. Intravenous ibuprofen can serve as an acceptable alternative and might be more effective than ketorolac in acute LBP in the ED.

articles.title: Does dispensing medication from the emergency department reduce return visits and subsequent hospitalisation? A systematic review and meta-analysis.
Troponin elevation strongly predicts hospital admission but not 30-day outcomes in emergency department paroxysmal SVT: a propensity-matched cohort study.
Beyond the desk: digital self-registration as a redesign of the emergency department front door.
Absence of miosis does not exclude opioid exposure in emergency department patients with respiratory depression: a diagnostic accuracy study.
Context is king.
Diagnostic accuracy of a prehospital 0/1-hour point of care high-sensitivity troponin testing pathway.
Journal update monthly top five.
Stakeholder perspectives on sustainable antenatal point-of-care ultrasound (APOCUS) implementation in rural Australia: a qualitative study of professional body submissions and clinician focus groups.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Antenatal point-of-care ultrasound (APOCUS) may improve access to essential obstetric imaging in rural and remote settings where formal ultrasound services are limited. However, sustainable implementation requires accessible training, governance and accreditation pathways.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To explore stakeholder perspectives on the sustainable implementation of APOCUS training and practice in Australia.

abstract.label: DESIGN
abstract.text: Qualitative descriptive study using online focus groups and invited written submissions from Australian professional organisations and colleges.

abstract.label: SETTING AND PARTICIPANTS
abstract.text: Six online focus groups (including one pilot) were conducted with 35 clinicians with expertise in rural health, obstetrics, ultrasound, education and policy. Participants were purposively recruited to ensure professional diversity (doctors, midwives, nurses and sonographers). Written submissions were received from seven peak professional bodies.

abstract.label: ANALYSIS
abstract.text: Data collection and analysis were informed by the Australian National Strategic Framework for Rural and Remote Health and the COM-B Behaviour Change Wheel. Reflexive thematic analysis using a mixed inductive–deductive approach was undertaken. A comprehensive coding framework, supported by dual coding and kappa analysis, was applied across both datasets. Reporting followed the Consolidated Criteria for Reporting Qualitative Studies (COREQ) guidelines.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Stakeholders identified interrelated barriers and enablers to implementing APOCUS across education and health systems. Key challenges included limited access to rural training, funding constraints, inconsistent governance and accreditation, workforce capacity, supervision requirements, inequitable professional recognition and scope of practice uncertainty. Recommended priorities included consistent national standards; modular, locally accessible training; flexible, multidisciplinary accreditation pathways; expanded supervision and mentoring networks; technology-enabled support; and integration into health profession education. Stakeholders also emphasised patient-centred models of care, stronger rural engagement and local planning, alignment with national rural health priorities, and further research to inform implementation, funding and policy.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Stakeholder perspectives indicate that successful integration of APOCUS will require coordinated policy, workforce, training and governance strategies, including clear standards, defined scopes of practice, accessible education and accreditation pathways, equitable professional recognition and appropriate funding mechanisms. Technology-enabled support, expanded supervision networks and integration into existing models of care may facilitate scalable implementation. These findings provide a foundation for policy development, implementation strategies and future research evaluating the effectiveness, feasibility and sustainability of these approaches.

articles.title: Fatigue, anxiety and depression 12 months after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest: a population based cohort study.

abstract.label: AIM
abstract.text: To determine the prevalence and factors associated with fatigue, anxiety, and depression 12 months after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA); examine their associations with health-related quality of life (HRQoL) and functional recovery; and compare symptom burden with population norms.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This prospective, population-based cohort study included adults (≥18 years) who received EMS-attempted resuscitation and survived to hospital discharge following non-traumatic OHCA in Victoria, Australia, between July 2019 and June 2022. Survivors were identified from a statewide OHCA registry and completed a 12-month telephone interview. Primary outcomes were fatigue (Modified Fatigue Impact Scale), anxiety and depression (Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale). Secondary outcomes included HRQoL (EQ-5D, SF-12), functional recovery (GOSE), living arrangement, and return to work.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 1068 eligible 12-month survivors, 728 (68.2%) completed follow-up (median age 61 years; 555 [76.2%] male). Fatigue was reported by 35.8% (250/699), anxiety by 22.6% (162/716), and depression by 18.0% (129/716). Higher symptom burden was associated with lower EQ-5D and SF-12 scores, worse GOSE outcomes (all p < 0.001) and reduced return-to-work rates. Compared with population norms, survivors reported greater fatigue (SMD 0.64; 95%CI, 0.50-0.78; p < 0.001), and depression (SMD, 0.12; 95%CI, 0.02-0.21; p = 0.02) but lower anxiety (SMD, -0.27; 95%CI, -0.35 to -0.18; p < 0.001). In adjusted models, younger age, preexisting anxiety or depression, diabetes and initial non-shockable arrest were associated with higher symptom burden, whereas EMS-witnessed arrests were associated with lower symptom burden.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Fatigue, anxiety, and depression were common at 12 months after OHCA and are associated with poorer recovery. Fatigue exceeded population norms and may be an under-recognised component of cardiac arrest survivorship.

articles.title: Regional implementation of a prehospital advanced life support program with video-assisted physician direction and outcomes after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: The smart advanced life support (SALS) program was introduced to provide prehospital advanced life support under real-time video-assisted physician direction for out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA). This study evaluated the association between regional SALS implementation and OHCA outcomes.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective cohort study used difference-in-differences and event-study analyses with data from the OHCA surveillance system in South Korea and included adult OHCA cases (aged ≥19 years) from 2 years before through 4 years after SALS implementation in August 2015. The exposure was region-level implementation of SALS. Outcomes were the prehospital time interval, prehospital return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC), survival to discharge, and favorable neurological outcome. Pre- to post-implementation changes were compared between regions with and without SALS.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 129,207 cases were included. SALS regions had greater increases in the prehospital time interval (4.12 min; 95% confidence interval [CI], 2.91-5.33) and prehospital ROSC (1.35 percentage points; 95% CI, 0.56-2.15) than regions without SALS. No significant additional improvements were observed in survival to discharge (-0.35 percentage points; 95% CI, -1.31 to 0.62) or favorable neurological outcome (-0.35 percentage points; 95% CI, -1.08 to 0.37). Event-study analyses suggested differential pre-intervention trends for prehospital time, but not for the other outcomes.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: SALS regions showed greater increases in prehospital time and prehospital ROSC without significant improvements in survival to discharge or favorable neurological outcome, but the finding for prehospital time should be interpreted cautiously because differential pre-intervention trends were observed.

articles.title: Association between capnographic changes during pulse checks of varying durations and clinical outcomes during cardiopulmonary resuscitation: a multicenter study from Türkiye (CaPTuRe).

abstract.label: AIM
abstract.text: To investigate the association between capnographic changes during pulse checks of different durations and cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) outcomes.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This multicenter, prospective, controlled, quasi-randomized study categorized patients according to pulse check duration: Group A (≤5 s) and Group B (>5-≤10 s). Five measurements were obtained during the first six CPR cycles. Four capnographic parameters were evaluated for each measurement: Post-CPR end-tidal carbon dioxide (ETCO2), Pre-CPR ETCO2, loss rate (percentage decrease between Post- and Pre-CPR ETCO2), and recovery time (time required to regain the previous cycle's Post-CPR ETCO2).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The study included 252 cardiac arrest patients (Group A, n = 124; Group B, n = 128).
