In Group A, patients with return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) had markedly lower loss rates and shorter recovery times than non-survivors, together with higher pre- and post-CPR ETCO2 values (all p < 0.001). Group A also had a higher ROSC rate than Group B (36.3% vs. 19.5%; p = 0.005). Logistic regression identified pulse check duration as an independent predictor of ROSC, with Group A having 2.39-fold higher odds of ROSC than Group B (odds ratio [OR] = 2.39, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 1.347-4.242; p = 0.003). Pre-CPR ETCO2 was strongly negatively correlated with loss rate (ρ = -0.770), whereas Pre- and Post-CPR ETCO2 values (ρ = 0.96) and loss rate and recovery time (ρ = 0.89) were strongly positively correlated.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Pulse checks completed within 5 s were associated with more favorable capnographic dynamics and higher ROSC rates than those lasting 6-10 s. These findings are hypothesis-generating and warrant prospective validation.

articles.title: Identifying the operational bottleneck to shock delivery after automated external defibrillator activation.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Cardiac arrest registries record automated external defibrillator (AED) use and shock delivery but not post-activation operational timing. We aimed to identify the largest measurable bottleneck and an exploratory pad-application target for shock delivery within 60 s of AED power-on.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We retrospectively analyzed timestamps from remotely monitored Nihon Kohden AEDs between January 2018 and February 2026. After excluding inspection records, we grouped records into activation events and quantified intervals. Shock-timing and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analyses were restricted to initially shock-advised events with recorded shock delivery.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: We analyzed 8115 activation events. Median times were 42 s (interquartile range [IQR], 30-56) from power-on to completion of pad application, nine seconds (IQR, 9-11) from pad application to the first analysis, and 52 s (IQR, 40-66) from power-on to the first analysis endpoint. The power-on-to-pad-application interval accounted for a median of 81% (IQR, 75-85) of the total power-on-to-first-analysis interval, increasing to 87% (IQR, 85-90) when first analysis occurred more than 60 s after power-on. Among 900 initially shock-advised events with recorded shock delivery, the median pad-application-to-shock interval was 15 s (IQR 13-17). Exploratory ROC analysis yielded a power-on to pad-application threshold of ≥51 s in relation to first recorded shock delivery occurring more than 60 s after AED power-on.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: The interval from AED power-on to electronically detected completion of pad application, encompassing all intervening actions, was the largest measurable post-activation bottleneck. Completion within 50 s may serve as an exploratory process target for first recorded shock delivery within 60 s among initially shock-advised events.

articles.title: Association between burst-suppression with identical bursts and multimodal measures of cerebral oxygenation after cardiac arrest.
authors: Pittsburgh Post Cardiac Arrest Service Investigators

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Burst-suppression with identical bursts (BSIB) is an electroencephalographic (EEG) pattern associated with severe post-cardiac arrest brain injury (PCABI). Whether modifiable mechanisms of brain injury underlie BSIB is unknown. We hypothesized BSIB is associated with impaired cerebral oxygen metabolism, reflected as pathologically elevated jugular bulb venous oxygen saturation (SjvO2), higher brain tissue oxygen tension (PbtO2), normal jugular bulb venous-to-arterial carbon dioxide gradient (PbCO2 gap, and lower intracranial pressure (ICP) compared to other EEG patterns.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This single-center retrospective study included patients resuscitated from cardiac arrest who underwent EEG and SjvO2 or PbtO2 monitoring. We categorized EEG patterns as BSIB, malignant without BSIB, and non-malignant. Using mixed effects linear regression, we examined associations between EEG and SjvO2, PbCO2 gap, PbtO2, and ICP.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The SjvO2 and PbtO2 cohorts included 109 and 33 patients, respectively. SjvO2 did not differ between BSIB and malignant EEGs (β = 3; 95% CI, -0.6 to 7.0), but was higher with BSIB compared to non-malignant patterns (β = 12; 95% CI, 7.0 to 16.0). BSIB was associated with lower PbCO2 gap compared to malignant (β = -1.4; 95% CI, -2.6 to -0.3) and non-malignant (β = -2.6; 95% CI, -4.1 to -1.0) patterns. PbtO2 was highest with BSIB, but not significantly higher compared to malignant patterns in our adjusted model (β = 4.0; 95% CI, -4.7 to 13.0). ICP was lower in those with BSIB compared to malignant patterns (β = -19.0; 95% CI, -32.5 to -5.6).

abstract.label: INTERPRETATION
abstract.text: BSIB may represent a distinct subtype of PCABI characterized by impaired oxygen metabolism with preserved oxygen delivery and diffusion.

articles.title: Real-time feedback during bag-valve-mask ventilation for out-of-hospital cardiac arrest: a before-and-after study (VEntilation during Cardiac Arrest Resuscitation Study, VECARS-2).
authors: Paris Fire Brigade Cardiac Arrest Task Force

abstract.text: This study compared bag-valve-mask ventilation quality and adherence to the guideline-recommended ventilation volume range during 30:2 cardiopulmonary resuscitation for out-of-hospital cardiac arrest before and after the implementation of real-time feedback. We conducted a before-and-after observational study of two sequential adult cohorts with out-of-hospital cardiac arrest managed by basic life support teams from the Paris Fire Brigade. A bidirectional sensor measured insufflated volume (Vi) and expiratory tidal volume (Vt). The display was masked during Period-1 and provided real-time feedback during Period-2. We assessed adherence to the guideline-recommended range using mixed-effects regression; we analyzed Vt and leak volume using gamma log-link generalized linear mixed models. We analyzed 4300 ventilations in 163 patients, 96 without feedback and 67 with feedback. Median Vi was lower with feedback (471 mL) than without (513 mL, p = 0.03 for the first ventilation of each cycle) but median Vt was unchanged (235 vs. 243 mL, p = 0.84). Vi dispersion was reduced by 35% (mean within-patient IQR ratio 0.65 [95%-CI, 0.53-0.77]). Vi was 400-600 mL in 68% of ventilations with feedback vs. 42% without feedback. In contrast, Vt was 400-600 mL in only 14% of ventilations with feedback vs. 15% without feedback. In multivariable analysis, leak volume was 12% lower with feedback (mean ratio, 0.88 [95%-CI, 0.77-0.99]). Real-time feedback was associated with improved adherence to the guideline-recommended range for Vi, less dispersed VI, and lower leak volume. Causal inference, clinical significance, and generalizability warrant further evaluation.

articles.title: When Insulin Must Wait: The Role of Renal Replacement Therapy in Refractory Hypokalemia During Severe Diabetic Ketoacidosis.
articles.journal_full: The American journal of case reports

abstract.text: BACKGROUND Diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) is a common life-threatening metabolic emergency characterized by hyperglycemia, high-anion-gap metabolic acidosis, and ketosis. Severe hypokalemia before insulin therapy is uncommon but may complicate management and delay treatment. CASE REPORT A 37-year-old man presented to the emergency department with a 2-day history of generalized abdominal pain and progressive shortness of breath. He was drowsy and tachypneic, with Kussmaul respirations. Laboratory evaluation revealed severe DKA, acute kidney injury, and severe hypokalemia. Insulin therapy was initially withheld according to the DKA protocol. Intravenous potassium supplementation failed to achieve sustained correction, resulting in repeated interruptions of insulin therapy. Due to refractory hypokalemia, an emergency 2-hour session of intermittent hemodialysis was performed, followed by continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT). During CRRT, serum potassium increased, serum creatinine decreased, metabolic acidosis improved, and the anion gap closed. Insulin therapy was resumed without further interruption. However, the clinical course was complicated by severe septic shock, disseminated intravascular coagulation, and catastrophic intracerebral hemorrhage, ultimately resulting in death. CONCLUSIONS Severe hypokalemia at presentation in DKA poses a critical therapeutic challenge because insulin therapy must be withheld until the electrolyte abnormality is corrected. In rare cases of refractory hypokalemia, CRRT may serve as an adjunctive strategy to facilitate metabolic stabilization and safe DKA management. This case adds to the limited literature and highlights the need for further studies to clarify the role and effectiveness of this approach. Biochemical resolution of DKA may not correspond to clinical recovery, and critically ill patients warrant continuous monitoring.

articles.title: Ask the experts: a practitioner-centred approach to resilience in emergency medical services.

abstract.text: Background: Resilience in high-stress occupations is commonly framed as a trait, an outcome, or the absence of psychopathology. None of these framings captures what practitioners in emergency medical services actually do, and interventions built on trait-based models have produced weak or inconsistent effects.Objective: This study argues that frontline resilience in emergency medical services is better understood as a domain-specific expert skill, and that work mode - a deliberately entered state, akin to an athlete's game face, in which the demands of the task rather than the emotional force of the scene govern functioning - is its central empirical signature. The aims were to identify factors that intensify traumatic impact, characterise the strategies practitioners use to maintain functioning, and explore systemic and relational barriers that constrain coping.Method: Twenty Queensland Ambulance Service paramedics and dispatchers (tenure 2-38 years) participated in semi-structured interviews, analysed via reflexive thematic analysis.Results: Three intensifiers of traumatic impact (unpredictability, moral weight, personal threat) defined the operational demands against which resilience was enacted. Three coping themes (baseline buffers, work mode, social scaffolding) described the architecture of sustained functioning. Work mode exhibited the defining features of skilled performance: domain specificity, a phased temporal structure (preparation, containment, recovery), and a developmental trajectory from effortful to automatic execution. Two further themes (organisational distrust, the outsider gap) described the systemic and relational conditions that constrain coping.Conclusions: Treating resilience as expertise shifts the field from descriptive stressor-outcome accounts towards assessable, trainable capacities, and exposes the limitations of trait-based self-report measures that cannot distinguish genuine resilience from unsustainable stoicism.

articles.title: Comment on evaluating clinical characteristics and outcomes associated with body stuffers presenting to the emergency department.
Key agricultural pesticides responsible for acute pesticide poisoning in rural Sri Lanka - data to guide policy decisions.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Acute pesticide poisoning is a major public health problem among agricultural communities in low-and middle-income countries. Using recent surveillance data, this analysis identifies key pesticides responsible for acute poisoning in Sri Lanka to inform timely, evidence-based policy interventions, with relevance to similar agricultural settings.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We analyzed interim data from two prospective studies in rural Sri Lanka: 1) a suicide surveillance system (Oct 2023-Apr 2025) and 2) a community-based cohort of 1,200 pesticide sprayers (Jan-Dec 2024). Self-poisoning deaths were identified through police, coroner, and household follow-up data, while occupational poisoning was monitored through bimonthly cohort follow-up. Descriptive analyses were identified the pesticides and active ingredients responsible for poisoning events.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 1,040 suicides identified, 236 (22.7%) involved pesticide ingestion; a single pesticide was confirmed in 184 (78.0%) of deaths. Insecticides accounted for 165/184 (89.7%) deaths, predominantly the carbamate carbosulfan (120/184, 65.2%; 95% Confidence Intervals (CI) 58.3-72.1) and organophosphorus profenofos (20/184, 10.9%; 95% CI 6.4-15.4), with a small proportion involving illegal pesticides (13/184, 7.1%) or herbicides (19/184, 10.3%). Pesticide sprayers reported 1,311 incidents of acute occupational pesticide poisoning, with 856 events occurring after use of a single identified pesticide. Insecticides were the most frequently implicated, led by profenofos (167/856, 19.5%; 95% CI 16.9-22.1), followed by herbicides, including pretilachlor (125/856, 14.6%; 95% CI 12.2-17.0) and glyphosate (81/856, 9.5%; 95% CI 7.5-11.5).

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: These findings show that most pesticide poisoning is concentrated in two insecticides: carbosulfan and profenofos. Their continued prominence despite earlier regulatory actions suggests ongoing pesticide substitution and highlights the need for strengthened surveillance and targeted regulation.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Carbosulfan and profenofos now account for most pesticide suicides in Sri Lanka, while profenofos is also the leading cause of acute occupational pesticide poisoning. These findings highlight the need for ongoing surveillance and timely regulatory review.

articles.title: Unexpected naloxone response in pediatric olanzapine massive monointoxication.
Joint American Academy of Dermatology-Hidradenitis Suppurativa Foundation guidelines of care for the management of hidradenitis suppurativa.
articles.journal_full: Journal of the American Academy of Dermatology

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Hidradenitis suppurativa affects 0.7% to 1.5% of the global population and causes substantial disability and meaningfully impairs quality of life.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To provide evidence-based recommendations for the management of hidradenitis suppurativa.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A workgroup conducted a systematic review and applied the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluation approach to assess the certainty of evidence and to develop recommendations.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: This guideline presents 37 evidence-based recommendations. Strong recommendations are made for adalimumab, bimekizumab, infliximab, secukinumab, and routine pain assessment. Conditional recommendations are made for topical clindamycin, resorcinol, and ruxolitinib; oral doxycycline, tetracycline, and clindamycin with rifampin; intravenous ertapenem; spironolactone; short-term systemic corticosteroids; upadacitinib; specific procedural interventions; tobacco cessation; supportive pain management; and zinc supplementation and vitamin D repletion.

abstract.label: LIMITATIONS
abstract.text: Analysis is limited to best evidence available from systematic review.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: These guidelines provide evidence-based recommendations for the management of hidradenitis suppurativa.

articles.title: Takotsubo Cardiomyopathy Associated With Severe Medetomidine Withdrawal: A Case Report.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Takotsubo cardiomyopathy (TCM) is a transient syndrome of cardiac dysfunction with no occlusive coronary arterial disease, which may mimic an ischemic cardiac event. The pathogenesis of TCM is thought to be primarily driven by the effects of a temporary catecholamine surge on cardiac and vascular tissue. Medetomidine (an a2 agonist commonly found in the Philadelphia fentanyl supply) withdrawal is characterized by agitation and sympathetic hyperactivity that can precipitate a catecholamine surge. Though withdrawal from other Central Nervous System (CNS)-depressing substances such as opioids and clonidine have been found to be associated with TCM, there is little documentation of this phenomenon occurring from medetomidine withdrawal.

abstract.label: CASE
abstract.text: A 51-year-old woman with no reported medical history other than opioid use disorder presented to the emergency department due to concern for withdrawal from fentanyl and medetomidine. Her opioid withdrawal was well controlled with methadone and oxycodone. Shortly after coming off her dexmedetomidine infusion (started for medetomidine withdrawal), she developed acute ST-segment changes on electrocardiogram, elevated troponin levels on bloodwork, and regional wall-motion abnormalities on transthoracic echocardiogram. Her coronary angiography showed no occlusion and repeat cardiac laboratory workup days later had normalized with improvement in ejection fraction on cardiac echocardiography and magnetic resonance imaging. This signifies a temporary stress cardiomyopathy, likely from a2 agonist withdrawal.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: This case describes TCM in a patient experiencing medetomidine withdrawal. This patient's cardiac dysfunction was transient, temporally correlating with the cessation of her dexmedetomidine infusion. This suggests an a2 agonist mediated withdrawal leading to sympathetic hyperactivity which can precipitate TCM.

articles.title: Impact of Opt-Out Versus Opt-In Recruitment on Engagement of FDNY WTC-Exposed Responders in a Tobacco Cessation Intervention.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: World Trade Center (WTC)-exposed Fire Department of the City of New York (FDNY) rescue/recovery workers have an elevated risk of smoking-related morbidity. Despite access to free tobacco cessation treatment, some individuals in this population continue to smoke. In other settings, opt-out treatment approaches increase treatment initiation, but effectiveness in occupational health programs is unclear. Accordingly, we (1) assessed whether an opt-out strategy increases engagement with a Tobacco Cessation Program and (2) identified factors associated with engagement.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This was a randomized trial among FDNY firefighters and Emergency Medical Service (EMS) who self-reported smoking and were eligible for the WTC Health Program Lung Cancer Screening Program. 1:1 randomization occurred prior to contact for opt-out recruitment with Enhanced Care treatment (Opt-Out/Enhanced) or opt-in recruitment with Standard Care treatment (Opt-In/Standard). Opt-Out/Enhanced included proactive outreach and tailored biofeedback during counseling; Opt-In/Standard included participant-initiated engagement and standard counseling. Both groups were offered identical no-cost pharmacotherapy (varenicline). Engagement was defined as: consented enrollment (expressed interest and provided informed consent) and treatment initiation (attendance at ≥1 counseling session). Engagement differences were evaluated using logistic regression; sociodemographic and health-related factors were characterized descriptively without formal testing due to small numbers.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Overall, 312 individuals were randomized (Opt-Out/Enhanced, n = 156 and Opt-In/Standard, n = 156). Engagement was low (7.4%). Consented enrollment (n = 23; OR = 3.05; 95% CI = 1.11-9.72) and treatment initiation (n = 18; OR = 2.08; 95% CI = 0.72-6.73) were higher in Opt-Out/Enhanced versus Opt-In/Standard. Treatment initiators had a median age of 60.5 (vs 65.0 years among non-initiators); 38.9% were EMS (vs 18.0%), 22.2% were female (vs 6.9%), 77.8% had a prior cessation attempt (vs 23.5%), and 55.6% had abnormal lung function (vs 32.9%). Participants were too few to analyze cessation outcomes in depth.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Despite low engagement overall, opt-out treatment had higher engagement with tobacco cessation treatment. This supports other work that has found opt-out treatment to be encouraged for hard-to-reach populations.

articles.title: Mental health experiences and barriers: Black adolescents presenting for suicide risk and their caregivers.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Health disparities in suicidal behaviors exist for Black youth. There are many barriers that Black adolescents and their caregivers encounter when attempting to access mental health (MH) care. However, there is limited information available concerning their experiences, barriers, and facilitators of MH services.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Qualitative interviews were conducted with Black adolescents (ages 10-18) presenting in a pediatric emergency department with past-year suicidal ideation and/or behaviors and/or their caregivers. The sample consisted of 9 adolescents and 11 caregivers. Qualitative analysis was conducted by structured annotation and thematic analysis.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Adolescent and caregiver interviews identified seven themes: (1) emotional and behavioral experiences; (2) impact of previous MH treatment; (3) MH barriers; (4) facilitators for future treatment; (5) MH communication; (6) support; and (7) community resources.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Themes highlighted by both adolescents and caregivers were the impact of previous treatment, MH barriers, facilitators for future treatment, MH communication, and support. Although the interviews are consistent with research literature documenting the negative experiences and barriers to care for Black adolescents, MH experiences can be positive and helpful if provided in a culturally responsive manner.

articles.title: Association Between Early Bedside Clinical Findings and Need for Organ Support or Mortality in Critically Ill Children: A Multicenter Study.
authors: Critically Ill Patient Working Group of the Spanish Society of Pediatric Emergencies (SEUP)

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: To identify early bedside clinical predictors of the need for organ support and mortality among critically ill children presenting to pediatric emergency departments (EDs).

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a prospective, registry-based, multicenter observational study across 21 pediatric emergency departments endorsed by the Spanish Society of Pediatric Emergencies. Critically ill children evaluated on the 4th, 14th, and 24th days of each month between February 2021 and July 2024 were included. Critical illness was defined as pediatric intensive care unit admission or advanced airway or circulatory intervention in the ED. The Pediatric Assessment Triangle (PAT) was recorded at arrival. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with severe clinical outcomes and mortality. Model discrimination was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: We included 412 critically ill children; 63 (15.3%) had severe clinical outcomes, and 12 (2.9%) died. Abnormal circulation and appearance when evaluating the PAT and abnormal systolic blood pressure were independently associated with severe clinical outcomes (AUC: 0.75; 95% CI: 0.68-0.82). Prior pediatric intensive care unit admission and abnormal appearance and abnormal circulation when evaluating the PAT were independently associated with mortality (AUC: 0.85; 95% CI: 0.76-0.95).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Structured bedside assessment at ED presentation may provide clinically meaningful prognostic insight, supporting earlier prioritization and escalation of care for critically ill children, pending external validation.

articles.title: Traumatic Brain Injury in First Responders: From Hidden Burden to Occupational Health Action.
articles.journal_full: The Journal of head trauma rehabilitation

abstract.text: Traumatic brain injury (TBI), including concussion, is an important but often underrecognized occupational injury among first responders. Despite frequent exposure to circumstances that increase the risk of TBI, law enforcement officers, firefighters, and emergency medical services personnel often lack consistent pathways for injury recognition, reporting, clinical assessment, rehabilitation, and safe return to duty. This topical issue of the Journal of Head Trauma Rehabilitation brings together emerging evidence on TBI prevalence, underrecognition, mental health, functional recovery, and occupational reintegration in first responder populations. Collectively, the articles demonstrate a substantial burden of TBI, persistent gaps in diagnosis and treatment, and the complex relationships among TBI history, psychological health, and occupational functioning. They also highlight the limited evidence available to guide rehabilitation and determine readiness to resume safety-sensitive duties. A multidisciplinary consensus statement included in this issue offers 28 recommendations addressing recognition and reporting, early assessment, return to duty, mental health, prevention, and organizational policies. Although first responder-specific evidence remains limited, these recommendations provide a practical framework for improving care while identifying priorities for future research. Advancing TBI care in first responders will require coordinated efforts among healthcare professionals, first responder organizations, researchers, and policymakers to establish supportive reporting systems, improve access to appropriate care, and develop and evaluate occupation-specific return-to-duty pathways. Addressing TBI in first responders requires moving beyond individual injury management toward a coordinated occupational health approach that protects first responders and the communities they serve.

articles.title: Effect of blood transfusion on respiratory failure in severe trauma patients: A post hoc analysis of a randomized multicenter trial in Japan.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Severe trauma patients often need a large amount of blood transfusion including red blood cells (RBCs), fresh frozen plasma (FFP) and platelet. The blood transfusion can cause serious transfusion-related adverse events including respiratory complications, however, the risks of blood transfusion in trauma patients have not been well documented. We evaluated the hypothesis that the amount of blood transfusion during the acute post-injury phase was associated with respiratory failure among severe trauma patients at risk of active bleeding using a database of a randomized multicenter trial.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We used data from the Restrictive Transfusion Strategy for Critically Injured Patients (RESTRIC) trial, a cluster-randomized, crossover, non-inferiority multicenter trial conducted in Japan from May 7, 2019 to October 31, 2021 in Japan. The trial enrolled adult trauma patients transferred to the emergency department with severe bleeding or suspected severe bleeding and circulatory shock. All patients registered in this trial were included in this study. The primary outcome measure was the occurrence of respiratory failure within 7 days after admission. A logistic regression analysis on respiratory failure adjusted for sex, Injury Severity Score (ISS), chest Abbreviated Injury Scale (AIS) score, and the amount of RBCs, FFP, and platelet transfusions within 24 h was performed.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 417 trauma patients, 40 (9.8%) developed respiratory failure. Logistic regression analysis revealed that sex, chest AIS score, and platelet transfusion volume were associated with respiratory failure with 7 days after admission after adjustment (odds ratio [OR]: 0.300, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.113-0.794, p = 0.015, OR: 1.732, 95% CI: 1.267-2.367, p < 0.001, OR: 1.071, 95% CI: 1.021-1.122, p = 0.005 respectively). ISS, RBC, and FFP transfusions were not associated with respiratory failure (all p ≥ 0.05).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Among severe trauma patients with severe bleeding or circulatory shock transferred to the emergency department, platelet transfusion volume within 24 h may be a risk factor for respiratory failure within 7 days after admission. In contrast, RBC and FFP transfusions were not associated with respiratory failure.

articles.title: Bacterial cellulose-sericin gold nanoparticle conduit functionalized with GDNF for peripheral nerve regeneration: An experimental sciatic nerve injury model in rats.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Although the application of autografts continues to be regarded as the gold standard for the treatment of peripheral nerve injuries, there exists a necessity for alternative grafting materials. This study investigates the effects of a nerve conduit obtained from bacterial cellulose (BC) membranes modified with gold nanoparticles (AuNP) and functionalized with the GDNF neurotrophic factor on repair in peripheral nerve injury.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Bacterial cellulose membranes obtained from Gluconacetobacter xylinus cell culture were modified with sericin-gold nanoparticles produced by green synthesis and functionalized with glial-derived neurotrophic factor to become conduits. A unilateral 8 mm sciatic nerve defect was created in Wistar rats (n = 21). Rats were divided into three groups as autograft (n = 7), BC-AuNP (n = 7), and BC-AuNP/GDNF (n = 7). Gait analysis and electromyography (EMG) measurements were performed at the end of the 8th week. Tissues from the sciatic nerve were obtained for histological and immunohistochemical analysis.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: By the result of the 8th week, the BC-AuNPs/GDNF group attained results comparable to those of the autograft group, as indicated by the sciatic function index derived from gait analysis and EMG measurements. Examinations of axon diameters, myelin sheath thickness, and vessel count demonstrated that the autograft and BC-AuNPs/GDNF groups exhibited significantly elevated values in comparison to the BC-AuNPs group.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: In the management of peripheral nerve injury, the application of BC-AuNP/GDNF yielded healing outcomes that were comparable to those achieved through autograft, both functionally and histologically.

articles.title: Profound motorcycle risks: a national mileage exposure-adjusted analysis.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Motorcycle crashes (MCC) account for a minority of vehicle miles in the United States, but their exposure-adjusted burden among trauma admissions is not well defined. The purpose of this study was to compare the injury burden of MCC versus motor vehicle crashes (MVC) using outcomes standardized by annual vehicle miles traveled (VMT).

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A retrospective cohort study of American College of Surgeons Trauma Quality Programs (ACS-TQP) admissions from 2017 to 2023 was performed for adults aged 18-80 years admitted after MCC or MVC. Primary outcomes were admission, intensive care unit (ICU) admission, amputation, and in-hospital mortality per 100 million VMT using Federal Highway Administration denominators. Motorcycle VMT was used for MCC, and light-duty vehicle VMT was used for MVC. Secondary outcomes included Injury Severity Score thresholds (≥16 and ≥25), severe head/neck injury, open long-bone fracture, ventilation, and return to the operating room. Relative risks (RRs) were estimated using binomial regression models with a log link.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 1,419,094 admissions, 334,310 followed MCC and 1,084,784 followed MVC. MCC accounted for 23.6% of admissions but only 0.71% of included VMT. Per 100 million VMT, MCC had higher rates of admission (236.4 vs. 5.49; rate ratio, 43.0), ICU admission (70.8 vs. 1.57; rate ratio, 45.1), amputation (5.06 vs. 0.028; rate ratio, 183.0), and in-hospital mortality (6.4 vs. 0.12; rate ratio, 51.6). Among admitted patients, MCC was associated with higher risks of open long-bone fracture (14.7% vs. 6.6%; RR, 2.22), amputation (2.1% vs. 0.5%; RR, 4.25), and in-hospital mortality (2.7% vs. 2.2%; RR, 1.20).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: MCCs contribute a disproportionately high burden of severe trauma in the United States, with higher mileage-adjusted rates of ICU admission, amputation, and in-hospital mortality than MVCs.

articles.title: Changes in patient concentration and accessibility across 5 Pediatric Emergency Departments in Daegu, Korea.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: The coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic has substantially altered Pediatric Emergency Department (PED) utilization. However, longitudinal changes across multiple PEDs after major policy transitions remain unclear.

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: This study aimed to evaluate changes in utilization, patient distribution, accessibility to pediatric emergency care, and clinical characteristics across 5 participating PEDs in Daegu, Korea.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This multicenter retrospective study analyzed 140,017 visits among patients aged <16 years between January 2019 and May 2023. Concentration was assessed using monthly institutional shares and the Herfindahl- Hirschman Index (HHI), while the segmented interrupted time-series regression incorporated the Prais-Winsten correction and seasonal terms. The door-to-emergency room (door-to-ER) distance was defined as the WGS84 geodesic distance between the residential administrativedong centroid and fixed coordinates of the visited PED. We also evaluated the Korean Triage and Acuity Scale (KTAS) score, proportion of ambulance arrivals, and Emergency Department length of stay.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Median monthly population-standardized visit rates were 580.9, 315.8, and 500.1/100,000 child personmonths in the pre-COVID, COVID, and post-COVID periods, respectively (P<0.001); the post-COVID rate did not differ significantly from the pre-COVID rate after Bonferroni adjustment. Center D's share increased from 25.7% in the pre-COVID period to 44.4% in the post-COVID period. The HHI showed no immediate level change but increased in slope after May 2022 (β=0.00437/mo; 95% confidence interval, 0.00072-0.00801; P=0.020). Median door-to-ER geodesic distance increased from 6.44 to 8.68 km, and visits originating ≥20 km away increased from 16.8% to 20.9%, with a more pronounced distance increase among Daegu residents. The proportion of KTAS level 3 visits increased from 44.9% to 60.5%, and that of KTAS levels 1-2 from 3.0% to 4.3%.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: These findings indicate patient redistribution across the 5 participating PEDs serving Daegu and Gyeongsangbuk-do. Visit volume recovered after the COVID period, whereas patient distribution became increasingly concentrated with longer door-to-ER distances and greater reliance on emergency medical services, suggesting reduced accessibility.

articles.title: Visual behavior of flight nurses during initial prehospital care inside an ambulance: A cross-sectional observational study using wearable eye-tracking technology.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Prehospital emergency care requires rapid acquisition and prioritization of visual information under time constraints and in confined clinical environments. Although healthcare expertise is often associated with efficient visual scanning, evidence from real-world clinical settings remains limited because most studies have been conducted in controlled simulations.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To quantitatively analyze flight nurses' visual behavior during initial prehospital care provided inside an ambulance after their rendezvous with the ground ambulance crew and examine whether gaze behavior is associated with their experience levels.

abstract.label: DESIGN
abstract.text: A cross-sectional observational study using wearable eye-tracking technology.

abstract.label: SETTING
abstract.text: A helicopter emergency medical service base hospital in Japan, with observations focused on initial prehospital care provided inside an ambulance after rendezvous with the ground ambulance crew.

abstract.label: PARTICIPANTS
abstract.text: Nine flight nurses were included: two in the novice group, four in the intermediate group, and three in the expert group. These groups contributed 10, 30, and 20 cases, respectively, for a total of 60 cases.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Gaze behavior was recorded using a Tobii Pro Glasses 3 wearable eye-tracking device. Fixation count per minute, visit count per minute, and total fixation duration per minute were calculated across 11 areas of interest. Principal component analyses were conducted separately for each gaze measure. Generalized estimating equations, with flight nurses specified as the subject, were used to examine associations between principal component scores and experience group. A sensitivity analysis was conducted using the natural logarithm of the cumulative dispatch count as a continuous predictor.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Four principal components were retained for each of the three gaze measures. Significant associations with experience groups remained for four components after adjustment for multiple comparisons. The novice group showed higher team-related fixation than the intermediate and expert groups, higher body- and measurement-related visits than the expert group, higher team- and documentation-related visits than both other groups, and higher body- and measurement-related total fixation duration than the intermediate group. In the sensitivity analysis, a greater cumulative dispatch experience was associated with lower scores for the body- and measurement-related and team-related fixation components, as well as the body- and measurement-related and team- and documentation-related visit components.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Flight nurses' visual information acquisition during ambulance-based initial prehospital care was associated with experience level, particularly for gaze behavior involving body and measurement information, team members, and documentation. These findings suggest that experience-related gaze patterns during ambulance-based initial prehospital care may inform future approaches to visual information acquisition training for flight nurses.

abstract.label: REGISTRATION
abstract.text: Not registered.

articles.title: Concussion Safety Beliefs and Participation Decisions Among US Adults With a History of Concussion.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Concussion safety education must address specific participation decisions as well as general beliefs.

abstract.label: METHOD
abstract.text: An anonymous, opt-in online survey of 100 US adults with self-reported concussion history was analyzed descriptively.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Ninety-one percent endorsed avoiding same-day return after suspected concussion, and 81% would not allow a child to continue immediately after a "mild" concussion. Among the 91 endorsing no same-day return, 9 would allow immediate continuation, 7 selected sport-dependent participation, and 2 were unsure. Medical clearance was supported by 88% on an agreement item, whereas 77% selected clearance after every concussion on a separate question.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Responses varied across differently worded safety questions; they do not establish actual behavior or national prevalence.

abstract.label: PRACTICAL APPLICATIONS
abstract.text: Education could distinguish immediate removal from later graduated return and explicitly address injuries described as mild. These descriptive findings support testing such messages, rather than demonstrating their effectiveness.

articles.title: Neurological causes of cardiac arrest in adults: Epidemiology, mechanisms, diagnosis, and clinical implications.

abstract.text: Neurological conditions account for a small but poorly quantified proportion of cardiac arrests in adults. Recognising them means separating the disease that triggered the arrest from the hypoxic-ischaemic injury that follows it, a distinction that the initial presentation often obscures. Electrocardiographic abnormalities suggestive of a coronary origin, non-epileptic convulsive movements, and injury sustained during the fall are all confounders. Reported proportions, approximately 3-8% across series, depend on recruitment, on access to investigations, and on the attribution rules applied. This Review examines the conditions involved, the pathways by which they compromise ventilation and cardiovascular control, and the features that point to a neurological cause after return of spontaneous circulation. It sets out what this attribution implies for aetiological treatment, for prevention, and for the interpretation of prognosis, since the performance and calibration of standard multimodal algorithms are insufficiently established when a primary brain injury preceded the arrest.

articles.title: Youth Mental Health-Related Emergency Department Visits After Hurricane Helene: A Difference-in-Differences Analysis.
articles.journal_full: The Journal of adolescent health : official publication of the Society for Adolescent Medicine

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: Extreme weather can disrupt social supports, schooling, and access to behavioral health services, potentially affecting youth mental health. This study examined changes in youth mental health-related emergency department (ED) visits following Hurricane Helene (2024).

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: ED surveillance data from North Carolina (2022-2024) were used to assess mental health-related visits among youth aged 5-26. A difference-in-difference (DID) design compared FEMA-designated disaster counties with nondeclared counties before and after the storm. Multilevel intersectional analyses evaluated risk by sex, race/ethnicity, age, and insurance.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Anxiety-related ED visits increased in disaster-exposed counties post-Helene (DIDRR = 1.14, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.01-1.29), with larger increases among females than males (DIDRR = 1.18, 95% CI: 1.03-1.35). Depression also showed greater relative increases among females (difference-in-difference-in-differencesRR = 1.28, 95% CI: 1.09-1.51). Self-harm visits declined overall (DIDRR = 0.70, 95% CI: 0.52-0.94).

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: Hurricane Helene was associated with shifts in youth mental health-related ED use, demonstrating the need to strengthen adolescent and young adult behavioral health services in disaster-prone rural communities.

articles.title: Swallowed dental prosthesis causing late oesophageal obstruction and tracheo-oesophageal fistula in a young patient.

abstract.text: A 25-year-old man presented to the emergency department after a rugby accident having swallowed a dental plate. Initial assessment at the time of ingestion, including a chest radiograph, was unremarkable and the plate was presumed to have been expectorated. Five years later he presented with progressive dysphagia, recurrent food bolus obstruction, and haemoptysis. Computed tomography of the thorax performed 5 years later revealed circumferential oesophageal thickening and a large inflammatory mass around a retained radio-opaque foreign body at the level of the carina, with an associated tracheo-oesophageal fistula. Endoscopy confirmed near-complete obstruction of the oesophagus. He underwent a right thoracotomy with oesophagectomy, removal of the retained dental prosthesis and repair of the fistula. He made a slow but steady recovery and has required anastomotic dilatation for a stricture. This case highlights the risk of complications from retained oesophageal foreign bodies and the limitations of plain radiography in detecting non-radio-opaque dental plates.

articles.title: Active Exsanguination Behind a Urinary Tract Infection (UTI) Diagnostic Label: A Quadruple-Hit Cardiorenal Collapse Following Ambulatory Urological Care.

abstract.text: We report the case of a 95-year-old man with a previous history of myocardial infarction, pulmonary oedema, and hypertension who developed recurrent collapse while undergoing ambulatory urological follow-up for a six-week history of macroscopic haematuria. Following a recent outpatient review, he had received oral antibiotics for a presumed urinary tract infection (UTI). Throughout this six-week ambulatory period, no full blood count or other blood tests were performed, leaving the extent of blood loss and its haematological consequences clinically occult. The patient subsequently experienced three episodes of sudden collapse within one week at home. The episodes were preceded by a prodrome of marked weakness. On assessment by ambulance clinicians, a profound postural blood-pressure drop was identified. Given the postural component and presumed recent urinary infection, dehydration was considered the initial explanation, and intravenous fluid resuscitation was commenced. However, hospital point-of-care investigations substantially changed the diagnostic picture. Venous blood gas analysis demonstrated a haemoglobin concentration consistent with profound anaemia. ECG demonstrated a right bundle branch block, left axis deviation, and a prolonged PR interval, indicating significant conduction-system disease in the context of previous ischaemic myocardial injury. Serum biochemistry demonstrated elevated creatinine and urea, alongside a severely reduced estimated glomerular filtration rate, consistent with severe renal dysfunction. Venous blood gas analysis further showed a low pH and elevated lactate, indicating significant metabolic acidosis. The clinical picture suggested an interaction between severe blood-loss anaemia, impaired cardiovascular compensatory reserve, postural haemodynamic stress, and renal hypoperfusion. Severe anaemia substantially reduces arterial oxygen content, necessitating compensatory increases in cardiac output and oxygen extraction. When cardiovascular reserve is already compromised, this compensation may be inadequate. Emergency packed red blood cell transfusion and careful fluid-volume optimisation were undertaken. Given the recurrent collapse and significant conduction abnormalities, an urgent cardiology transfer was arranged for permanent pacemaker insertion. Severe renal dysfunction prompted urgent nephrology involvement and transfer.

articles.title: Race, Gender, and Survival: a Scoping Review of Disparities in ICU Post-Resuscitation Care and Neurological Outcomes Following Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest.
articles.journal_full: Journal of racial and ethnic health disparities

abstract.text: Racial and ethnic disparities in healthcare are well documented, yet limited attention has been given to the intersection of race/ethnicity and gender in high-acuity critical care. Black women experience compounded inequities affecting access to and quality of intensive care unit (ICU) treatment following out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA). Because outcomes after OHCA are influenced by each link in the chain of survival, disparities in early intervention and subsequent clinical decision-making may contribute to differences in survival and neurological recovery. This study synthesizes evidence on disparities in ICU treatment and outcomes among Black women in the United States while examining how inequities across the chain of survival may influence post-resuscitation care, neurocritical care, and outcomes following OHCA. We conducted a scoping review, guided by the Arksey and O'Malley framework, to analyze peer-reviewed studies identified through electronic databases (e.g., PubMed, CINAHL, and ScienceDirect). Fifteen studies met inclusion criteria and were analyzed using thematic synthesis. Findings indicate persistent disparities, including lower bystander cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) rates, delayed emergency response, reduced access to ICU interventions, and higher rates of early do-not-resuscitate (DNR) orders and withdrawal of life-sustaining therapies (WLST). These inequities may contribute to poorer outcomes and likely reflect a combination of systemic, institutional, and social factors, although relatively few studies directly examined Black women from an intersectional perspective. Addressing these disparities requires improved data disaggregation, culturally responsive care, and interdisciplinary interventions to promote equitable post-resuscitation care and outcomes.

articles.title: Public Health Impact of Adjuvanted RSVPreF3 Vaccination Among US Adults Aged ≥60 Years Residing in Long-Term Care Settings.
articles.journal_full: Journal of the American Medical Directors Association

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: Adults aged ≥60 years and adults with certain health conditions are at increased risk for severe respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) disease, which can have a substantial clinical burden. Residents in long-term care settings often have multiple risk factors, including age ≥60 years, underlying health conditions, and/or frailty, compounding risk for severe RSV disease. This study evaluated the public health impact of adjuvanted RSV prefusion F3 (RSVPreF3) vaccination on averted RSV disease burden.

abstract.label: DESIGN
abstract.text: Public health impact analysis using a static, multicohort Markov model.

abstract.label: SETTING AND PARTICIPANTS
abstract.text: United States (US) adults aged ≥60 years residing in long-term care settings.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Adjuvanted RSVPreF3 vaccination vs no vaccination was simulated over 5 years using real-world RSV vaccination uptake data. Other model inputs have been previously validated and reported. This analysis estimated avoided RSV-related health outcomes due to vaccination, as well as the number needed to vaccinate (NNV) to avoid RSV-related outcomes.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among the modeled 2,113,600 US adults aged ≥60 years residing in long-term care settings, 378,656 were simulated to receive 1 dose of adjuvanted RSVPreF3. RSV vaccination resulted in 33,989 fewer RSV cases, including 7688 fewer RSV-upper respiratory tract disease cases and 26,302 fewer RSV-lower respiratory tract disease cases (RSV-LRTD). Avoided healthcare resource use included 19,639 fewer outpatient visits, 1556 fewer emergency department visits, and 11,634 fewer hospitalizations. RSV-related deaths declined by 1355 over 5 years, alongside 7221 and 6043 fewer discounted life years and quality-adjusted life years lost, respectively. To avoid 1 RSV-LRTD case, the estimated NNV was 14 individuals.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS AND IMPLICATIONS
abstract.text: Adjuvanted RSVPreF3 vaccination avoided a substantial number of negative health outcomes among US adults aged ≥60 years residing in long-term care settings, providing evidence of its impact as a prevention strategy. Future efforts are needed to ensure that long-term care residents have access to RSV vaccination.

articles.title: "Surgical Outcomes in Body Contouring Procedures: A Retrospective Cohort Study of 168 Patients".

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Transgender and gender diverse (TGD) individuals may undergo feminizing body contouring (FBC), liposuction with or without fat grafting to the buttocks and hips, to fulfill embodiment goals. There is currently little literature describing FBC outcomes.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A retrospective review of patients who were ≥18 years old with ≥1 postoperative appointment who underwent FBC from 1/2019-10/2024 by four surgeons was performed. Demographic data, medical history, perioperative details, and complications were reviewed.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 168 primary procedures were completed. Most patients (n=161, 96.4%) used hormones for an average of 8.5 years. Average age was 37.1 years old and average BMI was 29.3 kg/m2. Average fat transferred was 2.2 L, most commonly from the abdomen (98.8%), back (94.6%), and medial thighs (59.5%). A third of patients (33.3%) attended at least one hyperbaric oxygen chamber therapy session with an average of 12.7 sessions. At average follow-up of 318.5 days, 19.6% of patients experienced any complication, 4.2% with contour deformity, 3.0% with fat necrosis, 2.4% with cellulitis, 2.4% having seroma, and 2.4% being readmitted. Revision rate for fat loss or deformity was 20.2%. Increased age was associated with fat necrosis (p=0.05) and increased HBOT sessions was associated with decreased odds of any complication (p=0.03). While BMI did not correlate with complication rates, increasing fat grafting volume trended toward statistical significance for association with any complication (p = 0.07).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: FBC appears to be a safe and customizable procedure for transfeminine patients, with relatively low rates of major complications. Clinical counseling should emphasize potential need for revision due to fat loss or contour deformity.

articles.title: Technological Integration in Triage With AI and Machine Learning Compared With Conventional Triage and Narrative Synthesis of Telehealth for Patient Prioritization in Emergency and Acute Care Settings: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Conventional triage relies on clinician judgment and limited information available at first contact. AI and machine learning (ML) may improve early risk stratification, whereas tele-triage and patient-facing tools primarily support remote assessment, access, and care routing.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic and prognostic performance of AI- and ML-assisted triage systems and summarize evidence on tele-triage, workflow, implementation, economic, and equity outcomes.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Comparative studies published between January 1, 2010, and December 31, 2025, evaluating AI-, ML-, natural language processing-, telehealth-, or digitally enhanced triage. At first, clinical contacts were included. PubMed/MEDLINE, CINAHL, Web of Science, Scopus, preprint servers, trial registries, and conference proceedings were searched. Screening and data extraction were performed independently in duplicate. Risk of bias was assessed using design-appropriate tools. Clinically comparable area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) estimates were synthesized using random-effects meta-analysis; heterogeneous diagnostic, operational, implementation, economic, and equity outcomes were summarized narratively. Exploratory scenario modeling projected effects per 10,000 emergency department (ED) visits.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Twenty-seven studies were included, comprising 13 studies in the quantitative evidence stream and 14 in the narrative synthesis. Four adult ED studies evaluating critical care or deterioration outcomes demonstrated high pooled discrimination for AI-assisted triage (AUC 0.874; 95% CI 0.845-0.898; I²=94.4%; 95% prediction interval 0.803-0.922). Four studies reported directly extractable within-study comparisons favoring AI-assisted models (AUC differences of 0.097, 0.120, 0.108, and 0.065), although these could not be pooled because paired variance estimates were unavailable. Admission/disposition studies reported AI-model AUCs ranging from 0.80 to 0.93 and were summarized descriptively because extreme heterogeneity precluded meaningful pooling. Two pediatric studies (AUCs of 0.85-0.99) were summarized descriptively. Prediction-model studies were primarily limited by deficiencies in model analysis, calibration reporting, and external validation. Narrative evidence suggested improved front-door operational metrics with tele-triage, including reported reductions of 15%-40% in time to clinical assessment and 2-8 percentage points in left-without-being-seen rates, whereas patient-facing symptom checkers generally favored sensitivity over specificity. Exploratory scenario modeling illustrated that, under specified prevalence and threshold assumptions, AI-assisted triage could be associated with 12-38 fewer missed critical illness cases and 45-120 additional false-positive escalations per 10,000 ED visits. Economic and equity findings were assumption-dependent projections rather than observed clinical, cost-effectiveness, or equity outcomes.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: AI- and ML-assisted triage models demonstrate promising discrimination for adult ED risk stratification; however, AUC-based discrimination does not establish superiority at clinically relevant decision thresholds, improved patient outcomes, or readiness for clinical implementation. Interpretation is limited by substantial heterogeneity, incomplete threshold-level performance and calibration reporting, limited external validation, and sparse pediatric evidence. Prospective multicenter validation, workflow assessment, subgroup calibration and equity auditing, and formal economic evaluation are required before routine implementation.

articles.title: Heart Failure With Reduced Ejection Fraction Is Associated With Greater Cardiovascular Risk Following Lumbar Interbody Fusion.

abstract.text: Study DesignRetrospective cohort study.ObjectiveTo compare perioperative cardiovascular outcomes between patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) and reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) following transforaminal or posterior lumbar interbody fusion (TLIF/PLIF).MethodsThe TriNetX Research Network was used to identify patients undergoing elective TLIF or PLIF between 2011 and 2025. Cohorts were defined by heart failure phenotype and propensity score-matched (PSM) 1:1 for baseline demographics and comorbidities. Outcomes included postoperative atrial fibrillation or flutter (AF/AFL), myocardial infarction (MI), and secondary complications within 90 days. Odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals were calculated. Significance was defined as p < 0.05.ResultsOf 46,431 patients, 1,253 (2.7%) had HFrEF, 1,920 (4.1%) had HFpEF, and 43,258 (93.2%) had no heart failure. After PSM, both phenotypes carried elevated risk relative to non-HF controls across measured complications, including acute respiratory failure, pneumonia, AF/AFL, acute kidney injury, venous thromboembolism, and 90-day emergency department visits (all p<0.05). In the direct phenotype comparison (1,217 matched pairs), acute MI occurred more frequently in HFrEF than HFpEF patients (14.4% vs. 8.7%, p<0.001). HFrEF was associated with greater odds of acute MI (OR 1.760 [95% CI: 1.363, 2.273], p<0.001) and AF/AFL (OR 1.278 [95% CI: 1.079, 1.513], p=0.005) compared with HFpEF.ConclusionAmong patients with heart failure undergoing TLIF or PLIF, those with HFrEF are at increased risk of postoperative AF/AFL and MI compared with HFpEF patients. These findings highlight the importance of distinguishing heart failure phenotype during preoperative risk stratification and may support enhanced perioperative precautions.

articles.title: A National Trauma Data Bank Analysis of Work-Related Versus Non Work-Related Trauma Injury Admissions in the United States, 2017-2022.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Trauma registry data have unique characteristics differentiating them from traditional occupational injury surveillance data sources. This study analyzed trauma injury admissions (which includes emergency department encounters regardless of discharge disposition) in the American College of Surgeons National Trauma Data Bank (NTDB) to compare worker and injury characteristics of work-related and non-work-related admissions.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This cross-sectional study analyzed admissions among patients aged 14 years and older from the NTDB during 2017-2022. We calculated frequencies for demographic, injury, and outcome characteristics stratified by work-relatedness (injury occurrence during paid employment). Multivariable logistic regression assessed the relationship between demographic and injury characteristics with work-relatedness as the outcome, adjusted for age, sex, race/ethnicity, and mechanism of injury.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 5,901,246 injuries, 241,328 injuries (4.1%) were work-related. More work-related injuries were in males (87.6% vs. 59.5% of non-work-related) and were unintentional (95.6% vs. 85.1%). The highest proportion of work-related injuries were in the construction industry (29.6%). More work-related admissions required the operating room (19.8% vs. 10.9%). Patients ages 25-44 years and men had higher odds of sustaining work-related injuries compared with other age groups and women. The mechanism of injury with the highest odds of work-relatedness compared to falls (reference) was from machinery (ORadj 9.39, 95% CI 8.63-10.22).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Trauma registry data can contribute to occupational injury research and surveillance. Strengths include a large sample size, industry and occupation coding, and data on severity, demographics, injury mechanisms, and outcomes. NTDB data could be used to study occupational injury trends among U.S-workers.

articles.title: Integrated Bedside Hemodynamic Assessment and Monitoring of Venous Congestion With Venous Excess Ultrasound (VExUS): A Narrative Review.

abstract.text: This review evaluates the venous excess ultrasound (VExUS) score as a bedside tool for quantifying systemic venous congestion and predicting congestive end-organ injury, particularly acute kidney injury (AKI). By assessing flow patterns in the hepatic, portal, and renal veins alongside inferior vena cava (IVC) size, VExUS enables serial monitoring of congestion trajectories. While highly prognostic in heart failure, its predictive performance varies in more heterogeneous populations. Ultimately, integrating VExUS with cardiac output indices may help clinicians identify specific hemodynamic phenotypes, guiding targeted, individualized therapeutic strategies.

articles.title: Weathering the storm: Predictors and resource burden of paroxysmal sympathetic hyperactivity after severe traumatic brain injury.
articles.journal_full: The journal of trauma and acute care surgery

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Reported incidence of paroxysmal sympathetic hyperactivity (PSH) after severe traumatic brain injury (TBI) approaches one-third, largely from cohorts that excluded early deaths. Predictors and resource consequences remain unclear. We identified predictors of PSH development and associations between diagnosis, PSH Assessment Measure (PSH-AM) subscores [clinical features scale (CFS) and diagnosis likelihood tool (DLT)], and resource utilization.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of adults with severe TBI admitted to a tertiary care center intensive care unit (ICU) (October 2020-September 2025), stratified by PSH diagnosis. Two reviewers assigned PSH-AM scores. PSH cannot be diagnosed until the syndrome declares itself over days, so exposure is conditioned on survival; mortality is reported descriptively. Multivariable logistic regression identified predictors of PSH diagnosis. Log-transformed linear regressions estimated associations of PSH diagnosis and subscores with hospital length of stay (LOS), ICU LOS, and ventilator days. Thirty-day composite outcomes, inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW), and landmark analysis evaluated robustness.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 509 patients with severe TBI, 86 (17%) developed PSH. Younger age [odds ratio (OR): 0.97 (95% CI: 0.96-0.98); P<0.001) and higher ISS [1.05 (1.02-1.07); P<0.001] independently predicted PSH. PSH was associated with longer hospital LOS (372.9%), ICU LOS (278.3%), and more ventilator days (266.4%; all P<0.001). Mortality was 11.6% (PSH) versus 35.9% (non-PSH). IPTW demonstrated PSH had fewer days alive and out of hospital (-46.8%; P<0.001) and landmark analysis highlighted fewer ventilator-free days (-40.2%; P=0.0097) and ICU-free days (-46.9%; P<0.001). Higher DLT subscores were associated with longer hospital (36.3%; P=0.001) and ICU (23.3%; P=0.005) stays, whereas the CFS subscore showed no associations.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: The PSH diagnosis is contingent on survival. Younger patients with severe TBI who survive their initial injuries are more likely to develop PSH and occupy hospital beds meaningfully longer. The diagnosis likelihood tool, not the clinical features scale, tracks with that burden.

abstract.label: LEVEL OF EVIDENCE
abstract.text: Level III, prognostic/epidemiological.

articles.title: Patterns of urologic emergency visits and hospital admissions: experience of a tertiary care center.

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: Based on steady increase in the number of visits in German emergency departments, the present study examined patterns of urologic emergency visits and inpatient hospital admissions at a tertiary care center in Germany.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Urologic visits in two selected years (2018 and 2022) to the emergency department were identified. Patient characteristics, time, type and reason for presentation, diagnostic and therapeutic measures were tabulated.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Overall, 2,223 urologic emergency visits were recorded in 2022, and 2,795 in 2018. In 2022 vs. 2018, median age was 54 vs. 50 years, 74 vs. 70% were male, 73 vs. 69% self-referrals, and 16 vs. 19% repeat visits. The majority of visits (55 vs. 60%) took place during on-call time. The most common reasons for presentation were lower-acuity infections (18 vs. 19%), followed by urolithiasis (13 vs. 16%) and displacement or loss of catheters (12 vs. 11%). Inpatient hospital admission rates were 22% in 2022 and 26% in 2018. In 2022 multivariable adjusted subgroup analyses, older age and referral by ambulance services, external hospitals, office-based urologists, and general practitioner were associated with inpatient hospital admission, unlike referral by on-call medical services.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Most urologic visits in the two selected years were self-referrals, occurred outside of regular working hours, and did not require hospital admission. The present findings suggest that expanding office-based urologic emergency consultation hours and providing targeted urologic training for on-call medical staff may represent potential strategies for optimizing emergency care pathways. However, the effectiveness and appropriateness of these measures warrant prospective evaluation.

articles.title: Prevalence of respiratory viruses among pilgrims in Saudi Arabia during the Hajj 2026: a cross-sectional study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Hajj is one of the world's largest annual mass gatherings and provides favorable conditions for respiratory virus transmission because of intense crowding and extensive international travel. Contemporary post-pandemic molecular surveillance data remain limited. This study investigated the prevalence, determinants, and characteristics of respiratory virus detections among pilgrims during the 2026 Hajj season.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A cross-sectional study was conducted among adult domestic and international pilgrims over an extended peri-Hajj period (before, during and after Hajj) in the year 2026. Participants completed a structured questionnaire and provided combined nasopharyngeal and oropharyngeal swab specimens for multiplex real-time RT-PCR detection of common respiratory viruses. A subset of positive samples underwent genomic sequencing for viral subtype and variant characterization. Logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with laboratory-confirmed respiratory viral infection.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 412 enrolled pilgrims across all three phases, 58 (14.1%) tested positive for at least one respiratory virus. The prevalence of viral detection was 6.7% pre-Hajj, 16.0% during Hajj and 21.4% post-Hajj. Influenza A was the predominant virus (34.5%), followed by rhinovirus (24.1%), SARS-CoV-2 (20.7%), respiratory syncytial virus (13.8%), adenovirus (5.2%), and seasonal human coronaviruses (1.7%). Diabetes mellitus, chronic lung disease and smoking were independently associated with increased odds of respiratory virus detection. Conversely, receipt of pre-travel health advice, influenza vaccination and regular facemask use were independently associated with reduced odds of respiratory virus detection.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Respiratory virus transmission remains an important public health concern during Hajj. Strengthening pre-travel health advice, promoting influenza vaccination, and reinforcing personal preventive measures may reduce respiratory viral transmission during Hajj and other international mass gatherings.

articles.title: Trauma Quality Programs Mortality Reporting System Case Reports: Unanticipated Mortality Due to Prolonged Operative Course.
articles.journal_full: The journal of trauma and acute care surgery
authors: American College of Surgeons Trauma Quality Programs Mortality Reporting System Work Group
Madera, California and The American College of Surgeons Trauma Quality Programs Mortality Reporting System Work Group

abstract.text: The American College of Surgeons Trauma Quality Programs Mortality Reporting System is an online anonymous case reporting system designed to share experiences from rare events that may have contributed to unanticipated mortality at contributing trauma centers. This report analyzes cases, summarizes opportunities for truncated operating room time, and offers a defined framework to assess the need for a damage control strategy.

articles.title: POCUS Image Archiving in Emergency Medicine: A Systematic Review of Clinical and Financial Impacts.

abstract.text: Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) has become an essential diagnostic tool in emergency medicine, providing rapid bedside information that supports clinical decision-making. However, the full potential of POCUS may extend beyond image acquisition, with effective documentation and integration into electronic health record (EHR) systems potentially contributing to improved clinical and operational outcomes. This systematic review evaluated the clinical, operational, and financial impacts of POCUS image archiving within EHRs in emergency department settings. Following PRISMA guidelines, a comprehensive search was performed in PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and Web of Science, eligible studies included emergency department-based research reporting original data on POCUS image storage or archiving within EHR systems, whereas studies without specific archiving outcomes were excluded. Two independent reviewers conducted study selection and data extraction, with risk of bias assessed using an adapted NIH quality assessment tool. A total of 225 records were identified, and 11 studies met the inclusion criteria. The included studies demonstrated that structured POCUS image archiving improved documentation completeness, image quality, accessibility to prior examinations, and clinical review processes. Implementation of automated or semi-automated workflows was consistently associated with improved compliance, enhanced organization of ultrasound services, and more efficient resource management. Financial outcomes were also positively affected, with reported increases in billing compliance, reimbursement, and institutional revenue after workflow integration. Despite these benefits, substantial heterogeneity among studies and limitations regarding study design, confounding factors, and generalizability remain. Future research should focus on standardized implementation strategies, cost-effectiveness analyses, and adoption models applicable to diverse health care settings, including low-resource environments.

articles.title: Comparative Diagnostic Accuracy of Blinded Lung Ultrasound and Clinicians in Pulmonary Consolidations: A Prospective Cohort Study.

abstract.text: Bedside lung ultrasound (LUS) is an increasingly utilized technique as an adjunct to clinical history and physical examination. This study aims to assess the added value of LUS by comparing the diagnostic accuracy of a blinded sonographer's ultrasound findings against the clinical suspicion of pulmonologists and emergency physicians at admission. A prospective single-center consecutive study of hospitalized patients (n=101) with imaging-detected consolidations was conducted. Ultrasound was performed by a blinded operator unaware of the physician's diagnostic suspicions. Definitive diagnoses were established through clinical-radiologic follow-up at 12 months, biopsy, and/or microbiological studies. The pulmonologist and emergency physician correctly estimated the probability of benignity/malignancy in 88.1% and 80% of the cases, respectively, whereas the blind operator achieved a 90% accuracy rate. Combining LUS findings with pulmonologists' clinical data improved benign/malignant classification accuracy to 96%. The agreement with the definitive dichotomous diagnosis (benign/malignant), assessed through Cohen kappa, was 0.664 for pulmonologists, 0.129 for emergency physicians, and 0.747 for the ultrasonographer. Ultrasound demonstrated a sensitivity (Se) of 85% and specificity (Spe) of 92% for diagnosing cancer. For pulmonologists, Se was 65% and Spe was 96%, whereas for emergency physicians, Se was 12% and Spe was 97%. The approach to hospitalized patients with imaging-detected consolidations that achieves the highest diagnostic accuracy (96%) combines clinical suspicion with ultrasound findings. Our findings confirm the importance of LUS, particularly in suspected malignancy.

articles.title: Wrong hospital, wrong outcome: Impact of care fragmentation following trauma laparotomy.
articles.journal_full: The journal of trauma and acute care surgery

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Care fragmentation (CF), defined as readmission to a nonindex hospital, has been identified as a potential predictor of poor outcomes after traumatic injury. Trauma laparotomy (TL) is a common procedure with perioperative risk of complications and readmission. Incidence of CF following TL, its risk factors, and its effects on outcomes are unknown. We hypothesized that CF after TL is associated with increased mortality during hospital readmission compared with continuity of care (CC).

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: The Nationwide Readmissions Database (2016-2022) was queried for hospitalized adult (≥18) patients with traumatic injury and open surgery of gastrointestinal or genitourinary systems during index admission, and unplanned readmission within 90 days. Demographics, comorbidities, injury severity, procedures, and disposition data were collected for patients with CF and compared with patients with CC. The primary outcome was in-hospital death during readmission. Univariate comparisons and multivariable logistic regression were performed.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 14,773 TL patients were included in the analysis. From these, 2,059 (13.9%) were readmitted within 90 days. The average age of readmitted patients was 43 years, and the majority (68.6%) were male. Of the readmissions, 441 (21.4%) experienced CF. Discharge home from the index admission was associated with lower odds of CF (OR 0.52, 95% CI: 0.32-0.84, p=0.008). On multivariable regression analysis, CF was significantly associated with in-hospital death during readmission (OR 5.09, 95% CI: 1.22-21.16, p=0.03).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: CF is common following TL and is associated with an increased risk of death on readmission, even after adjustment for baseline comorbidities and other hospital characteristics. Patients who are discharged home are less likely to experience CF. TL survivors may represent a patient population that would benefit from targeted efforts to reduce CF.

abstract.label: LEVEL OF EVIDENCE
abstract.text: Therapeutic; Level III.

articles.title: Estimated plasma volume status (ePVS) as a prognostic marker in polytrauma: predicting 30-day mortality and coagulation support needs.

abstract.text: Estimated plasma volume status (ePVS), derived from a simple formula based on haematocrit and haemoglobin values, has been associated with an unfavourable prognosis in many cardiovascular conditions, demonstrating a correlation with volume overload and the haemodynamic status of the patient. Indeed, ePVS was demonstrated to estimate the degree of congestion and was independently associated with cardiovascular outcomes, rehospitalization, and death in patients with heart failure (HF), confirming its prognostic value also in inflammatory pathologies. Due to its easy and immediate availability even in the emergency department (ED), ePVS may be useful in trauma patients to improve their initial evaluation and management. The aim of this retrospective observational study was to evaluate the role of ePVS at ED admission in predicting mortality and blood products use, red blood cells (RBC) and fresh frozen plasma (FFP), in trauma. We included 790 patients, of whom 67.7% were male; mean age 43.9 years; median Injury Severity Score (ISS) 7.5. The 30-day mortality rate was 2.8% (22/790). The median ePVS was significantly increased in deceased as compared to survivors (5.76; 4.79-8.36 versus 4.41; 3.92-5.05; p < 0.001). Multivariable logistic regression analysis demonstrated that ePVS is an independent risk factor even after adjusting for other variables associated with 30-day mortality (odds radio, OR of 1.23; 95% confidence interval, CI 1.016-1.478, p = 0.034). Prediction of 30-day mortality for ePVS showed an AUROC of 0.776 (95% CI 0.666-0.887). Moreover, ePVS showed a positive correlation with the number of packed RBC and FFP units transfused, both during ED management, within the first 24 h, and over the entire hospital stay. The present findings suggest ePVS as a quick and easy tool to predict 30-day mortality and the need for blood resuscitation in trauma patients. Future studies may validate ePVS as a quick and easy tool for trauma victims' stratification and for predicting resource needs and mortality.

articles.title: Emergency surgery for blunt abdominal trauma in polytrauma - the impact of time to laparotomy on outcomes.
articles.journal_full: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: Blunt abdominal trauma (BAT) is common in polytrauma patients. Emergency surgery is required for haemodynamically significant solid organ injury and intra-abdominal hollow organ injury. The effect of time to surgery on outcomes in patients requiring emergency laparotomy remains uncertain.

abstract.label: MATERIALS & METHODS
abstract.text: Adult polytrauma patients (ISS > 16) who underwent emergency laparotomy for blunt abdominal trauma between 1996 and 2020 from a trauma registry of a single level one trauma centre were included.
