Patients were divided into two groups based on the time elapsed from admission to emergency laparotomy: "Super Early" (≤ 60 min) and "Early" (60-180 min). Length of stay (LOS), intensive care unit (ICU)-LOS, ventilation time, re-look operations and mortality were assessed. Adjusted logistic regression was used to determine the independent predictive parameters, including timing of surgery, for mortality.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The study included 190 polytrauma patients with concomitant blunt abdominal trauma (mean age 42 years (± 17), median ISS of 36 (IQR: 19)). There were 95 patients in each group. Patients in the "Super Early" group had a compromised haemodynamic status and a higher ISS. Liver injury and serous membrane injury were more common in the super early group. The mortality rate was significantly higher in the "Super Early" group (51.6%) compared to the "Early" group (26.3%) (p < 0.001). Death due to haemorrhagic shock was significantly more frequent in the "Super Early" group (36.8%) compared to the "Early" group (13.7%) (p < 0.001). A regression model was adjusted to determine the independent predictors of mortality. Time to emergency laparotomy was not an independent predictor of mortality. However, increased ISS (OR = 1.04, p = 0.049), age (OR = 1.03, p = 0.037) and decreased systolic blood pressure (OR = 0.98, p = 0.025) were found to be significant predictors of mortality.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The timing of surgery showed no independent association with mortality as long as an emergency laparotomy was performed within 3 h of admission. The data suggests that patient-specific characteristics, injury severity and clinical status are more important for survival than the timing of an early emergency laparotomy. Future research should focus on determining the role of delayed laparotomy on outcomes in specific subgroups of patients.

articles.title: High-velocity trauma by social media: a new mechanism of injury in pediatric traumatology?
articles.journal_full: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: Over the past two decades, social media challenges have emerged as a significant cause of injuries among adolescents. This study evaluates a sudden cluster of severe upper limb injuries resulting from the viral "Superman challenge" to raise clinical awareness of digital behaviors in pediatric trauma.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A retrospective study at a tertiary pediatric trauma center evaluated patients aged < 18 years admitted in December 2024 following the "Superman challenge."

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Eight patients were admitted within a 10-day window following high-energy injuries from the challenge. The cohort showed a female predominance (62.5%) with a mean age of 13.25 (±1.03) years. The high-velocity mechanism led to atypical, severe injury patterns distinct from routine accidental falls. We observed an unusual cluster of severe distal forearm fractures in five patients, which uniformly required surgical treatment. Three patients even suffered bilateral distal radius fractures. Additional associated injuries included fractures of the ulnar styloid process (n = 5) and concomitant TFCC tears (n = 2), reflecting the high-energy nature of the challenge.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: The rapid, viral spread of physical social media challenges such as the 'Superman Challenge' can lead to dangerous injury mechanisms involving high-velocity trauma among children and adolescents. These trends could lead to sudden, localized clusters of atypical high-energy injuries-a scenario that, under specific conditions, risks overtaxing conventional healthcare systems, as previously demonstrated in the literature. Medical staff need to be aware of changing digital behaviors, which represent a new mechanism of injury in pediatric trauma.

articles.title: Surgical stabilization of rib fractures in a high-altitude trauma cohort: in-hospital clinical outcomes and resource use in a propensity score-weighted retrospective cohort study.
articles.journal_full: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: Surgical stabilization of rib fractures (SSRF) is increasingly used in the management of traumatic rib fractures, but its in-hospital outcomes in high-altitude trauma settings remain uncertain. We evaluated the association of SSRF with in-hospital pulmonary complications and length of stay in a high-altitude (≈ 3,500 m) trauma system.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study of adults with CT-confirmed traumatic rib fractures admitted from 2015 to 2023 and managed with SSRF or non-operative management. Confounding was addressed using stabilized inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) with augmented outcome models; overlap weighting, propensity score matching, and time-dependent exposure analysis were used as sensitivity analyses. The primary outcome was a composite of in-hospital pneumonia, atelectasis, or respiratory failure. Pulmonary risk ratios (RRs) were estimated using modified Poisson regression, while ICU and hospital length of stay were analyzed using log-transformed weighted models.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 324 patients, 121 underwent SSRF and 203 received non-operative management. Before adjustment, SSRF patients had greater injury severity. In IPTW-augmented analyses, the pulmonary estimate was imprecise (RR 0.86, 95% CI 0.23-3.21; P = 0.822), and no significant difference was detected in ICU length of stay (exp[β] 1.04, 95% CI 0.97-1.10; P = 0.286). Hospital length of stay was longer with SSRF (exp[β] 2.31, 95% CI 2.02-2.65; P < 0.001).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Adjusted analyses found no statistically detectable difference in pulmonary complications or ICU length of stay, although the pulmonary estimate remained imprecise and does not establish equivalence or safety. SSRF was associated with longer hospital length of stay.

abstract.label: TRIAL REGISTRATION
abstract.text: Not applicable.

articles.title: Trauma, time, and transformation: A comparative study of immediate and 1-year psychological outcomes in military body handlers.
articles.journal_full: Psychological trauma : theory, research, practice and policy

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Personnel assigned to recover and identify human remains following mass violence are exposed to intense occupational trauma, yet longitudinal data on their psychological adaptation remain limited. This study compared an immediate cohort of military reservists' body handlers with a similar cohort 1-year postmission. The two groups served as body handlers following the Hamas's October 7, 2023, mass-casualty attack in southern Israel.

abstract.label: METHOD
abstract.text: Eighty-four reservists were assessed approximately 1 year after mission completion (Cohort 2) and compared with an independent cohort assessed immediately postmission (N = 161; Cohort 1). Measures included posttraumatic stress symptoms (via Posttraumatic Stress Disorder Checklist for Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, Fifth Edition), posttraumatic growth (PTG via Posttraumatic Growth Inventory), and resilience (10-item Connor-Davidson Resilience Scale). The prevalence of probable posttraumatic stress disorder was calculated using a validated cutoff.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: One year postmission, 33.3% of participants met the criteria for probable posttraumatic stress disorder, significantly higher than the 20.5% observed immediately after mission completion. Resilience was associated with lower posttraumatic stress symptoms and higher PTG in Cohort 2 but only with PTG in Cohort 1. Posttraumatic stress symptoms showed a significant curvilinear relationship with PTG among Cohort 2, which differed from the small positive linear association found among Cohort 1.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Compared with the immediate postmission cohort, the 1-year postmission cohort demonstrated a higher prevalence of probable posttraumatic stress disorder. The evolving association between distress and growth suggests that early reports of growth do not necessarily indicate long-term adaptation or even genuine growth. Resilience is associated with better long-term adaptation, not immediate adaptation after a mission. (PsycInfo Database Record (c) 2026 APA, all rights reserved).

articles.title: Cost‑effectiveness analysis of the mRNA‑1345 RSV vaccine for older adults in Italy.

abstract.label: AIMS
abstract.text: To evaluate the potential public health impact and cost-effectiveness of vaccination using mRNA-1345 administered as a single dose compared with no vaccination in Italian high-risk adults aged 60-74 years and all adults aged ≥75 years.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A static decision-analytic model was developed to project clinical and economic outcomes over a five-year time horizon, assuming 50% vaccination coverage among eligible adults. Economic outcomes were evaluated from the Italian National Health Service (Servizio Sanitario Nazionale, SSN) perspective. Model inputs were informed by the most recent Italian epidemiological, clinical, and economic evidence, supplemented by published international data when necessary. Deterministic, probabilistic, and scenario analyses were conducted to assess the impact of uncertainty in model inputs and assumptions on the study results.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Vaccination with mRNA-1345 in high-risk adults aged 60-74 years and all adults aged ≥75 years was projected to avert over 19,800 hospitalizations, 4,000 emergency department visits, 381,000 outpatient visits, 6,000 RSV-attributable deaths, and 212,000 antibiotic prescriptions compared with no vaccination over a five-year period. The total incremental cost of €1,143 million and the additional 47,477 QALYs gained resulted in an ICER of €24,078 per QALY gained, which was below the commonly referenced willingness-to-pay range of €33,000-40,000/QALY. Sensitivity analyses confirmed robustness of the analysis results.

abstract.label: LIMITATIONS
abstract.text: Due to limited epidemiological evidence for Italy, selected epidemiological inputs were informed by studies conducted in other high-income countries. In addition, vaccine efficacy beyond the two-year clinical trial follow-up was projected to five years using nonlinear waning curves fitted to the observed trial data.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Vaccination with mRNA-1345 is a cost-effective strategy for the prevention of RSV in high-risk adults aged 60-74 years and all adults ≥75 years in Italy, in comparison to no vaccination, and has the potential to provide substantial public health benefits.

articles.title: A Drone-Integrated Artificial Intelligence-Based System for Mass-Casualty Triage and Remote Monitoring.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Triage and data transfer are critical to the medical management of mass-casualty incidents (MCIs). However, the chaotic nature of such events makes it difficult to classify casualties according to structured triage protocols. Furthermore, even when triage is implemented effectively, communication disruptions between the incident scene and dispatch centers can hinder response operations. The aim of this study was to present a drone-integrated system that enables non-contact vital sign measurement, remote triage, and real-time data transmission during MCIs.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: The system development process involved three steps: (1) developing the Vital-Sign Measurement Module; (2) developing the Triage Decision Support Module; and (3) developing the User Interfaces and Data Transmission Module to enable information transmission between dispatch centers and response teams. Within the Vital-Sign Measurement Module, heart rate (HR), respiratory rate (RR), oxygen saturation (SpO2), and body temperature (BT) measurement algorithms were developed using the following techniques, respectively: video-based photoplethysmography (vPPG), analysis of thermal temperature fluctuations around the nose, a regression-based neural network approach, and heat maps and thermal thresholding. A pilot study was conducted under controlled indoor conditions to evaluate the accuracy of these algorithms.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The system can measure vital signs by processing drone-captured images, can provide triage decision support, and can transmit victims' locations, vital signs, and triage categories to response teams and dispatch centers via dedicated user interfaces. A pilot evaluation of the Vital-Sign Measurement Module showed that the relative accuracy rate of the non-contact vital-sign measurement algorithms ranged from 86% to 99%.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: The system provides an innovative approach to improving medical response management in MCIs by enabling remote triage and monitoring. Its non-contact vital sign measurement, triage decision support, and near real-time data transmission capabilities provide an infrastructure that can contribute to faster response and improved operational coordination. However, further field trials and development are required to improve the robustness of the vital-sign measurement algorithms to motion, to improve their adaptability to changing environmental conditions, and to maintain high accuracy despite individual differences.

articles.title: Palpitations in children and adolescents in the emergency department: a state-of-the-art narrative review of arrhythmia risk, diagnostic strategy, and disposition.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Palpitations are not an uncommon complaint in the paediatric emergency department, causing significant anxiety for families concerned about serious heart disease. However, most cases are benign, often stemming from normal physiological responses like fever or anxiety. Primary cardiac arrhythmias are rare in this clinical setting.

abstract.label: PROBLEM
abstract.text: The main challenge is identifying the few children with dangerous arrhythmias among the many benign cases. Fear of missing a life-threatening condition often leads to extensive, costly, and stressful investigations, even in low-risk patients, without significantly improving detection rates.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: This review aims to create a structured, risk-based framework for evaluating paediatric palpitations in the emergency department. The goal is to help clinicians efficiently distinguish benign from potentially life-threatening causes, thereby optimising resource use and reducing family anxiety.

abstract.label: FINDINGS
abstract.text: A thorough clinical history, physical exam, and a standard 12-lead electrocardiogram are the most effective evaluation tools. "Red-flag" features-such as palpitations with fainting (syncope), onset during exercise, or a family history of sudden cardiac death-successfully identify nearly all children with significant arrhythmias. Barring certain risk factors and any abnormalities on a 12 lead electrocardiogram, a dangerous cardiac condition is highly unlikely.

abstract.label: RECOMMENDATIONS
abstract.text: A stratified approach is recommended. Low-risk children (no red-flag features, normal electrocardiogram) can be safely discharged with reassurance. High-risk patients require immediate, aggressive evaluation, including cardiology consultation and potential hospital admission. This strategy improves accuracy, is cost-effective, and enhances patient safety.

articles.title: Acute behavioural disturbance in the context of substance use: case series analysis of coroner reports.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Acute behavioural disturbance (ABD) is a contested term describing severe agitation and behavioural dysregulation, often preceding sudden death. Concerns regarding diagnostic clarity, racial bias and law enforcement restraint have been raised, and its clinical and forensic utility have been questioned.

abstract.label: AIMS
abstract.text: To characterise fatal ABD cases following substance use to inform clinical management, forensic interpretation and policy.

abstract.label: METHOD
abstract.text: Fifty-one deaths consistent with ABD were identified from the National Programme on Substance Use Mortality (NPSUM) using textual screening and Royal College of Emergency Medicine and Faculty of Forensic & Legal Medicine criteria.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: All cases met Royal College of Emergency Medicine criteria and most met Faculty of Forensic & Legal Medicine (84.3%) criteria. Agitation was the most frequently observed sign (86.3% of cases). Stimulants, particularly cocaine and amphetamines, were also detected in 86.3% of cases, but not necessarily in the same cases, and the rate of stimulant detection was almost three times higher than that in in the broader NPSUM cohort (32.1%). Cocaine concentrations were higher in ABD cases than in all NPSUM cocaine-related deaths (0.848 mg/L v. 0.105 mg/L). Compared with the NPSUM cohort, ABD decedents were significantly younger (30.2 ± 7.5 v. 40.5 ± 13.4) and more likely to be male (92.2 v. 73.4%), from racially minoritised backgrounds (21.7 v. 3.9%) and living in deprived areas (87.0 v. 75.9%).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Variability in diagnostic criteria highlights a need for clearer ABD definitions. Toxicology testing may assist in refining the ABD construct, but its results must be interpreted within broader clinical and social contexts. These findings support avoiding use of ABD as a stand-alone cause of death but retaining it as a clinical descriptor prompting urgent treatment, monitoring and reduced reliance on prolonged restraint.

articles.title: Latent Safety Threats During Simulated Internal Mass Casualty Incidents: A Multicenter Simulation-Based Systems Testing Study.
articles.journal_full: Disaster medicine and public health preparedness

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Internal mass casualty incidents (MCIs) challenge hospital systems by requiring rapid coordination across clinical, operational, and communication domains. Simulation-based clinical systems testing (SbCST) can identify latent safety threats (LSTs), but cross-institutional patterns in internal MCI preparedness remain poorly characterized.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a multicenter simulation-based systems assessment using in situ SbCST and Failure Modes and Effects Analysis (FMEA) during simulated internal MCIs. LSTs were identified through triangulation of structured field observations, facilitator observations, and participant self-report during debriefing. Observations were consolidated through structured review, categorized into system-level domains using the HFMEA (Healthcare Failure Mode and Effect Analysis) framework by multidisciplinary consensus, and prioritized using FMEA with expert scoring followed by consensus reconciliation.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Approximately 75-80 raw observations yielded 53 unique LSTs across 2 hospitals. Recurrent vulnerabilities involved leadership, patient flow, communication, triage, and system interfaces. A substantial proportion were classified as high or very high priority, with comparable median FMEA scores across sites (Site 1: 30 [IQR 24-36]; Site 2: 32 [IQR 24-48]). Mitigation strategies were proposed for approximately 60-65% of LSTs.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Multicenter SbCST identified recurrent, high-priority system-level vulnerabilities across 2 hospitals. Prospective tracking of mitigation implementation and re-simulation are needed to determine whether identified threats are reduced over time.

articles.title: Human Factors-Driven Optimization of Pediatric Resuscitation Workflow Using Integrated Color-Coded Systems: A Randomized Crossover Study.

abstract.label: AIM
abstract.text: This study evaluated whether a human factors-driven, integrated, color-coded resuscitation system that combines equipment standardization and prefilled-medication cognitive aids improves workflow efficiency and accuracy compared with a conventional crash cart during simulated pediatric resuscitations.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A prospective, randomized, crossover simulation study was conducted with 28 health care professionals. Each team participated in 2 pediatric resuscitation scenarios using either the SCC or the CCCC in random order. All sessions were video-recorded to measure equipment retrieval and medication preparation times. Statistical comparisons were made using paired statistical tests appropriate for crossover designs, with significance set at P<0.05.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Use of the CCCC significantly reduced the time to locate airway devices (13.1±6.9 vs. 41.7±22 s, P<0.001) and airway adjuncts (13.8±11.9 vs. 30.8±17.4 s, P=0.03). Prefilled color-coded syringes significantly reduced medication preparation time (median: 16 vs. 19 s; absolute reduction 3 s, P=0.04), with no dosing errors observed. Teams using the CCCC demonstrated more consistent workflow and fewer procedural delays.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In this randomized crossover simulation study, the integrated color-coded system reduced equipment retrieval and medication preparation times for selected pediatric resuscitation tasks. These findings are limited to the simulation setting and should be interpreted in light of the Broselow framework's use for both cart organization and assessment of correct equipment selection. Further research is needed to evaluate the feasibility of color-coded prefilled syringes and determine whether the observed workflow benefits translate to real-world pediatric patient care.

articles.title: Association Between Childhood Opportunity Index and Pediatric Emergency Department Utilization of Youth With Experiences of Trafficking: A National Multicenter Retrospective Cohort Study.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To understand associations between the Child Opportunity Index (COI), a neighborhood-based measure of resources that influence child health and development, and pediatric ED utilization among youth with experiences of trafficking in the United States, as well as to describe their range of COI, sociodemographic characteristics, and pediatric ED utilization.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This was a retrospective, observational, cohort study. We identified (by ICD-10 code) youth with experiences of trafficking who presented to pediatric EDs across 50 US children's hospitals between January 2018 and February 2023 within the Pediatric Health Information System database. Descriptive analyses and multivariate regression were performed.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: We identified 908 youth with experiences of trafficking who presented to pediatric EDs. Among them, 55% (n=499) were from neighborhoods with Very Low and Low COI, while 45% (n=409) were from neighborhoods with Moderate to Very High COI. Mental health diagnoses were common (n=584, 65.3%), and mental health, child abuse, and physical trauma were the top diagnosis categories for ED visits. Low-resource intensity visits were uncommon (12.8%). One-third of patients had an ED visit in the year prior. We did not find major statistically significant associations between COI and hospital utilization.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In this cohort of youth with experiences of trafficking, all levels of COI and a wide range of visit acuity levels were represented. Further study is needed to better understand the prevalence and health needs of youth with experiences of trafficking who receive ED care, to develop effective screening and intervention programs to support these youth.

articles.title: Continuous Pulse Oximetry Analysis to Predict Outcomes in Young Infants With Bronchiolitis Presenting to the Emergency Department.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Predictive analytics using continuously measured vital signs from bedside monitors has improved outcomes in critically ill children. We investigated whether continuous pulse oximetry data collected during emergency department (ED) evaluation can identify infants ≤90 days old with bronchiolitis at low risk of respiratory deterioration.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study of infants ≤90 days old with bronchiolitis who presented to a tertiary-care pediatric ED from November 2021 to November 2025. Infants were identified using the ICD-10 code with manual eligibility confirmation. Heart rate and oxygen saturation features were generated from continuous pulse oximetry during the first 2 hours of ED evaluation. The primary outcome was respiratory deterioration within 24 hours of ED arrival, defined as initiation of high-flow nasal cannula, continuous/bilevel positive airway pressure, or invasive mechanical ventilation. Data were split into derivation and validation cohorts (70/30, stratified by outcome). An L2-regularized logistic regression model estimated the probability of respiratory deterioration, with a classification threshold selected to prioritize sensitivity.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 290 infants meeting clinical eligibility, 117 had sufficient continuous pulse oximetry data; 57 (49%) had respiratory deterioration. The primary model included 3 features: the median and interquartile range (IQR) of heart rate, and oxygen saturation IQR. In the validation cohort, the model showed moderate sensitivity (0.78, 95% CI: 0.58-0.95) and fair discrimination (AUROC=0.78, 95% CI: 0.62-0.93).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: We derived and validated a model using data from continuous pulse oximetry to identify low-risk infants with bronchiolitis. With further refinement and integration into monitor design systems, this approach may enhance clinical utility of continuous pulse oximetry.

articles.title: Diagnostic Challenges in Pediatric Infectious Encephalitis: Applicability of the International Encephalitis Consortium Criteria and Prognostic Factors in a Multicenter Study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: The International Encephalitis Consortium (IEC) criteria are widely used to diagnose pediatric encephalitis, although their performance has not been evaluated.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To evaluate IEC criteria in children with suspected encephalitis and identify prognostic factors associated with adverse outcomes.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Secondary analysis of a retrospective multicenter study including children aged <18 years undergoing cerebrospinal fluid polymerase chain reaction testing for suspected encephalitis in 10 Spanish Pediatric Emergency Departments between 2017 and 2023. Patients were classified according to the IEC criteria. Children fulfilling the major criterion and 1 minor criterion plus pathogen confirmation were classified as subthreshold encephalitis. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify prognostic factors for adverse outcomes.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 446 children, 118 met IEC criteria (60 confirmed, 15 probable, 43 possible encephalitis). Twenty additional cases were classified as subthreshold encephalitis. Rates of adverse outcomes were similar in both groups (31.4% vs. 30.0%). Independent predictors of adverse outcomes were abnormal neuroimaging (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 3.2; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.6-6.4; P < 0.001), focal neurologic deficits (aOR, 2.6; 95% CI, 1.3-5.2; P = 0.01), bacterial etiology (aOR, 2.7; 95% CI, 1.05-6.8; P = 0.03), seizures (aOR, 2.1; 95% CI, 1.0-4.5; P = 0.04) and microbiologic confirmation (aOR, 1.9; 95% CI, 1.0-3.6; P = 0.048).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Children with altered mental status and an encephalitis-associated pathogen but only 1 minor IEC criterion may represent missed encephalitis cases. Microbiologic confirmation, particularly bacterial etiology, and 3 minor IEC criteria were independently associated with worse outcomes, with abnormal neuroimaging being the strongest predictor.

articles.title: Craniovertebral junction injuries in children: a single center retrospective review.
articles.journal_full: Child's nervous system : ChNS : official journal of the International Society for Pediatric Neurosurgery

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: The craniovertebral junction is a unique structure consisting of the occipito-atlantal and atlanto-axial joints and their associated ligaments. The aim of the present study was to characterize the presentation, underlying mechanism of trauma, clinical and radiological findings, management, and outcome of children with craniovertebral junction injury treated in our institution.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We undertook a retrospective review of all patients with craniovertebral junction injuries treated at our institution between January 2016 and June 2024. Craniovertebral junction injury was defined as presence of one or more of (i) bony fracture or dislocation of the occipital condyles and/or any part of the atlas or axis, (ii) atlanto-axial dislocation/subluxation identified as per standard radiological criteria as described in literature, (iii) ligamentous injury identified on MRI or instability identified on dynamic imaging, and (iv) spinal extra-axial and spinal parenchymal hemorrhage at the level of craniovertebral junction. Patients who had non-traumatic anomalies of the craniovertebral junction and who had incomplete records were excluded from the study.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: From 732 patients who underwent imaging evaluation at the emergency department for traumatic cervical spine injury, we identified 33 patients who met our inclusion criteria for craniovertebral junction injury. Motor vehicle accidents were the most common cause of injury, with the majority of patients suffering from ligamentous injury. Fractures of the occipital condyle were the most common bony injury of the craniovertebral junction. Most of the patients had good neurological outcomes, with mortality reported in 2/33. Multiple correspondence analysis identified a high-severity phenotype characterized by CVJ injury together with neurological and systemic compromise. An exploratory eight-item CVJ Injury Score was derived to characterize this phenotype.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Craniovertebral junction injury in children is relatively rare, occurring in 4.5% of patients undergoing imaging evaluation for cervical spine injury in our series. It encompasses a broad clinical spectrum, ranging from injuries successfully managed non-operatively to severe injuries associated with neurological, vascular, and systemic physiological compromise. The proposed CVJ Injury Score represents an exploratory framework for characterizing this high-severity phenotype and requires external multicenter validation.

articles.title: Harnessing the potential of response surface methodology-based optimized scaffolds in volumetric muscle loss repair in sprague dawley rat.

abstract.text: Volumetric Muscle Loss (VML) is a complex tissue injury characterised by loss of tissue beyond the body's intrinsic regenerative capacity, resulting in impaired muscle regeneration and functional recovery. Limited cellular proliferation and poor in situ healing make VML one of the most challenging issues in tissue engineering. Conventional approaches of acidic gelling and use of artificial substrates compromise the structural integrity, biocompatibility and functional performance of tissue-engineered constructs. Moreover, the irregular geometries of muscle defects make surgical reconstruction technically challenging and often insufficient to achieve complete functional restoration. In this study, a novel porous scaffold containing collagen, fibronectin, and raloxifene (a cell-proliferative drug) was prepared for VML repair. The concentration of scaffold components was optimized using Response Surface Methodology (RSM) to obtain an effective scaffold composition. The regenerative efficacy of the optimized scaffold was evaluated in a Sprague-Dawley rat model of VML. The results suggested that RSM-optimized scaffold significantly improved VML repair after 21 days (p < 0.05) in vivo. A prominent development of muscle fibre and deposition of collagen was observed. At molecular level, a significant increase in the expression of MyoD and STAT3 genes was observed in optimized scaffold group, suggesting enhanced myogenesis and tissue repair. The findings indicate that RSM may be utilized to optimize the tissue-engineered construct to improve VML repair.

articles.title: Acellular fish-skin grafting complex soft tissue defects in orthopedic trauma: Technique and outcomes of a consecutive case series.

abstract.text: This article describes a surgical technique for applying an acellular fish-skin graft (Kerecis Omega3 Wound; Kerecis, Ísafjörður, Iceland) in orthopedic trauma and reports outcomes from a consecutive series of patients treated at an urban Level I trauma center. After institutional review board approval, we reviewed 27 adult patients with complex extremity wounds who were treated with acellular fish-skin grafting between January 1st, 2023, and December 30th, 2025. Wound etiologies included traumatic soft tissue injuries, postoperative wound dehiscence, necrotizing soft tissue infections, and chronic osteomyelitis with associated soft tissue compromise. Acellular fish-skin grafting was indicated in this series of patients for full-thickness skin loss (or deeper), including those with exposed tendons, bone, or ligaments, in whom flap reconstruction was contraindicated. Patients underwent serial irrigation and debridement followed by application of an acellular fish-skin graft. The primary outcome was complete wound healing without flap-based soft-tissue reconstruction. Secondary outcomes included the number of graft applications, duration of negative-pressure wound therapy (NPWT), time to split-thickness skin grafting (STSG), and all complications. Acellular fish-skin grafting facilitated wound healing in most patients, including those with infection, exposed bone, tendon, and/or ligaments, and substantial medical and social comorbidities. Twenty-two patients (84%) achieved definitive wound coverage without flap reconstruction. Five patients (19%) were referred to plastic surgery after grafting. Two ultimately achieved limb salvage with local wound care alone, whereas the remaining three required amputation. None of the referred patients were salvaged with flap reconstruction. One patient died on postoperative day two from unrelated medical causes, and one was lost to follow-up. Consequently, acellular fish-skin grafting may be a useful adjunct in managing complex orthopedic trauma wounds, particularly in high-risk patients or in settings with limited access to reconstructive surgery. Prospective comparative studies are needed to better define indications, effectiveness, and cost-effectiveness.

articles.title: Comparative study of autologous bone graft and bone morphogenetic protein-2 for bone regeneration using a novel rabbit Masquelet technique model.

abstract.text: The Masquelet technique is widely used for reconstructing critical-sized bone defects; however, autologous bone grafting (ABG) is associated with donor-site morbidity such as pain and bleeding. Bone morphogenetic protein-2 (BMP-2) has attracted attention as a potential alternative strategy for promoting bone regeneration. Studies on direct comparisons between BMP-2 and autologous bone grafting within the context of the Masquelet technique are limited. The purpose of this study was to establish a novel rabbit femoral Masquelet model and compare the bone regenerative capacity of ABG with β-tricalcium phosphate (β-TCP) loaded with BMP-2. A 20-mm segmental defect was created in the femur of 24-week-old New Zealand White rabbits and stabilized with a locking plate. The defect was filled with polymethyl methacrylate cement, which was removed four weeks later to induce membrane formation. The defect was subsequently filled with autologous iliac bone (ABG group) or β-TCP granules containing BMP-2 (BMP-2 group). Bone regeneration was evaluated 12 weeks after the second surgery using radiographic, histological, micro-computed tomography (μCT), and biomechanical analyses. Radiographic evaluation demonstrated satisfactory bone union in both groups, without substantial difference in union rate. Histological analysis showed cortical continuity and new bone formation in both groups. μ-CT revealed that the bone volume/tissue volume ratio of total calcified callus was significantly higher in the ABG group, whereas the tissue mineral density was significantly higher in the BMP-2 group. Biomechanical testing showed no significant differences in ultimate stress, extrinsic stiffness, or failure energy between the two groups. In this rabbit femoral Masquelet model, BMP-2 delivered with β-TCP achieved bone regeneration comparable to that of autologous bone grafting. These findings suggest that BMP-2 may represent a promising option for bone reconstruction using the Masquelet technique.

articles.title: Oxidative stress in osteoarthritis: From mitochondrial homeostasis to targeted delivery systems.

abstract.text: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a chronic joint disease characterized by cartilage degradation, in which oxidative stress and mitochondrial dysfunction play a pivotal role. Excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) production, driven by inflammation, metabolic reprogramming, and systemic risk factors, leads to mitochondrial damage, impaired mitophagy, and disrupted mitochondrial dynamics, forming a vicious cycle that accelerates OA progression. Although traditional antioxidant molecules show therapeutic potential, their rapid clearance from the joint cavity limits clinical efficacy. Recent advances in tissue engineering and smart delivery systems-such as ROS-responsive hydrogels, microspheres/nanocarriers, and exosome-based platforms-enable targeted, sustained, and on-demand drug release, offering new opportunities to restore redox balance and break the pathological amplification loop. This review systematically summarizes the molecular mechanisms linking oxidative stress to mitochondrial homeostasis in OA and highlights the design principles and application status of emerging delivery strategies, aiming to provide a theoretical foundation for next-generation precision therapies.

articles.title: Pembrolizumab-Associated Adrenal Insufficiency Presenting as Adrenal Crisis: A Case Report.

abstract.text: Immunotherapy regimens containing the programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) inhibitor pembrolizumab are widely utilised in the management of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, the administration of pembrolizumab is associated with unique immune-related adverse events. Adrenal insufficiency is a rare, potentially life-threatening endocrinopathy that can manifest even after the cessation of planned treatment. A male in his 50s with metastatic pulmonary adenocarcinoma developed an acute adrenal crisis 12 days after completing a 24-month course of pembrolizumab immunotherapy. Routine outpatient blood tests first identified critical hypocortisolaemia (morning serum cortisol <50 nmol/L), prompting the patient to attend hospital. The patient subsequently developed severe hypotension (58/45 mmHg) and reported malaise, anorexia, and vomiting after oral intake. Septic shock was considered but felt to be less likely given the absence of infective symptoms. The patient was successfully resuscitated in the emergency department with administration of fluids and high-dose intravenous hydrocortisone. Following clinical stabilisation, under the supervision of the endocrinology team, he was transitioned to a long-term oral maintenance regimen consisting of hydrocortisone and fludrocortisone. This case illustrates that pembrolizumab-associated adrenal insufficiency can present as an abrupt, life-threatening crisis in the immediate post-treatment phase. Frontline clinicians must remain vigilant for late-onset endocrinopathies, regardless of the treatment completion date. Proactive patient education and long-term biochemical surveillance are imperative to ensuring early clinical intervention and avoiding catastrophic management delays and poor clinical outcomes.

articles.title: Relative Brain Perfusion Differences in a Patient With Persistent Fatigue and Subjective Cognitive Symptoms: A Case Report.

abstract.text: Persistent fatigue may be accompanied by subjective cognitive symptoms when the available evaluation does not identify a single explanatory disorder. We report the case of a 57-year-old woman with persistent fatigue, reduced mental clarity, and subjective memory difficulties without a loss of independence in daily functioning. Cognitive, mood, attention, and laboratory assessments were performed, although important diagnostic domains remained unassessed or incompletely characterized. Brain perfusion single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT) was subsequently obtained as an adjunctive functional imaging study. Brain perfusion SPECT depicts relative regional tracer distribution rather than providing an absolute measurement of cerebral blood flow, and the study demonstrated a nonspecific mixed pattern of relative cortical and subcortical tracer distribution. An individualized management plan was subsequently implemented that included a nonstandardized oxygen-enriched hyperbaric intervention using concentrator-supplied chamber air rather than conventional hyperbaric oxygen therapy (HBOT). At approximately 60 days of follow-up, the patient reported improvement in fatigue and exercise tolerance, including the resumption of hiking. However, the improvement was based on patient self-report, standardized pre- and post-treatment outcome measures were not obtained, and additional interventions were recommended concurrently; therefore, the independent contribution of the hyperbaric intervention cannot be determined. This case illustrates the potential descriptive value of adjunctive functional imaging and longitudinal clinical observation in a complex presentation of persistent fatigue and subjective cognitive symptoms while emphasizing that imaging findings and short-term clinical changes should be interpreted within the broader clinical context.

articles.title: Arthroscopic Circumferential Labral Repair and Biceps Tenodesis in Elite Throwing Athletes: Technical Considerations.

abstract.text: SLAP lesions are a common cause of shoulder pain in overhead athletes and are often seen together with circumferential labral tearing, partial-thickness rotator cuff tearing, and biceps pathology. Isolated repair of the superior labrum has produced inconsistent outcomes, with low return-to-play rates in professional throwers. In patients with these complex cases, instability and anterior shoulder pain often coexist, and isolated labral repair or tenodesis may not be adequate treatment. Conversely, tenodesis without superior labral repair may increase glenohumeral translation. The senior author believes long head of the biceps tendon release reduces traction on the SLAP repair and may support healing. We describe an arthroscopic technique for circumferential labral repair, with knotless all-suture anchors performed in the beach-chair position, combined with open subpectoral biceps tenodesis and adjunct subacromial decompression. This technique restores stability, removes the biceps as a pain generator, eliminates traction on the repaired labrum, and preserves motion.

articles.title: Night-Time Presentation as an Independent Predictor of Unnecessary Appendectomy in Children: A Prospective Cohort Study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Unnecessary appendectomy (UA) remains an important quality indicator in pediatric emergency surgery, reflecting persistent diagnostic uncertainty despite advances in clinical assessment and imaging. The aim of this study was to identify predictors of UA in children.

abstract.label: METHOD
abstract.text: This investigation was designed as a prospective cohort study involving consecutive pediatric patients who underwent appendectomy for suspected acute appendicitis during January 2022 through December 2025. Unnecessary appendectomy was defined as the removal of a macroscopically and histologically normal appendix.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 653 children were included, of whom 53 (8.1%) underwent UA. The median age was 9.5 years, and males represented 66.8% of the cohort. Univariate analysis identified several factors potentially associated with UA. After adjustment for confounding variables, four factors remained independently associated with UA. These independent predictors included night-time admission (OR 3.51; 95% CI 1.83-6.71; p < 0.001), a NLR below 5 (OR 3.12; 95% CI 1.60-6.12; p = 0.001), a CRP level below 10 mg/L (OR 2.13; 95% CI 1.12-4.06; p = 0.021), and a negative US result (OR 5.67; 95% CI 2.98-10.76; p < 0.001).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Unnecessary appendectomy in children is influenced not only by clinical and biological variables but also by contextual factors related to the timing of presentation. Recognition of night-time admission as a high-risk context may support more cautious decision-making strategies and help reduce avoidable surgical interventions in pediatric emergency care.

articles.title: Critical constraints to ecological buffering in a rapidly changing Arctic: A long-term seabird study.

abstract.text: Long-term ecological studies testing global change impacts are rare yet essential in the Arctic, a region warming nearly four times faster than the global average. These rapid environmental changes reshape ecosystem functioning across the pan-Arctic and affect the livelihoods of local communities. Seabirds are widely recognised indicators of environmental change. Identifying species-specific critical constraints is therefore essential for detecting early warning signals of population decline and ecosystem reorganisation. Little auks (Alle alle), the most abundant Arctic seabirds, are key ecosystem engineers shaping coastal environments through for example food-web interactions and guano deposition. We present a 20-year study (2005-2024) of an East Greenland little auk population, combining long-term demographic monitoring with behavioural, physiological and ecotoxicological data. We quantified fitness-related traits (adult body condition, overwinter survival and chick growth) alongside potential constraints, including parental foraging effort, trophic ecology, winter distribution, and mercury contamination in adults, eggs and chicks. Over the study period, climate-driven ocean warming, sea-ice decline, altered zooplankton communities, and increasing mercury exposure reshaped environmental conditions. Faced with these changes, little auks exhibited marked behavioural and dietary plasticity, allowing them to maintain relatively stable fitness metrics in most years. However, sustained monitoring revealed key constraints that undermine this apparent resilience: (a) Elevated mercury burdens may reduce aerobic diving capacity and thermal tolerance in adults and were associated with reduced reproductive performance. (b) Chick growth was strongly impaired during years with increased summer storm activity, which disrupted adult foraging trips and provisioning rates. Winter storms are also likely to negatively affect adult overwinter survival. Together, these findings show that little auks can partially buffer rapid Arctic change through behavioural flexibility, but multiple interacting climatic and contaminant stressors impose increasing, possibly cumulative constraints on performance. Identifying such critical constraints is crucial for understanding the limits of resilience in wild populations and for improving predictions of ecosystem responses to ongoing climate change.

articles.title: Practice changing articles: restrictive or liberal transfusion strategy in myocardial infarction and anemia.
articles.journal_full: The American journal of emergency medicine

articles.title: Implementation of regional interfacility transfer guidelines for patients with isolated facial trauma: A preliminary report.
articles.journal_full: The American journal of emergency medicine

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Secondary overtriage (SO) of isolated craniomaxillofacial (CMF) fractures overwhelm trauma centers and represent a significant resource burden while ultimately delaying patient care. The objective of this study was to implement an interfacility transfer protocol at a tertiary level 1 trauma center and review the preliminary utilization findings.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A tertiary academic medical center adopted the protocol via the AgileMD pathway in regional referral centers. The protocol indicates the necessity of on-call specialist consultation based on a patient's clinical presentation. This study conducted a retrospective cohort analysis for patients with isolated CMF trauma and AgileMD pathway activation over a one year period. The main outcome was transfer center activation.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The pathway was utilized 55 times for isolated CMF trauma patients in one year. The majority of traumas involved nasal bone fractures (52.7%) and were most often caused by falls (49.1%). On-call specialist consultation occurred 18.2% of the time - down from 100% of cases prior to guideline institution. The majority of patients (78.2%) were discharged with 40.9% follow-up, while 16.4% were transferred. These dispositions followed the guidelines 90.9% of the time.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: This is the first pilot study on the implementation of isolated CMF trauma interfacility transfer guidelines. The 81.8% reduction in on-call specialist consultation suggests a meaningful call burden reduction for surgical providers, while a discharge rate of 78.2% and outpatient follow-up rate consistent with pre-implementation levels reflects significant preservation of trauma resources. Broader adoption of similar protocols can further reduce SO, hospital costs, and wait times.

articles.title: Navigating emergency medicaid and securing long-term medicaid coverage- patient education series: understanding trauma and emergency surgery conditions.
Post-intensive care syndrome (PICS), an AAST Critical Care Committee Consensus Guideline: expectations, mental health impairments, financial hardship, and caregiver burden in PICS.
Sex dimorphic outcomes after whole blood resuscitation in trauma patients: a national database study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Injured females experience improved outcomes after component therapy resuscitation. We hypothesize that females <52 transfused with whole blood (WB) have improved survival, lower blood utilization, and lower complication rates compared with males and females ≥52.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective analysis assessed Trauma Quality Improvement Program Participant Use File patients aged 18-90 transfused WB 1/1/2020-12/31/2022. Patients who were pregnant, transferred, anticoagulated, died <1 hour, had a blood dyscrasia, or severe head injury were excluded. Outcomes were compared between: female and male patients <52, female and male patients ≥52, and females <52 and ≥52, separated by injury mechanism. Univariate and multivariate analyses were applied, with the latter controlled for injury factors, race, medical history, time to hemorrhage control procedure, and complications.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: 15 051 patients met inclusion. Male sex was associated with greater need for massive transfusion, higher blood product utilization, and acute kidney injury than females, regardless of mechanism (p<0.05, all comparisons). Among those injured by blunt mechanism, females received fewer of all individual blood component transfusions than males at all ages (all p<0.01). Females <52 with blunt mechanisms had equivalent mortality compared with males, whereas females ≥52 had decreased mortality (20.1% vs 24.2%, p=0.01). Compared with females ≥52, younger females had lower mortality (14% vs 20.1%, p<0.01) after blunt injury despite having worse injuries and receiving more component transfusions. These differences were not seen in patients injured by penetrating mechanism. On multivariable analysis, mortality was higher in males and females ≥52 compared with younger females (all p<0.01), regardless of mechanism.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: After WB, being female and younger was generally associated with fewer blood transfusions, complications, and mortalities, but these differences were more pronounced in those with blunt mechanism. Females <52 demonstrated lower mortality compared with older patients. Further investigation is required to elucidate the mechanisms of these findings.

abstract.label: LEVEL OF EVIDENCE
abstract.text: III, Prognostic/Epidemiological.

articles.title: Modernization of emergency general surgery through technical expertise and operational development for our patients and teams.

abstract.text: Emergency general surgery (EGS) procedures are frequent and associated with higher morbidity than elective operations. Improving surgical quality for EGS patients is an admirable goal, which is fraught with several clinical and operational challenges. Surgeons must develop a skillset that is prepared to maintain clinical excellence and overcome the operational challenges that often prevent the initiation of new quality programs. This narrative review is from the Modernization of EGS short course at the 2026 EAST Annual Scientific Assembly. The session is divided into four parts highlighting specific EGS topics: hepatobiliary, alimentary tract, abdominal wall, and special patient populations. Topics were selected to provide current evidence-based approaches to commonly encountered pathological findings and notoriously challenging clinical scenarios. Included are expert opinion sections on the fundamental aspects of building a quality EGS program given by acute care surgery leaders with proven success.

articles.title: Defying Gravity: Strategies for Reducing the Impact of Falls - AAST Virtual Grand Rounds.

abstract.text: Injuries from falls and their sequelae represent a significant source of morbidity and mortality. This impact is predominantly felt by patients with pre-existing health conditions and poor health. For these patients, comorbidities, frailty, use of anticoagulation, and other factors result in the development of severe injuries after relatively low-impact falls. Many strategies exist to counter the negative effects of falls-both thinking about how to reduce the incidence of falls by engaging in fall prevention strategies and techniques for reducing trip hazards or finding ways to minimize the potential impact of falls on vulnerable populations. These efforts can be combined to create local and regional fall-prevention networks, which have been highly successful and effective in addressing fall risk. This publication summarizes the contents of an American Association for the Surgery of Trauma's Virtual Grand Rounds that highlighted the epidemiology of falls, the effects of falls, and strategies for countering these effects at individual and locoregional levels.

articles.title: Craniofacial injuries in victims of non-fatal intimate partner violence treated in US emergency departments, 2018-2022.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Intimate partner violence (IPV) is a significant public health crisis, and craniofacial injuries are among the most common consequences. However, nationwide estimates of IPV-related craniofacial injuries remain limited.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a retrospective descriptive study of non-fatal IPV-related injuries using the National Electronic Injury Surveillance System (NEISS)-All Injury Program from 2018 to 2022. Cases were restricted to intentional assaults from a spouse or intimate partner. Craniofacial injuries were defined as injuries to the head, face, mouth, eyeball, neck, or ear. National estimates were generated using NEISS sampling weights, and rates per 100,000 population were calculated using US Census denominators stratified by sex, age, and race/ethnicity.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: An estimated 888,279 emergency department visits were attributable to IPV-related injury during the study period, of which 58.3% (517,769 cases) involved craniofacial trauma. Female patients comprised the majority of cases (81.9%), experiencing an average annual rate of 97.6 per 100,000 compared with 20.4 per 100,000 for males. The highest rates were observed among women aged 20-26 (223.1 per 100,000) and 27-34 years (232.7 per 100,000). Black patients had the highest racial/ethnic burden (62.9 per 100,000), nearly four times higher than non-Hispanic white patients. Common diagnoses included internal injuries (28.9%), contusions/abrasions (28.0%), lacerations (17.4%), and concussions (4.2%). Most injuries occurred at home (85.2%) and resulted from being struck or hit (92.2%).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: These findings underscore the need for targeted prevention, improved clinical recognition, and survivor-centered services addressing the neurological and psychosocial consequences of IPV-related head trauma.

articles.title: Prognostic factors and visual outcomes in badminton-related ocular injuries: A retrospective study.

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: To evaluate a large cohort of eye patients from India for the epidemiology, clinical presentation, and visual outcomes of ocular injuries sustained while playing badminton.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Medical records of patients presenting with badminton-related ocular injuries were reviewed to compare the predicted visual outcome with that stipulated by the Ocular Trauma Score (OTS). The patients' data on demographics, mode of injury, clinical evaluation, and treatment modalities were compiled, analysed and interpreted to contrast alongside OTS, the standardised prediction of visual outcomes after indexing the severity of eye injury.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 486 patients were included. Blunt trauma from being hit by badminton shuttlecock was the most common mechanism, followed by racquet injury, and spectacle injury. Closed-globe injury was predominant (97.33%). None of the players were using protective eyewear. Visual prognosis was generally favourable in closed-globe injury (mean final BCVA 0.32 ± 0.56 logMAR) compared to open-globe injury (0.46 ± 0.68 logMAR). Significant predictors of visual outcome included presenting BCVA, early post-injury BCVA, cataract, secondary glaucoma, optic disc involvement, iridodialysis, and OTS. OTS categories 3-5 showed better visual outcomes than predicted by the original OTS model.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Closed-globe injury represented the most common injury in badminton-related ophthalmic trauma. Initial visual acuity, lens status, optic disc involvement, secondary glaucoma, eye surgery performed, OTS score and posterior segment injury were statistically significant in predicting final visual outcomes. Additionally, this study emphasizes how important it is to use protective glasses when playing badminton.

articles.title: Equity-Related Factors in Emergency Medical Service Use for Acute Coronary Syndromes: A Systematic Review.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Emergency medical service (EMS) use reduces time to treatment and improves outcomes in acute coronary syndrome (ACS), yet it is unknown whether all Australians have equitable access to EMS. This systematic review examined whether equity-related factors are associated with disparities in EMS use for patients with ACS in Australia.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: The review was pre-registered with PROSPERO (CRD42023466951). Six databases (MEDLINE, CINAHL, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, Cochrane and Scopus) were searched in June 2025 for articles published from inception until May 2025. Eligible studies involved adults presenting to Australian hospitals or emergency departments with ACS or acute non-traumatic chest pain and reported EMS use by at least one PROGRESS-Plus equity-related factor. Risk of bias was assessed using JBI checklists. Findings were synthesized using tabular analysis and a vote-counting summary.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Fourteen studies were identified, with twelve rated high quality. EMS utilization ranged from 36% to 79% and increased over time. Disparities were evident across multiple equity-related factors. Adults aged under 49 years had up to 68% lower odds of EMS use than those 65 years or older. Men had up to 11% lower odds than women. People born outside Australia had up to 15% lower odds, and those preferring non-English languages had 6-20% lower odds. Residents of remote areas had up to 25% lower odds than major city residents, while individuals living alone had up to 48% higher odds than those living with others. Findings for socioeconomic status measures were mixed.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: EMS use for ACS in Australia is consistently lower among younger adults, men, people born overseas, those preferring non-English languages, and residents of remote areas. These findings can inform targeted interventions to improve EMS accessibility. Future research should examine the mechanisms underlying these access barriers, particularly for populations experiencing multiple forms of disadvantage.

articles.title: Mixed Presentation of Hyperglycemic Hyperosmolar State and Diabetic Ketoacidosis in a Pediatric Patient: a Case Report and Literature Review.
articles.journal_full: Journal of clinical research in pediatric endocrinology

abstract.text: The coexistence of diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) and hyperglycemic hyperosmolar state (HHS), known as mixed hyperglycemic crisis, is a rare but potentially fatal metabolic emergency in pediatrics, and is frequently underrecognized because it is misclassified as isolated DKA. It carries a higher risk of complications than either entity alone, particularly in patients with complex comorbidities. We describe the case of a 16-year-old female with myelomeningocele, neurogenic bladder, obesity, and insulin resistance, who had self-discontinued treatment with metformin, atorvastatin, and allopurinol one year prior and presented with sudden neurological deterioration. Initial workup revealed extreme hyperglycemia (1,777 mg/dL), severe hyperosmolarity (431 mOsm/kg), decompensated metabolic acidosis (pH 7.13), and positive urine ketones (+++), consistent with a mixed DKA-HHS presentation. She subsequently developed septic shock of urinary origin, acute kidney injury, and acute pancreatitis (lipase 3,911 U/L). Despite intensive management guided by International Society for Pediatric and Adolescent Diabetes-ISPAD recommendations, she progressed to refractory shock and multiorgan failure, dying within 48 hours of admission. To the best of our knowledge, this represents one of the most extreme metabolic derangements reported in pediatric mixed hyperglycemic crisis. The convergence of extreme hyperosmolarity, concurrent sepsis, and structural comorbidities created a lethal risk phenotype in which sepsis, rather than the degree of metabolic derangement alone, appeared to determine the fatal outcome. Early recognition and an individualized therapeutic approach are essential to improve outcomes in vulnerable pediatric patients.

articles.title: Using a Single Dose of Dexamethasone at 0.6 Versus 0.15 mg/kg of Body Weight for the Treatment of Croup: A Multicenter Retrospective Chart Review.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To compare the effectiveness and adverse events associated with treating children with croup with dexamethasone at 0.15 versus 0.6 mg/kg body weight.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective cohort study included children (younger than 18 y) with a clinical diagnosis of croup in 4 pediatric emergency departments (EDs) between January 2017 and December 2019. The primary outcome was return visit to the ED for croup within 7 days, and the secondary outcomes were hospitalization within 7 days and occurrence of adverse events within 30 days. Both χ2 tests and logistic regression models were used to compare differences in the proportions of children with ED return visits, hospitalizations, and adverse events associated with dose.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: We included 14,205 children in the final analysis. Of the 13,437 croup episodes from children treated with dexamethasone at 0.15 mg/kg (n=172) or 0.6 mg/kg (n=13,265), 2.9% and 4.1%, respectively, were ED return visits within 7 days following treatment. The difference in the proportion of ED return visits following treatment with the 2 doses was not statistically significant (1.2%; 95% CI: -1.31 to 3.76). In a multivariable-adjusted model, 0.15 mg/kg was not associated with ED return visits within 7 days [adjusted odds ratio (aOR)=0.88; 95% CI: 0.31-1.97], but was associated with hospitalization (aOR=3.18; 95% CI: 1.52-6.00). A total of 135 (1%) of all croup episodes had at least 1 adverse event within 30 days. Of those treated with 0.15 or 0.6 mg/kg, 1.2% and 1%, respectively, had at least 1 adverse event within 30 days. The most common adverse event was pneumonia (0.8%).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Our findings suggest that low-dose dexamethasone, 0.15 mg/kg, may be as effective as 0.6 mg/kg with comparable proportions of ED return visits and adverse events within 7 days. However, low-dose dexamethasone was associated with increased hospitalization. Clinicians should weigh the potential risk of hospitalization when choosing 0.15 mg/kg of dexamethasone.

articles.title: Pre-hospital pulse pressure as an early predictor of active hemorrhage in trauma patients.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Early identification of active hemorrhage (AH) is a critical challenge in trauma care. Narrowed pulse pressure (PP) has been associated with AH at the time of emergency department arrival; however, its role in the prehospital setting remains unclear. The aim of this study was to evaluate the utility of prehospital PP as an early predictor of AH in trauma.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a retrospective multi-centre study (January 2017 - January 2020) including adult trauma patients at all three level 1 trauma centers in Alberta, Canada. AH was defined as either operative or interventional radiology hemorrhage control within 24 h of arrival, or transfusion of ≥ 4 units of packed red blood cells within 4 h. ROC and multivariable logistic regression analyses were used to characterize associations between prehospital PP and AH.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: 2177 patients met inclusion criteria, of whom 68 (3%) had active hemorrhage. Compared to non-bleeding patients, AH patients had significantly narrower median prehospital PP (40 mmHg, IQR 29-52 vs 53, IQR 42-67; p < 0.001) and lower median systolic blood pressure (SBP; 111 mmHg, IQR 101-136 vs 138, IQR 122-156; p < 0.001). Prehospital PP demonstrated moderate ability to predict hemorrhage (AUC 0.73, 95% CI 0.67-0.79), comparable to SBP (AUC 0.74, 95% CI 0.67-0.81). Narrowed prehospital PP was independently associated with AH (odds ratio 1.51, 95% CI 1.28-1.79), reflecting a 51% increase in the risk of hemorrhage for each 10 mmHg the PP narrowed. Compared to non-bleeding patients, AH patients had worse outcomes including increased risk of ICU admission (63% vs 18%; p < 0.001), prolonged hospital length of stay (22 days, IQR 8-53 vs 7 days, IQR 4-15; p < 0.001), and increased mortality, although this did not reach statistical significance (18% vs 10%; p = 0.068).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Prehospital PP ≤ 45 mmHg identifies patients at risk for active hemorrhage and given its high negative predictive value, is most useful to rule-out patients without active hemorrhage in the prehospital setting. PP is a useful adjunct to support early recognition of hemorrhage in trauma. This is particularly relevant for trauma centres serving large geographic regions, where prolonged transport times delay definitive hemorrhage control. Its incorporation into the prehospital assessment has potential to help facilitate timely mobilization of hemorrhage control resources that actively bleeding patients require.

articles.title: How have management and outcomes of periprosthetic proximal femoral fractures changed? A comparison of two 8 year time periods in a high volume centre.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Periprosthetic femoral fractures (PFFs) are now the leading cause of major reoperation following total hip arthroplasty (THA). Patients are often frail and surgeries increasingly complex. We reviewed PFFs over two consecutive 8-year periods to analyse trends in incidence, management and outcomes to assess the evolving clinical and service impacts.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A retrospective review was conducted using data from the Fracture Outcomes Research Database (FORD) and the National Hip Fracture Database (NHFD) across two 8-year periods (2007-2015 and 2016-2024). Radiographic and clinical records were reviewed. Fracture classification, management, comorbidities and mortality were recorded and compared. A regression analysis was performed to determine co-morbidities that significantly increased the risk of 12-month mortality. In the 2016-2024 period, data on re-operations rates were recorded.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: PFF increased from 189 to 320 across the two periods, totalling 509 patients. The incidence of Vancouver B2 fractures increased more than 1.5x, rising from 42/189 (22.2%) to 117/320 (36.6%) patients. Fixation remained the most common treatment across the two periods (75.1% and 63.4%), while revision arthroplasty was performed in 22.8% and 18.4% respectively. B2 fracture management changed significantly with fixation increasing (59% v 9.5%; p < 0.001) and revision arthroplasty rates decreasing (38.5% vs 85.7%; p < 0.001). Time to theatre improved (5-3.7 days; p = 0.028) and a higher proportion of patients returned to their pre-injury residence (30.2%; 57/189 vs 39%; 96/320, p = 0.068). No difference in mortality was observed at 30 days (2.6-3.1%; p = 0.796) or 90 days (5.8% vs 9.1%; p = 0.233) but mortality was higher at 12 months (12.2-20%; p = 0.028). ASA 4 patients increased (14%; 25/179; vs 29.1%; 82/282, OR = 2.526 (95% CI 1.54-4.14), p < 0.001). Re-operation rates were lower in the fixation group than in the revision group (12; 5.9% vs 8; 13.6%; p = 0.095).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The incidence and mortality associated with PFFs are rising within our unit, despite improved time to theatre and improved discharge outcomes. This trend may reflect a frailer cohort with higher ASA grades. We demonstrate a shift in practice, with more B2 fractures treated with fixation, achieving good outcomes suggesting fixation may be a safe treatment option in selected frail patients.

articles.title: Outcomes of circular frame external fixation for tibia fracture in the elderly: comparison with a fracture-matched younger cohort.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Circular frame fixation is a management method often used for complex fractures, or fractures with soft tissue compromise. Tibia fractures in older adults can be difficult to manage due to an association with osteoporosis, poor quality soft tissues, and a requirement for post-operative weight bearing to maintain function and independence. There is a paucity of evidence for the use of circular frames for tibia fractures in older adults. The available evidence suggests it is an effective treatment option, however, no study has compared treatment outcomes between older and younger patients.

abstract.label: AIM
abstract.text: To compare adverse events and outcomes between an 'older' cohort and 'younger' cohort of patients managed with circular frame for tibia fracture.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: The 'younger' cohort aged 18-50 and the 'older' cohort aged over 64 were identified from our institutional database. Injuries were classified using the AO/OTA and Gustilo-Anderson classifications. Data collection was retrospective and extracted from patient records. Adverse events were classified according to Paley as problems, obstacles or complications. Statistical analysis was performed, and significance set at p < 0.05.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: 135 patients were included; 66 in the 'younger' cohort and 69 in the 'older' cohort. There were significantly more females in the 'older' cohort, with a higher proportion having systemic co-morbidity (85% vs 24%) and diabetes (25% vs 3%). There were more smokers in the 'younger' cohort (33% vs 12%). There was no significant difference in rate of or time to union. The 'younger' cohort was more likely to require further procedures to achieve union. More patients in the 'older' cohort suffered a problem (30% vs 3%); pin site infection accounted for all problems in the 'older' group, and half the problems in the 'younger' group. The rate of obstacles and complications was not different CONCLUSION: Circular frame fixation is a suitable management option for 'older' patients who sustain tibia fracture, as there is no difference between rate or time to union when compared to a 'younger' cohort. 'Older' patients are more likely to encounter pin site infection and should be counselled regarding this. There is no difference between rate of more significant obstacles or complication.

articles.title: Development of zein-coated Ag-NPs integrated into decellularized fish skin extracellular matrix as a hybrid scaffold for wound healing: In-vitro and in vivo study.

abstract.text: Chronic wounds complicated by bacterial infections and poor tissue regeneration continue to present a major clinical problem in wound healing. This work describes a new hybrid scaffold made from zein-coated silver nanoparticles (Zein-Ag NPs) embedded in decellularized fish skin extracellular matrix (ECM). This scaffold has been designed to synergistically provide antimicrobial activity and enhance tissue repair. The Ag NPs were synthesized by chemically reducing silver nitrate with sodium borohydride and then coated with zein to improve the stability and biocompatibility of the Ag NPs. Upon evaluating the Ag NPs using dynamic light scattering (DLS), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), transmission electron microscopy (TEM), Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), and X-ray diffraction (XRD), it was determined that optimal Ag NPs were produced using a silver nitrate precursor concentration of 5 mM, which produced nanoparticles of ~35 nm in diameter. The fish skin ECM was decellularized using the optimized physical method. The Zein-Ag/ECM scaffolds exhibited strong antimicrobial activity in vitro against Candida species and bacteria, including Staphylococcus aureus, Escherichia coli, and Pseudomonas aeruginosa, when tested using disk diffusion assays, and their controlled release of Ag⁺ minimized cytotoxicity. The biocompatibility of the material (hemocompatibility) was determined to be < 5% in vitro at 5 mM. Additionally, the material demonstrated support for the growth of fibroblasts in vitro. In vivo studies in rats showed that using the material to treat excisional wounds led to accelerated healing of the wounds, i.e., 90-95% healed by day 14, increased re-epithelialization, decreased inflammation, and improved organization of the collagen deposition in the wound site. Histopathology (using H&E and Masson Trichrome staining) confirmed this.

articles.title: [Establishing reference ranges for right ventricular functional parameters on neonatal echocardiography: a multicenter, prospective observational study].
articles.journal: Zhongguo Dang Dai Er Ke Za Zhi
articles.journal_full: Zhongguo dang dai er ke za zhi = Chinese journal of contemporary pediatrics

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: To establish reference ranges for right ventricular functional parameters at defined postnatal time points in neonates, thereby providing a basis for precise hemodynamic assessment and clinical management of critically ill neonates.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In a prospective multicenter observational study, clinical and echocardiographic data were collected from 406 term neonates who were admitted to neonatal departments or seen in outpatient clinics of three centers (Children's Hospital of Chongqing Medical University, Yinchuan First People's Hospital, and Inner Mongolia Maternal and Child Health Care Hospital) between June 2023 and May 2024. Bedside echocardiography was used to measure right ventricular functional parameters. Spearman rank correlation was applied to assess associations between each parameter and sex, birth weight, gestational age, and postnatal age. Reference ranges were constructed using the 95% confidence interval approach for postnatal days 1, 3, 7, 14, and 28, with stratification by gestational age and birth weight.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among the right ventricular functional parameters, right ventricular fractional area change (RV-FAC), tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion (TAPSE), and tricuspid annular peak systolic velocity were positively correlated with gestational age and birth weight (all P<0.05). RV-FAC, TAPSE, right ventricular outflow tract velocity-time integral, tricuspid annular peak systolic velocity, tricuspid inflow E-wave peak velocity, tricuspid inflow E/A ratio, and peak early diastolic velocity of the lateral tricuspid annulus (e') were positively correlated with postnatal age (all P<0.05). None of the right ventricular parameters was correlated with sex (all P>0.05). Reference ranges for postnatal days 1, 3, 7, 14, and 28 were established with stratification by gestational age and birth weight.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Multiple parameters of neonatal right ventricular systolic and diastolic function are associated with postnatal age, gestational age, and birth weight. The comprehensive, stratified reference ranges for right ventricular functional parameters established in this study may serve as an important reference for refined hemodynamic assessment and management in critically ill neonates.

articles.title: Latent Profiles of Early Personal Mastery and Their Association with Out-of-Hospital Rehabilitation Exercise Adherence One Month After Hip Arthroplasty: A Single-Centre Prospective Observational Study.

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: In this single-centre prospective observational study, we aimed to identify latent profiles of early personal mastery in patients after hip arthroplasty, examine factors associated with profile membership, and explore differences in out-of-hospital rehabilitation exercise adherence across profiles.

abstract.label: PATIENTS AND METHODS
