abstract.text: A total of 350 patients who underwent primary hip arthroplasty at a tertiary hospital in Urumqi, Xinjiang, from August to December 2024, were recruited by convenience sampling; 17 were lost to follow-up, and 333 completed the 1-month assessment and were included in the analysis. Personal mastery was assessed on postoperative day 1-2 with the Personal Mastery Scale, together with a general information questionnaire; adherence to out-of-hospital rehabilitation exercise was assessed at 1 month postoperatively with the Functional Exercise Adherence Scale for Orthopedic Patients. Latent profile analysis (LPA) was used to identify profiles of personal mastery, and multinomial logistic regression to examine factors associated with profile membership. Differences in adherence across profiles were analysed using the Bolck-Croon-Hagenaars (BCH) approach to account for classification uncertainty, and were additionally examined in linear models adjusted for demographic and clinical covariates.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of the 350 patients recruited, 17 were lost to follow-up, giving a 1-month follow-up retention rate of 95.14%. LPA identified three profiles of early personal mastery: low (31.53%), intermediate (32.13%) and high (36.34%) personal mastery. In the multinomial logistic regression, age, gender, education level, employment status and chronic comorbidities were independently associated with profile membership (p < 0.05), whereas place of residence was not. Adherence at 1 month differed significantly across profiles (χ 2 = 81.398, p < 0.001), and profile membership remained independently associated with adherence after adjustment for demographic and clinical covariates (total adherence score F(2, 307) = 23.23, p < 0.001). The intermediate and high personal mastery profiles did not differ significantly from each other on the learning dimension, the physical dimension or the total adherence score.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Early personal mastery in hip arthroplasty patients is heterogeneous and is associated with out-of-hospital rehabilitation exercise adherence at 1 month. These findings suggest that interventions tailored to patients' mastery profiles warrant investigation, although causal relationships remain to be established.

articles.title: General anesthesia is associated with increased postoperative morbidity and mortality in frail patients undergoing hip fracture fixation.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Anesthetic management of hip fracture fixation has two primary modalities: general anesthesia (GA) and spinal anesthesia (SA). Choice of anesthesia often depends on institutional protocols and the individual anesthesiologist, due to a lack of consensus guidelines. Most studies have conflicting evidence and focus primarily on elderly age as a risk factor, without accounting for frailty. This study investigates whether frailty influences the relationship between anesthetic modality and postoperative outcomes.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective study queried the ACS-NSQIP from 2015 to 2020 for patients who underwent hip fracture fixation with open reduction internal fixation with plate and screws or intramedullary implant insertion. Patients were separated based on whether they received GA or SA. Frailty was evaluated using the 5-Item Modified Frailty Index (mFI-5). Patients classified as frail or severely frail were included. Multivariable regression adjusting for age, sex, ASA classification, smoking, and the comorbidities significant on univariate regression was performed. The outcomes examined were mortality, unplanned readmission, and overall complications within 30 days postoperatively.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: This study included 24,401 patients under GA and 6193 patients under SA. On multivariable regression analysis, GA was independently associated with increased odds of mortality, unplanned readmission, and all complications among frail patients. Severely frail patients under GA had increased odds of unplanned readmission and all complications. When looking at both frail and severely frail patients together, GA remained a significant predictor of mortality, unplanned readmission, and all complications.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: After controlling for ASA classification, our study found that frail and severely frail patients undergoing GA for hip fracture fixation had significantly increased odds of mortality, unplanned readmission, and all complications. Our findings suggest that SA may be safer compared to GA in frail patients undergoing hip fracture fixation. Frail patients that undergo GA may benefit from increased postoperative monitoring to help mitigate complications.

articles.title: The impact of socioeconomic deprivation on outcomes following open upper-limb fractures.

abstract.text: Socioeconomic deprivation is associated with increased trauma burden and poorer outcomes following open fractures. However, its impact on open upper-limb fractures remains unclear. This study examined whether socioeconomic deprivation influenced physiological status at presentation, Injury Severity Score and Gustilo-Anderson grade, time to surgical debridement, and early postoperative outcomes in patients treated within a regional major trauma network. We performed a retrospective cohort study using a prospectively maintained regional trauma registry at a Level I Major Trauma Centre. Consecutive patients presenting between 1 April 2014 and 1 April 2023 with open fractures of the humerus, radius, ulna, scapula, or clavicle were identified. Deprivation was determined using the postcode-linked 2019 Index of Multiple Deprivation. Patients without valid English IMD linkage were excluded. Outcomes were time to debridement, length of stay, 30- and 90-day readmission, reoperation within 1 year, and postoperative infection. Multivariable models adjusted for age, sex, American Society of Anesthesiologists grade, Injury Severity Score category, and Gustilo-Anderson grade. Of 297 identified patients, 291 were included. Patients from more deprived areas had poorer baseline physiological status, with ASA 3-4 status in 31.8% of the most deprived quintile compared with 10.0% of the least deprived quintile (p = 0.030). Gustilo-Anderson grade distribution differed across deprivation quintiles (p = 0.016), whereas Injury Severity Score category did not (p = 0.637). Time to debridement differed across IMD quintiles in unadjusted analysis (p = 0.017), but there was no linear association with continuous IMD decile after adjustment. IMD decile was not independently associated with length of stay, 90-day readmission, reoperation within 1 year, or postoperative infection. There was no statistically significant association with 30-day readmission (odds ratio 1.196, 95% CI 0.979-1.480; p = 0.080), although the estimate was imprecise. Patients from more deprived areas presented with poorer physiological status, and the distribution of Gustilo-Anderson grades differed across deprivation quintiles. However, after adjustment for measured clinical covariates, there was no clear evidence that deprivation was independently associated with delay to surgery or worse early postoperative outcomes. Standardised trauma care may help mitigate socioeconomic differences in early outcomes after upper-limb fractures.

articles.title: Treatment and outcome of proximal femur fractures in a resource limited setting: a prospective observational study in rural Tanzania.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Proximal femur fractures are a common type of fracture worldwide and are known to result in high disability and mortality rates. In resource-limited settings, these fractures are suspected to be an underreported problem. This study provides an overview of the different treatment modalities and outcomes of patients with a proximal femur fracture in rural Tanzania.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A prospective observational study was conducted in a rural referral hospital in Tanzania. Between August 2019 and August 2020 patients admitted with a proximal femur fracture were included. Data on fracture type, treatment and outcome were collected up to one year after admission. Outcome included mortality, disability (Harris Hip Score (HHS), WHODAS 2.0) and Quality of Life (EQ-5D-3L, QoL).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Diagnosis: forty-seven patients were included, with a median age of 70 years (IQR 58-81). Thirty patients (30/47, 64%) sustained their injury due to a fall from standing height and eight patients were involved in a motor traffic accident. Eleven patients (11/47, 23%) sustained a femoral neck fracture, 24 patients (51%) sustained an intertrochanteric fracture and five patients (11%) sustained a subtrochanteric fracture. Five patients had additional injuries.

abstract.label: TREATMENT
abstract.text: eleven patients (11/47, 23%) received no treatment; 27 patients (57%) were treated conservatively; seven patients (15%) received an intramedullary nail. One Girdlestone (2%) was performed and one patient (2%) was referred to another hospital for operative treatment.

abstract.label: OUTCOME
abstract.text: The one-year follow-up rate was 96% (45/47). One-year mortality rate was 28% (13/47). Eleven patients (11/32, 34%) recovered to the disability level as reported prior to the injury (WHODAS 2.0). The HHS score showed a poor result in 21 patients (21/32, 66%; mean 62, SD 18). Seven patients had regained normal squat function. The QoL VAS at 3 months after admission was comparable to pre-injury reported general perceived health.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Most of the patients with proximal femur fractures are treated non-operatively and not according the current standard of care which is operative fixation or arthroplasty, resulting in limited functional outcome and high mortality rates. This data shows the importance of increased attention and the need for urgent improvement of fracture treatment and outcome in resource-limited settings.

articles.title: Rapid bolus versus 3-h continuous infusion of 3% hypertonic saline for acute symptomatic hyponatremia.
articles.journal_full: The American journal of emergency medicine

abstract.label: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: Hyponatremia is a common electrolyte disorder in emergency care that requires careful clinical management. Sodium correction, safety, 30-day hyponatremia-related hospital readmission, and mortality were compared between a 20-min rapid intermittent bolus (RIB) and a 3-h slow continuous infusion (SCI) of 3% hypertonic saline in adults with acute symptomatic hyponatremia.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This prospective cohort study included 58 adults presenting to the emergency department with acute symptomatic hyponatremia patients were assigned to RIB (20 min; n = 29) or SCI (3 h; n = 29) using a study-specific allocation list. Sodium kinetics through 24 h, safety, and 30-day outcomes were assessed using ANCOVA, repeated-measures ANOVA, multivariable regression, and ROC analysis.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Twenty-four-hour sodium correction was comparable between groups. One overcorrection occurred with SCI; no osmotic demyelination syndrome occurred. Thirty-day hyponatremia-related hospital readmission was 13.8% with RIB and 41.4% with SCI (p = 0.019); In an exploratory adjusted analysis, SCI was associated with higher adjusted odds (aOR) of readmission (aOR:7.04; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.56-31.80; p = 0.011). Higher baseline Glasgow Coma Scale score was associated with lower 30-day-all-cause mortality (aOR, 0.39; 95% CI, 0.17-0.88; p = 0.025). A baseline sodium cutoff of ≤115.5 mmol/L showed exploratory discrimination for second dose requirement with an area under the curve of 0.754.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Both RIB and SCI protocols demonstrated similar short-term sodium correction, with few observed adverse events. The difference in 30-day hyponatremia-related hospital readmission and exploratory associations involving baseline neurological status and serum sodium require confirmation in larger studies.

articles.title: Acute-on-Chronic Carbamazepine Overdose: A Toxicology Simulation Case for Fourth-Year Medical Students.
articles.journal_full: MedEdPORTAL : the journal of teaching and learning resources

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Carbamazepine is an antiepileptic medication used to treat seizures, trigeminal neuralgia, and bipolar disorder. Although carbamazepine overdose occurs frequently, it receives limited attention in undergraduate medical curricula. Multimodal, experiential learning provides a safe, structured learning environment. We developed a simulation of carbamazepine overdose to address this educational gap.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Fourth-year medical students enrolled in a toxicology course completed a pretest and a Likert-scale questionnaire assessing confidence in managing carbamazepine overdose. Students received a 30-minute lecture and participated in a 15-minute simulation involving a 26-year-old patient with an intentional carbamazepine overdose followed by a 15-minute debrief. Critical actions included obtaining a focused history, neurological assessment, and carbamazepine level; administering multidose activated charcoal; and requesting toxicology and psychiatric consultation. Required equipment included a high-fidelity manikin, IV supplies, and standard pharmaceuticals. We evaluated students with a critical actions checklist and posttest. Students then completed additional Likert-scale questionnaires assessing workshop reactions, confidence, and intent to change practice.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Forty-nine students participated across 10 sessions. Mean pretest and posttest scores were 67% (SD = 19) and 98% (SD = 5), respectively, with significant improvement (Wilcoxon W = 0.0, P < .001). All groups completed the critical actions checklist. Median confidence scores for identifying clinical manifestations, ordering and interpreting diagnostic studies, and initiating treatment increased from 3's and 4's to 5 across all domains (Mann-Whitney U P < .001). Students rated the workshop favorably and most reported intent to change practice.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: Experiential learning is an effective pedagogical technique to teach carbamazepine overdose.

articles.title: Adult intestinal malrotation: A rare incidental finding in trauma imaging.

abstract.text: Intestinal malrotation is a congenital anomaly resulting from abnormal rotation and fixation of the midgut during embryonic development. It is typically diagnosed in infancy, and its detection in adults-particularly in asymptomatic individuals-is rare. In adults, clinical presentation ranges from chronic, nonspecific symptoms to acute intestinal obstruction and midgut volvulus. A 36-year-old woman presented to the emergency department following a motor vehicle collision. She reported no gastrointestinal complaints and denied any history of recurrent abdominal pain, bilious vomiting, abdominal distension, food intolerance, or symptoms suggestive of bowel obstruction. Contrast-enhanced abdominopelvic CT performed to evaluate traumatic injuries showed no evidence of acute intra-abdominal injury. However, it demonstrated predominantly right-sided small-bowel loops, a left-sided cecum and appendix, an abnormal course of the duodenum, and an anterior position of the superior mesenteric vein relative to the superior mesenteric artery. These findings were consistent with midgut malrotation. There was no evidence of volvulus, obstruction, bowel ischemia, or pneumoperitoneum. The patient was referred to the surgical service for further evaluation and management planning, and she was educated regarding warning signs. Although midgut malrotation is uncommon in adults, it may be identified incidentally on imaging performed for unrelated indications. Familiarity with the anatomic and mesenteric vascular patterns of this anomaly on CT is essential for accurate diagnosis, prevention of misinterpretation, and timely recognition of potentially life-threatening complications. Management of asymptomatic cases should be individualized based on clinical status, imaging findings, and surgical assessment.

articles.title: The validity of three suicide risk screening tools among Native American youth in a reservation-based ED.

abstract.text: Suicide is a leading cause of death among adolescents, with disproportionately high rates among American Indian/Alaska Native (AI/AN) youth. Early identification is critical for youth suicide prevention, and the Emergency Department is an important and viable setting for targeting suicide risk. The Emergency Department Study for Teens at Risk for Suicide (ED-STARS) was a prospective, multi-site cohort study conducted across 13 EDs in the Pediatric Emergency Care Applied Research Network, and one Indian Health Service site. The present study examined the comparative validity of the Ask Suicide Screening Questions (ASQ), Patient Health Questionnaire (PHQ-2) and Comprehensive Assessment of Suicide Screening in Youth (CASSY) in AI youth from the White Mountain Apache site of the ED-STARS parent study. A total of 174 AI adolescents from the Whiteriver IHS hospital site were included in the analytic sample. The CASSY performed well in this sample with an overall AUC of 0.86 [95% CI, 0.79-0.93], and, importantly, did not miss identifying anyone at risk who went on to have a subsequent suicide event. The ASQ and PHQ-2 did not perform as well as the CASSY in terms of AUCs (0.82 and 0.72 respectively). Both the ASQ and PHQ-2 missed a substantial number of individuals with a subsequent suicide event. Given the relatively widespread implementation of suicide screening in hospitals, this data has substantial clinical and public health significance. AI/AN youth experience disproportionately high suicide risk, yet screening tools lack validation in these populations.

articles.title: The impact of heatwaves on maternal, neonatal and child health outcomes in Western Australian climate zones: A protocol paper for a retrospective cohort study.
authors: Western Australian Healthy Environments And Lives Aboriginal Steering Group (WA HEAL ASG)

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Rising global temperatures have resulted in an increase in the frequency and severity of heatwaves. Pregnancy is a time of substantial physiological change and thus maternal and neonatal health outcomes are susceptible to adverse effects of heat. There is a lack of knowledge about thermoregulation in pregnancy, including how effectively pregnant people adapt in different climate contexts and what specific environmental conditions present the largest thermoregulatory challenges. The primary aim of this study is to examine the associations between exposure to heatwaves during pregnancy and maternal, neonatal, and child health outcomes in Western Australia climatic regions.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: All neonates born in Western Australia between 1991 and 2023 will be identified from perinatal records (~960,000 neonates). Perinatal records will be linked to weather data from the ERA5 database using Statistical Area 2 geocoding to identify heatwave exposed pregnancies. Commonly used definitions of heatwave exposure will be tested against three neonatal outcomes (pre-term birth, low birth weight, and congenital anomalies). From this, a single or small number of definition will be selected to examine maternal, neonatal, and child health outcomes using linked hospital, emergency department, and education assessment data, as well as data from the Western Australian congenital anomalies and death register. The association between heatwaves during pregnancy and health outcomes will be performed using generalised estimating equations, adjusting for covariates including, but not limited to, cigarette smoking, parity, maternal age, socio-economic status, and Aboriginality where appropriate. Stratification by socio-economic status and geographic region will also be carried out.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: Examining the association between exposure to heatwaves in pregnancy and maternal, neonatal and child outcomes is important given the increasing frequency of heatwaves. The study will highlight which heat definitions confers the highest vulnerability as well as demographic and geographic subgroups who are particularly vulnerable to the effects of heatwaves. It will provide valuable information for future public health planning, including targets for intervention.

articles.title: Socioeconomic impact of upper and lower extremity fractures among temporary migrant workers: A prospective longitudinal cohort study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Temporary migrant workers may be particularly vulnerable to financial and occupational consequences after fracture. This study evaluated longitudinal income changes and socioeconomic outcomes following appendicular fractures in this population.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This prospective cohort study included temporary migrant workers in Kuwait aged 18-65 years presenting with appendicular fractures between January 2023 and January 2025. Pre-injury income and income at 1, 3, 6 and 12 months were recorded and expressed as a percentage of individual baseline income. Unadjusted and exploratory multivariable analyses examined complete income loss at 12 months.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 601 patients assessed, 430 were included. Complete income loss affected 19.1% at 1 month, peaked at 35.1% at 3 months and persisted in 23.3% at 12 months. Mean income retained at 12 months was 65.8% of baseline: 55.5% in physically demanding labour versus 80.1% in professional roles. By 12 months, 77.0% had returned to work, but 58.0% of returners earned less than before injury. Self-employment (adjusted OR 3.02; 95% CI 1.57-5.82) and multiple fractures (2.21; 1.25-3.92) remained associated with complete income loss after adjustment; the occupational association was attenuated.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Appendicular fractures were followed by persistent socioeconomic disruption, with greater observed income deficits among physically demanding and self-employed workers and those with more extensive injuries. Returners often remained below baseline income at 12 months. Recovery assessment should include income and occupational stability.

articles.title: Acceptability and adherence to antiseptic gargling among Malaysian umrah pilgrims: A mixed-methods quasi-experimental pilot study.
articles.journal_full: Journal of Taibah University Medical Sciences

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Respiratory tract infections are common among Umrah pilgrims due to crowding, close interpersonal contact, shared accommodation, and prolonged exposure to respiratory pathogens. Gargling has been proposed as a simple non-pharmaceutical respiratory hygiene intervention, but evidence on its feasibility, adherence, and acceptability during pilgrimage remains limited.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A mixed-methods, quasi-experimental pilot-controlled study was conducted among 90 Malaysian Umrah pilgrims from two travel batches, allocated by batch to an intervention group (n=46) or control group (n=44). The intervention group received mouthwash and was instructed to gargle with 20 mL twice daily. Quantitative outcomes included self-reported respiratory symptoms, coughing frequency, impact on Umrah activities, and adherence. Open-ended responses explored perceived benefits, facilitators, barriers, and user experiences.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Most participants were female (65.6%) and aged 40-59 years. Cough and sore throat were the most commonly reported symptoms in both groups. No statistically significant differences were observed between groups for individual respiratory symptoms, number of symptoms, coughing frequency, or impact on Umrah activities (all p > 0.05). The intervention group showed non-significant trends towards lower prevalence of runny nose and less disruption of activities. Among respondents, 68.2% reported gargling twice daily almost every day. However, only 22/46 intervention participants completed the post-pilgrimage adherence assessment, representing 52.2% loss to follow-up. Participants generally perceived gargling as beneficial for respiratory and oral health, while forgetfulness and busy schedules were the main barriers.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Significant reductions in respiratory symptoms were not observed, but antiseptic gargling was acceptable, feasible, and generally well received. Larger multicentre studies incorporating objective microbiological outcomes and adherence-enhancing strategies are warranted.

articles.title: From trauma capacity to neurotrauma capacity: A scoping review of existing assessment frameworks.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Neurotrauma, comprising traumatic brain injury (TBI) and traumatic spinal cord injury (tSCI), remains a major global health issue, with low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) bearing a disproportionate burden. Effective neurotrauma care requires timely and coordinated access to prehospital care, imaging, surgery, neurocritical care, and rehabilitation, yet current assessment frameworks often fail to capture these interdependent requirements.

abstract.label: RESEARCH QUESTION
abstract.text: What instruments are currently available to evaluate trauma and neurosurgical capacity across diverse global settings, and to what extent do these tools capture indicators relevant to neurotrauma care?

abstract.label: MATERIAL AND METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a scoping review following JBI methodology and PRISMA-ScR guidelines. We searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science, and Global Health from inception to March 2026, supplemented by grey literature. We included studies describing instruments assessing system or facility-level capacity for trauma or neurosurgical care. Data extraction and domain mapping were performed independently by two reviewers.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Twenty-six documents were included, describing 19 distinct instruments. Instruments were categorized as surgical capacity (n = 4), trauma capacity (n = 4), neurosurgical/neurocritical care capacity (n = 4), and quality indicator sets (n = 7). Emergency and imaging readiness was the most frequently covered domain (89%), followed by quality and audit systems (68%), operative capacity (53%), and neurocritical care (47%). Prehospital referral systems and workforce/training were the least covered domains (37% each). Only two instruments covered all six predefined neurotrauma domains.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION AND CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Existing tools assess important components of trauma and neurosurgical capacity but remain heterogeneous and fragmented. No identified instrument provides a comprehensive, multidisciplinary assessment of neurotrauma capacity across the full continuum of care. These findings support the development of an integrated framework combining indicators across the neurotrauma care pathway.

articles.title: Man With Acute Unconsciousness.
articles.journal: J Am Coll Emerg Physicians Open
articles.journal_full: Journal of the American College of Emergency Physicians open

articles.title: Individual-level health effects of living near a gas-fired "Peaker" power plant.
articles.journal_full: The journal of climate change and health

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: "Peaker" electrical power plants operate only during periods of peak energy needs. Rapid fossil-fuel combustion ramp-up produces high emissions, and peaker plants are significant sources of CO2 and particulate air pollution. We evaluated whether residents living near a gas-fired peaker plant experienced increased pollution-associated emergency department/urgent care (ED/UC) visits associated with air pollution related to the "on" phases of peaker operation.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: ED/UC visits for patients in a primary care practice serving the neighborhoods surrounding a peaker plant in Massachusetts were analyzed for 5 years (2017-2021) for visit diagnoses including respiratory and cardiovascular conditions, headache, and pregnancy complications. Daily exposure to peaker-related emissions using HyADS, an air-parcel trajectory model-derived unitless measure of exposure magnitude, was assigned by the zip code of each patient's residential address. A case-crossover design evaluated the association between daily peaker exposure and cause-specific ED/UC visits, adjusting for heat index, PM2.5 from other sources, holidays, and seasonality.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Average daily peaker plant exposure was 1.4 (unitless); large variability reflected plant intermittency (SD=16). Background PM2.5 exposure was 8.5 μg/m³ (SD=6.4). Analyses included 2,310 ED/UC visits for assessed diagnoses among patients residing ≤ 30 km from the plant. Main analyses showed a positive association between short-term peaker emissions and increased risk of ED/UC visits for respiratory conditions (OR 1.044; 95 % CI 1.001-1.090). In addition, we found respiratory disease-related visits were elevated among the non-white group (OR 1.347; 95 % CI 1.034-1.755). There was no association noted between peaker emissions and visits for cardiovascular, headache, or pregnancy diagnoses.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The peaker plant worsened air quality when turned on. Although we did not observe consistent associations across all assessed ED/UC visit categories, there was a positive same-day association between modeled peaker-plant exposure and respiratory-related visits. Replacing combustion-driven peaker plants with renewable energy in densely populated neighborhoods could yield measurable global and local air quality-related health benefits.

articles.journal: J Am Coll Emerg Physicians Open
articles.journal_full: Journal of the American College of Emergency Physicians open

articles.title: National Guidelines for Public Health Emergency Surveillance within the Brazilian Unified Health System.
articles.journal_full: Epidemiologia e servicos de saude : revista do Sistema Unico de Saude do Brasil

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To describe the national guidelines for public health emergency surveillance within the Brazilian Unified Health System (Sistema Único de Saúde, SUS).

abstract.label: GUIDELINES
abstract.text: The increasing frequency of health, environmental, and technological events has led to more public health emergencies, requiring systems capable of early threat detection, risk assessment, and timely response. Public health emergency surveillance is an integral component of health surveillance and encompasses strategies such as indicator-based, event-based, hospital-based epidemiological, mass gathering, wastewater, community-based, and participatory surveillance. These strategies are complementary and should be supported by continuous monitoring and systematic risk assessment, while incorporating multisectoral approaches, risk communication, and One Health. Strengthening public health emergency surveillance involves integrating information systems, building workforce capacity, institutionalizing contingency plans and standard operating procedures, activating situation rooms and emergency operations centers, conducting timely outbreak investigations, communicating risks, and conducting intra-action and after-action reviews. Factors such as territorial inequalities, social vulnerabilities, and population-specific characteristics influence risk exposure, detection capacity, and the impacts of emergencies, underscoring the need to incorporate equity into surveillance explicitly.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The guidelines help consolidate public health emergency surveillance as a core component of preparedness and response within the Unified Health System, reinforcing participatory, integrated, and equity-oriented approaches to protect health and reduce harm.

articles.title: From exploitation to emergency room: Health care discrimination, utilization, and health outcomes among youth who experienced commercial sexual exploitation.

abstract.text: Discrimination in health care settings presents a significant barrier to accessing quality care, particularly for youth with experiences of commercial sexual exploitation of children (CSEC). This study examines how discrimination within primary care and emergency room (ER) settings mediates the relationship between CSEC victimization and negative health outcomes. Using data from a sample of 534 young people who experienced or are at high risk for experiencing CSEC, we employ structural equation modeling (SEM) to test three models: (1) the association between health care discrimination and negative health outcomes among CSEC survivors, (2) the mediating role of discrimination in primary care settings on health outcomes for CSEC survivors, and (3) the extent to which discrimination mediates the link between CSEC experiences and health outcomes through ER use. Findings indicate that CSEC experiences are significantly associated with poorer physical and mental health outcomes, both directly and indirectly through increased exposure to health care discrimination. Specifically, discrimination from health care providers fully mediated the relationship between CSEC and negative health outcomes in models including emergency room use, while discrimination was not a significant mediator in models focused on primary care utilization. This distinction is crucial because ER settings are often the first point of contact for CSEC survivors, making them a critical area for intervention. These results highlight the importance of addressing discrimination in ER settings to reduce barriers to care and improve health outcomes for CSEC survivors. The study underscores the need for trauma-informed, non-discriminatory health care approaches to ensure equitable access to care for vulnerable youth.

articles.title: Ammonia Co-Firing in a Staged-Air Pulverized-Coal Boiler: Reactor-Network Prediction of Carbon Reduction and Nitrogen-Oxide Emissions.

abstract.text: As power systems pursue deep decarbonization while retaining dispatchable capacity, retrofitting the existing coal-fired boiler fleet with carbon-free fuels such as ammonia is a pragmatic option, but practical implementation is constrained by the coupled behavior of combustion stability, char burnout, and NO formation. In this work, a Chemkin-based chemical reactor network (CRN) is developed for a 350 MW pulverized-coal boiler with staged air, combining perfectly stirred reactors for the main furnace zones with detailed gas-phase kinetics and heterogeneous NO-char/soot reactions. The CRN is validated against staged drop-tube-furnace measurements for pure coal and 20% ammonia cofiring (dry 6%O2), predicting outlet O2, CO2 and CO within ∼10% and capturing the measured NO rise. With ammonia introduced in the flame zone, simulations for 0-80% blending (20% step) show near-linear reductions in CO2 and CO (-21%/-73% at 20%; -84%/-98% at 80%), while char consumption is delayed and the NO/burnout peaks shift downstream. NO varies nonlinearly, increasing from 20% to 60% but decreasing at 80%. Reaction analysis attributes this trend to competition for H/OH radicals: at high ammonia fractions, NH3 dehydrogenation depletes H/OH, promotes N2 formation via NHi, and suppresses NO production. At 20% cofiring, injection location is critical: postflame injection minimizes CO2/CO (-33%/-80%) but increases NO (∼+88%), whereas burnout-zone injection causes a much larger NO penalty (about +571%). Among the 20% cofiring cases, flame-zone injection yields the lowest predicted NO emission. The outlet NH3 values are conditional on the ideal-mixing assumptions of the CRN and are not interpreted as quantitative predictions of ammonia slip under practical high-ratio operation. The results provide a chemical-kinetic interpretation of the effects of blending ratio and injection location within the modeled conditions. The results relate the predicted outlet species concentrations to nitrogen-conversion pathways under the prescribed network and operating conditions.

articles.title: Risk stratification of pediatric chest pain: red flags, diagnostic yield, and an evidence-informed clinical framework.

abstract.text: Chest pain in children and adolescents is usually noncardiac, but uncommon cardiac and other serious conditions require timely recognition. Existing reviews describe etiologies and diagnostic investigations; translating this evidence into decisions across clinical settings remains challenging. This narrative review integrates pediatric chest-pain cohorts, diagnostic studies, pathway evaluations, and professional guidance to clarify how clinical context should influence testing and disposition. A reproducible, focused literature update was performed on 27 September 2026 using PubMed records accessed through Europe PMC, with additional verification of references and institutional guidance. Evidence was interpreted according to study design, population selection, and applicability rather than pooled into a new effect estimate. Observational studies support history- and examination-directed evaluation, but heterogeneous outcome definitions, selective testing, and limited follow-up constrain conclusions about safety. We propose an assessment framework separating physiological instability, stable presentations with cardiac warning features, stable presentations suggesting a noncardiac disorder, and provisionally low-risk presentations. Low risk is a conditional clinical assessment requiring an adequate history, reassuring vital signs and examination, and no concerning disease-specific features; it is not a quantified probability or a discharge rule. Conservative outpatient management additionally requires a workable reassessment plan. Troponin testing should address a plausible concern for myocardial injury, and its interpretation depends on pretest probability, assay characteristics, and symptom timing. Point-of-care ultrasound is an optional, expertise-dependent adjunct with limited direct evidence in unselected pediatric chest pain. Clinical setting, access to investigations and specialists, and follow-up reliability affect the appropriate next step. The framework organizes existing evidence and identifies implementation gaps; it has not been derived or validated as a clinical decision rule and requires prospective evaluation before protocol-level adoption.

articles.title: Contextual conditions shaping the upward referral of obstetric emergencies from community health centres in the Eastern Cape: a Straussian Grounded Theory study.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Maternal mortality remains a significant public health concern in South Africa, particularly in resource limited settings where timely access to higher-level care is vital. Community Health Centres are the first point of contact for women faced with obstetric emergencies, yet systemic, contextual, and operational challenges impede effective upward referral. Guided by Straussian Grounded Theory, this qualitative study explored the contextual conditions shaping the upward referral of obstetric emergencies in the OR Tambo district, Eastern Cape.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Data was collected through focus group discussions, in-depth interviews, document analysis, and observations, and analysed using open, axial, and selective coding.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Findings revealed four key categories which were resource limitations, workforce and budget gaps, communication and Emergency Medical Services, geographical and socioeconomic barriers.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: These interrelated conditions contribute to delayed, unsafe, and fragmented referrals, placing mothers and newborns at heightened risk of further complicated conditions. Addressing these systemic challenges requires multi-sectoral interventions, including regular multidisciplinary emergency obstetric training, strengthened referral communication, investment in transport infrastructure and facility-based ambulances.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: This study indicates that strengthening referral process is essential in enhancing timely and safe obstetric care, ultimately reducing preventable maternal and neonatal mortality.

articles.title: Development and evaluation of an intelligent centralized transportation dispatching information system in a large tertiary hospital: a single-center retrospective observational study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Traditional hospital central transportation adopts manual telephone dispatch, bringing high communication costs, poor traceability, mismatched resources and weak quality control, which impede clinical efficiency and patient safety. This study designs an intelligent dispatching system integrating RFID, IoT and mobile terminals, and assesses its performance in a large tertiary hospital.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A single-center retrospective observational study was carried out at West China Hospital. The system combines RFID-IoT real-time positioning and multi-objective scheduling algorithms, with two-way connections to HIS, examination platforms and PDAs. We analyzed system data of transport tasks, time metrics, tool utilization and patient satisfaction from Jan 1 to Jun 30, 2026 (post-implementation). Pre-2025 non-digital records were only used for qualitative reference; incomplete raw data excluded formal statistical comparison and inter-period hypothesis testing. Continuous variables were median (interquartile range); categorical variables n (%).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Over 6 months, the system handled four core transport scenarios. Post-implementation median single-task dispatch time reached 0.57 (0.31-0.82) min, and emergency examination transport time 24.3 (13.41-32.87) min. Among 24,545 tool records, independent ambulation (54.5%) and wheelchairs (32.0%) made up 86.5% of transports, stretchers (6.5%) and hospital beds (7.0%) for critical and postoperative patients accounted for the rest 13.5%. In 5,508 surveyed inpatients, overall transport satisfaction hit 97.78%, with item-level satisfaction rates ranging from 95.51% (staff attentiveness) to 98.14% (staff appearance/professional grooming).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: This single-center retrospective evaluation shows the RFID/IoT intelligent dispatching system achieves brief dispatch & transport durations and high patient satisfaction. Without matched complete pre-implementation baseline data, results only describe post-launch performance instead of causal improvement evidence. Prospective multi-center or interrupted-time-series studies with standardized baselines are required to verify its incremental value.

articles.title: Abbreviated Point-of-Care-Ultrasound Volume Assessment for Outpatient Hemodialysis Patients.
articles.journal: Mayo Clin Proc Innov Qual Outcomes
articles.journal_full: Mayo Clinic proceedings. Innovations, quality & outcomes

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To evaluate the safety and feasibility of an abbreviated lung and inferior vena cava (IVC) point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) protocol for outpatient hemodialysis volume assessment when compared with standard practice.

abstract.label: PATIENTS AND METHODS
abstract.text: In this prospective case-control study, adults receiving long-term in-center hemodialysis underwent abbreviated POCUS-assisted assessment (n=15, 34%) or standard clinical assessment (non-POCUS, n=29, 66%). POCUS was performed during dialysis using a 6-zone lung ultrasound protocol with IVC assessment. Hypervolemia was defined as ≥3 B lines in ≥2 lung zones with bilateral involvement or an IVC diameter ≥2.1 cm with <50% collapsibility. The primary outcome was change in estimated dry weight (EDW) guided by POCUS when compared with standard clinical assessment. Secondary outcomes included falls, all-cause and hypervolemia-related hospitalizations, antihypertensive medication changes, and mortality.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: All POCUS participants (15/15, 100%) met hypervolemia criteria at the initial assessment and underwent EDW reduction; 46.7% met criteria at repeat assessment. Median POCUS examination time was 6 minutes (range 4-10). Reductions in prescribed EDW occurred more frequently in the POCUS group (100% vs 41.4%). Postdialysis weight remained higher relative to new prescribed EDW in the POCUS group at study end. No significant differences were observed in intradialytic blood pressure (P=.24), falls (P=.98), or hospitalizations (P=.67), and no hypervolemia-related hospitalizations (P=.54) occurred in the POCUS group.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: An abbreviated 6-zone lung and IVC POCUS protocol is feasible and safe in outpatient hemodialysis and prompts earlier EDW adjustment. Larger randomized studies are needed to determine its impact on sustained volume control and clinical outcomes.

articles.title: A comparison of health care utilization among insured working-age adults in the state of Virginia, U.S. by long COVID and disabling condition status in 2022.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Americans with disabilities experience more medical interactions and greater access barriers than those without. After the COVID-19 pandemic, Long COVID (LCOVID) emerged as a chronic condition. Few studies examine patterns among people with disabling conditions who develop LCOVID. This study compared healthcare utilization rates among individuals with and without LCOVID and/or a potentially disabling condition (PDC) among working-age adults in Virginia's insurance plans in 2022.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Retrospective analysis using 2021-22 administrative claims data from Virginia's All-Payer Claims Database estimated rates of primary, emergency, and inpatient care among adults aged 18-64 with PDC(s) and LCOVID. Disabling conditions were identified using specifications from the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services, and LCOVID was identified using the ICD-10 code U09.9. Members were grouped by PDC/LCOVID status, sex and age. We applied regression models to estimate rates and compare differences across diagnostic groups.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among most groups, individuals with both PDCs and LCOVID had the highest rates of primary, emergency, and inpatient utilization. Those with LCOVID or PDC alone also often had higher utilization than those with neither.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: These findings underscore the need for accessible, cost-effective care for people with disabling conditions and Long COVID.

articles.title: Case Report: Fatal recurrent rupture of multiple pancreatic pseudoaneurysms following acute alcoholic pancreatitis.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Pancreatic pseudoaneurysm (PPA) is a severe and life-threatening vascular complication of pancreatitis. This case highlights the critical need for comprehensive vascular assessment and surveillance in patients with alcoholic pancreatitis to prevent fatal adverse outcomes.

abstract.label: CASE PRESENTATION
abstract.text: A 53-year-old man with a 30-year history of heavy alcohol intake (500 mL of 52% ABV Baijiu daily, corresponding to an estimated 205 g pure ethanol per day) presented to our emergency department with hematemesis and hemorrhagic shock on 2 April 2026. He was diagnosed with acute pancreatitis complicated by a pancreatic pseudocyst at another hospital in November 2025 but did not receive standardized follow-up and treatment. Contrast-enhanced CT confirmed rupture of a pancreatic head pseudoaneurysm with hemorrhage extending into the duodenum. Emergency transarterial embolization of the gastroduodenal artery was performed, and hematemesis resolved temporarily. Subsequently, the patient developed progressive abdominal pain, distension, and peritoneal irritation signs. Repeat CT confirmed recurrent intra-abdominal hemorrhage. A second digital subtraction angiography (DSA) identified an unrecognized feeding branch arising from the superior mesenteric artery (SMA) supplying the pancreatic head pseudoaneurysm, which was successfully embolized. The patient's condition stabilized temporarily, with a gradual increase in hemoglobin levels. On 14 April 2026, the patient suffered sudden severe abdominal pain and abdominal distension. Follow-up contrast-enhanced CT revealed enlargement and rupture of a pre-existing tiny pseudoaneurysm in the splenic hilum, resulting in massive intra-abdominal hemorrhage. The patient developed refractory hemorrhagic shock followed by cardiac arrest during preparation for emergency endovascular intervention and ultimately died. Post-embolization hemodynamic changes may have contributed to progressive enlargement and subsequent rupture of the pre-existing lesion, although this causal mechanism cannot be definitively proven in this single case.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: This case illustrates that pancreatitis-associated pseudoaneurysms may be multifocal. Successful control of a dominant bleeding lesion does not eliminate the risk of rupture of the separate pre-existing small pseudoaneurysm, and incomplete initial angiography limited only to the celiac trunk may miss SMA feeding branches, even after technically successful initial endovascular intervention for pancreatitis-associated pseudoaneurysm.

articles.title: Knowledge, attitudes, and practices of emergency nurses regarding sepsis nutritional management: a multicenter cross-sectional study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Nutritional management is an important component of supportive care for patients with sepsis, but its implementation in emergency settings may be challenging alongside other time-critical priorities. This study assessed emergency department (ED) nurses' knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) regarding nutritional management in patients with sepsis.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This multicenter cross-sectional study was conducted among ED nurses from hospitals in Jiangsu Province, China, between January and May 2026. A structured Chinese questionnaire with satisfactory internal consistency was used to assess KAP, with KAP levels descriptively classified using modified Bloom's cut-off criteria. Multivariable linear regression was performed to identify factors associated with KAP scores, and structural equation modeling (SEM) was used to further evaluate the direct and indirect relationships among KAP domains.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 630 valid questionnaires were analyzed, including 558 female nurses (88.6%). The median knowledge, attitude, and practice scores were 9.00 (9.00, 15.00), 40.50 (36.00, 45.00), and 29.00 (22.25, 36.00), respectively, out of possible ranges of 0-18, 9-45, and 9-45. In multivariable analyses, nurses without recent training had significantly lower knowledge scores (β = -4.676, 95% CI: -5.386 to -3.965, p < 0.001) and practice scores (β = -3.014, 95% CI: -4.296 to -1.732, p < 0.001). Higher knowledge scores were independently associated with more positive attitudes (β = 0.419, 95% CI: 0.337 to 0.501, p < 0.001) and better practices (β = 0.860, 95% CI: 0.723 to 0.997, p < 0.001), while higher attitude scores were also independently associated with better practices (β = 0.415, 95% CI: 0.294 to 0.537, p < 0.001). SEM demonstrated that knowledge had significant direct effects on attitude (β = 0.470, 95% CI: 0.404-0.536, p < 0.001) and practice (β = 0.512, 95% CI: 0.432-0.589, p < 0.001), and also had an indirect effect on practice through attitude (β = 0.100, 95% CI: 0.061-0.140, p < 0.001).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: ED nurses showed insufficient knowledge, positive attitudes and moderate practice toward nutritional management in patients with sepsis. The observed associations of knowledge with both attitude and practice support the potential value of targeted, practice-oriented training, together with standardized documentation and workflow-based support.

articles.title: Constipation Not So Vibrant: A Case Report of Colonic Obstruction From Capsule Retention.
articles.journal: J Am Coll Emerg Physicians Open
articles.journal_full: Journal of the American College of Emergency Physicians open

abstract.text: Vibrating capsules represent a novel, nonpharmacologic approach for chronic idiopathic constipation, with favorable safety profiles in clinical trials, showing no reported retention events. Although generally well tolerated, patients with severe motility disorders and use of narcotics pose risk of retention of capsules. We report a case of a 73-year-old woman with a history of gastroparesis and slow-transit constipation, who developed colonic retention of multiple vibrating capsules, requiring colonoscopic retrieval. Careful patient selection, monitoring, and timely imaging may prevent complications when treating patients with vibrating capsules.

articles.title: Temporal trends in bystander cardiopulmonary resuscitation and favourable neurological outcome among older patients with out-of-hospital cardiac arrest stratified by bystander-patient relationship and age: a JCS-ReSS study.

abstract.label: AIM
abstract.text: To describe temporal trends in bystander cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) and favourable neurological outcomes among older patients with bystander-witnessed out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) according to bystander-patient relationship and age.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A total of 322,943 patients aged ≥65 years with bystander-witnessed OHCA of cardiac origin were enrolled from the All-Japan Utstein Registry (2005-2022). Patients were stratified by age (65-74, 75-89, and ≥90 years) and bystander type (family member, friend/colleague/passerby, or other). Temporal trends in the proportions of bystander CPR and favourable neurological outcome at 1-month, defined as Cerebral Performance Category (CPC) 1-2, were assessed using the Cochran-Armitage test.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: During the study period, the annual proportions of bystander CPR and CPC 1-2 in family member-witnessed OHCAs significantly increased across all age groups (all p for trend <0.001). However, bystander CPR remained at approximately 50% in all age groups. In other-witnessed OHCAs, bystander CPR also significantly increased across all age groups (all p for trend <0.001). However, CPC 1-2 significantly increased only in those aged 65-74 years (p for trend <0.05), with no significant temporal trend in older groups. Among those aged ≥90 years, bystander CPR increased to approximately 80%, whereas CPC 1-2 remained at approximately 1%, with no significant temporal trend.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Temporal trends in bystander CPR and CPC 1-2 varied according to bystander-patient relationship and age. Further investigation is warranted to identify the factors underlying the observed differences in bystander CPR and favourable neurological outcomes.

articles.title: Evaluating cardiopulmonary resuscitation in "The Pitt": accuracy, clinical realism, and adherence to international resuscitation guidelines.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Medical television dramas shape public perceptions of cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR). The Pitt has been praised for its clinical realism but has not been systematically evaluated. We assessed adherence of televised CPR to current European Resuscitation Council (ERC) and American Heart Association (AHA) guidelines.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: All cardiac arrest (CA) scenarios requiring chest compressions or defibrillation in seasons 1 & 2 (30 episodes) of The Pitt were prospectively analysed using a standardized assessment via an electronic case report form based on Utstein-style variables by at least 2 emergency and/or intensive care physicians experienced in CA management.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Seventeen CA were identified. Most occurred in hospital (65%, n = 11/17) and had medical causes (59%, n = 10/17). ROSC was achieved in 56% (n = 9/16), and survival to discharge in 46% (n = 6/13). Key elements of the initial assessment, including consciousness and pulse checks, were fully guideline compliant, and correct hand placement was observed in 94% (n = 15/16). In contrast, guideline-compliant compression rate were achieved in only 19% (n = 3/16) of assessable cases, respectively, and pre-airway 30:2 compression-to-ventilation ratios were absent. Immediate post-shock rhythm reassessments were observed in 78% (n = 7/9) of appropriate cases. Nevertheless, no inappropriate shocks were delivered during asystole, and rhythm-based pharmacotherapy was appropriate, although medication timing and sequence could not be reliably assessed.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The Pitt provides a highly realistic portrayal of cardiac arrest, although manual CPR technique and some algorithmic details remain imperfect.

articles.title: Missed Perforated Appendicitis in a Nonverbal Patient with Autism and Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy: A Case Report.

abstract.text: Background and Clinical Significance: A 4-year-old nonverbal boy with level 3 autism spectrum disorder and Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) who was receiving chronic prednisone therapy presented to the emergency room with acute appendicitis. The diagnosis was significantly delayed due to atypical pain presentation, a potentially blunted inflammatory response from chronic steroid use, and an uncertain contribution from DMD-related muscle weakness. Case Presentation: The patient presented with five days of fever, poor oral intake, decreased stool output and behavioral changes. Initial physical examination and evaluation over two emergency department visits failed to establish the diagnosis. By the third visit, the patient exhibited abdominal distension, hypoactive bowel sounds, and bandemia. Computed tomography demonstrated perforated appendicitis with a walled-off abscess. Nonoperative management was unsuccessful, resulting in the development of multiple intra-abdominal abscesses that required percutaneous drainage. Following a 10-day hospitalization, the patient improved and was discharged. He subsequently underwent a scheduled laparoscopic appendectomy two months later, with pathology demonstrating persistent inflammation. Conclusions: This case raises awareness of the atypical presentation of pain in children with autism and the potential for DMD and chronic steroid therapy to complicate clinical assessment. These factors should prompt clinicians to maintain a low threshold for advanced imaging when clinical concern is present. It also illustrates the importance of close monitoring during nonoperative management of perforated appendicitis in medically complex or immunosuppressed children.

articles.title: Effect of AI-assisted radiographic fracture detection on paediatric emergency department length of stay through fracture exclusion: A before-after cohort study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Artificial intelligence-assisted radiographic fracture detection tools (AI-RFDT) have the potential to support confident fracture exclusion by physicians in the paediatric emergency department (ED), where presentations for suspected fractures substantially outnumber confirmed fractures. This study aimed to evaluate whether implementation of AI-RFDT in a paediatric ED is associated with reduced length of stay (LOS) among patients presenting with suspected fractures, and to determine whether any observed effect is specifically mediated through the fracture-exclusion pathway.

abstract.label: PATIENTS AND METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective before-after cohort study was conducted at a single tertiary paediatric ED. AI-RFDT (BoneView, Gleamer, Paris, France) was deployed on 1 October 2023 as a passive, second-read decision-support tool. The study population comprised 4172 paediatric patients with rule-out fracture diagnoses (fracture-excluded; F-E) during standard working hours (08:00-15:59; pre-AI n = 2514; post-AI n = 1658). Fracture-confirmed (F-C) patients served as a pre-specified internal control (n = 1155). The primary outcome was ED LOS; secondary outcomes were orthopaedic consultation rate, LOS by consultation status, anatomical subgroup LOS, and 30-day re-admission.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Orthopaedic consultation rates in the paediatric ED decreased from 73% to 68.3% (Δ -4.7 %age points, p = 0.002). The greatest reduction was observed in patients discharged without orthopaedic consultation (2.25→1.78 h, Δ -28 min, p < 0.001), while those with confirmed fractures demonstrated no significant change in LOS (Δ+3 min, p = 0.51). 30-day re-admission rates remained unchanged (6.9% vs 6.9%, p = 1.00). Wrist and forearm injuries demonstrated the greatest LOS reduction (Δ -24 min, p = 0.004).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Deployment of AI-RFDT in a paediatric ED was associated with a reduction in LOS that was concentrated among patients discharged without orthopaedic consultation. The absence of LOS change in confirmed-fracture controls supports a mechanism specific to fracture exclusion rather than generalised care acceleration.

articles.title: Parental perceptions of child and family mental health and behavioural adjustment following a mass school shooting in Serbia.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Study examined parental perceptions of their own and children's mental health and behavioural responses among parents who were not directly or indirectly exposed to the 2023 school shooting in Serbia.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: The study sample included 1,927 parents. The questionnaire assessed pre-event child mental health characteristics and support utilisation, parental threat perception, emotional distress, functional disruption of daily routines, observed child emotional and behavioural changes, help-seeking behaviour, and perceived access to mental health support.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Prior to the shooting, 11.7% of children had a psychiatric diagnosis. Following the shooting, 85.2% of parents reported moderate-to-high concern for child safety, 38.7% reported marked difficulty sending children back to school, and 48.0% reported difficulty controlling intrusive thoughts about child victimization. Most parents observed no emotional or behavioural changes in their children; this finding should be interpreted as an absence of parent-observed changes rather than clinically defined resilience, given the reliance on parental report alone. However, children with pre-existing difficulties showed significantly higher rates of post-event worsening. Mothers reported greater distress and impairment than fathers across all domains. Post-event utilisation of formal mental health services was low (3.8% for children, 2.9% for self).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Findings suggest that mass school shootings may be associated with substantial parental distress and functional disruption even without direct or indirect exposure. The gap between epidemiological estimates and low pre-event diagnosis rates raises concern about possible under-recognition of child mental health needs. Low help-seeking highlights the importance of accessible, non-stigmatising psychosocial support, particularly school-based psychoeducation, rather than formal clinical treatment alone. Findings should be interpreted in light of methodological limitations.

articles.title: Principles, concepts, and perspectives for the improvement of decompression procedures: a Neo-Haldanian approach bridging bubble physics and decompression physiology.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: This paper is a narrative review and theoretical perspective presenting principles, concepts, and perspectives for improving decompression procedures. It distinguishes three levels of evidence: established observations, hypotheses with experimental support, and mechanistic scenarios that remain hypothetical.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We organize decompression around two linked dimensions: bubbles as the primary physical event and microparticles (MPs) as a physiological consequence. We hypothesize that a substantial proportion of decompression-related microbubbles originate from pre-existing gas micronuclei associated with active hydrophobic sites (AHS) at three locations: distal arterial, venous, and extravascular. From these assumptions, five bubble scenarios are considered: growth and detachment from distal arterial AHS; growth and detachment from venous AHS; pulmonary bubble filtration; survival of arterial gas microbubbles and their potential target organs; and intravascular bubble development. Physiological factors may generate MPs, endothelial dysfunction, systemic inflammation, and possibly a secondary generation of microbubbles.

abstract.label: RESULTS AND DISCUSSION
abstract.text: The proposed scenarios align with decompression sickness (DCS) pathophysiology across five target organ systems: skin, brain, inner ear, spinal cord, and musculoskeletal tissue. Inflammatory stress appears important for defining post-dive intervals and multiday diving patterns. Designing decompression procedures therefore requires integrating individual variability and dive history; dive characteristics such as rapid ascents, yo-yo diving, and surface decompression; the bubble scenarios triggered during ascent; and accumulated oxidative stress, oxy-inflammation, and endothelial damage that modify susceptibility to DCS.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: There is no single ultimate decompression algorithm; rather, different strategies reflect different experience, assumptions, and operational contexts.

articles.title: Development and internal validation of triage-stage prediction models for short-term critical outcomes among adult emergency department patients entering observation or hospital-based care: a retrospective study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Risk stratification at emergency department triage may help identify patients who require closer assessment or monitoring. However, prediction models that rely only on information available at the triage stage remain less well evaluated. This study aimed to develop and internally validate machine learning models based on triage-stage information for predicting short-term critical outcomes in adult emergency department patients and to interpret a representative explainable model using SHAP analysis.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective observational study included 1,842 consecutive adult patients who completed standardized electronic triage and subsequently entered an emergency observation or hospital-based care pathway at a tertiary general hospital between January 2022 and December 2025. The prediction time point and landmark were defined as completion of electronic emergency triage. Only patients who were free of all outcome components at the landmark were included, and candidate predictors were restricted to routinely available information recorded no later than triage completion. The primary outcome was the first critical event occurring during the subsequent 72 h: intensive care unit admission, endotracheal intubation or invasive mechanical ventilation, cardiopulmonary resuscitation, objectively documented escalation involving an implemented resuscitation-level intervention, or in-hospital death. Additional sensitivity analyses restricted the outcome to intensive care unit admission, intubation or invasive ventilation, cardiopulmonary resuscitation, or death and refitted the model without emergency triage level. The cohort was randomly divided into a development cohort and a 30% hold-out cohort. Because the hold-out cohort had already been examined during the original analysis, it was not considered an independent validation set. The primary internal-validation analysis therefore consisted of 10 repetitions of nested cross-validation within the development cohort, using five stratified outer folds for performance estimation and four stratified inner folds for preprocessing and hyperparameter tuning. Logistic regression, random forest, support vector machine, XGBoost, and LightGBM were evaluated using the same resampling framework. The previously examined exploratory hold-out cohort was retained only for secondary exploratory analysis. Model performance was assessed using discrimination, calibration, classification metrics, Brier score, decision-curve analysis, and SHAP-based interpretation. Bootstrap optimism correction was additionally used to assess overfitting.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: All 1,842 included patients were event-free at triage completion, and 214 experienced a short-term critical outcome during the subsequent 72-hour period, corresponding to an event rate of 11.6%. The development cohort included 1,289 patients with 150 events, and the previously examined exploratory hold-out cohort included 553 patients with 64 events. In 10 repetitions of nested cross-validation, the mean AUCs were 0.821 ± 0.012 for logistic regression, 0.817 ± 0.015 for random forest, 0.752 ± 0.018 for support vector machine, 0.831 ± 0.013 for XGBoost, and 0.833 ± 0.014 for LightGBM. XGBoost was highest ranked in 42% of repeated outer-validation results, LightGBM in 48%, and logistic regression in 10%. These primary internal-validation results supported broadly comparable performance among XGBoost, LightGBM, and logistic regression rather than consistent superiority of one algorithm. In the secondary exploratory analysis, the representative XGBoost model achieved an AUC of 0.828 in the previously examined exploratory hold-out cohort. At the development-derived threshold of 0.106, its accuracy was 0.770, sensitivity 0.656, specificity 0.785, positive predictive value 0.286, negative predictive value 0.946, F1 score 0.398, and Brier score 0.080. Its paired comparisons, sensitivity analyses, calibration, decision-curve analysis, and SHAP findings in this cohort were interpreted as exploratory.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Repeated nested cross-validation showed broadly comparable discrimination for XGBoost, LightGBM, and logistic regression in predicting post-triage short-term critical outcomes. XGBoost was retained as a representative explainable model, whereas its performance and benchmark comparisons in the previously examined exploratory hold-out cohort should be regarded as secondary exploratory analyses. The study does not establish the superiority or independent validation of XGBoost. Evaluation in a genuinely unused temporal cohort and external prospective validation remain necessary before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Case Report: Delayed complete transection of the sigmoid colon after severe pelvic fracture leading to septic shock.

abstract.text: Severe pelvic fractures caused by high-energy trauma may be complicated by bowel injuries. These injuries may be evident at initial presentation or remain occult, resulting in delayed diagnosis. Delayed complete transection of the sigmoid colon associated with pelvic fractures is extremely rare. We describe a 57-year-old woman who was admitted to the Intensive Care Unit (ICU) following a traffic accident that resulted in a Young-Burgess lateral compression type III pelvic ring injury, hemorrhagic shock, impaired consciousness, and multiple associated injuries. Abdominal CT on post-injury days 1, 2, and 3, emergency focused assessment with sonography for trauma (FAST), and repeated bedside ultrasonography showed no definite bowel injury. Bowel sounds were normal on admission, reduced on day 2, and absent from day 3, but abdominal symptoms could not be assessed reliably. Some inflammatory and organ-function indices partially declined after antimicrobial and supportive treatment. On day 6, abrupt biomarker re-elevation, high fever, progressive abdominal distension, and hemodynamic deterioration prompted repeat CT, which demonstrated extraluminal gas adjacent to the sigmoid colon. Emergency laparotomy confirmed complete sigmoid transection with partial stump necrosis and extensive fecal contamination. The patient survived after colectomy, colostomy, prolonged intensive care, and staged pelvic fixation. This case shows that bowel injury may continue to progress despite repeated negative CT and ultrasonographic examinations and transient improvement in inflammatory markers. When a high-risk mechanism and the clinical trajectory remain discordant, renewed surgical assessment and escalation beyond repeated noninvasive observation should be considered.

articles.title: The mediating role of out-of-hospital adherence between health literacy and quality of life in Chinese stroke survivors: a cross-sectional study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Stroke, the second foremost cause of mortality globally, imposes a considerable disease burden in China. Limited health literacy and difficulties adhering to post-discharge care may be associated with poorer quality of life among stroke survivors. However, the extent to which out-of-hospital adherence statistically accounts for the association between health literacy and quality of life remains insufficiently characterized.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To examine associations among health literacy, out-of-hospital adherence, and quality of life, and to assess whether out-of-hospital adherence statistically mediates the association between health literacy and quality of life in a cross-sectional sample of stroke survivors.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A cross-sectional study included 509 participants recruited through convenience sampling from four traditional Chinese medicine hospitals in Shanghai. Health literacy, out-of-hospital adherence, and stroke-specific quality of life were assessed using Chinese-language instruments. Statistical mediation was examined using PROCESS Model 4 with 5,000 bootstrap resamples.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Stroke survivors' health literacy averaged 31.40 ± 6.78 (below threshold), with analysis skills scoring lowest (5.37 ± 1.17); Health literacy was positively correlated with quality of life (r = 0.409, p < 0.001) and out-of-hospital adherence (r = 0.223, p < 0.001). Adherence was also positively correlated with quality of life (r = 0.461, p < 0.001). The standardized indirect effect through adherence was 0.087 (bootstrap 95% CI: 0.048-0.134), corresponding to approximately 21.3% of the total association in the specified model.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: These cross-sectional findings carry public-health-relevant implications for older adult stroke survivors, a fast-growing vulnerable subgroup amid China's population aging. Population-level targeted strategies to improve health literacy and post-discharge adherence may advance healthy aging by mitigating stroke-related health disparities among older adults, particularly for socio-economically disadvantaged subgroups including those with low educational attainment and rural residence. Further implementation research is required to translate these observational associations into community-tailored preventive interventions for aging populations.

articles.title: The association between older adult abuse and emergency department attendance and mental health service use.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Older adult abuse is associated with a higher risk of mental health disorders but to date older adult abuse has not been investigated as a predictor of mental healthcare outcomes. The purpose of this study was to systematically ascertain recorded abuse and analyse its consequences in older people receiving mental healthcare.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In a large South London mental healthcare data platform, recorded older adult abuse was ascertained using natural language processing algorithms during the first 3 months of contact and investigated in relation to risk of subsequent emergency department attendance and 12-month mental health service contacts. Analyses were stratified by gender, ethnicity, marital status, and deprivation.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 14,591 patients seen by mental health services, 8.4% were recorded as having experienced some form of abuse. Physical abuse was the most common type and financial abuse the least common. In adjusted models, only emotional abuse was associated with emergency department attendance (adjusted hazard ratio: 1.13, 95% CI: 1.02-1.26), but all abuse subtypes were associated with higher mental health service contact, most strongly for recorded sexual abuse (adjusted incidence rate ratio: 2.35, 95% CI: 1.93-2.86).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Abuse experiences are commonly recorded in older adults receiving mental healthcare and are associated with a higher level of mental health service contact. With the use of natural language processing, we were able to successfully gain a deeper insight into the outcomes of abuse experienced by adults referred to a range of services.

articles.title: Receipt of needed care coordination and emergency department utilization among US children with chronic physical pain: a pooled analysis of the 2022-2024 National Survey of Children's Health.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Children with chronic physical pain often require complex, multidisciplinary services across medical, behavioral, and community systems. However, whether receipt of needed care coordination is associated with acute healthcare utilization and care access in this population remains poorly characterized.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a pooled cross-sectional analysis of the 2022-2024 National Survey of Children's Health (NSCH). The analytic cohort included US children aged 6-17 years with caregiver-reported chronic physical pain who had an identified need for care coordination. The exposure was receipt of needed care coordination. The primary outcome was all-cause emergency department (ED) utilization (≥1 visit) in the prior 12 months. Survey-weighted multivariable logistic regression was used, with a minimally adjusted model (sociodemographic factors) and a fully adjusted model (additionally including insurance status, anxiety, depression, and functional difficulties) reported side by side.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 6,326 eligible children (representing an average of 878,491 children annually), weighted 12-month ED visit rates were 29.0% (95% CI, 25.4%-32.5%) for those who received needed care coordination versus 40.0% (95% CI, 36.4%-43.7%) for those who did not. In the minimally adjusted model, receipt of needed care coordination was associated with lower odds of ED utilization (adjusted OR [aOR] 0.61; 95% CI, 0.48-0.76; P < .001; n = 6,310). This association persisted in the fully adjusted model (aOR 0.69; 95% CI, 0.54-0.87; P = .0019; n = 6,145) and was consistent for recurrent ED visits (≥2 visits: aOR 0.54; 95% CI, 0.36-0.79; P = .0015).
