Receipt of care coordination was also associated with substantially lower odds of unmet healthcare needs (aOR 0.32; 95% CI, 0.23-0.45) and forgone mental health care (aOR 0.21; 95% CI, 0.13-0.33). The estimate for hospital stay was imprecise and included the null (aOR 0.61; 95% CI, 0.37-1.01; P = .053).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Among US children with chronic physical pain who needed care coordination, receipt of needed care coordination was associated with lower odds of all-cause ED use and reported healthcare access gaps. These cross-sectional findings do not establish temporal ordering or causal effects and should be evaluated in prospective studies.

articles.title: Hotspot-targeted life support training reduces code blue alarms in a tertiary children's hospital: a single-center observational before-after study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Code Blue emergency alarms are activated by hospital staff for life- threatening patient situations. Despite their low frequency in children's hospitals, ward staff must bridge the first critical minutes until arrival of dedicated emergency response teams. Thus, the aim of this study was to identify hotspots and causes of emergencies, and to evaluate whether a hotspot-specific pediatric basic life support training (PBLS) reduces Code Blue alarms.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This analysis included all Code Blue alarms at the University Children's Hospital Bern before (January 2021-April 2023) and after (January 2024-December 2025) introduction of a hotspot-targeted PBLS program. Following identification of ward-specific hotspots and recurring emergency situations during Period 1, standard PBLS training was reorganized and supplemented by short simulation-based trainings tailored to the most frequent local emergencies. Variables between periods were statistically compared. Incidence rates were calculated per 1000 patient days.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: 65 Code Blue alarms were analyzed. Respiratory emergencies and seizures were the most common causes, with infants and toddlers being the most affected age group. No weekend but a lunch-time effect was observed. Code Blue incidence decreased from 0.58 to 0.21 alarms per 1000 patient-days after implementation (IRR 0.36, 95% CI 0.19-0.66, p < 0.001). Fragility analysis confirmed result robustness, with no evidence of bias from missing data, case mix index, PICU transfer rates, or non-Code Blue Medical Emergency Team (MET) consultations.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Hotspot-specific PBLS training was associated with a marked reduction in pediatric Code Blue alarms. Identification of local emergency patterns may help hospitals develop targeted ward-based training strategies to improve in-hospital emergency management.

articles.title: Rhythm-specific regional variation in neurological outcomes after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest: a nationwide registry study in Japan.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Regional variation in outcomes after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) has been reported worldwide; however, whether its magnitude differs by initial cardiac rhythm remains unknown. This study aimed to evaluate prefecture-level variation in neurological outcomes after OHCA according to initial cardiac rhythm.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective observational study included adult patients with atraumatic OHCA registered in the All-Japan Utstein Registry from 2019 to 2023. Patients were categorized as presenting with a shockable rhythm, pulseless electrical activity (PEA), or asystole according to the initial cardiac rhythm. Mixed-effects logistic regression models were fitted separately for each rhythm group, with favorable neurological outcome at 1 month (defined as a Cerebral Performance Category of 1-2) as the dependent variable and prefecture as a random effect. Prefecture-level variation was quantified using the median odds ratios (MORs).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 616,519 participants, 46,575 had a shockable rhythm, 142,073 had PEA, and 427,871 had asystole. Favorable neurological outcomes occurred in 22.3%, 2.7%, and 0.2% of patients, respectively. The MORs were 1.19 for shockable rhythm, 1.31 for PEA, and 1.65 for asystole, indicating progressively greater prefecture-level variation across rhythm categories.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: The magnitude of prefecture-level variation in favorable neurological outcomes differed by initial cardiac rhythm categories and was greatest among patients with asystole. The mechanisms underlying these regional differences remain unclear. Future investigations of regional and healthcare system characteristics may help identify potentially modifiable factors associated with disparities in OHCA outcomes.

articles.title: Age-specific trends in poisoning-related out-of-hospital cardiac arrest in Japan: a retrospective nationwide registry study.

abstract.label: AIM
abstract.text: Poisoning-related out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) may have distinct age-specific trends. We examined temporal changes in its proportion among all OHCA, population-based incidence, and neurological outcomes in Japan.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In this retrospective nationwide registry study, we analyzed adults aged ≥18 years OHCA treated by emergency medical services (EMS) in the Japanese Utstein registry from 2013 to 2023. Age-specific logistic regression estimated annual trends in the proportion of poisoning-related OHCA, adjusted for age and sex. Poisson regression with age-group population as the exposure estimated incidence trends. Neurological outcome trends were examined secondarily.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 1,400,951 adults with OHCA treated by EMS, 3723 (0.27%) had poisoning-related OHCA. In adults aged 18-29 years, the adjusted odds of poisoning-related OHCA increased (odds ratio per year, 1.027; 95% CI, 1.001-1.054), whereas population-based incidence showed a nonsignificant upward trend (incidence rate ratio, 1.020; 95% CI, 0.995-1.046). All-cause OHCA incidence declined among adults aged 18-29 years (incidence rate ratio, 0.991; 95% CI, 0.983-0.9997). The poisoning proportion decreased at ages 50-64 and ≥65 years; poisoning incidence declined significantly only at ≥65 years. Favorable neurological outcome after poisoning-related OHCA showed no clear improvement (adjusted odds ratio per year, 0.998; 95% CI, 0.949-1.050).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Poisoning-related OHCA became increasingly prominent among young adults but declined among older adults. Although the incidence increase in young adults was not statistically significant, its upward direction, declining all-cause OHCA incidence, and lack of clear neurological outcome improvement suggest increasing clinical importance of poisoning-related OHCA in young adults.

articles.title: Repeated self-directed CPR testing enhances compression depth: evidence from a large retrospective cohort.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: High-quality chest compressions are critical to survival after cardiac arrest, yet CPR skills decline after conventional training. Low-dose, high-frequency (LDHF) training may sustain competence, but large-scale longitudinal evidence from self-directed stations remains limited.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study of healthcare professionals completing at least two manikin-based CPR assessments between June 2023 and April 2026. Automated testing was performed using a self-directed manikin-based simulation station without real-time feedback. Mixed-effects models assessed associations of interval and test-day number with compression depth, rate, recoil, and guideline compliance. Sensitivity analyses modeled test-day number categorically and adjusted depth models for age and recorded sex.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 2558 participants (6232 tests), mean depth increased from 49.8 ± 9.2 mm on test day 1 to 52.5 ± 7.6 mm on test day 2 and remained within guideline targets thereafter; rate and recoil were stable. Interval had a negligible association with depth (0.027 mm per 30 days, p = 0.027) that was attenuated after demographic adjustment (p = 0.101). Per 30 days, interval was weakly associated with depth compliance, but not rate or combined compliance. Later test-day number was associated with higher depth (1.59 mm per test day, p < 0.001), with consistent categorical and adjusted findings.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Later test-day number was consistently associated with higher depth, whereas interval explained little variation. Although the observational design cannot establish station effectiveness or an optimal refresher interval, this study provides one of the largest longitudinal descriptions of repeated self-directed CPR assessment in certified healthcare professionals.

articles.title: Association between family member bystander CPR and survival for out-of-hospital cardiac arrest.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Bystander CPR is associated with higher likelihood of survival in out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA). Whether family member-administered bystander CPR is associated with higher survival is not fully understood, even though family members are often present when arrests occur at home and are best positioned to initiate CPR.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Within the Cardiac Arrest Registry to Enhance Survival (CARES) registry, we conducted a retrospective cohort study. Using multivariable mixed-effect logistic regression, we examined the association between family member (FM) and non-family member (non-FM) bystander CPR, as compared to those not receiving bystander CPR, with a primary outcome of survival to hospital discharge and secondary outcome of favorable neurological survival (survival without severe neurological deficits).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: We identified 824,960 non-traumatic OHCAs between 2013 and 2024. Mean age was 62.2 ± 17.1 years and 35.6% were female. Overall, 78,139 (9.5%) people survived to hospital discharge. Compared to those with no bystander CPR (7.3%), higher survival rates occurred in those receiving FM-bystander CPR (9.6%; adjusted OR: 1.31 [95% CI: 1.29-1.34], p < 0.001) and non-FM bystander CPR (17.3%; adjusted OR: 1.58 [95% CI: 1.55-1.62], p < 0.001). When directly comparing the two bystander groups, those with non-FM bystander CPR had higher rates of survival than those with FM bystander CPR (adjusted OR: 1.21 [95% CI: 1.18, 1.24], p < 0.001). A similar pattern was observed with the outcome of favorable neurological survival.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Both non-FM and FM-bystander CPR were associated with higher survival outcome rates compared to no bystander CPR while non-FM CPR was associated with higher survival compared to FM-CPR.

articles.title: Fight, flight, freeze, fawn: mapping emergency department staff stress responses to workplace violence - a mixed-methods study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Workplace violence and aggression are escalating in emergency departments (EDs) globally, yet the self-reported psychological and behavioural responses in clinicians to such stressors remain underexplored. Trauma theory conceptualises stress responses as fight, flight, freeze, and fawn (4Fs); but how these responses manifest in ED staff before, during and after violent incidents has received limited empirical attention.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This mixed-methods study analysed data collected between 2019 and 2023 across four emergency departments within one Australian local health district. Data sources included semi-structured interviews (2019; n = 20), focus groups (2021; n = 30 participants), a cross-sectional survey (2023; n = 61), and follow-up interviews (2023; n = 12). Qualitative data were analysed using Braun and Clarke's six-phase thematic analysis, applying a deductive framework informed by the 4Fs. Quantitative survey data were integrated to examine the distribution of stress responses across reported incidents.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Across all data sources, 123 ED staff described 145 coded instances of the 4F stress responses: fight (n=94); flight (n=24), freeze (n=15), and fawn (n=12). Four overarching themes that underpinned these responses were identified: 1) Moral and emotional impact on clinicians, 2) Safety systems interface, 3) Organisational constraints and environment and 4) Patient Complexity. Participants described sustained hyperarousal, anticipatory vigilance, moral distress, emotional withdrawal, and appeasement behaviours arising from repeated exposure to violence. While Code Black responses were viewed as a structured and effective "organised fight" mechanism, this was compromised by inconsistent training, role ambiguity, and limited post-incident support which contributed to burnout, disengagement, and workforce attrition.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Emergency department clinicians operate in persistently threatening environments that drive recurrent activation of fight, flight, freeze, and fawn responses with cumulative individual and system-level consequences. Behavioural emergencies warrant the same level of preparation, standardisation, and organisational support as other high-risk clinical events, such as a Code Blue - a life-threatening medical event with a responding Medical Emergency Team. Trauma-informed education team-based training, and embedded post-incident support are critical to safeguarding staff wellbeing and sustaining the ED workforce.

articles.title: Incidence of and return to play from head injury assessments in female, semi-elite, rugby league players.
articles.journal_full: Journal of science and medicine in sport

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: To determine the incidence of Head Injury Assessments in female, semi-elite rugby league players and to explore age- and sex-related differences in Head Injury Assessment rates and return to play periods.

abstract.label: DESIGN
abstract.text: Retrospective cohort study.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Head Injury Assessment data from all matches (n = 258) and training sessions undertaken by Under 17 (U17), Under 19 (U19), and Open-age (Open) group players during the 2023 and 2024 Queensland Rugby League competitions were analysed. Head Injury Assessment incidence rates and ratios, and return to play times following positive Head Injury Assessments (diagnosed concussion) calculated and compared between groups.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Across 2023 and 2024, younger female players (U17 and/or U19) demonstrated significantly higher observed positive Head Injury Assessment rates than Open females, a pattern also observed in male competitions in 2024. Significant age differences were found in incidence rate ratios [95% confidence intervals] for observed positive Head Injury Assessments (2023 female U19 > Open, 2.88 [1.34-6.87], p = 0.003; 2024 female U17 and U19 > Open, 2.66 [1.32-5.51], p = 0.0045 & 1.96 [1.00-3.97], p = 0.037; and 2024 male U17 > Open, 2.18 [1.30-3.57], p = 0.002). Significant sex-related differences were found for the U19 female incidence rate ratios for observed positive and total Head Injury Assessments in 2023 compared to males (2.13 [1.17-3.98], p = 0.008 and 2.13 [1.17-3.98], p = 0.008). Return to play from observed positive Head Injury Assessments was comparable across age groups and sexes in 2023 while in the 2024 timeframes was significantly longer for younger compared to Open age groups.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Younger players demonstrated greater observed positive Head Injury Assessment incidence rates/ratios than their older counterparts, with policy changes between 2023 and 2024 likely contributing to the extended return to play timeframes for younger age groups.

articles.title: In-hospital medication administration prior to in-hospital cardiac arrest: a matched case-control study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Limited research has examined medication administration in patients with in-hospital cardiac arrest (IHCA). We aimed to identify and describe in-hospital medications administered 24 h prior to IHCA compared with matched controls.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This study was a registry-based, matched, case-control study including patients who were hospitalized in the Central Denmark Region from 2017 to 2022. Patients with IHCA were matched with hospitalized controls on age, sex, length, and period of admission. The index time was defined as the time of IHCA for cases, and a corresponding index time was assigned to matched controls. Medication administrations within 24 h prior to index time were identified and divided into 21 groups based on ATC codes, e.g. QTc-prolonging drugs. New medication administrations were defined as no prior redeemed prescription for the same ATC code within 2 years.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 1976 cases and 19,716 controls met the study criteria and were included in the study. Among cases, the most frequently administered medication groups were antithrombotic agents (43% of cases), antibiotics (42%), and diuretics (35%), whereas for controls the groups were antibiotics (33% of controls), antithrombotic agents (33%), and opioids (24%). Overall, cases were administered a median of 11 (IQR: 0-20) medications within 24 h prior to the index time as compared to 5 (IQR: 0-14) medications for controls.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Medications administered in-hospital within 24 h prior to IHCA differed from those in matched controls and were characterized by a higher proportion of newly initiated treatments. These findings may help form new hypotheses on strategies on prevention of IHCA.

articles.title: Emerging therapeutic strategies for medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaw: From microenvironmental modulation to precision medicine (Review).

abstract.text: Medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaw (MRONJ) is a challenging complication associated primarily with antiresorptive and antiangiogenic therapies. Its pathogenesis involves a complex interplay of impaired bone remodeling, angiogenesis, inflammation and infection, immune regulation and soft tissue healing. Established management includes conservative care, antimicrobial and symptomatic treatment when indicated and surgical intervention, however clinical outcomes remain variable. The present review aimed to summarize pharmacological, regenerative, biomaterial-based and physical or adjunctive strategies targeting the pathological microenvironment of MRONJ, with emphasis on their mechanisms of action and clinical evidence. The present review also examines the potential role of precision medicine in individualized risk assessment and treatment. Teriparatide, pentoxifylline/tocopherol, autologous platelet concentrates and human amniotic membrane have varying degrees of clinical support, although evidence remains limited or heterogeneous for several approaches. By contrast, geranylgeraniol, hydrogels, most mesenchymal stromal cell-based or cell-derived strategies, natural products and melatonin are supported predominantly by preclinical or limited clinical evidence. Other adjunctive approaches, including hyperbaric oxygen, ozone therapy, photobiomodulation, laser-assisted surgery and antimicrobial photodynamic therapy, require further validation. Overall, these strategies may complement established management, but their clinical readiness varies. Standardized clinical studies and integration of multidimensional patient data may facilitate more robust evaluation and individualized MRONJ management.

articles.title: Prevalence and predictors of burnout among Chinese medical postgraduates: a multicenter cross-sectional study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Burnout is a vital concern in healthcare and causes multiple adverse outcomes. This study explored the prevalence of burnout among Chinese medical postgraduates and its associated factors.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This cross-sectional study was conducted among medical postgraduates at 15 teaching hospitals across eight cities in Anhui Province, China. Structured questionnaires were administered to collect data on sociodemographic characteristics, occupational exposures, occupational safety factors, anxiety symptoms, and burnout. Multivariate linear regression analysis was applied to identify the predictors of burnout.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 1,276 full-time medical postgraduates were included, with a mean age of 26.68 ± 2.65 years and females accounting for 57.29%. Overall, 30.02% of participants reported no burnout, 32.68% mild, 20.22% moderate, and 17.07% severe burnout. In the fully adjusted model, academic postgraduate and strict compliance with standard operating procedures were independently associated with reduced emotional exhaustion; anesthesiology specialty, a history of sharp injury within the past year, concern about occupational exposure, and anxiety symptoms predicted greater emotional exhaustion. Academic postgraduate, pursuing a doctoral degree, intensive care/emergency medicine specialty, strict compliance with standard operating procedures, hospital pre-training safety education, and adequate access to personal protective equipment independently predicted lower depersonalization; surgery and anesthesiology specialties and anxiety symptoms were linked to greater depersonalization. Advanced age and university occupational safety education were independently associated with lower levels of reduced personal accomplishment; anxiety symptoms were significantly correlated with higher levels of reduced personal accomplishment.

abstract.label: LIMITATIONS
abstract.text: The cross-sectional design only allows assessment of associations rather than causal relationships; reliance on self-reported questionnaires may introduce response bias and social desirability effects; and the sample recruited solely from Anhui Province limits the generalizability of the findings to other regions.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: These findings provide targeted insights for developing effective intervention strategies to alleviate burnout and improve the quality of clinical training.

articles.title: Signal detection of substance-related emergency department visits during UEFA EURO 2024 in Germany: enhancing public health surveillance for future mass gatherings.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Germany hosted the men's UEFA European Championship (EURO 2024) in summer 2024, attracting millions of visitors across multiple cities. Mass gathering events (MGEs) can rapidly alter social environments which impact substance use behaviors, potentially increasing demand on local healthcare systems. In response, the German national public health institute (Robert Koch Institute, RKI) piloted substance-related indicators using routine emergency department (ED) data from the Emergency Department Data Registry throughout the tournament to explore their applicability for real-time emergency department surveillance.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We aimed to monitor substance use patterns in ED visits during EURO 2024 by developing an umbrella syndrome definition for psychotropic substance intoxication (SATX) and two more specific syndrome definitions for acute alcohol intoxication (ATX) and substance intoxication other than alcohol (STX), based on diagnoses, chief complaints, and age criteria. Descriptive analyses compared identified cases during the tournament period (14 June-14 July 2024) with a reference period. Analyses were stratified by sex, age group, and triage level. A quasi-Poisson regression model was used to estimate expected values and 95% prediction intervals (95% PI) for each indicator during the tournament period. Signals were detected when observed case counts exceeded the upper threshold of the 95% PI.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Between 1 January 2018 and 9 September 2024, 5,602,933 visits from 39 EDs were included. Across both the tournament and reference periods, SATX, ATX, and STX cases were more common among males, particularly for ATX. Most SATX and ATX cases occurred among individuals aged 30-59 years, whereas STX cases were most frequent among those aged 20-39 years. Relative increases in triage level 4 cases were observed during the tournament period. During EURO 2024, signals exceeding the upper threshold of the 95% PI were detected for all indicators, including 16 SATX, three ATX, and 13 STX signals. The largest deviation was observed for SATX on 29 June 2024, with 127 observed cases compared to 74 expected cases.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: This study demonstrated that rapid changes in substance-related ED utilization during MGEs can be effectively monitored using the syndrome definitions and signal detection methods, whose application can support public health surveillance during future events.

articles.title: Co-creating point-of-care ultrasound education for family medicine in Ethiopia: reflections on pedagogy, faculty development, and academic partnership.

abstract.text: Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) is increasingly becoming an essential clinical and educational tool in low to middle income countries (LMICs), where formal imaging is often delayed or inaccessible. This commentary reflects on the co-creation and longitudinal implementation of a Family Medicine-focused point-of-care ultrasound education initiative at Addis Ababa University (AAU), developed through the Toronto Addis Ababa Academic Collaboration in Family Medicine (TAAAC-FM). We discuss how this initiative, while addressing an immediate diagnostic need, also functions as a curricular lever for faculty development, a pathway for professional identity formation, and can foster unique pathways for ongoing departmental sustainability. We discuss the partnership structures and equity considerations that shaped program design and situate this work within broader efforts to strengthen Primary Health Care (PHC) and advance Universal Health Coverage (UHC). These reflections offer transferable insight for academic collaborations seeking to align educational innovation with health system transformation in resource-constrained settings.

articles.title: Surgical treatment of osteoradionecrosis of the jaw following radiotherapy for oropharyngeal cancer: A retrospective clinical analysis in a single-center.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND/PURPOSE
abstract.text: Osteoradionecrosis of the jaw (ORNJ) is an intractable disease that develops within the radiation field in patients with head and neck cancer. This study aimed to investigate differences in healing rates among surgical treatments for mandibular ORN that developed after radiotherapy for oropharyngeal cancer.

abstract.label: MATERIALS AND METHODS
abstract.text: We retrospectively evaluated 318 patients who underwent radiotherapy or chemoradiotherapy for oropharyngeal cancer at our institution to determine the incidence of ORNJ. Furthermore, 16 patients (15 males and 1 female) with a mean age of 63.3 years were included in the surgical analysis. Healing was defined as the absence of symptom recurrence for 3 months after surgery. Various factors, including age, sex, use of hyperbaric oxygen therapy, type of surgical treatment, smoking history, alcohol consumption, and nutritional status, were investigated.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among the 318 patients, 36 developed ORNJ, resulting in an incidence rate of 11.3%. Among the 16 surgically treated patients, primary treatments included sequestrectomy in 8 cases, mandibular marginal resection in 1 case, and segmental resection in 7 cases. The overall healing rate was 50.0% (8/16). Of the 16 cases, 8 required secondary treatment. Most cases initially treated with sequestrectomy required secondary treatment, whereas segmental resection achieved the highest healing rate.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: For refractory ORNJ, segmental resection with a vascularized free flap may provide reliable healing by removing necrotic tissue and restoring local blood supply to the ischemic area.

articles.title: Time-deterministic and instruction-dynamic execution: A field-programmable gate array quantum-control processor.

abstract.text: Long-running quantum computations, including error-corrected workloads, place joint demands on instruction availability, measurement-dependent control, and calibration updates. We present time-deterministic and instruction-dynamic execution, a field-programmable gate array (FPGA) quantum-control processor supporting runtime revision at both instruction and parameter levels. Dynamic Instruction Parameter Update (DIPU) supplies one-shot, next-match patches before parameter capture, while Dynamic Instruction Stream Overwrite (DISO) provides guarded replacement, logical deletion, and out-of-line insertion in eligible future regions of a resident program. A moving fetch-visibility guard coordinates instruction updates with execution, and event commitment isolates complete descriptors for independent hardware-timed dispatch. Revision applicability depends on update timing and execution progress; deterministic service applies to committed events under the stated scheduling conditions. The Xilinx ZCU102 implementation uses a 250-MHz control core and a 425-MHz timing/update domain. FPGA-resident measurements at the registered digital interfaces confirmed programmed-cycle dispatch for all tested descriptors committed at least one timing-domain cycle before their timestamps, with downstream ready and the stated first-in, first-out ordering conditions. Separate tests confirmed post-commit timestamp and payload invariance. The minimum all-success mapped DIPU margin was four control-domain cycles, and a replacement of L instruction words completed in L + 5 update-domain cycles under continuous payload delivery. Within the tested guard-distance range, rejected DISO requests reported an error and preserved the resident path, whereas all admitted revisions tested here executed complete revised sequences. These results provide a hardware execution basis for incorporating runtime-generated sequences and parameter corrections into precisely timed quantum computations with feedback.

articles.title: Telemedicine Consultation for Pediatric Trauma in Community ED Visits and Parent Experience of Care: A Stepped-Wedge Cluster-Randomized Clinical Trial.

abstract.label: IMPORTANCE
abstract.text: Telephone consultations for acutely injured children receiving care in emergency departments (EDs) in nonpediatric trauma centers frequently exclude direct communication and informed decision-making with parents. The use of telemedicine to facilitate real-time expert consultation and parental communication with pediatric trauma specialists is underexplored and may improve family experience and support clinical decision-making.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To examine the impact of telemedicine on parent experience of care, parent distress, and transfer frequency for acutely injured children presenting to EDs in nonpediatric trauma centers.

abstract.label: DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS
abstract.text: This stepped-wedge cluster-randomized clinical trial recruited patients between November 30, 2020, and November 27, 2022. Participants included families of children younger than 18 years with acute physical trauma presenting to 1 of 10 nonpediatric trauma centers in northern California. Analyses were conducted between June 2023 and March 2026.

abstract.label: INTERVENTIONS
abstract.text: EDs were randomized to use telemedicine following a standard telephone consultation or the standard of care (telephone consultation only) when consulting with pediatric trauma physicians.

abstract.label: MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES
abstract.text: Primary outcomes were parent experience of care and parent distress measured 3 days or more following the child's injury. Experience of care was measured using ED Consumer Assessment of Healthcare Providers and Systems (CAHPS) questions. Distress was measured using the State-Trait Anxiety Inventory Form Y survey. Modified intention-to-treat analyses were performed to evaluate outcomes.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The study included 595 children with acute physical trauma with a mean (SD) age of 7.6 (5.1) years, of whom 369 (62.0%) were assigned to telemedicine and 226 (38.0%) to standard of care. Summary scores for parent experience of care 3 days post injury were similar between cohorts (adjusted mean difference [AMD], 0.041 [95% CI, -0.008 to 0.090; P = .10]), as were parent distress summary scores (AMD, -0.031 [95% CI, -0.297 to 0.235; P = .82]). The adjusted odds ratio for transfer of patients assigned to telemedicine was 0.59 (95% CI, 0.16 to 2.16; P = .43). Subscale analyses found significantly higher parental ED discharge and/or transfer experience ratings for patients assigned to telemedicine (AMD, 0.104 [95% CI, 0.023 to 0.186; P = .01]).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE
abstract.text: In this randomized clinical trial, telemedicine consultations did not differ statistically significantly from standard care with respect to parent experience of care, distress, and transfer rates. Subscale analyses suggested a potential improvement with telemedicine consultations in parent experience related to ED discharge and interfacility transfers, highlighting a potential benefit in communication and preparation during care transitions.

abstract.label: TRIAL REGISTRATION
abstract.text: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04469036.

articles.title: Storage and Disposal of Unused Prescription Opioids for Acute Pain After Emergency Department Discharge.
authors: Quantity of Opioids for Acute Pain and Limit Unused Medication Group (OPUM), on behalf of the Network of Canadian Emergency Researchers

abstract.label: IMPORTANCE
abstract.text: Opioid misuse is a major public health concern, and unused prescription opioids can contribute to this problem.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To estimate the proportion of unused opioids among patients discharged from the emergency department (ED) for acute pain, evaluate opioid storage and disposal practices, and identify factors that may motivate patients to return unused opioids.

abstract.label: DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS
abstract.text: This cohort study, which was a preplanned substudy of a Canadian multicenter prospective cohort study (Quantity of Opioids for Acute Pain and Limit Unused Medication Group [OPUM] study, with recruitment beginning in May 2019 and follow-up ending in January 2024), included consecutive patients aged 18 years or older discharged from the EDs of 7 hospitals in Québec and Ontario with an opioid prescription for an acute pain condition. Participants were followed up at 2 weeks and 3 months.

abstract.label: EXPOSURE
abstract.text: Opioid prescription for acute pain at ED discharge.

abstract.label: MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES
abstract.text: The main outcomes were the proportion of participants with unused opioids at 2 weeks and 3 months after ED discharge, opioid storage practices at 2 weeks, and opioid disposal practices at 3 months.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 2590 enrolled participants in the cohort, 2047 (79.0%) completed the 2-week follow-up and 1835 (70.8%) completed the 3-month follow-up. Among participants who completed the 3-month follow-up, mean (SD) age was 51.3 (15.4) years, 947 (51.6%) were male, and mean pain intensity score at triage was 7.1 (2.3) out of 10. At 2 weeks, 1521 of 1811 participants (84.0%; 95% CI, 82.2%-85.6%) reported unused opioids; 102 of 1525 (6.7%; 95% CI, 5.5%-8.1%) stored their opioids in a locked area and 393 of 1525 (25.8%; 95% CI, 23.6%-28.0%) out of reach of children or teenagers. At 3 months, 926 of 1495 (61.9%; 95% CI, 59.4%-64.4%) reported unused opioids, kept mostly for possible future pain (534 [57.7%; 95% CI, 54.4%-60.9%]) or because participants forgot or lacked time to return them (262 [28.3%; 95% CI, 25.4%-31.3%]). Only 614 of 1835 participants (33.5%; 95% CI, 31.3%-35.7%) indicated they would voluntarily return opioids to the pharmacy if prompted, while 479 (26.1%; 95% CI, 24.1%-28.2%) would not return them regardless of incentive offered.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE
abstract.text: In this cohort study, 3 months after their ED visit, many participants kept unused prescription opioids at home under suboptimal storage conditions; only one-third were willing to return their opioids to a pharmacy, while more than one-fourth were not. These findings support tailoring opioid prescriptions to individual patient needs to reduce unused medication, alongside strengthening take-back networks and enhancing patient education on safe use, storage, and disposal of opioids.

articles.title: Timeliness of Emergency Care for Intracerebral Hemorrhage Compared With Acute Ischemic Stroke.

abstract.label: IMPORTANCE
abstract.text: Clinical data comparing time to presentation and stroke quality metrics for intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) and acute ischemic stroke (AIS) are limited. Understanding these differences is essential to provide timely care to all stroke subtypes.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To compare prehospital and emergency department (ED) process quality metrics between patients with ICH and AIS.

abstract.label: DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS
abstract.text: Cohort study included patients with AIS and ICH admitted to Get With The Guidelines (GWTG)-Stroke participating hospitals from January 1, 2015, to June 30, 2024, who arrived by emergency medical services (EMS). Data were analyzed from 195 hospitals across the US.

abstract.label: MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES
abstract.text: Prehospital-based and ED-based process metrics (eg, EMS prenotification, door to ED physician assessment time, door to initial brain imaging order) were assessed. Logistic and linear regression models were sequentially adjusted for patient demographics, medical history and presenting factors, and hospital characteristics. Temporal trends of prehospital care metrics were examined.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 195 659 patients (median [IQR] age, 74.0 [63.0-83.0] years; 97 978 [50.1%] female; 31 464 with ICH and 164 195 with AIS) from 195 hospitals were included. The median (IQR) National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score was 14 (6-23) for ICH vs 6 (2-13) for AIS (absolute standardized difference, 0.694). ICH (vs AIS) was associated with higher odds of door-to-ED physician assessment of 10 or fewer minutes after adjusting for patient demographics (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 1.08; 95% CI, 1.02-1.14). This association reversed after adding adjustment for medical history and presenting factors (including NIHSS) and hospital characteristics (aOR, 0.94; 95% CI, 0.89-0.99). This pattern was observed for door to initial brain imaging order of 20 or fewer minutes (demographic-adjusted: aOR, 1.09; 95% CI, 1.02-1.16; fully adjusted with medical history and hospital characteristics: aOR, 0.91; 95% CI, 0.85-0.97). Median last known well to arrival time increased by 32.5% for AIS (151 to 200 minutes; P < .001) and 34.3% for ICH (108 to 145 minutes; P < .001), while rates of EMS prenotification largely remained stable for both ICH and AIS.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE
abstract.text: In this cohort study of patients with acute stroke, patients with ICH arrived at the ED faster but were less likely to achieve care targets. In the context of emerging hyperacute ICH therapies and bundled care models, addressing these differences is essential to optimizing acute stroke outcomes.

articles.title: Minimised SARS-CoV-2 transmission during Tokyo 2020 Olympic and Paralympic Games: insights from enhanced integrated surveillance, Japan, July to September 2021.
articles.journal_full: Euro surveillance : bulletin Europeen sur les maladies transmissibles = European communicable disease bulletin

abstract.text: BACKGROUNDAmid the COVID-19 pandemic, stringent public health measures were taken during the Tokyo 2020 Olympic and Paralympic Games (Tokyo 2020).AIMWe describe SARS-CoV-2 transmission among Games participants and in-person contributors (GPIPC)s.METHODSTokyo 2020-related SARS-CoV-2 infection cases were individuals linked to the event, testing positive for the virus between 1 July-19 September 2021, reported to the Tokyo Metropolitan Government. Attack rates among athletes and team officials were determined. Enhanced case-based surveillance integrating genomic sequencing data supported viral spread investigations among various GPIPC groups.RESULTSA total 804 cases (median age: 35 years, interquartile range (IQR): 27-45; 194 female/610 male) were reported. Among athletes and team officials, attack rates were 0.6% (65/11,400) in Olympic Games and 0.6% (30/4,800) in Paralympic Games. These 95 infections concerned mainly overseas travellers (n = 92), 85 of whom were diagnosed within 14 days of arrival in Japan. Among the 804 cases, whole-genome sequencing data were obtained for 304 (median age: 38 years, IQR: 29-47; 67 female/237 male) with sufficient viral load (as indicated by RT-PCR Cq ≤ 32), including 79% (75/95) of athletes and team officials cases, 74% (131/176) of Games' organisers and media cases, and ˂ 20% (98/533) of remaining cases. Delta variants dominated (94%; 285/304), with domestic (AY.29 lineage) Delta strains prominent among Delta-variant-affected resident cases (96%; 104/108) and Games' organisers and media cases diagnosed ≥ 15 days after entering Japan (97%; 63/65). Overseas Delta strains mostly affected travellers within 14 days of entry, particularly athletes and team officials (97%; 66/68) and Games' organisers and media (29/34).CONCLUSIONMultilayered-risk-reduction measures likely minimised SARS-CoV-2 transmission to athletes.

articles.title: Establishing the Priorities for Emergency Care Research in Australia and Aotearoa New Zealand.

abstract.text: Emergency departments across Australia and Aotearoa New Zealand provide care to nearly 11 million patients annually, yet only a small proportion of care is supported by high-quality evidence. Identifying unanswered research questions that matter most to patients, consumers, whanau, carers and clinicians is essential to reducing research waste and duplication and improving emergency care. The Australasian College for Emergency Medicine, through its Clinical Trials Network, is undertaking a Priority Setting Partnership with the James Lind Alliance and supported by the College of Emergency Nursing Australasia and College of Emergency Nurses New Zealand to establish a prioritised research agenda for emergency care over the next five to 10 years. Using a transparent, evidence-informed process, the partnership aims to ensure research reflects the diverse needs of communities across both countries, including groups historically under-represented in research. Meaningful participation of consumers and clinicians will be essential to translate these priorities into research, funding and improvements in emergency care.

articles.title: Retrospective Assessment of Pulmonary Embolism in Pregnancy and Evaluation of Pregnancy-Adapted YEARS Algorithm.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To explore the diagnostic performance of the pregnancy adapted YEARS algorithm applied to an Australian patient population with concurrent evaluation of its efficacy towards scan reduction.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: The pregnancy adapted YEARS algorithm was applied to pregnant patients retrospectively at this single site study to determine a theoretical pathway in comparison to actual management.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 119 included patients, six (5%) had pulmonary emboli (PE). Retrospective application of the pregnancy-adapted YEARS algorithm missed no PE diagnosis. Theoretical application would have resulted in an 11.7% reduction in total CTPA and V/Q scans performed.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Our study supports the diagnostic performance benefits of the pregnancy adapted YEARS algorithm and can potentially reduce unnecessary imaging.

articles.title: From Deprivation to Expertise: Reframing RRR Emergency Medicine Training.

abstract.text: Regional, rural and remote (RRR) healthcare is frequently compared to metropolitan models despite fundamental differences in geography, service provision, patient preferences and local cultures. Metropolitan bias is reinforced through educational and professional language and by literature that can perpetuate narratives of deprivation, rather than recognising the expertise required to manage uncertainty and resource limitations. The ACEM Emergency Medicine Education and Training (EMET) programme provides on-site FACEM supervision and multidisciplinary education. This is valuable in strengthening trainee confidence, supporting clinical governance and maintaining high training standards in resource-limited settings. However, challenging metropolitan bias also requires strengthening the status of RRR medicine. With research infrastructure concentrated in metropolitan centres, rural hospitals remain under-represented, highlighting the importance of grassroots research initiatives that generate locally relevant data. Challenging metropolitan bias therefore requires a shift in how RRR emergency medicine is represented, taught, researched and governed. EMET offers an important step towards reframing RRR placements as rigorous, supported, and professionally valuable, with potential implications for workforce recruitment and retention.

articles.title: Prognostic Value of Thromboelastography Parameters for Early Trauma-Induced Coagulopathy in Severely Injured Patients: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.journal_full: Academic emergency medicine : official journal of the Society for Academic Emergency Medicine

abstract.label: BACKGROUND AND IMPORTANCE
abstract.text: Early trauma-induced coagulopathy (eTIC) is a major contributor to hemorrhage-related mortality after severe trauma. Viscoelastic testing using thromboelastography (TEG) has been increasingly implemented in trauma resuscitation; however, its prognostic value compared with conventional coagulation testing remains uncertain.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: We evaluated the ability of TEG parameters to detect eTIC, hypofibrinogenemia, and hyperfibrinolysis in severely injured trauma patients. In addition, we assessed their prognostic performance for transfusion requirements and mortality compared with conventional laboratory parameters.

abstract.label: DESIGN
abstract.text: Retrospective single-center cohort study.

abstract.label: SETTINGS AND PARTICIPANTS
abstract.text: Severely injured adult trauma patients admitted to the resuscitation room of a Level I trauma center, between January 2019 and October 2024 were screened.

abstract.label: OUTCOME MEASURES AND ANALYSIS
abstract.text: Primary outcomes were detection of eTIC (INR > 1.2), severe coagulopathy (INR > 1.5), hypofibrinogenemia (< 200 mg/dL), and thrombocytopenia (< 100,000/μL). Secondary outcomes included the ability of coagulation parameters to predict the need for transfusion of ≥ 5 units of packed red blood cells within the first 24 h after admission and in-hospital mortality.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 262 patients were included; median ISS was 29 (IQR 23-41), and in-hospital mortality was 22.8%. eTIC was present in 31.5% of patients. TEG parameters showed moderate discriminatory performance for coagulopathy detection. For eTIC, maximum amplitude achieved an AUC of 0.73, while R-time achieved an AUC of 0.65. Predictive performance improved for severe coagulopathy, with R-time reaching an AUC of 0.81. Hyperfibrinolysis (LY30 > 7%) was uncommon (6.9%). Conventional laboratory parameters, particularly INR, consistently outperformed TEG-derived parameters for prediction of transfusion requirements (AUC 0.85) and mortality (AUC 0.79).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: In severely injured trauma patients, conventional coagulation testing, particularly INR, demonstrated superior prognostic performance compared with individual TEG parameters. Viscoelastic testing may provide complementary information but did not replace standard laboratory testing for prediction of transfusion needs or mortality in this cohort.

abstract.label: TRIAL REGISTRATION
abstract.text: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT07186712.

articles.title: Trainee Access to Major Procedures in an Academic Emergency Department: Are We Doing Enough?

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: The Australasian College for Emergency Medicine requires trainee competency in many procedures; however, real-world practicalities may not align with expectations. The objective of this study was to record the number of procedures performed by trainees in an academic emergency department (ED). Any gaps identified in exposure to procedures could help guide alternative forms of training.

abstract.label: METHOD
abstract.text: A prospective observational study was conducted in a tertiary ED in Perth, Western Australia, between 1 February 2024 and 31 January 2025. Data were collected on 14 procedures via self-reporting using a QR code linked to a Microsoft form. Procedure numbers, median per trainee, and range of procedures are reported. Full-time versus part-time rates were compared. Six-monthly sub-analyses were performed to account for changes in personnel mid-year.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 1413 procedures, 771 (54.6%) were performed by trainees. The median number performed was 10.5 (IQR = 6-23). There was no significant difference between those working full-time versus part-time (median = 15, IQR = 9-23 vs. median = 8, IQR = 4-16; p = 0.11). There was no significant difference between the two 6-month periods (median = 8.5, IQR = 4.3-13.8 vs. median = 9, IQR = 5.75-15, p = 0.51). Procedures commonly performed were sedation (207/405, 51.1%), intubation (121/193, 62.7%) and arterial lines (90/150, 60%).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Access to procedures is limited. Alternative forms of training should be incorporated into education programmes. A lack of exposure has wider implications for assessing competency in emergency medicine and should be considered in any future curriculum update.

articles.title: Chronic Conditions in Residential Care Communities: United States, 2025.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: This report uses 2025 National Post-acute and Long-term Care Study (NPALS) data to examine the characteristics of residential care communities that reported four selected chronic conditions among their current residents: Alzheimer disease and other dementias, heart disease, diabetes, and depression. Data are presented overall and by selected organizational characteristics and adverse events.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Data for this report are from the residential care community survey component of the 2025 wave of the biennial NPALS, conducted by the National Center for Health Statistics. Data analyses were performed using SAS version 9.4, SAS-callable SUDAAN version 11.0.3, and Stata/SE version 17. Analyses accounted for the study's complex survey design, included complex survey weights, and used appropriate subsetting techniques. All estimates presented meet the NCHS standards for confidentiality and reliability unless indicated otherwise.

abstract.label: KEY FINDINGS
abstract.text: In 2025, almost one-half of residential care communities reported all four selected chronic conditions (48%)-Alzheimer disease or other dementias, diabetes, depression, and heart disease-diagnosed among their current residents. Larger (11 or more beds), nonmetropolitan, Northeast, and Midwest residential care communities more commonly reported having all four conditions represented. A higher percentage of nonprofit (54.3%) and chain-affiliated (54.3%) residential care communities, as well as communities using electronic health records (56.7%), reported having all four chronic conditions represented. Residential care communities that reported adverse events among their residents (emergency department visits, hospitalizations, or falls) showed a higher prevalence of having all four conditions represented.

articles.title: Reliability and Validity of the Australian Mental Health Triage Scale in Children's Hospitals.
articles.journal_full: Academic emergency medicine : official journal of the Society for Academic Emergency Medicine

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To evaluate interrater reliability and validity of the Australian Mental Health Triage Scale (AMHTS) for children presenting to the emergency department (ED) with behavioral health symptoms.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a prospective observational study of ED visits by children aged 3-17 with a primary behavioral health symptom at two US children's hospitals. Nurses assigned Emergency Severity Index (ESI) and AMHTS Scores. Interrater reliability was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs) on visits with two independently assigned AMHTS Scores. To evaluate validity, quasi-Poisson regression examined the association of AMHTS Scores and ED resource utilization, adjusted for sociodemographic and clinical factors. Resource use was categorized using the standard ESI definition and an expanded definition incorporating behavioral health-specific resources.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: We included 454 visits (45.4% aged 10-14, 56.2% female) with at least one AMHTS Score, of which 94.1% were ESI 2 and 26.9% were AMHTS 2. Among 221 visits with two AMHTS Scores, ICC was 0.48 (95% CI 0.37, 0.58). Higher-acuity AMHTS Scores were associated with greater resource utilization. Standard resource use was higher for AMHTS Score 1 (Incidence Rate Ratio [IRR] 1.82, 95% CI 1.12, 2.96) and Score 2 (IRR 1.64, 95% CI 1.15, 2.40) versus AMHTS Score 5. When applying the expanded definition, resource use was higher for AMHTS Score 1-4 versus 5.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Interrater reliability of AMHTS was fair, and higher-acuity scores were associated with greater ED resource utilization. AMHTS Scores were more widely distributed than ESI Scores, suggesting a more responsive approach to pediatric behavioral health triage.

articles.title: Prospective analysis of medical conditions and interventions among athlete and non-athlete groups at 2 major international multi-sport tournaments.
articles.journal_full: Advances in clinical and experimental medicine : official organ Wroclaw Medical University

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Medical preparedness for major international multi-sport tournaments requires effective planning of venue medical services for athlete and non-athlete populations. Understanding differences in medical intervention patterns is essential for resource allocation.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: To compare on-site medical interventions, hospital transports, and related medical conditions managed by venue medical teams (VMTs) between athlete and non-athlete populations during 2 international multi-sport tournaments, and to identify sport disciplines associated with higher hospital transport rates among athletes.

abstract.label: MATERIAL AND METHODS
abstract.text: Prospective data from the World Games 2017 and the European Games 2023, both held in Poland, were analyzed. The study included 9,672 athletes and 355,215 non-athletes. Interventions were classified as on-site medical interventions and hospital transports. Medical conditions were classified as injuries or illnesses and as mild or severe. Incidence rates per 1,000 participant-days and event rates per 100 participants were calculated.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 1,021 medical interventions and 114 hospital transports were recorded. Compared with non-athletes, athletes demonstrated substantially higher incidence rates across all analyzed outcomes. The pooled incidence rate ratio (IRR) was 5.88 (95% confidence interval (95% CI): 5.19-6.65) for total medical interventions and 16.69 (95% CI: 11.24-24.77) for hospital transports, with the largest between-group differences observed for injury-related medical interventions (IRR = 10.87, 95% CI: 8.76-13.49) and injury-related hospital transports (IRR = 24.44, 95% CI: 15.30-39.05). Mild conditions predominated in both groups, whereas injury-related conditions accounted for a greater proportion of medical interventions among athletes and illness-related conditions among non-athletes. Hospital transports were uncommon in both groups but occurred substantially more frequently among athletes and were predominantly injury-related. Muaythai, American football, BMX freestyle cycling, sumo, and beach handball had the highest hospital transport rates.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Athletes and non-athletes demonstrated distinct patterns of medical interventions and related medical conditions during major international multi-sport tournaments. Combined surveillance of both populations provides a comprehensive assessment of VMT workload and supports evidence-based medical planning for future tournaments.

articles.title: Moderate and Severe Traumatic Brain Injury Outcomes-A 20 Year (2002-2021) Analysis.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Although recognised as a leading cause of death and disability, it is unclear whether current treatment strategies have improved outcomes from blunt moderate to severe traumatic brain injuries (msTBI) due to a lack of available epidemiological data. This study sought to determine if in-hospital mortality and early functional outcomes of msTBI patients have changed over 20 years. Early functional outcomes were determined through the surrogate measure of the proportion of patients discharged directly to home.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A longitudinal cohort study using The Alfred Health Trauma Registry data. Subjects were aged 16-70 years with blunt msTBI (Head Abbreviated Injury Scale 3-5) admitted to The Alfred Trauma Service between 1 January 2002 and 31 December 2021.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 8222 patients presented with msTBI over the period, with 692 deaths (8.5%). Unadjusted in-hospital mortality decreased from 12.1% in 2002 to 4.0% in 2021 (OR 0.96, 95% CI 0.95-0.97, p < 0.001). Sensitivity analysis demonstrated a statistically significant reduction in the odds of death even after adjusting for injury severity (OR 0.96, 95% CI 0.93-0.99, p < 0.0001). The proportion of patients discharged to home increased from 30.6% to 60.8% over the period (OR 1.05, 95% CI 1.04-1.06, p < 0.001).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: There was a reduction in in-hospital mortality and an increase in the proportion discharged home for adults hospitalised with msTBI at The Alfred Hospital over the last two decades. These results foster optimism for the care of neurotrauma patients, but further research is required to identify the modifiable factors associated with these improved outcomes.

articles.title: Beyond canonical homeostasis: Dynamic, plastic, and intermittently unregulated physiology as the norm.

abstract.text: Homeostasis is often taught as steady-state regulation keeping internal variables within narrow limits-reflecting a mammalian bias. Yet, canonical homeostasis is far from universal. In many animals, including humans, normal physiological states allow some variables to fluctuate cyclically or stochastically while others remain tightly controlled. Indeed, across non-mammalian species, broad physiological variability is frequently normal rather than exceptional. Here we present case studies showing that plastic, variable regulation-sometimes approaching randomness-is both common and adaptive. Examples include intermittent breathing during diving, episodic feeding and digestion, pulsatile hormone release, variable sleep cycles, irregular gastric emptying, fluctuating renal blood flow, and stochastic immune responses. These complex regulatory patterns represent evolved strategies-not failures of homeostasis-allowing organisms to function efficiently in dynamic environments. Such flexible regulation, including unregulated intervals, may minimize energetic costs compared with continuous tight control, enhancing evolutionary fitness. We propose that variable degrees of physiological regulation have evolved as energy-efficient solutions shaped by natural selection. Expanding the concept of homeostasis to include intermittent and stochastic forms will improve our understanding of physiological adaptation, with significant implications for ecology and evolutionary biology. We further advocate new experimental approaches to distinguish adaptive variability from true regulatory failure.

articles.title: Nursing Competencies in Helicopter Emergency Medical Services (HEMS) in Spain: A Qualitative Study of Professional Profiles and Advanced Training.

abstract.label: AIM(S)
abstract.text: To explore how HEMS professionals perceive the role, competencies, training and professional development of nursing within aeromedical transport services in Spain, incorporating the perspectives of different professional profiles involved in HEMS operations.

abstract.label: DESIGN
abstract.text: An interpretative qualitative study using phenomenologically informed thematic analysis.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Semi-structured, in-depth interviews were conducted and analysed using phenomenologically informed thematic analysis. Data were systematically coded through open coding and organised into themes and subthemes using ATLAS.ti.

abstract.label: DATA SOURCES
abstract.text: Primary qualitative data were obtained from 17 purposively selected HEMS professionals through individual interviews. Interviews lasted 45-60 min, were audio-recorded and transcribed verbatim.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Four main categories emerged from the analysis: (1) access to the HEMS environment; (2) technical skills and competencies; (3) professional perspective and role development; and (4) structured professionalisation of the HEMS profile. Participants perceived that extensive prior experience in critical care settings, specialised academic training, supervised practice and advanced clinical simulation were necessary. Fully online training was widely perceived as insufficient. Participants identified core competencies, including advanced technical skills, knowledge of aerophysiology, aviation safety training, Crew Resource Management and Helicopter Underwater Escape Training. In addition, participants identified emotional resilience and physical fitness as personal attributes relevant to HEMS practice.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: According to participants, HEMS nursing in Spain was described as a complex and highly specialised professional profile, characterised by extensive critical-care experience, advanced technical competencies and structured, practice-oriented training. The absence of a formalised training pathway contrasts with international standards and points to a perceived need for greater professional recognition and standardisation of competencies to support safe and high-quality care.

abstract.label: IMPLICATIONS FOR THE PROFESSION AND/OR PATIENT CARE
abstract.text: The findings provide qualitative evidence that may inform the future development of structured training pathways, competency frameworks and professional recognition for HEMS nurses in Spain. The findings may also inform future research on standardised education, advanced simulation and aviation safety training. Further research is needed to determine whether these educational approaches improve clinical decision-making, patient safety and operational effectiveness in aeromedical transport.

abstract.label: IMPACT
abstract.text: The findings highlight the lack of a clearly defined and standardised competency framework and training pathway for HEMS nursing professionals in Spain. Participants perceived effective HEMS practice as requiring extensive prior critical-care experience, advanced technical competencies, supervised practical training and specific personal attributes, including emotional resilience and physical preparedness. These findings are relevant to HEMS nurses, educators, policymakers and healthcare managers involved in aeromedical services in Spain and may also contribute to international discussions on advanced nursing practice in air medical transport.

abstract.label: REPORTING METHOD
abstract.text: This study was reported in accordance with the Consolidated Criteria for Reporting Qualitative Research (COREQ) guidelines.

abstract.label: PATIENT OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION
abstract.text: No Patient or Public Contribution.

articles.title: Two-Step Sequential Screening for Frailty in Patients With Chronic Liver Disease: A Triage Efficiency Study of Liver Frailty Index Components.

abstract.label: AIM
abstract.text: To develop and validate a nurse-administered two-step sequential screening pathway based on single Liver Frailty Index components for identifying frailty in people with chronic liver disease.

abstract.label: DESIGN
abstract.text: A single-centre cross-sectional diagnostic accuracy study.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Overall, 606 hospitalised patients with chronic liver disease were enrolled between August 2021 and August 2025. Timed chair-stands and grip strength served as step-one index tests against frailty defined by the Liver Frailty Index (score of 4.5 or higher); bedridden patients were counted as screen-positive. Cutoffs were derived with the Youden index and stress-tested with bootstrap resampling and split-sample validation.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Frailty prevalence was 18.6%. The either-positive rule (chair stands of 16.55 s or longer, or grip strength of 23.42 kg or lower) achieved 100% sensitivity and a negative predictive value of 1.000, missing zero frail patients, while sparing 62.3% of patients from the complete index assessment. Zero missed cases were reproduced in five split-sample analyses.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: In this cohort, nearly two-thirds of full assessments could have been avoided without missing LFI-defined frailty cases. Prospective multicentre external validation of the frozen cutoffs is required before routine implementation.

abstract.label: IMPLICATIONS FOR THE PROFESSION AND/OR PATIENT CARE
abstract.text: The pathway may reduce the burden of complete frailty assessment in inpatient hepatology nursing practice, pending external validation.

abstract.label: IMPACT
abstract.text: Universal frailty screening in chronic liver disease is hindered by the burden of completing the full index. In this cohort, the first step identified all LFI-defined frailty cases while avoiding nearly two-thirds of complete assessments. These findings matter to hepatology nurses and inpatient hepatology services seeking feasible, guideline-concordant universal screening.

abstract.label: REPORTING METHOD
abstract.text: This study adhered to the Standards for Reporting of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies (STARD) 2015 guideline.

abstract.label: NO PATIENT OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION
abstract.text: Patients or the public were not involved in the design, conduct, reporting, or dissemination plans of this research.

articles.title: Symptomatic meningioma in the third trimester of pregnancy: a case report from Kenya.

abstract.text: Meningiomas, the most common primary central nervous system (CNS) tumors, are typically benign and hormonally responsive. They have a higher incidence in women, particularly during the reproductive years. Pregnancy may trigger rapid tumor progression and symptom onset due to elevated hormone levels. Although rare in pregnancy, meningiomas may adversely affect maternal and fetal outcomes, increasing the risk of complications such as preterm labor and gestational hypertension. Management strategies range from conservative monitoring to surgical intervention depending on gestational age, tumor size, severity of symptoms, and maternal-fetal stability. This report describes the case of a 34-year-old woman (para 1 + 2, gravida 4), with a history of type 1 diabetes mellitus, who presented to an obstetric emergency unit at 32 weeks of gestation. She had a one-day history of projectile vomiting (three episodes), severe global headache, right-sided hemiparesis, speech difficulty, and reduced fetal movement. She also had pre-existing anemia and a Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score of 14/15 on admission. Brain MRI revealed a left medial sphenoid meningioma with midline shift and hydrocephalus. On day 2, she underwent emergency caesarean section due to fetal tachycardia and distress. She was later admitted to intensive care after her GCS score dropped to 10/15 and she developed feeding difficulties. 2D echocardiography revealed a left ventricular ejection fraction of 38%. An emergency craniotomy was performed on day 4, and the tumor adherent to the middle cerebral artery was excised. She was discharged after 14 days with marked improvement. Six months post-discharge, she had made a full clinical recovery. Meningiomas in pregnancy pose diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. Management must be tailored to individual patient needs. A multidisciplinary team approach is essential to optimize both maternal and fetal outcomes.

articles.title: Brain edema progression rate on serial CT predicts neurological outcome after cardiac arrest: a region-specific biomarker of hypoxic-ischemic brain injury.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: To evaluate the prognostic performance of the attenuation change rate on serial brain computed tomography (CT), a novel quantitative marker of temporal cerebral attenuation change, for predicting poor neurological outcome after cardiac arrest (CA).

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This was a retrospective analysis of a prospective cohort. CA patients who underwent cranial CT both within 12 h and between 12 h and one week after return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) were included. The attenuation change rate, calculated as the HU difference between paired scans divided by the time interval, was measured in 12 predefined brain regions. Neurological outcome was assessed using the Cerebral Performance Category (CPC) at discharge.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 53 patients enrolled, 17 (32.1%) had favorable neurological outcomes at discharge. Patients with poor outcomes exhibited significantly greater attenuation decline rates in all gray matter regions except for gray matter at the centrum semiovale level, including the caudate nucleus (-0.01 vs. 0.02 HU/h), putamen (-0.02 vs. 0 HU/h), thalamus (-0.02 vs. 0.01 HU/h), gray matter of the high convexity (-0.02 vs. 0 HU/h), and cerebellar gray matter (-0.02 vs. 0.03 HU/h) (all P < 0.01), whereas no statistically significant differences were observed in any of the white matter regions. ROC analysis demonstrated AUCs ranging from 0.725 to 0.778, with cerebellar gray matter achieving the highest AUC (0.778; sensitivity, 75.0%; specificity, 76.5%). At the 100% specificity threshold, the caudate nucleus showed the highest sensitivity for predicting poor outcome (36.1% at a decline rate of -0.040 HU/h).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Serial CT-derived attenuation change rate may serve as an exploratory quantitative marker of cerebral edema progression after cardiac arrest. However, this single-center, small-sample study does not support its use for withdrawal of life-sustaining treatment decisions. Multicenter validation is warranted.

articles.title: Need-based Compared to Guidelines-based Fluid Administration in Dengue Patients with Warning Signs: An Open-label Randomized Study.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Fluid therapy is fundamental in dengue management. We evaluated an individualized, hemodynamic parameter-guided fluid strategy compared with standard World Health Organization (WHO) guideline-based care in dengue patients with warning signs.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In this open-label randomized controlled trial conducted at a tertiary care hospital in New Delhi (December 2019-October 2023), 80 adult dengue patients with warning signs were randomized (1:1) to receive either WHO guideline-based fluid therapy (control) or need-based therapy guided by noninvasive cardiac output monitoring (NICOM) and point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) (intervention). The primary outcome was hemodynamic stability assessed by systolic blood pressure (SBP), pulse pressure (PP), and mean arterial pressure over 48 h. Secondary outcomes included hospital stay, progression to severe dengue, and mortality.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Baseline characteristics were comparable across groups. The intervention arm demonstrated higher mean PP at 8 h (45.2 ± 11.6 mmHg vs. 39.8 ± 8.7 mmHg), 12 h (45 ± 11.3 mmHg vs. 38.9 ± 8.1 mmHg), and 24 h (44.1 ± 9.6 mmHg vs. 39.1 ± 6.6 mmHg) (P < 0.05). SBP was higher at 8 h (P = 0.02). However, progression to severe dengue (17.5% in both groups), hospital stay (5.4 vs. 5.5 days; P = 0.87), and mortality (none) were similar.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Although NICOM/POCUS-guided fluid therapy improved selected hemodynamic parameters, it did not translate into measurable improvements in clinical outcomes compared with WHO guideline-based care. Larger, multicenter studies powered for clinical endpoints in high-risk subgroups are warranted.

articles.title: The hidden severity of new psychoactive substances: clinical evidence from emergency and intensive care admissions in Taiwan.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: New psychoactive substances (NPS) have emerged as a growing threat in Taiwan, yet their clinical severity compared with traditional illicit drugs (TID) remains uncertain. This study aimed to compare the clinical characteristics and critical outcomes between patients with NPS and TID poisoning confirmed by liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS).

abstract.label: METHODS AND RESULTS
abstract.text: We conducted a multicenter retrospective cohort study across 10 hospitals within six medical systems in Taiwan. Between March 2019 and January 2020, 1,378 patients with suspected drug intoxication underwent urine LC-MS/MS analysis at certified toxicology laboratories. A total of 362 patients (26.3%) tested positive, including 147 (40.6%) with NPSs, 130 (35.9%) with TIDs, and 85 (23.5%) with mixed substances.Demographic, clinical, and laboratory data were collected through a chart review. Synthetic cathinones and ketamine analogs were the most frequently detected NPSs, whereas methamphetamine/amphetamine and morphine were predominant among TID cases. Critical outcomes were defined as intensive care unit admission or death in the emergency department. The overall rate of critical outcomes was 18.3% (252/1,378). The odds of critical illness did not significantly differ between NPS and TID users (adjusted odds ratio, 0.94; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.51-1.74). Kaplan-Meier survival analysis revealed no significant difference in short-term survival among the NPS, TID, and mixed-drug groups (log-rank p = 0.665).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: No statistically significant difference in clinical severity or mortality risk was observed between NPS and TID poisoning. These findings highlight that NPS exposure has a similar potential for critical illness and should be managed with the same clinical vigilance as conventional drug poisoning.

articles.title: Prehospital predictors of clinical outcomes in out-of-hospital cardiac arrest with pulseless electrical activity: a JCS-ReSS report.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) with pulseless electrical activity (PEA) has a poor prognosis and is aetiologically heterogeneous. We aimed to identify prehospital predictors of a favourable outcome, overall and by presumed aetiology.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This nationwide cohort study analysed 442,630 adults with OHCA and an initial rhythm of PEA from the All-Japan Utstein Registry between 2005 and 2024. The primary outcome was a favourable neurological outcome at 1 month. Two models were fitted, at the scene and at hospital arrival, each also within each aetiology. Epinephrine and advanced airway management (AAM) were assessed by time-dependent propensity score sequential matching.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: At the scene, a witnessed arrest (risk ratio [RR], 1.65) predicted a favourable neurological outcome, and a longer response time predicted a worse one (RR, 0.66; 10 versus 5 min). The gradient with age was steeper in cardiac than non-cardiac PEA (RR, 0.38 versus 0.78). At hospital arrival, prehospital return of spontaneous circulation (RR, 23.31) was the strongest predictor, but conversion to a shockable rhythm predicted a favourable outcome only in cardiac PEA and a worse outcome in non-cardiac PEA (RR, 1.37 versus 0.73). Standardised to a common covariate distribution, 1-month survival was higher in non-cardiac PEA, whereas a favourable neurological outcome was more likely in cardiac PEA. After time-dependent adjustment, the apparent harm from epinephrine and AAM was attenuated.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Prehospital information available before hospital arrival predicted a favourable neurological outcome, but its prognostic meaning depended on the presumed aetiology. These independent prehospital predictors could inform future risk stratification.

articles.title: Scapulothoracic Disarticulation of the Right Upper Limb After a Car-to-Obstacle Collision: A Case Report.

abstract.text: This report details the case of a 26-year-old man, victim of a car-to-barrier collision followed by a rollover. The patient, found conscious, was intubated by the pre-hospital team and admitted in severe hypovolemic shock, with extensive injury to the shoulder and right upper limb. After hemodynamic stabilization, the team performed bilateral chest drainage, a massive transfusion protocol, and a forequarter amputation of the right upper limb with ligation of the subclavian vessels, in a joint procedure by the orthopedic and vascular surgery teams. Postoperatively, he remained in the intensive care unit (ICU), developing ventilator-associated pneumonia, treated with meropenem and vancomycin. After 10 days, the patient was transferred to a ward. He was discharged from the hospital after 15 days of hospitalization and continued with outpatient follow-up, where he presented with phantom limb pain initially treated with gabapentin and controlled with physiotherapy. In the end, he was definitively discharged with good healing, pain improvement, and favorable clinical evolution.

articles.title: Management of pain and anxiety in children in the emergency department.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
